title: [Bug]: chatgpt/ device-code auth is synchronous and blocks the proxy event loop for up to 900s, killing the worker
body:
- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. Searched `is:issue "device code"` — 9 results, none reports this. #27175, #24562 and #17065 are different faults. ### What happened? A single request for a `chatgpt/*` model froze both of our proxy replicas for ~6.5 minutes each, until Kubernetes killed them. The proxy stopped answering every request, including `/health/liveliness`, and emitted no log output at all for the duration. The cause is that ChatGPT's device-code login is synchronous, and it is reached from an `async def` request handler: ``` async def async_response_api_handler() llms/custom_httpx/llm_http_handler.py:2730 → provider_config.validate_environment() llm_http_handler.py:2764 ← plain def, runs inline on the loop → ChatGPTResponsesConfig.validate_environment() llms/chatgpt/responses/transformation.py:41 → Authenticator.get_access_token() llms/chatgpt/authenticator.py:43 → _login_device_code() authenticator.py:143 → print(device code to stdout) authenticator.py:152 → _poll_for_authorization_code() authenticator.py:199 _get_httpx_client() :200 ← sync client while time.time() - start < DEVICE_CODE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: :203 time.sleep(...) :224, :230, :241 ``` The budget is set by the constants at `authenticator.py:25-28`: | Constant | Value | | --- | --- | | `DEVICE_CODE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `15 * 60` — 900 s | | `DEVICE_CODE_POLL_SLEEP_SECONDS` | `5` | | `DEVICE_CODE_COOLDOWN_SECONDS` | `5 * 60` | So one request can hold the event loop for up to 900 seconds. `_wait_for_access_token()` (`:362`, `while` at `:364`, `time.sleep` at `:373`) does the same for a second request arriving inside the cooldown. ```mermaid flowchart TD R["POST /v1/responses, model chatgpt/*"] --> H["async def async_response_api_handler()"] H --> V["validate_environment() — sync, no await point"] V --> P["device-code poll loop
time.sleep, up to 900 s"] P -.->|"event loop never yields"| S["starved on the same thread"] S --> S1["/health/liveliness and /health/readiness
never dispatched → orchestrator kills the worker"] S2["every other in-flight request"] --- S S3["uvicorn's own access log → total silence"] --- S ``` Three things turn this from slow into fatal on a proxy: 1. `validate_environment` is part of the sync provider-config interface. Every other provider returns headers in microseconds; this one waits on a human. Network I/O with sleeps does not belong behind a synchronous interface method. 2. It blocks during header construction, *before* any call to the model — so the model name after the prefix is irrelevant, and every `chatgpt/*` model is affected. 3. With `NUM_WORKERS=1` there is no sibling worker to answer the health probe, so the container fails its liveness check and is killed. Our probe error was `Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers` — the TCP connection was accepted, but no HTTP response ever came. This is not a one-time setup problem. The token file lives at `~/.config/litellm/chatgpt/auth.json` inside the container, so it is lost on every restart, and `_is_token_expired` re-arms the flow whenever the token expires. `llms/github_copilot/authenticator.py` has the same shape — sync `_get_httpx_client()`, `time.sleep(5)` at `:325`, `print(` at `:349` — so a fix should probably cover both. **What I expected instead:** a request that cannot authenticate returns an error promptly. A server should never print an interactive prompt to stdout, and should never block its event loop waiting for one to be answered. Either refuse the device flow when no TTY/interactive session exists and return a clear "ChatGPT auth not configured, run the login flow first" error, or run it in a thread with a short timeout so the loop keeps serving. ### User Flow **Before a (hypothetical) fix** — one user's request takes the proxy offline for everyone until the container is restarted. 1. User A sends `POST https:///v1/responses` with `{"model": "chatgpt/gpt-5.6-terra", "input": "hi"}` and a valid virtual key. 2. The request never returns. User A's client hangs with no status code and no error. 3. User B sends `POST https:///v1/messages` with a Claude model that has always worked. It returns `503 Service Unavailable` from the load balancer in front of the proxy. 4. User B sends `GET https:///health/liveliness`. The connection is accepted but no response headers ever arrive; the client times out. 5. This continues for ~6.5 minutes across ~300 requests from other users, all `503`. 6. The container is killed and restarted. Requests then succeed again, and User A's original request is gone with no response. 7. Any user holding a valid key can repeat step 1 at will and take the proxy down for every other user. **After a (hypothetical) fix** — the same request fails on its own and nobody else notices. 1. User A sends `POST https:///v1/responses` with `{"model": "chatgpt/gpt-5.6-terra", "input": "hi"}` and a valid virtual key. 2. The request returns promptly with an error explaining that ChatGPT authentication has not been completed for this deployment. 3. User B sends `POST https:///v1/messages` with the same Claude model. It returns `200 OK`. 4. User B sends `GET https:///health/liveliness`. It returns `200 OK`. 5. No other request is affected, and nothing is logged as an outage. 6. The container is not restarted. 7. A user holding a valid key can no longer affect any other user's requests. ### Proof the bug occurs **Setup.** Proxy on Kubernetes, one replica set of 2 pods, `NUM_WORKERS=1`, `litellm-gateway:v1.99.0`. Relevant config (models unrelated to the trigger removed, credentials redacted): ```yaml general_settings: store_model_in_db: true master_key: litellm_settings: callbacks: [...] model_list: - model_name: gpt-5.6-terra litellm_params: model: bedrock/openai.gpt-5.6-terra aws_region_name: us-east-1 model_info: mode: responses use_openai_responses_path: true ``` Liveness probe: `/health/liveliness`, `periodSeconds: 15`, `timeoutSeconds: 10`, `failureThreshold: 6`. Readiness probe: `/health/readiness`, `periodSeconds: 10`, `timeoutSeconds: 10`, `failureThreshold: 3`. No `chatgpt/*` model was in `model_list`. This was not a synthetic test — it is a production incident, and I have not re-run it deliberately because doing so takes the gateway offline. **Step 1-2 — the request that hangs.** A developer ran `codex --model chatgpt/gpt-5.6-terra` against the proxy. Both pods printed this to stdout within 533 ms of each other, with a different code each, and then went completely silent. Note there is no access-log line for the triggering request, because uvicorn logs only on completion: ``` 2026-09-02T15:23:37.192Z Sign in with ChatGPT using device code: 2026-09-02T15:23:37.192Z 1) Visit https://auth.openai.com/codex/device 2026-09-02T15:23:37.192Z 2) Enter code: XXXX-XXXXX 2026-09-02T15:23:37.192Z Device codes are a common phishing target. Never share this code. ``` Log output per pod, showing the gap — normal traffic right up to the prompt, then nothing until the replacement process boots: ``` pod A: 513 events 15:20:03 → 15:32:58, largest gap 403.8 s (15:23:37 → 15:30:20) pod B: 378 events 15:20:00 → 15:32:59, largest gap 410.9 s (15:23:37 → 15:30:28) ``` **Step 3 — other users get 503.** Load-balancer metrics per minute. `ELB_5XX` is generated by the load balancer itself; `Target_5XX` is what the proxy returned: ``` minute ELB_5XX ELB_503 Target_5XX TargetConnectionError 15:24 30 30 - - 15:25 22 22 - - 15:26 63 63 - - 15:27 45 45 - - 15:28 41 40 - - 15:29 65 65 - - 15:30 36 36 - - ``` `Target_5XX` and `TargetConnectionError` are empty for the whole window: the proxy returned nothing, so all ~301 errors were synthesised by the load balancer once both targets had dropped out of rotation. **Step 4 — health endpoints stop answering.** From the orchestrator, for both pods: ``` Liveness probe failed: Get "http://:4000/health/liveliness": context deadline exceeded (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers) Readiness probe failed: Get "http://:4000/health/readiness": context deadline exceeded (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers) ``` The connection was accepted and no headers came, i.e. the process was alive with a stalled loop. For contrast, a pod that was genuinely shutting down later reported `connect: connection refused`. **Step 6 — the container is killed.** Container state after the event, both pods: ``` reason=Error exit=137 (SIGKILL from the failed liveness probe, not OOMKilled) pod A: died 15:30:08, restarted 15:30:08, back up 15:30:20 pod B: died 15:30:15, restarted 15:30:15, back up 15:30:28 ``` The kill arrived at ~400 s, i.e. it interrupted the 900 s poll budget less than half way through. **Line references** were verified against the `litellm==1.99.0` wheel from PyPI, not the `main` branch. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.99.0 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details No response

title: Send x-opencode-session header on API requests (required by OpenCode Go from 09/05)
body:
Hi — we operate the OpenCode Go managed-inference API, and 635 of your users' orgs call it through LiteLLM (UA `litellm/1.98.0`).

Starting 09/05, requests without an `x-opencode-session` header will error on our side — we need a stable per-conversation ID for routing/optimization. LiteLLM doesn't send it in any version we've seen.

**Ask:** include `x-opencode-session: <stable-id-per-conversation>` on all outbound inference HTTP requests. Any stable UUID per conversation works. Happy to confirm from our telemetry once a build ships it. Thanks!

title: [Bug]: 41 of 85 openrouter/* entries disagree with openrouter.ai's own API on price (20 of them cite the page that contradicts them)
body:
### What happened?

41 of the 85 comparable `openrouter/*` entries in `model_prices_and_context_window.json` disagree with OpenRouter's own published price on at least one cost field — in both directions, from -89% to +3025%. **20 of the 41 carry a `source` field pointing at the exact OpenRouter model page that contradicts them.**

Anything that computes spend from `openrouter/*` entries — `completion_cost()`, the proxy's cost tracking, budgets and alerts — is off by these factors.

Verified 2026-09-03 against `GET https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models`, which is the same source `.github/scripts/auto_update_price_and_context_window_file.py` names, and spot-corroborated against the public model pages:

| model | registry | openrouter.ai API | public page |
|---|---|---|---|
| `openrouter/qwen/qwen3.5-plus-02-15` | $0.40 / $2.40 | $0.26 / $1.56 | "$0.26 / $1.56 per 1M" |
| `openrouter/openai/gpt-oss-120b` | $0.18 / $0.80 | $0.037 / $0.17 | "$0.03 / $0.17 per 1M" |

That OpenRouter's listed price is the intended value is confirmed by your own curated entries: `openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-5` has `source: https://openrouter.ai/anthropic/claude-opus-5` and matches that page exactly on all four cost fields.

### The drift is concentrated, not uniform

Correct today: **anthropic 11/11, google 6/6, openai 18/21**. Wrong today: **qwen 1/12, deepseek 1/9, z-ai 0/5, xiaomi 0/2, mistralai 4/9**. The frontier-lab families get audited; the open-weight long tail does not.

And these are not 41 independent typos. Several are one upstream repricing each — entries whose input *and* output are wrong by the identical factor:

- **×1.5385 (+53.8%) on both fields, n=4:** `qwen/qwen3-coder-plus`, `qwen/qwen3.5-27b`, `qwen/qwen3.5-flash-02-23`, `qwen/qwen3.5-plus-02-15` — consistent with a single ~35% Qwen price cut upstream that was never picked up.

| `openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v3.2` | 0.28 → 0.269 (+4%) | — | — | no |

### Why CI does not catch this

`.github/workflows/test-model-map.yml` runs exactly two things: `jq empty` (is it JSON) and `ci_cd/generate_model_prices_schema.py --check` (is the schema in sync).

The second one **generates the schema from the data file it is validating** — `build_schema(prices)` takes `all_keys` from the union of keys present, and takes the `mode` enum from `{entry["mode"] for entry in entries.values()}`. A schema derived from the data cannot reject that data's content. It can only reject a key name `classify()` can't place — and `classify()` sends anything containing `"cost"` to a non-negative number and anything starting with `"supports_"` to a boolean, so most novel names land softly too.

That is a useful thing to have (it keeps types and docs honest) but it is not a check on whether a number is *true*, and nothing else in CI is either. A cost value only has to be a non-negative float.

### Please don't fix this by switching on the existing auto-updater

`.github/workflows/auto_update_price_and_context_window.yml` is scheduled weekly, but no PR with its hard-coded title (`Update model_prices_and_context_window.json file`) has ever been opened, and the file's history is entirely hand-written commits — so it appears dormant. Three things in it would need fixing first; I'm flagging them as latent, not as live damage:

1. **`"max_tokens": row["context_length"]` writes the wrong field.** Your schema documents `max_tokens` as *"max output tokens if the provider specifies it, else max input tokens"*, and the curated entries use it that way — `openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-5` has `max_tokens: 128000` against a 1,000,000 context. Because `sync_local_data_with_remote()` does `local_data[key].update(remote_data[key])`, a run would overwrite the curated max-output value with the context window on every entry that has both.
2. **The `supports_vision` test is dead.** It fires on `architecture.modality == 'multimodal'`, and **0 of the 424** models in today's API use that value — the field is now `text+image->text` and 14 other compound forms. 256 live models accept image input. In the registry this shows up as 7 entries that are vision-capable upstream with no `supports_vision` (`openrouter/openai/gpt-5`, `-mini`, `-nano`, `openrouter/openai/gpt-5.2-codex`, `openrouter/mistralai/mistral-small-3.1-24b-instruct`, `-3.2-`, `openrouter/bytedance/ui-tars-1.5-7b`) and 3 that still carry `supports_vision: true` although upstream is now `text->text` (`openrouter/minimax/minimax-m2.1`, `openrouter/z-ai/glm-4.7`, `openrouter/z-ai/glm-4.7-flash`). None of the 7 are rescued by `fallback_generalizations` — all 7 rules are Claude/Bedrock-specific. `.update()` merges, so it can add or overwrite a field but never remove one; a flag that goes stale stays.
3. **It would fail your own schema check.** `openrouter/auto` and `openrouter/bodybuilder` return `"prompt": "-1"` as a sentinel; the importer does `float(...)` on it, and the generated schema gives every `*cost*` field `minimum: 0`.

### What I did not check

- Only the `openrouter/*` namespace. I did not look at any other provider.
- OpenRouter prices change whenever they like; this is a 2026-09-03 snapshot, and small deltas (the four entries under 10%) may just be recent moves rather than neglect.
- I excluded `openrouter/auto` and `openrouter/bodybuilder` from the 85 — the registry's `0` is arguably more sensible than the API's `-1`, and I'm not calling those defects.
- 60 live models now carry `pricing.overrides` (time-of-day and day-of-week rates) which this registry has no field for. I compared only the headline rate and am **not** counting those as errors — noting it only because it means a straight import wouldn't be complete either.
- I have not traced runtime resolution end to end, so what I am reporting is that the file disagrees with the source it names, not a measured billing delta in a running proxy.

Related but distinct: #33068 (openrouter Claude entries *missing*; still missing as of today — `openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`, `claude-opus-4.8` and `claude-fable-5` are live upstream and absent here). This issue is about entries that exist and are wrong.

### Reproduce

```bash
curl -s https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models -o or.json
python3 - <<'PY'
import json
reg={k:v for k,v in json.load(open('model_prices_and_context_window.json')).items()
     if isinstance(v,dict) and v.get('litellm_provider')=='openrouter'}
live={f"openrouter/{r['id']}": r for r in json.load(open('or.json'))['data']}
for k in sorted(set(reg)&set(live)):
    e,pr=reg[k],live[k]['pricing']
    for rf,lf in [('input_cost_per_token','prompt'),('output_cost_per_token','completion'),
                  ('cache_read_input_token_cost','input_cache_read')]:
        if rf in e and lf in pr and abs(e[rf]-float(pr[lf])) > 1e-9*max(e[rf],float(pr[lf])):
            print(f"{k:55s} {rf:30s} registry={e[rf]:<12g} live={float(pr[lf])}")
PY
```

author: reyyuy222

title: mid-stream fallback asymmetry: chat completions may lose partial usage, Responses API preserves it
body:
A third finding from the 30-project conformance check, following #39057 (cache-hit accounting) and #39455 (retry log inflation).

**The observation**

The router handles mid-stream failures differently depending on the API surface (`litellm/router.py`):

- **Chat completions**: if a stream has already produced content and then receives `MidStreamFallbackError` (~L2471-2477), the original exception is re-raised — no fallback. Whether the partial stream's usage was already logged depends on whether the failure logging path carries the accumulated usage (static analysis suggests it may not).

- **Responses API**: only pre-first-chunk failures trigger fallback (~L2479-2485, L2521). When fallback does occur, `stream_chunk_builder` extracts partial usage from the failed stream and merges it into the fallback stream (`_combine_fallback_usage` ~L2382-2404).

- **`FallbackStreamWrapper`** (~L2443-2450) reuses the original `model_response.logging_obj`, so the final success logging carries combined usage in one record.

**The question**

For the chat-completions "content already produced, no fallback" path: is the partial stream's usage (tokens consumed by the provider before the mid-stream error) captured in the failure log? If not, the cost of that partial generation exists on the provider bill but is invisible in spend_logs — a measurement blind spot for mid-stream failures.

The asymmetry itself is worth documenting: the Responses API path explicitly preserves partial costs via `_combine_fallback_usage`, while the chat-completions path may not.

Context: AgentMeasure conformance check; LiteLLM has been the most responsive project in the campaign (independent enforcement case + published fixture + maintainer engagement). This is the last high-priority finding from our audit.
author: roy-tong

title: router retries: how should consumers derive logical operations from inflated log counts?
body:
A follow-up measurement question from the 30-project conformance check, building on the cache-hit discussion in #39057.

**The observation**

The router's retry loop (`litellm/router.py`, ~L7152, `async_function_with_retries`) calls `self.make_call(original_function, ...)` for each attempt (~L7210, L7254). Each attempt is a complete `litellm.acompletion` invocation with its own Logging object, triggering success/failure callbacks independently.

Dollar spend is handled correctly: failed attempts without usage produce failure logs without spend, so the dollar total is not double-counted. But request/log counts inflate: a logical operation that succeeded on retry 3 produces 3 log entries (2 failure + 1 success), and any analytics counting "requests" or "calls" from the logs table counts 3 where the user intended 1.

The `attempted_retries` / `max_retries` metadata written into each request (~L7180, with the comment "used for spend logs retry tracking") suggests the authors are aware of the multi-entry shape.

**The question**

Is there guidance for consumers on how to derive "logical operations" from the logs table? E.g., group by a request correlation ID and count groups rather than rows? Or would an `operation_id` or `retry_group_id` field be considered useful on spend_logs entries?

Context: AgentMeasure conformance check; the attempt/operation boundary is our core invariant. LiteLLM has been one of the most responsive projects to this campaign — the cache-hit discussion in #39057 produced an independent enforcement case and a published fixture.
author: roy-tong

title: [Bug]: /v1/models omits mode for auto_router models even when set in model_info (max_input_tokens/max_output_tokens work fine)
body:
## What happened?

`GET /v1/models` never includes a `mode` field for a model whose `litellm_params.model` is `auto_router/<router_id>` (Auto Router / Complexity Router), even when `mode: chat` is explicitly set under that model's `model_info` in `config.yaml`.

This breaks Claude Code's gateway model discovery: Claude Code CLI relies on `/v1/models` to determine a custom model's context window / chat capability, and silently drops or errors on any model missing `mode`. As a result, an Auto Router configured for Claude Code (routing between e.g. Opus/Sonnet/Haiku tiers by prompt complexity) cannot be used as a normal selectable model in Claude Code — only real backing models can.

Note that `max_input_tokens` / `max_output_tokens` **do** come through correctly for the auto-router entry (via `Router.get_configured_token_limits`), so the config is being read — just not for `mode`.

## Root cause (found in source)

In `litellm/proxy/utils.py`, `create_model_info_response()`:

```python
try:
    model_cost_info: ModelInfo | None = get_model_info(model_id)
except Exception as e:
    ...
    model_cost_info = None

max_input_tokens: int | None = None
max_output_tokens: int | None = None
if model_cost_info is not None:
    max_input_tokens = coerce_token_limit(model_cost_info.get("max_input_tokens"))
    max_output_tokens = coerce_token_limit(model_cost_info.get("max_output_tokens"))
    mode: Final = model_cost_info.get("mode")
    if isinstance(mode, str):
        base["mode"] = mode

if llm_router is not None:
    configured_input, configured_output = llm_router.get_configured_token_limits(model_id)
    if configured_input is not None:
        max_input_tokens = configured_input
    if configured_output is not None:
        max_output_tokens = configured_output
```

`mode` is populated **only** from `litellm.get_model_info(model_id)` (the built-in cost map). For `auto_router/...` models this lookup fails/returns nothing (it's not a real provider model), so `model_cost_info` is `None` and `mode` is never set — regardless of what's configured in `model_info.mode`.

By contrast, `max_input_tokens`/`max_output_tokens` have a second, router-config-based fallback (`llm_router.get_configured_token_limits`). There is no equivalent `llm_router.get_configured_mode(...)` fallback for `mode`.

## Steps to Reproduce

`config.yaml`:
```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: claude-sonnet-5
    litellm_params:
      model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5
  - model_name: claude-opus-5
    litellm_params:
      model: anthropic/claude-opus-5
  - model_name: claude-auto
    litellm_params:
      model: auto_router/complexity_router
      return_raw_model_name: true
      complexity_router_config:
        tiers:
          SIMPLE: claude-sonnet-5
          COMPLEX: claude-opus-5
      complexity_router_default_model: claude-sonnet-5
    model_info:
      mode: chat
      max_input_tokens: 1000000
      max_output_tokens: 128000
```

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:4000/v1/models -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" | jq
```

## Actual

```json
{
  "id": "claude-auto",
  "object": "model",
  "created": 1677610602,
  "owned_by": "openai",
  "max_input_tokens": 1000000,
  "max_output_tokens": 128000
}
```
(no `mode`)

vs. a normal model (`claude-sonnet-5`) in the same list:
```json
{
  "id": "claude-sonnet-5",
  "object": "model",
  "created": 1677610602,
  "owned_by": "openai",
  "mode": "chat",
  "max_input_tokens": 1000000,
  "max_output_tokens": 128000
}
```

## Expected

`claude-auto` should also carry `"mode": "chat"`, sourced from its configured `model_info.mode` when the cost-map lookup fails (mirroring the existing token-limit fallback), so client-side discovery (e.g. Claude Code's `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` gateway integration) treats Auto Router models the same as any other configured chat model.

## Relevant log

Confirmed on a fresh `docker pull ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:latest` (digest `sha256:a53a7d3ffebede1925bd3ee8a21e4a7b9b63e2e68ec883af136edcccb6eeb82c`, reported proxy version `1.99.1`, pulled 2026-09-03). Also present on the previous `1.99.0` image (pulled 2026-09-01) — so this is not a recent regression, and predates it: the token-limit fallback (`get_configured_token_limits`) was added around #33721 (2026-07-18) without an equivalent for `mode`.

Related but distinct symptom: #20558 (Auto Router not shown in the `/model/info` admin table) — closed not-planned. This issue is specifically about the OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible `/v1/models` listing used for client-side model discovery, not the admin UI.

title: [Bug]: /v1/messages streaming delays message_start until the model's thinking pass finishes, even with no fallbacks configured
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

Streaming `/v1/messages` requests to an adaptive-thinking Bedrock model (e.g., Claude Sonnet 5 with `thinking: {"type": "adaptive"}`) deliver `message_start` and `content_block_start` only after the model's entire thinking pass finishes, instead of immediately when Bedrock actually sends them. The identical request sent directly to Bedrock, bypassing the proxy entirely, delivers `message_start` within about two seconds every time, regardless of how long the model then thinks before producing visible content.

Depending on `output_config.effort` and `max_tokens`, a model's thinking pass can take anywhere from a few seconds to several minutes. For that entire window, a client of the proxy sees nothing but periodic SSE keepalive pings, with no way to tell a genuinely slow request apart from a hung one, even though the underlying provider already answered with its lifecycle frames in about two seconds.

This reproduces with zero fallback deployments configured for the model, so there is no fallback attempt this behavior could be protecting.

Expected: `message_start` and `content_block_start` reach the client as soon as the provider sends them, independent of how long the model then takes to produce its first real content.

## Suggested fix

`Router._aanthropic_messages_streaming_iterator` wraps every streaming `/v1/messages` response so a mid-stream provider error can retry against a fallback deployment before any lifecycle frame commits the client to the current attempt. To make that safe, it buffers `message_start`, `content_block_start`, and any `ping` behind buffered frames, only releasing them once the first `content_block_delta` arrives, since forwarding `message_start` and then falling back would produce two overlapping message lifecycles on one SSE stream

That buffering is applied unconditionally, with no check for whether the router has any fallback deployment configured to retry against in the first place. For an adaptive-thinking model, Bedrock's first `content_block_delta` does not arrive until the entire thinking pass finishes, so the buffering ends up holding `message_start`, an event that carries no content and is not itself part of what a fallback would need to redo, hostage for the full length of that pass, even when there is nothing to fall back to

The fix: gate the buffering behind whether any fallback (general, context-window, content-policy, or a catch-all default) could actually resolve for the requested model group. With no fallback destination configured, forward the source stream live, exactly as it streams without this wrapper, since there is nothing left to protect. When a fallback is configured, keep the existing buffer-until-content behavior unchanged

This router-level fix needs to land together with the existing httpx `chunk_size=1024` fix on the Bedrock invoke reader (already present at the commit this proof was captured against). Tested in isolation, the router fix alone gets `message_start` out in about two seconds, but `content_block_start` still doesn't arrive until the thinking pass finishes: httpx's byte-chunker slices the raw stream into fixed 1024-byte pieces regardless of where an event-stream frame boundary falls, so `content_block_start`'s frame can get split across that boundary and its remainder sits buffered inside httpx until more bytes happen to arrive. Both fixes together are needed for every lifecycle frame to forward live, not just the first one


### User Flow

Before a (hypothetical) fix: a developer streaming a request through the proxy's `/v1/messages` endpoint sees no bytes at all for as long as the model spends thinking, even though the exact same request straight to Bedrock starts streaming in about two seconds

1. They send `POST https://<proxy-domain>/v1/messages` with `model` set to a Bedrock adaptive-thinking model (e.g. `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5`), `"thinking": {"type": "adaptive"}`, `"output_config": {"effort": "max"}`, and `"stream": true`
2. Their client's own timing log shows no data for many seconds, with only an `event: ping` frame arriving roughly every 15 seconds
3. The first real event, `event: message_start`, does not appear until the model finishes its entire thinking pass, which for a large `max_tokens` ceiling can be a minute or more later
4. Sending the identical request body directly to Bedrock, bypassing the proxy, returns `event: message_start` within about two seconds every time, so the developer has no way to tell in advance whether their next call through the proxy will start in two seconds or two minutes

After a (hypothetical) fix: the same developer sees `event: message_start` arrive within about two seconds, matching a direct call to Bedrock, and only the model's own thinking time (not the proxy) accounts for any further wait before visible content

1. They send the same `POST https://<proxy-domain>/v1/messages` with the same body
2. `event: message_start` and `event: content_block_start` arrive within about two seconds
3. `event: ping` keepalives may still appear while the model keeps thinking, but only after the real lifecycle events already reached the client
4. The remaining wait for `event: content_block_delta` matches the model's own thinking time exactly, the same as calling Bedrock directly


### Proof the bug occurs


Config the proxy ran with (no fallbacks configured anywhere in the file):

```yaml
model_list:
- litellm_params:
    model: us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5
    aws_region_name: us-west-2
  model_info:
    litellm_provider: bedrock
    input_cost_per_token: 2.2e-06
    output_cost_per_token: 1.1e-05
    id: us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5
  model_name: us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5
```

Ran with `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` set (a short-term Bedrock API key), which rules out AWS credential resolution as a factor

Version / commit: `x-litellm-version: 1.101.0`, commit `2ffe6a1dc846d5168b375110b5ab3ffb36439a93`

Commands and their full output: 

[aws_support_bedrock_thinking_stall_repro.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31761028/aws_support_bedrock_thinking_stall_repro.py)

[ttfb_litellm_direct.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31761080/ttfb_litellm_direct.py)


title: [Bug]: /team/list omits a user's member teams in other orgs when they hold org_admin anywhere (_authorize_and_filter_teams if/elif)
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

Related (same class of bug — a caller's scope being re-filtered — but a different code path and the **inverse** symptom): #30215 (`/v2/team/list`, org_admin sees too *few* teams in their *own* org) and #25493. This report is about `/team/list` (v1) and `_authorize_and_filter_teams`.

### What happened?

A user who is `org_admin` of **any** organization cannot see teams they are a plain `user`-role member of in **other** organizations via `GET /team/list` — even when passing their own `user_id`, and even with no `organization_id` filter.

A user with **no** `org_admin` role anywhere gets their member teams back correctly. So this only affects the mixed-role case (admin in one org, plain member in another), which is likely why it isn't widely reported. It surfaces in the dashboard's key-creation team picker, which is populated by `fetch_teams` → `teamListCall(accessToken, orgId, userID)` → `/team/list`.

### Reproduction (API)

Setup:
- Org **A** and org **B**.
- User **U** is `org_admin` of A (via `/organization/member_add`, `role: org_admin`).
- Team **T** lives in B. U is a `user`-role member of T (via `/team/member_add`).
- U has a plain virtual key (no `team_id` on the key).

As U:

```bash
GET /team/list?user_id=<U>                       # -> only A's teams. T is missing.
GET /team/list?user_id=<U>&organization_id=<B>   # -> []          (T is missing)
GET /user/info                                    # -> teams: [..., <T>]   (membership is known)
```

Control — same setup but U holds **no** `org_admin` anywhere:

```bash
GET /team/list?user_id=<U>                       # -> [T]   (correct)
```

Confirmation: granting U `org_admin` on B makes T appear — i.e. the only "fix" is to over-grant admin on every org the user has a team in.

**Expected:** `GET /team/list?user_id=<U>` returns every team U is a member of, across all orgs (org-admin teams *plus* direct memberships).
**Actual:** only teams inside orgs where U is `org_admin`; direct memberships elsewhere are dropped.

### Root cause

`litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/team_endpoints.py`, `_authorize_and_filter_teams` (`main` @ `ed9d29a9b45d`, lines ~5261 and ~5275):

```python
if allowed_org_ids is not None:
    # Org admin: query DB for teams in their orgs
    org_teams = ...find_many(where={"organization_id": {"in": allowed_org_ids}})
    if not user_id:
        return list(org_teams)
    return [t for t in org_teams if <user_id in t.members_with_roles>]
elif user_id:
    # Regular user: fetch all and filter by membership
    ...
```

`allowed_org_ids` is populated whenever the caller holds `org_admin` in **any** org. The `if` branch then returns only teams *inside those orgs* and the function never reaches the `elif user_id:` membership branch. The inline comment states the intent was additive:

> `# Check if user is an org admin (even for own queries, so they see org teams)`

…but the `if`/`elif` makes it exclusive: org-admin teams **instead of** member teams, not **in addition to** them.

### Suggested fix

Compute both sets and return their union when the request is an own-query (`user_id == caller`):

- org-admin teams (existing `if` branch), **plus**
- all teams where `user_id` is in `members_with_roles` (existing `elif` branch),

de-duplicated by `team_id`. The `not user_id` early return (proxy/org admin listing all org teams) can stay as-is.

### Relevant log output

No error — the request returns `200` with a truncated list.

### What LiteLLM version are you on?

Reproduced on a self-hosted proxy at **v1.96.2**. The affected code is unchanged in `main` (`ed9d29a9b45d`). Not re-verified against v1.97.1 (released today), but the function is identical in `main`.
author: robbinsjd4

title: [Bug]: per-callback turn_off_message_logging is ignored when a request fails, so opted-out logging destinations receive full prompts
body:
### Check for existing issues

I searched the existing issues and this is not a duplicate. #16336 was the same class of problem, redaction not being applied on every path, but it covered a different field and is closed

### What happened?

LiteLLM lets you turn message logging off for a single logging destination rather than globally, so one tool can hold full traces while another holds redacted payloads. That scoping is honoured while requests succeed and is skipped when a request fails, so every failed request hands the complete user prompt to the destination that was configured never to receive it

The teams I work with depend on exactly this split, with one observability tool holding full content for debugging and a second, far more widely accessible one holding redacted payloads. Failed requests are the ones people actually go and inspect, so this is silent exposure on the worst possible sample

There is no configuration that avoids it today. Turning message logging off globally does cover failures, but it redacts in place for every destination at once, which destroys the full content traces the first tool exists for. The per-request redaction headers and the dynamic callback params are all or nothing for that request, so they cannot express "redact for this destination only"

What I expected: a logging destination that turned message logging off receives redacted messages on failed requests, the same way it already does on successful ones, while destinations that did not turn it off keep receiving full content

### User Flow

Before a (hypothetical) fix: an admin who set up one full-content logging destination and one redacted destination finds real user prompts sitting in the redacted one as soon as a request fails

1. The admin starts the proxy with two logging destinations configured, leaves global message logging on, and turns message logging off for the second destination only
2. A developer sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions for a Claude model, with a prompt containing a customer name and account number, and a max_tokens value the provider will reject
3. The provider rejects the call and the developer gets back HTTP 400 carrying an invalid_request_error about max_tokens
4. The admin opens the first destination and sees the request with the full prompt, which is what that destination is for
5. The admin opens the second destination and sees the same full prompt, "My name is Jane Doe and my account number is 12345678", where they expected "redacted-by-litellm"
6. Anyone who has access only to the second destination, deliberately the wider audience, can read prompt content for every failed request

After a (hypothetical) fix: the same failed request leaves prompt content only in the destination that is meant to hold it

1. The admin starts the proxy with two logging destinations configured, leaves global message logging on, and turns message logging off for the second destination only
2. A developer sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions for a Claude model, with a prompt containing a customer name and account number, and a max_tokens value the provider will reject
3. The provider rejects the call and the developer gets back HTTP 400 carrying an invalid_request_error about max_tokens
4. The admin opens the first destination and sees the request with the full prompt, which is what that destination is for
5. The admin opens the second destination and sees "redacted-by-litellm" in place of the prompt
6. Someone who has access only to the second destination can no longer read prompt content for failed requests, and full content debugging in the first destination is unchanged

### Proof the bug occurs

Config the proxy ran with, `config.yaml`:

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: claude-test
    litellm_params:
      model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929
      api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY

litellm_settings:
  turn_off_message_logging: false
  callbacks: ["custom_callbacks.redacted_logger", "custom_callbacks.full_logger"]
```

The two logging destinations, `custom_callbacks.py`, each writing what it was handed to a file so the contents are visible without standing up two SaaS accounts:

```python
import json
import os
from litellm.integrations.custom_logger import CustomLogger

OUT = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "out")


class RecordingLogger(CustomLogger):
    def __init__(self, name, turn_off_message_logging):
        super().__init__()
        self.name = name
        self.turn_off_message_logging = turn_off_message_logging

    def _dump(self, kwargs):
        slo = (kwargs or {}).get("standard_logging_object") or {}
        with open(os.path.join(OUT, f"{self.name}.json"), "w") as f:
            json.dump({"status": slo.get("status"), "messages": slo.get("messages")}, f, indent=2, default=str)

    async def async_log_failure_event(self, kwargs, response_obj, start_time, end_time):
        self._dump(kwargs)
```

title: [Bug]: Reset-budget job never self-heals a budget_duration=null row with a stale budget_reset_at — spend is silently zeroed on every tick forever
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

A team (or user/key) row with `budget_duration = null` (i.e., "no reset" configured) but a **non-null, past** `budget_reset_at` gets picked up by the reset-budget scheduler on **every single run**, has its `spend` zeroed each time, and is never rescheduled out of this state — because the reset logic that would normally advance `budget_reset_at` only runs when `budget_duration is not None`.

As of a recent version, `/team/update` (and the equivalent key endpoint) can clear a stuck `budget_reset_at` if an operator explicitly re-sends `"budget_duration": null` in the update payload — but this is a manual workaround, not a fix: it only helps once someone notices the row is stuck and knows to do this. The scheduler itself still has no self-healing path, so any row that reaches this state through some other route (a bulk import, a migration, a race with another writer, or simply before anyone notices) keeps having its spend silently zeroed every cycle indefinitely, with no automatic recovery and no alerting.

Root cause — selection query (`litellm/proxy/utils.py`, team/user/key branches; team shown, others have the same shape):

    elif query_type == "find_all" and reset_at is not None:
        response = await TeamRepository(self).table.find_many(
            where={
                "OR": [
                    {"AND": [{"budget_reset_at": None}, {"NOT": {"budget_duration": None}}]},
                    {"budget_reset_at": {"lt": reset_at}},
                ],
            }
        )

The second `OR` branch selects any row where `budget_reset_at < now`, with **no filter on `budget_duration`** — a null-duration row with a past `budget_reset_at` matches it every tick.

Reset logic (`litellm/proxy/common_utils/reset_budget_job.py`, `_reset_budget_common`):

    item.spend = 0.0
    if hasattr(item, "budget_duration") and item.budget_duration is not None:
        item.budget_reset_at = compute_budget_reset_at(budget_duration=item.budget_duration, settings=reset_settings)
    return item

`spend` is zeroed unconditionally; `budget_reset_at` only advances when `budget_duration is not None`, so a null-duration row is left exactly where it was — in the past — and matches again on the very next tick, forever.

**Related issues:** #27734 (closed by #28302) fixed the "`/team/update`/`/key/update` silently ignore `budget_duration: null`" bug — that PR only touched `key_management_endpoints.py` and `team_endpoints.py`, and is why the manual-clear workaround above exists. It did not touch `proxy/utils.py` or `reset_budget_job.py`, so it does not fix the scheduler-side defect reported here. #22013 (closed) fixed the mirror-image trigger for the `Budget` table (`budget_duration` set but `budget_reset_at` still null, immediately after creation) — that fix is the `{"AND": [{"budget_reset_at": None}, {"NOT": {"budget_duration": None}}]}` clause visible in the query above; it never added the missing `budget_duration IS NOT NULL` guard to the second `OR` branch, which is what this issue is about.

### User Flow

Before a (hypothetical) fix: a team has no reset schedule configured, but a leftover past "next reset" timestamp, and it never recovers on its own.

1. (However this state was reached) an admin calls GET https://<proxy-domain>/team/info?team_id=<id> and sees "budget_duration": null, "budget_reset_at" showing a timestamp already in the past, and "spend": 5.32 (real accumulated cost).
2. Some time later, with no action taken by anyone, the admin calls GET https://<proxy-domain>/team/info?team_id=<id> again and sees "spend": 0 — the team's spend has been wiped even though budget_duration is null and nobody asked for a reset. "budget_reset_at" is unchanged, still the same past timestamp.
3. The admin checks again later: if any usage occurred in between it has been zeroed again, and "budget_reset_at" is still stuck in the past. This repeats forever.
4. As a workaround, the admin calls POST https://<proxy-domain>/team/update with body {"team_id": "<id>", "budget_duration": null}. After this, GET https://<proxy-domain>/team/info?team_id=<id> finally shows "budget_reset_at": null — but this required an admin to notice the team was stuck and take manual action; a team nobody is watching stays trapped indefinitely.

After a (hypothetical) fix: the scheduler ignores budget_duration=null rows regardless of budget_reset_at, with no manual step required.

1. Same starting state: "budget_duration": null, "budget_reset_at": <past timestamp>, "spend": 5.32.
2. The admin calls GET https://<proxy-domain>/team/info?team_id=<id> repeatedly over time — "spend" keeps accumulating normally and is never zeroed, since no reset was ever configured for this team.
3. No call to POST https://<proxy-domain>/team/update is required to reach or maintain this state.

### Proof the bug occurs

Config the proxy ran with:

  general_settings:
    master_key: sk-****

Version: v1.97.0 (scheduler defect also confirmed unchanged on v1.83.10-stable and v1.84.10; the /team/update manual-clear step in the "Before" flow above only works on v1.97.0, not on the two older versions — it does not change the root cause)

Commands and full output:

  # Force a team into the trapped state directly (simulating how such a row is reached in
  # practice — legacy data, a migration, or a bug elsewhere — since /team/update alone can no
  # longer produce budget_duration=null + a non-null budget_reset_at from a clean team on this version):
  $ psql -c "UPDATE \"LiteLLM_TeamTable\" SET budget_duration = NULL, budget_reset_at = now() - interval '1 day', spend = 5.0, max_budget = 100 WHERE team_id = '3f0cb32c-b6be-4b27-98ba-c9a20d7dc252';"

  $ curl -sf http://localhost:4000/team/info?team_id=3f0cb32c-b6be-4b27-98ba-c9a20d7dc252 -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-local-test" | jq '.team_info | {spend, budget_duration, budget_reset_at}'
  {"spend": 5.0, "budget_duration": null, "budget_reset_at": "2026-09-01T18:18:26.275000Z"}

  # ~10 minutes later (default scheduler interval, no action taken):
  $ curl -sf http://localhost:4000/team/info?team_id=3f0cb32c-b6be-4b27-98ba-c9a20d7dc252 -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-local-test" | jq '.team_info | {spend, budget_duration, budget_reset_at}'
  {"spend": 0.0, "budget_duration": null, "budget_reset_at": "2026-09-01T18:18:26.275000Z"}

Container log confirming the scheduler tick fired and updated this team:

  18:27:44 - LiteLLM Proxy:DEBUG: reset_budget_job.py:502 - Keys to reset []
  18:27:44 - LiteLLM Proxy:DEBUG: reset_budget_job.py:682 - Updated teams [...]

spend dropped 5.0 -> 0.0 with no request made and no /team/update call; budget_reset_at never moved from the past timestamp.

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

v1.97.0

title: [Bug]: Team/user/key budget reset job silently defaults an unparseable budget_duration (e.g. "") to a daily reset
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

If a team (or user/key) row has `budget_duration` set to an empty string `""` (as opposed to `null`), LiteLLM's periodic reset job (`ResetBudgetJob`) — and the `/team/new` creation path itself — treats this as a "provided" duration and computes a reset schedule for it, which silently resolves to **"reset every 24 hours at midnight UTC"**, even though `""` was never intended to mean "daily." This wipes `spend` every 24 hours on any row that ends up with `budget_duration=""`, with no error and no way to reject the value up front.

Root cause: in `litellm/litellm_core_utils/duration_parser.py`, `get_next_standardized_reset_time` does:

    value, unit = _parse_duration(_normalize_duration(duration))
    if value is None:
        # Fall back to default if format is invalid
        return current_time.replace(hour=0, minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0) + timedelta(days=1)

`_parse_duration("")` can't match its regex against an empty string and returns `(None, None)`, so this silently computes "next midnight" instead of raising or treating the value as "no reset." The same fallback is reached with no validation in between from both `litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/team_endpoints.py::new_team` (computes `budget_reset_at` at creation time whenever `budget_duration is not None`, true for `""`) and `ResetBudgetJob._reset_budget_common` on every scheduler tick. No `field_validator` exists on any `budget_duration` field in `litellm/proxy/_types.py`, so `""` is never rejected at the API layer.

As of a recent version, this fallback also logs a `WARNING` ("Unrecognized budget_duration %r; falling back to a next-midnight reset...") — but the behavior itself is unchanged.

**Related issues:** #17993 is a different bug in the same file (`duration_parser.py`) — a day-rollover miscalculation for large second/minute/hour duration values — not a duplicate of this one, which is about an *unparseable* value (`""`) being silently accepted rather than rejected.


### User Flow

Before a (hypothetical) fix: an admin creates a team meaning it to never auto-reset, and it ends up on a silent daily reset instead.

1. Admin calls POST https://<proxy-domain>/team/new with body {"team_alias": "my-team", "budget_duration": ""}.
2. The response comes back HTTP 200 immediately, with "budget_duration": "" and "budget_reset_at" already set to next midnight UTC (e.g. "2026-09-03T00:00:00Z") — no error, even though a daily reset was never requested.
3. The next day, the admin calls GET https://<proxy-domain>/team/info?team_id=<id> and sees "spend": 0 — all of the team's accumulated spend is gone, and "budget_reset_at" has rolled forward to the following midnight.
4. This repeats every 24 hours indefinitely; the team's spend field never reflects more than one day of usage.

After a (hypothetical) fix: an empty/unparseable budget_duration is rejected or treated as "never reset."

1. Admin calls POST https://<proxy-domain>/team/new with the same body {"team_alias": "my-team", "budget_duration": ""}.
2. Either the request comes back with a 4xx validation error naming budget_duration, so the admin corrects it before the team is created — or the team is created with "budget_duration": null and "budget_reset_at": null, the same state as leaving the field blank.
3. GET https://<proxy-domain>/team/info?team_id=<id> the next day, and every day after, shows spend accumulating normally with no silent reset.

### Proof the bug occurs

Config the proxy ran with (general_settings/litellm_settings/model_list omitted here as not relevant to this bug — a minimal config with any working model_list reproduces this):

  general_settings:
    master_key: sk-local-test

Version: v1.97.0 (also confirmed unchanged on v1.83.10-stable and v1.84.10)

Commands and full output:

  $ curl -sf -X POST http://localhost:4000/team/new \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-**" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"team_alias": "issue1-empty-duration-test", "budget_duration": ""}'
  {
    "team_id": "1c8c0ae8-21c6-4d3a-9759-d78633e9dc3e",
    "team_alias": "issue1-empty-duration-test",
    "budget_duration": "",
    "budget_reset_at": "2026-09-03T00:00:00Z"
  }

Container log line confirming the fallback fired at creation time:

  18:17:57 - LiteLLM:WARNING: duration_parser.py:141 - Unrecognized budget_duration ''; falling back to a next-midnight reset. Use the <int><unit> format (e.g. '1h', '7d', '30d', '1mo').

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

v1.97.0

title: [Bug]: Chart issues within Istio enabled set-up
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

The following issue is related to charts, not LiteLLM itself.

## Istio automatic protocol selection on `Service` ports

Istio does automatic protocol selection when a service port is named in a specific way ([reference](https://istio.io/latest/docs/ops/configuration/traffic-management/protocol-selection/#explicit-protocol-selection)). LiteLLM exposes the port as `http` ([example from gateway service](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/litellm_internal_staging/helm/litellm/templates/gateway/service.yaml#L15)) which can break in an Istio enabled namespace.

In an ideal world, the name of the port or the `appProtocol`, should be customisable on the Helm chart. In general, most will want to set it up as `tcp` for Istio.

## Istio / NetworkPolicies targeting ports

Although the `Service` resource allows custom ports ([example](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/litellm_internal_staging/helm/litellm/templates/gateway/service.yaml#L12)), some resources might constrain pods and not services ports, such as Network Policies. As of now, the container ports declared in the Deployment pod template do not allow custom ports ([reference](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/litellm_internal_staging/helm/litellm/templates/gateway/deployment.yaml#L50-L53)), potentially requiring full chart fork if netpols must stay as they are.

### User Flow

1. User install charts within a Kubernetes cluster
2. HTTPRoute targeting the service does not work due to `http` protocol selection

### Proof the bug occurs

Chart version: 1.99.1

Other

v1.99.1

title: [Feature]: Support timeout override for /mcp (per-route and per-request)
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

**Body**  
## Summary
`/mcp` currently relies on a default timeout of 60s, which can be too short for valid MCP workloads.

## Request
Please add timeout override support for `/mcp`, aligned with the existing model used in `/chat/completions` (where timeout can be passed in the request body).

## Proposal
1. **Per-route timeout config** for `/mcp`  
2. **Per-request timeout** in `/mcp` request body

## Precedence
1. Per-request timeout  
2. `/mcp` route-level timeout  
3. Global/default timeout (60s)

## Why
- Avoid premature timeouts on longer MCP operations  
- Keep behavior consistent across `/chat/completions` and `/mcp`  
- Provide better operational control without breaking defaults

## Acceptance criteria
- `/mcp` accepts timeout override in request payload  
- `/mcp` supports route-level timeout configuration  
- Precedence is documented and tested  
- Default behavior remains unchanged when no override is provided

### User Flow

Without this feature, it is not possible to override MCP timeout per path/request.  
The only available workaround is increasing the global timeout, which affects unrelated routes and can mask real overhead/performance problems that should be diagnosed instead of broadly tolerated.

In practice, some MCP paths need longer execution windows while others do not.  
A global timeout change is too coarse-grained and reduces observability of path-specific latency issues.

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Error: {'error': 'timeout', 'message': 'MCP tool call timed out after 60.0s'}"}],"isError":true}}

title: [Bug]: Responses-to-Chat bridge keeps reasoning_effort dict when summary is set; strict OpenAI-compatible providers reject it (Codex CLI unusable)
body:
Reporting a third consumer-side manifestation of the dict-form `reasoning_effort` problem already tracked in #37452 (Ollama `TypeError: unhashable type: 'dict'`) and #35649 (Fireworks 400 via the Anthropic adapter) — this one is the **Responses→Chat bridge forwarding the dict to a strict OpenAI-compatible provider**, and it makes Codex CLI unusable against such upstreams:

## What happened

A model configured with `use_chat_completions_api: true` (upstream serves `/v1/chat/completions` only; strict Go-backed OpenAI-compatible schema). Codex CLI sends `reasoning: {"effort": "...", "summary": "auto"}` on **every** request. The bridge's summary-preserving branch (below) keeps the whole dict, sends it as chat `reasoning_effort`, and the provider rejects it:

```
litellm.InternalServerError: OpenAIException - json: cannot unmarshal object into Go struct field
GeneralOpenAIRequest.reasoning_effort of type string
```

Every request fails; Codex retries into its rate limit (`Maximum 8 requests within 1 minutes` on our route), producing a reconnect loop identical in effect to the Ollama report.

## Root cause

`litellm/responses/litellm_completion_transformation/transformation.py`, ~L275-291 (present on current main):

```python
if isinstance(reasoning_param, dict):
    # Keep the full dict when summary is set so the responses API bridge can
    # forward it; otherwise use the effort string for chat completion (e.g. Gemini).
    if "summary" in reasoning_param:
        reasoning_effort = reasoning_param        # dict -> chat wire
    elif "effort" in reasoning_param:
        reasoning_effort = reasoning_param.get("effort")  # correct string
```

The Chat Completions wire format defines `reasoning_effort` as a **string**; `summary` is a Responses-only field with no Chat Completions meaning. The branch's stated purpose ("so the responses API bridge can forward it") applies to *Responses-native* providers — but this code is also on the *chat bridge* path, where the dict is invalid for every strict-schema consumer. Tolerant providers (OpenAI itself) mask it, which is why this only surfaces per provider.

Two notes for triage:

* LiteLLM already contains the correct normalization — `OpenAIGPT5Config._map_openai_params` (`litellm/llms/openai/chat/gpt_5_transformation.py` ~L215-223) converts `{"effort": ..., "summary": ...}` → the effort string, with the docstring "Config/deployments may pass the Responses API format". But it only applies to models matching `is_model_gpt_5_model`, so any other model behind the `openai/` adapter (our case: `z-ai/glm-5.3-free`) takes the base `OpenAIGPTConfig` path, which has no normalization.
* Fixing this at the bridge (extract the effort string, drop `summary`) would resolve all three reports' shared root cause: #37452's crash comes from the same dict arriving in `OllamaChatConfig.map_openai_params`, and #35649's is the same dict shape produced by a different adapter.

## Reproduction (deterministic, no special client needed)

Against the bridged route, `POST /v1/responses` with `reasoning: {"effort": "low"}` succeeds; the identical body with `{"effort": "low", "summary": "auto"}` fails with the provider 500 above. Directly against the upstream `/v1/chat/completions`: `reasoning_effort: "high"` (string) → 200; `reasoning_effort: {"effort": "high"}` or with `summary` → the same unmarshal error. So the delta is purely dict-vs-string, and only the bridge's `summary` branch produces the dict.

Verified on LiteLLM **1.98.0** (Python 3.14, proxy/SDK) and the branch is unchanged on current main. Codex CLI always sends `summary`, so there is no client-side workaround.

## Suggested fix

In the Responses→Chat bridge transformation, always extract `reasoning_param.get("effort")` as the string when present, regardless of `summary` (the field has no Chat Completions semantics). The `summary` key can be dropped or serialized into a separate Responses-only passthrough if a native-Responses provider ever needs it. Happy to provide a PR with tests if that direction is agreed — wanted to check first whether the "keep the full dict" behavior is load-bearing for any provider you consider supported.

title: [Bug]: gpt-5.4+ tools+reasoning bridge to /v1/responses doesn't recognize custom OpenAI api_base still backed by the real api.openai.com (e.g. PrivateLink)
body:
### What happened?

`responses_api_bridge_check()` in `litellm/main.py` only auto-bridges gpt-5.4+ (e.g. gpt-5.6) requests with function `tools` and an **unset** `reasoning_effort` to `/v1/responses` when the resolved `api_base` is the literal default OpenAI URL (`https://api.openai.com/v1`) or Azure:

```python
on_constraint_enforcing_endpoint: Final = custom_llm_provider == "azure" or resolved_api_base.strip() in (
    "",
    _OPENAI_DEFAULT_API_BASE,
)
```

Any other custom `api_base` is assumed to be a "chat-only OpenAI-compatible backend" that tolerates function tools with reasoning on Chat Completions, so the bridge doesn't fire and the request is sent to `/v1/chat/completions` unmodified.

This assumption breaks when the custom `api_base` still points at the real `api.openai.com` — for example, when routing OpenAI traffic through a network-egress control endpoint such as AWS/Azure PrivateLink (something like `https://privatelink.<some-subdomain>.api.openai.com/v1`), which is a common enterprise deployment pattern and is explicitly supported by LiteLLM's `api_base` parameter. In that case the backend is genuinely `api.openai.com` and enforces the exact same constraint as the default endpoint, so Chat Completions rejects the request with:

```
Function tools with reasoning_effort are not supported ... use /v1/responses or set reasoning_effort to 'none'
```

Because reasoning defaults to "on" server-side for gpt-5.4+ when `reasoning_effort` isn't explicitly set, virtually every unset-effort tool-calling request against such a deployment hits this 400. A router-level fallback doesn't help since the fallback deployment gets the identical (still-incompatible) payload.

### Suggested fix

Recognize custom `api_base` hosts whose hostname still ends in `api.openai.com` (which covers PrivateLink-style hostnames) as constraint-enforcing, in addition to the literal default URL and Azure, so the bridge fires correctly for these deployments too.

### Relevant log output

```
litellm.exceptions.BadRequestError: OpenAIException - Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': "Function tools with reasoning_effort are not supported. Please use the Responses API (/v1/responses) or set reasoning_effort to 'none'.", 'type': 'invalid_request_error', ...}}
```

No

v1.98.0

title: [Bug]: Add baseten/zai-org/GLM-5.3 to the model pricing registry
body:
## Check for existing issues

- [x] I searched the existing LiteLLM issues and pull requests for `baseten/zai-org/GLM-5.3`; no matching report or change exists.

## What happened?

LiteLLM's current model pricing registry does not contain `baseten/zai-org/GLM-5.3` in either `model_prices_and_context_window.json` or `litellm/model_prices_and_context_window_backup.json`. A gateway using LiteLLM's native Baseten adapter can route requests to `baseten/zai-org/GLM-5.3`, but LiteLLM reports that the model is not mapped and cannot supply its provider pricing, token limits, or capability metadata unless every deployment duplicates that information locally.

The existing `zai/glm-5.3` entry is not a fallback for this route: it belongs to the Z.AI provider and has different cached-input pricing. The existing Baseten registry only includes `baseten/zai-org/GLM-5`.

Expected behavior: the built-in registry contains a `baseten/zai-org/GLM-5.3` entry in both generated registry files, backed by Baseten's public Model API documentation and pricing. Current Baseten values are $1.40 per million input tokens, $0.14 per million cached input tokens, and $4.40 per million output tokens; its live Model API advertises a 1,048,576-token context and a 262,144-token maximum output.

Suggested metadata includes the Baseten provider, chat mode, the three price fields, token limits, always-on reasoning with `low`/`high`/`max`, function/tool calling, parallel function calling, response schemas, prompt caching, and text-only modality. Please update both registry JSON files and add the normal metadata regression test so they cannot drift.

Baseten sources:

- https://www.baseten.co/pricing/
- https://docs.baseten.co/inference/model-apis/overview
- https://docs.baseten.co/inference/model-apis/reasoning

## User Flow

Before a hypothetical fix: a LiteLLM Proxy administrator exposes Baseten GLM-5.3, but the gateway cannot obtain the model's built-in pricing and limits.

1. The administrator configures a Proxy deployment with `model: baseten/zai-org/GLM-5.3` and a Baseten API key.
2. A user sends `POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions` with model `zai-org/GLM-5.3`.
3. The Baseten request can be routed, but the gateway has no built-in `baseten/zai-org/GLM-5.3` model metadata; inspecting the model through LiteLLM reports `This model isn't mapped yet` unless the administrator duplicates prices and limits in the deployment configuration.
4. The administrator must maintain a local pricing override, which can drift from Baseten's published rates.

After a hypothetical fix: the same Baseten route resolves its provider metadata from LiteLLM's built-in registry.

1. The administrator configures the same Proxy deployment with `model: baseten/zai-org/GLM-5.3` and a Baseten API key.
2. A user sends the same `POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions` request with model `zai-org/GLM-5.3`.
3. LiteLLM resolves the Baseten GLM-5.3 pricing, token limits, and capabilities without a deployment-local pricing override.
4. The administrator can remove the temporary local metadata and receive registry updates through normal LiteLLM upgrades.

## Proof the bug occurs

Config / setup:

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: zai-org/GLM-5.3
    litellm_params:
      model: baseten/zai-org/GLM-5.3
      api_key: os.environ/BASETEN_API_KEY
```

Versions checked:

- LiteLLM `v1.99.0`, commit `fa647f742d7baefe8eb1181899d9c81b41559772`
- Current `litellm_internal_staging`, commit `2ce4e3f8a99e12efce9433640059d9fca7bfb448`

Exact v1.99.0 runtime reproduction using the immutable published image:

```console
$ docker run --rm -i --entrypoint python ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:1.99.0@sha256:570a872d2fde8f1bc4a147634810941103c14697270f0f2918c5aa7d8201cac5 - <<'PY'
import json
import litellm

print("model key present:", "baseten/zai-org/GLM-5.3" in litellm.model_cost)
try:
    info = litellm.get_model_info(model="zai-org/GLM-5.3", custom_llm_provider="baseten")
    print(json.dumps(info, indent=2, sort_keys=True, default=str))
except Exception as exc:
    print(f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")
PY
model key present: False
Exception: This model isn't mapped yet. model=zai-org/GLM-5.3, custom_llm_provider=baseten. Add it here - https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/main/model_prices_and_context_window.json.
```

Current default-branch registry reproduction:

```console
$ sha=2ce4e3f8a99e12efce9433640059d9fca7bfb448
$ for path in model_prices_and_context_window.json litellm/model_prices_and_context_window_backup.json; do curl -fsSL "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/$sha/$path" | jq '."baseten/zai-org/GLM-5.3"'; done
null
null
```

This is a static model-registry defect and does not require sending a billable provider request: the missing exact key is the failing boundary. Baseten's public sources above provide the expected live prices and limits.

## What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Other — model pricing and context-window registry.

`v1.99.0`; also reproduced at current `litellm_internal_staging` commit `2ce4e3f8a99e12efce9433640059d9fca7bfb448`.

title: [Bug]: OpenAI reasoning-model prompt cache never carries forward through /v1/messages → Responses API bridge (encrypted_content dropped, even after #37953)
body:
## Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

## What happened?

When a client speaks Anthropic's `/v1/messages` protocol (e.g. Claude Code) and LiteLLM bridges that to an OpenAI **reasoning** model via the Responses API, prompt caching for the reasoning portion never hits across turns. Every turn re-prices as a cold cache miss for the reasoning tokens, no matter how long the conversation runs.

This is **not** the same bug as #24985 / #24425 / #36197 (all closed, fixed by #37953). Those fixed thinking blocks being flattened into visible assistant text (a correctness/leak bug). This issue is about **prompt-cache continuity** specifically, and #37953 explicitly does not address it — its own PR description states reasoning items "come back unsigned" and are never replayed with `encrypted_content`.

**Root cause:** OpenAI's prompt cache for reasoning models requires the *exact* prior-turn reasoning item to be either (1) replayed verbatim via `input` with its `encrypted_content`, or (2) chained via `previous_response_id` (server-side, OpenAI holds the state). Anthropic's own protocol correctly drops `thinking` blocks from conversation history once a turn completes — real Claude models don't need them replayed, since Claude's own server-side caching never depended on the client resending them. But that means the bridge has nothing from the client to replay to OpenAI. `#37953` fixed the *shape* of the round-trip (reasoning item vs. flattened text) but did not add `encrypted_content` request/replay or `previous_response_id` chaining, so OpenAI never receives anything it can use to continue the cache — even on a version containing that fix.

**Expected:** cache tokens on a reasoning model behind this bridge should compound turn-over-turn the same way they already do for a real Anthropic Claude model behind the same proxy.
**Actual:** cache tokens stay at (or near) zero on every single turn.

## User Flow

A developer runs Claude Code against a LiteLLM proxy in front of an OpenAI reasoning model, with extended thinking enabled, and has a multi-turn conversation.

### Before a (hypothetical) fix — cache never engages

1. The user starts Claude Code with `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` pointing at the proxy and a reasoning model selected. They ask a question that needs extended thinking.
2. Claude Code sends `POST https://<proxy>/v1/messages` with `"thinking": {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": 4000}` and the user's message.
3. A `200` comes back with a `thinking` block followed by a `text` reply; Claude Code shows "Thought for Ns" on screen, then the answer. The response body's `usage.cache_read_input_tokens` is `0` — expected, since there's nothing to cache yet on turn 1.
4. The user asks a related follow-up in the same session. Claude Code sends a second `POST https://<proxy>/v1/messages`, replaying the prior conversation per Anthropic's protocol (the `thinking` block from turn 1 is not resent — only the visible reply and any tool activity are replayed, exactly as a real Claude client behaves).
5. A `200` comes back with a new `thinking` block and answer. `usage.cache_read_input_tokens` in this response is again `0` — identical to a completely fresh conversation, even though the bulk of turn 2's input is identical to turn 1's.
6. The user continues the conversation for 10+ turns. `cache_read_input_tokens` stays at `0` (or negligible) on every single turn. Their usage/billing dashboard shows every turn priced as a full cold request — the discount for repeated context never appears, no matter how long the session runs.

### After a (hypothetical) fix — cache engages like it does for Claude

1. Same setup: user starts Claude Code against the proxy, reasoning model selected, asks a question needing extended thinking.
2. Same first `POST https://<proxy>/v1/messages` — same `200` response, `usage.cache_read_input_tokens` is `0` on turn 1 (still expected — nothing to cache yet).
3. User asks the same follow-up. Claude Code sends the same second `POST https://<proxy>/v1/messages`, replaying history the same way (no client-side change needed).
4. The `200` response's `usage.cache_read_input_tokens` is now **greater than zero**, tracking the size of the shared prefix from turn 1 (including the previously invisible reasoning). The billed cost for turn 2 reflects the cached-token discount.
5. Across a 10+ turn session, `cache_read_input_tokens` keeps growing turn-over-turn, matching how the same proxy already behaves for this same user's conversations against a real Anthropic Claude model.

## Proof the bug occurs

Verified on a real multi-turn conversation with a `gpt-5.6`-family OpenAI reasoning model, accessed through this bridge from Claude Code, at litellm `v1.98.0`. Checked two independent ways: litellm's own debug logs, and a separate wire-level capture of the traffic actually reaching `api.openai.com`.

- Turn-by-turn `cached_tokens` on the *unpatched* bridge: `0` on every turn, for the entire session — no compounding, regardless of how much of the conversation repeats turn-over-turn. This matches exactly what the root cause predicts: with no `previous_response_id` chaining and no `encrypted_content` replay, every turn is sent as an independent request with nothing for OpenAI's cache to match against.
- After prototyping a proxy-side fix (session-chained `previous_response_id`, described in "Suggested direction" above) on the same setup: `cached_tokens` compounded exactly hop-to-hop across 4 turns (`0 → 10124 → 10794 → 11245`), and each `previous_response_id` sent upstream was byte-identical to the prior turn's real response id. A 4th turn asking to summarize the whole conversation, with no other context given, correctly recalled all 3 prior turns — confirming the chained reasoning state was genuinely being used by the model, not just accepted without effect.

We're not including the raw debug-log/packet-capture output itself here, but the measurement above is real and reproducible with the reproduction steps and User Flow described earlier in this issue — happy to run the repro fresh at a maintainer's request if the aggregate numbers aren't enough to act on.

## What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

## What LiteLLM version are you on?

v1.98.0
