title: [Bug]: Background health check sends `supports_max_reasoning_effort` as a request field to Bedrock (400), for models without `supports_*_reasoning_effort` in the model map
body:
### What happened?

With `general_settings.background_health_checks: true`, `/health` reports a Bedrock Claude deployment as unhealthy. Bedrock returns **400** with:

```
{"message":"supports_max_reasoning_effort: Extra inputs are not permitted"}
```

`supports_max_reasoning_effort` is a **capability flag**, not a request parameter — it looks like it is leaking from the model metadata into the request body, but only on the health-check code path.

**The same deployment serves normal traffic fine.** Over 24h it handled 194 requests via `/chat/completions` with no occurrence of this error.

### What makes it a health-check-path issue

I reproduced the health-check payload through the normal completion path against the *same* deployment. All three succeed:

| Request via `/v1/chat/completions` | Result |
|---|---|
| `{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}` | 200 OK |
| same + `"max_tokens": 10` | 200 OK |
| `{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"test from litellm"}], "max_tokens": 10}` (mirrors the health-check payload) | 200 OK |
| **actual background health check on the same model** | **400** |

Same model, same deployment config, same effective payload — only the code path differs.

### What distinguishes an affected model

Two Bedrock Anthropic deployments in the same proxy, configured identically (both set `thinking`, `drop_params: true`, `additional_drop_params`):

| `model_info` field | affected model | unaffected sibling |
|---|---|---|
| `supports_max_reasoning_effort` | `None` | `True` |
| `supports_xhigh_reasoning_effort` | `None` | `True` |
| `bedrock_output_config_effort_ceiling` | `None` | `xhigh` |

Only the one **without** these flags fails. There is a related warning emitted for that same model:

```
anthropic_claude3_transformation.py:761 - Bedrock Invoke: stripping unsupported `output_config`
for model=<model> — neither `supports_output_config` nor any `supports_*_reasoning_effort`
flag is set in model_prices_and_context_window.json.
```

So the failure appears to be in the branch taken when those capability flags are absent.

### Relevant log output

```
litellm.BadRequestError: BedrockException - {"message":"supports_max_reasoning_effort: Extra inputs are not permitted"}
stack trace: Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../litellm/llms/custom_httpx/llm_http_handler.py", line 254, in _make_common_async_call
    response = await async_httpx_client.post(
  File ".../litellm/litellm_core_utils/logging_utils.py", line 289, in async_wrapper
    result = await func(*args, **kwargs)
  File ".../litellm/llms/custom_httpx/http_handler.py", line 667, in post
    await _raise_masked_async_error(e, stream)
  File ".../litellm/llms/custom_httpx/http_handler.py", line 454, in _raise_masked_async_error
    raise MaskedHTTPStatusError(e, message=_text, text=_text) from None
litellm.llms.custom_httpx.http_handler.MaskedHTTPStatusError: Client error '400 Bad Request'
for url 'https://bedrock-runtime.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/...'
```

Note the request does reach Bedrock — this is AWS rejecting the field, not client-side validation.

### Why it matters

The model is healthy and serving production traffic, but shows permanently red on `/health` and on any dashboard built on it. A health signal that is wrong on your busiest model trains people to ignore it.

### Impact / workaround

No good workaround. Setting the capability flags would silence it, but that means asserting a model capability we have not verified — papering over the symptom with a possibly false claim.

### What LiteLLM version are you on?

v1.93.0 (`LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True`), Python 3.13, provider `bedrock`, region `us-west-2`, deployed via the proxy on Kubernetes.
author: GordonWei

title: [Bug]: `langfuse_tags` header crashes router retry/fallback on deployments with `litellm_credential_name` (400 instead of failover)
body:
## What happened?

When the proxy runs a Langfuse callback (`langfuse_otel` or `langfuse`) and a request carries a `langfuse_tags` header, any request whose **first attempt fails cannot retry or fall back**. The next attempt dies with `AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'append'`, and the client gets a 400 `invalid_request_error` instead of a failover. The 400 also defeats retry policy (`BadRequestErrorRetries: 0` is a common setting) and misreports an internal crash as a client error.

### Root cause

Two writers share one mutable `metadata["tags"]` with different type contracts, across retry attempts that reuse the same kwargs dict:

1. `LangFuseLogger.add_metadata_from_header` (litellm/integrations/langfuse/langfuse.py, `metadata[trace_param_key] = proxy_headers.get(...)`) copies the raw header value — a **string** like `"org:x,agent:y"` — into the shared `litellm_params["metadata"]` **in place**. `langfuse_otel.py` reuses the same helper via `_extract_langfuse_metadata`.
2. `Router._update_kwargs_with_deployment` (litellm/router.py, "CREDENTIAL NAME AS TAG" branch; `router.py:3110` in v1.96.2, `~:3490` on main) assumes a **list**: `existing_tags.append(credential_tag)`.

Sequence: attempt 1 fails → failure logging runs the Langfuse callback → the callback overwrites `tags` with the header string → the router sets up the retry deployment → if it has `litellm_credential_name`, `str.append` raises → request returns 400.

The sibling `## DEPLOYMENT-LEVEL TAGS` branch just above has a silent variant: `list(existing_tags)` explodes the string into single characters (tag corruption, no crash).

## Reproduction (v1.96.2)

Config: `callbacks: ["langfuse_otel"]`; a model group with two deployments — one that fails (e.g. bad creds) and one with `litellm_credential_name`.

```bash
curl http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "langfuse_tags: org:x,agent:y" \
  -d '{"model":"<group>","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say ok"}]}'
```

Differential result (12 alternating requests, first attempt fails ~50%):
- With header: `200 200 200 400 400 400` — every first-attempt failure → crash.
- Without header: all `200` — identical failures silently fail over.

Unit-level:

```python
from litellm.integrations.langfuse.langfuse import LangFuseLogger
litellm_params = {"proxy_server_request": {"headers": {"langfuse_tags": "org:x,agent:y"}}, "metadata": {}}
metadata = litellm_params["metadata"]
returned = LangFuseLogger.add_metadata_from_header(litellm_params, metadata)
assert returned is metadata            # mutates the shared dict in place
assert metadata["tags"] == "org:x,agent:y"   # a str, not a list
metadata["tags"].append("Credential: x")     # AttributeError — the router's exact call
```

## Expected behavior

Header tags must not change retry/fallback behavior. `tags` should be parsed into a list at ingestion.

## Relevant log output

```
litellm.llms.azure.common_utils.AzureOpenAIError: Missing credentials. ...
  File ".../litellm/router.py", line 2819, in _acompletion
    self._update_kwargs_with_deployment(deployment=deployment, kwargs=kwargs)
  File ".../litellm/router.py", line 3110, in _update_kwargs_with_deployment
    existing_tags.append(credential_tag)
AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'append'
INFO: ... "POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1" 400 Bad Request
```

Client body: `{"error":{"message":"Invalid request format: 'str' object has no attribute 'append'","type":"invalid_request_error","code":"400"}}`

## Suggested fix

- Parse in `add_metadata_from_header`: for the `tags` key, split the header value on commas into a list (mirror of #36740, which already coerces header-sourced `mask_input`/`update_trace_keys` but not `tags`).
- Defensively, type-guard both router tag branches (`## DEPLOYMENT-LEVEL TAGS`, `## CREDENTIAL NAME AS TAG`).

## Related

- #7801 / #7825 fixed the same string at the logging **read** site only; ingestion and router sites remain.
- #30042 (open) rewrites the credential-tag lines for a different bug. As written it would mask this crash while corrupting: iterating the header string yields characters. Worth coordinating.

## LiteLLM version

v1.96.2 (both sites verified still present on `main` as of 2026-08-30).
author: chun-mavenagi

title: [Bug]: `stream_options.include_usage=true` collapses streamed tool-call arguments into an end-of-stream burst
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I searched existing streaming/usage/tool-call issues. This is not #36114, #28735, #37485, #29491, or #20711: those cover usage accuracy/spec shape or other adapters. This report is specifically about **client-visible chunk timing/granularity** on `/v1/chat/completions`.

## What happened

With an OpenAI-compatible vLLM upstream, LiteLLM changes a long streamed function/tool call from hundreds of incremental `delta.tool_calls[].function.arguments` chunks into roughly ten chunks, with most of the payload arriving in a burst near the end, **only when `stream_options.include_usage=true` is present**.

The same upstream request sent directly to vLLM streams correctly. Removing `include_usage` from the request sent through LiteLLM restores incremental delivery.

This matters for agent runtimes and UIs that consume tool-call arguments incrementally. In our case `@openai/agents` `OpenAIChatCompletionsModel` always sends `stream_options: {"include_usage": true}`, so the application cannot simply opt out without an ingress rewrite.

## Environment

- LiteLLM Proxy: `1.98.0-rc.1`
- Upstream: vLLM OpenAI-compatible `POST /v1/chat/completions`
- Client: `@openai/agents`, `OpenAIChatCompletionsModel`
- Model: reasoning/thinking model that emits a long function/tool call
- Streamed field consumed by the application: `choices[0].delta.tool_calls[0].function.arguments`
- `stream: true`

## Isolation / measurements

Same model, prompt, tools, and upstream deployment:

| Path | `include_usage` | Observed tool-argument stream |
|---|---:|---|
| client → vLLM directly | `true` | **218 argument-delta chunks**, spread over ~2.5 s; first around 9.7 s, last around 12.2 s |
| client → LiteLLM → vLLM | `true` | **~10 chunks**, most delivered in a final burst |
| client → LiteLLM → vLLM | omitted | incremental again |

Disabling reasoning also appears to reduce the symptom, but A/B testing isolated `include_usage` as the request-level trigger.

The direct-vLLM `include_usage=true` control is important: vLLM itself does **not** buffer the tool-call arguments when usage is requested.

## Minimal request shape

Any OpenAI-compatible reasoning model that emits a sufficiently large tool call should exercise the path. For example:

```json
{
  "model": "<openai-compatible-model>",
  "stream": true,
  "stream_options": {"include_usage": true},
  "messages": [
    {"role": "user", "content": "Call submit_document with a detailed multi-paragraph document."}
  ],
  "tools": [
    {
      "type": "function",
      "function": {
        "name": "submit_document",
        "description": "Submit a generated document",
        "parameters": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {"document": {"type": "string"}},
          "required": ["document"]
        }
      }
    }
  ],
  "tool_choice": "required"
}
```

A useful probe is to timestamp every received tool-argument delta:

```python
start = time.monotonic()
async for chunk in stream:
    for choice in chunk.choices:
        for tc in getattr(choice.delta, "tool_calls", None) or []:
            args = getattr(getattr(tc, "function", None), "arguments", None)
            if args:
                print(f"{time.monotonic() - start:.3f}s len={len(args)}")
```

Expected through LiteLLM: timing/granularity should remain close to the direct-vLLM control. Actual with `include_usage=true`: the argument events are heavily coalesced and arrive near EOS.

## Expected behavior

`stream_options.include_usage` should only cause the final usage information to be surfaced. It should **not** change the forwarding cadence or granularity of earlier content/tool-call deltas.

In particular, LiteLLM should forward each upstream tool-call argument delta as soon as it is available, while independently accumulating whatever shadow state is needed for logging/spend/usage.

## Actual behavior

Enabling `include_usage` changes the client-visible stream from hundreds of incremental tool-argument deltas to a small number of chunks concentrated at the end of generation.

For UI/document-generation tools this looks like a frozen stream followed by a nearly complete document appearing at once.

## Source-level observations

The current streaming implementation already appears intended to be non-buffering: `CustomStreamWrapper` keeps `self.chunks` as a shadow copy for usage/logging and normally returns `processed_chunk` from `__anext__()` immediately.

However, usage-bearing chunks take a special path: LiteLLM copies the chunk, strips `usage`, reconstructs a `ModelResponseStream`, and can `continue` if the reconstructed result is considered empty. At EOS it also rebuilds the complete response with `stream_chunk_builder()` for logging/usage.

Current `litellm_internal_staging` (which is ahead of `v1.100.0-rc.1`) still contains this special usage path. I have not yet claimed the production reproduction against staging; this report is against `1.98.0-rc.1`, with staging source inspected to identify the likely area and to prepare a regression test.

Normal success callbacks should also not require buffering the client stream; async success handling is dispatched separately after reconstruction. So the 218 → ~10 collapse looks unintended rather than a necessary consequence of usage accounting.

## Suggested regression test

Use a fake OpenAI-compatible async upstream stream that yields:

1. a role/tool-call-start chunk,
2. 100+ small `function.arguments` fragments with distinct values,
3. a `finish_reason="tool_calls"` chunk,
4. a usage-only chunk,
5. `[DONE]`.

Run it through the same proxy `/v1/chat/completions` path twice, with and without `stream_options.include_usage=true`.

Assert that:

- every argument fragment is emitted downstream in order,
- enabling `include_usage` does not reduce/coalesce the number of argument-bearing SSE frames,
- the terminal usage chunk is still correct,
- usage/spend logging still receives the assembled response.

## Related issues / why this is distinct

- #36114: streaming usage values are corrupted/undercounted; this issue is **stream delivery timing/granularity**.
- #28735: synthetic usage chunk has the wrong `choices` shape; not this timing issue.
- #37485: `prompt_tokens_details` lost during streaming usage reassembly; not client-visible tool delta buffering.
- #29491: tool input loss on another adapter/provider path; similar symptom family, different isolation.
- #20711 / #20712: Responses API tool-argument deltas dropped when later chunks omit tool-call `id`; this reproduction is native Chat Completions and occurs only with `include_usage`.

I can provide a patch/regression test against `litellm_internal_staging`; the desired invariant is that **usage tracking is side-band and must never gate forwarding of already-received upstream deltas**.

title: [Bug]: InfinityError uses a mutable default argument for headers, shared across all instances
body:
### What is the issue?

`InfinityError.__init__` in `litellm/llms/infinity/common_utils.py` (line 7) uses a mutable default argument for `headers`:

```python
class InfinityError(BaseLLMException):
    def __init__(self, status_code: int, message: str, headers: dict | httpx.Headers = {}):
```

Because default argument values are evaluated once at function-definition time, every `InfinityError` raised without an explicit `headers` argument shares the exact same `{}` object. Both real call sites do exactly that:

- `litellm/llms/infinity/embedding/transformation.py:120` - `raise InfinityError(message=raw_response.text, status_code=raw_response.status_code)`
- `litellm/llms/infinity/rerank/transformation.py:113` - `raise InfinityError(message=raw_response.text, status_code=raw_response.status_code)`

`headers` is forwarded straight to `BaseLLMException.__init__`, which stores it by direct reference (`self.headers = headers`, no copy). Any code that later does `some_infinity_error.headers["X"] = "Y"` (a plausible thing to do when adding retry-after/rate-limit metadata to a caught exception, which is a normal pattern elsewhere in the codebase for other `.headers` attributes) would silently leak that mutation onto every other `InfinityError` instance raised without explicit headers, past or future - same failure mode as #38874, just on `InfinityError.headers` instead of the vector store registries.

Every sibling provider's exception class already avoids this - `OpenAIError`, `AnthropicError`, and the shared `BaseLLMException` base class itself all correctly default `headers` to `None`:

```python
# litellm/llms/openai/common_utils.py
class OpenAIError(BaseLLMException):
    def __init__(
        self,
        status_code: int,
        message: str,
        ...
        headers: dict | httpx.Headers | None = None,
        ...
```

`InfinityError` appears to be the only provider error class in `litellm/llms/` still using the unsafe `= {}` default (checked via `grep -rn "headers.*=\s*{}\s*)" litellm/llms/ --include="*.py"`).

### Reproduction

```python
from litellm.llms.infinity.common_utils import InfinityError

e1 = InfinityError(status_code=500, message="first error")
e2 = InfinityError(status_code=500, message="second error")

print(e1.headers is e2.headers)  # True - shared mutable object

e1.headers["x-debug"] = "leaked"
print(e2.headers)  # {'x-debug': 'leaked'} - unrelated exception instance is corrupted
```

### Proposed Solution

Match the convention already used by `BaseLLMException`, `OpenAIError`, and `AnthropicError`:

```python
class InfinityError(BaseLLMException):
    def __init__(self, status_code: int, message: str, headers: dict | httpx.Headers | None = None):
        self.status_code = status_code
        self.message = message
        self.request = httpx.Request(method="POST", url="https://github.com/michaelfeil/infinity")
        self.response = httpx.Response(status_code=status_code, request=self.request)
        super().__init__(
            status_code=status_code,
            message=message,
            request=self.request,
            response=self.response,
            headers=headers,
        )
```

`BaseLLMException.__init__` already accepts and stores `headers=None` correctly (`self.headers = headers`), so no other change is needed downstream.
author: NinaadRao

title: [Bug] Proxy strips delta.reasoning_items from streaming chunks on the fast-serialization path
body:
### What happened

A streaming chat-completions response served **by the proxy** loses `delta.reasoning_items` — the provider's encrypted reasoning state. The same stream through the SDK's `CustomStreamWrapper` keeps the field, so the loss happens in the proxy's SSE serialization, after the stream wrapper is done with the chunk.

Clients of the proxy can therefore never round-trip encrypted reasoning: every turn of a multi-turn tool loop starts without the previous turn's reasoning state.

### Where

`_fast_serialize_simple_model_response_stream` (`litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py`) hand-builds the JSON for "simple" text chunks and emits only `role` and `content`. It declines richer chunks through `unsupported_delta_fields`, but `reasoning_items` is not in that tuple:

```python
unsupported_delta_fields: Final = (
    "function_call",
    "tool_calls",
    "audio",
    "images",
    "annotations",
    "reasoning_content",
    "thinking_blocks",
    "provider_specific_fields",
    "refusal",
)
```

The Responses-to-chat bridge emits its `response.completed` chunk as `Delta(content="", reasoning_items=[...])`. `content` is an empty string and none of the guarded fields is set, so the chunk is classified as simple text, takes the fast path, and the items are dropped on the floor.

### Minimal reproduction

```python
from litellm.proxy.proxy_server import _serialize_streaming_chunk
from litellm.types.utils import Delta, ModelResponseStream, StreamingChoices

chunk = ModelResponseStream(
    id="chatcmpl-x", created=0, model="gpt-5.1", object="chat.completion.chunk",
    choices=[StreamingChoices(index=0, delta=Delta(content="", reasoning_items=[
        {"id": "rs_abc", "type": "reasoning", "encrypted_content": "ENCRYPTED-BLOB"}]))],
)
print(_serialize_streaming_chunk(chunk))
```

Current output — the items are gone:

```json
{"id":"chatcmpl-x","object":"chat.completion.chunk","created":0,"model":"gpt-5.1","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":""}}]}
```

### Visible end to end as well

Against a running proxy with `stream=true` on a model routed through the Responses bridge, the chunk that should carry the reasoning item arrives as `{"delta":{"content":""}}` and the terminal chunk as `{"delta":{},"finish_reason":"stop"}`. The identical **non-streaming** request to the same model returns `reasoning_items` with a ~5 KB `encrypted_content`, and replaying those items back into a follow-up request is accepted (corrupting the blob by four characters makes the upstream reject it with a 400). So the state exists and round-trips fine — only the streaming proxy path drops it.

### Not a duplicate of #37655

#37655 fixes `stream_chunk_builder`, i.e. the *reassembled* response used for caching and for the bridge's own input rebuild. This issue is about the bytes the proxy writes to the client. Both drop `reasoning_items`, at different points, and fixing either one does not fix the other.

### Fix

One line: add `reasoning_items` to `unsupported_delta_fields` so the chunk falls through to the canonical `model_dump_json` path. PR incoming.
author: CNSeniorious000

title: [Bug]: PostHog batch callback silently loses events during flush and on send failure
body:
## What happened?

The PostHog batch callback can silently lose events in two independent ways on LiteLLM `v1.96.2` (`83d6d84bfb7abbbff70d456bc89028d426db8c33`):

1. `CustomBatchLogger.flush_queue()` records the queue length, awaits `async_send_batch()`, and then clears the whole live queue when `preserve_events_added_during_flush` is false. `PostHogLogger.async_send_batch()` snapshots/group events before its network await, so an event appended during that await is not sent and is then cleared.
2. `PostHogLogger.async_send_batch()` catches HTTP/client exceptions and does not re-raise them. The base logger therefore treats a failed send as success and clears the queued events instead of retrying them.

Relevant source:

- [`CustomBatchLogger.flush_queue()`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/83d6d84bfb7abbbff70d456bc89028d426db8c33/litellm/integrations/custom_batch_logger.py#L53-L88)
- [`PostHogLogger.async_send_batch()`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/83d6d84bfb7abbbff70d456bc89028d426db8c33/litellm/integrations/posthog.py#L320-L370)

A live self-hosted deployment showed a compatible symptom (two successful proxy requests but only one exact PostHog callback record after bounded waits), but that observation does **not** prove which of these paths occurred. The code-level reproductions below are deterministic.

## User flow

Before a fix: an operator enables the built-in PostHog callback and some successful LLM requests never appear in PostHog.

1. The operator configures `success_callback: ["posthog"]` on a LiteLLM `v1.96.2` proxy.
2. Applications send successful requests through the normal OpenAI-compatible proxy endpoint.
3. During a PostHog batch send, another completed request is queued, or the PostHog `/batch/` request fails transiently.
4. The proxy request itself returns normally, but one or more `$ai_generation` events never appear in PostHog and are no longer present for retry.

After a fix: the same request sequence preserves every unacknowledged callback event.

1. The operator uses the same PostHog callback configuration.
2. Applications send the same requests.
3. Events appended while a batch is in flight remain queued, and a failed `/batch/` send remains queued for retry.
4. Successfully acknowledged events are removed exactly once; unacknowledged events are retried with bounded memory/backoff behavior.

## Deterministic proof

The concurrent-append loss is reproducible without a provider call because it is entirely inside the batch queue:

```python
import asyncio
from litellm.integrations.custom_batch_logger import CustomBatchLogger

class BlockingLogger(CustomBatchLogger):
    def __init__(self):
        self.send_started = asyncio.Event()
        self.release_send = asyncio.Event()
        self.sent = []
        super().__init__(flush_lock=asyncio.Lock())

    async def async_send_batch(self):
        snapshot = list(self.log_queue)
        self.send_started.set()
        await self.release_send.wait()
        self.sent.extend(snapshot)

async def main():
    logger = BlockingLogger()
    logger.log_queue.append("event-before-flush")
    flushing = asyncio.create_task(logger.flush_queue())
    await logger.send_started.wait()
    logger.log_queue.append("event-during-flush")
    logger.release_send.set()
    await flushing

    print("sent=", logger.sent)
    print("queue=", logger.log_queue)

asyncio.run(main())
```

Observed on `v1.96.2`:

```text
sent= ['event-before-flush']
queue= []
```

The second event was neither sent nor retained. Separately, raising from the PostHog HTTP client reaches the `except` block at lines 369–370, is logged but not re-raised, and the base `flush_queue()` then executes the success clear.

## Expected behavior

- Remove only the exact snapshot that was successfully acknowledged.
- Keep events appended during an in-flight send.
- Propagate or otherwise signal send failure so the base queue does not acknowledge it.
- Apply bounded queue size, retry/backoff, and stable event IDs for downstream deduplication.

## Environment

- Component: Proxy / PostHog observability callback
- LiteLLM version: `v1.96.2`
- Commit: `83d6d84bfb7abbbff70d456bc89028d426db8c33`

Related but not duplicate: #28907 reports a similar retry/queue-loss symptom for S3; this report provides a deterministic PostHog/base-logger reproduction and isolates the two acknowledgement failures above.
author: sashalab

title: Auto Router v2: GUI edits to tier model settings not persisted — litellm_params keep stale values, router keeps routing on old model
body:
### Summary

When editing an Auto Router v2 in the LiteLLM Admin UI, the tier settings are not visible in the form ("the settings are gone"), and the persisted `litellm_params` are **not updated** when changes are made in the GUI. The router keeps routing on the **old model values** that remain inside the `litellm_params` JSON, so edits made in the UI have no effect.

In our case, we changed the model of a tier from `gemma4:12b-it-qat` to `gemma4-12b-it-optiq-4bit` in the GUI. The GUI showed the settings as gone/empty, and after saving, the router still routed requests to the old model — visible in the response header `x-litellm-model-name: ollama_chat/gemma4:12b-it-qat`. The change only took effect after manually editing the model inside the `litellm_params` JSON field of the deployment.

### Repro steps

1. Create an Auto Router v2 (e.g. `privacy-router`) with tier models pointing to model A.
2. Open the router in the Admin UI → the tier settings are not shown / appear empty.
3. Edit the tier model to model B and save.
4. Send a chat completion request through the router.
5. Observe the response header `x-litellm-model-name` — it still shows model A.
6. Inspect the deployment via `/model/info` — the `litellm_params` still contain model A.

### Expected behavior

- Editing tier model settings in the GUI updates the persisted `litellm_params`.
- `x-litellm-model-name` reflects the new model after saving.

### Actual behavior

- GUI edits are not written through to `litellm_params`; the old values remain.
- The router continues routing on the stale model (old model A), causing wrong routing behavior.

### Environment

- LiteLLM Docker image: `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:main-latest` (rolling tag, self-hosted)
- Backend: Postgres 16
- Admin UI used at `http://<host>:<port>/ui`
- Deployment was created/edited via the "Auto Router" tab in the model hub

### Frequency / Impact

- Reproducible: yes (observed repeatedly while switching tier models)
- Impact: administrators believe they changed the routing model, but the router silently keeps the old one — leads to wrong model usage and hard-to-trace timeouts/errors

### Related recent PRs

- #38453 — "fix(ui): carry a preset's per-tier litellm_params through the prefill" (closed 2026-08-27)
- #38570 — "fix(router): reject complexity-router settings written outside complexity_router_config" (closed 2026-08-28)

### What I already tried

- Saved the same edit several times in the GUI — no effect on routing.
- Only editing the model directly inside the `litellm_params` JSON field made the router use the new model.

*Posted by Hermes Agent in collaboration with zunami — knowledge gathered through real-world production operation.*

```
pip install litellm==1.98.0
python3.10 -c "import litellm"
```

```
File ".../litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/context_management/editors/compact.py", line 17, in <module>
    from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, Final, Literal, NotRequired, Optional, TypedDict, Union, cast
ImportError: cannot import name 'NotRequired' from 'typing'
```

Introduced in 1.98.0 (1.97.0 imports fine) and still present in 1.99.0rc2. Line 19 of that same file already imports `ReadOnly` from `typing_extensions`.

title: [Bug]: `VectorStoreIndexRegistry` and `VectorStoreRegistry` use mutable default list arguments (`[]`)
body:
### What is the issue?

In `litellm/vector_stores/vector_store_registry.py`, both `VectorStoreIndexRegistry.__init__` (line 35) and `VectorStoreRegistry.__init__` (line 104) use a mutable default argument `[]`:

```python
class VectorStoreIndexRegistry:
    def __init__(self, vector_store_indexes: list[LiteLLM_ManagedVectorStoreIndex] = []):
        self.vector_store_indexes: list[LiteLLM_ManagedVectorStoreIndex] = vector_store_indexes
```

```python
class VectorStoreRegistry:
    def __init__(self, vector_stores: list[LiteLLM_ManagedVectorStore] = []):
        self.vector_stores: list[LiteLLM_ManagedVectorStore] = vector_stores
```

Because default argument values are evaluated once when the function/class is defined in Python, any instances created with default arguments (`VectorStoreIndexRegistry()` or `VectorStoreRegistry()`) share the same underlying list object. When `upsert_vector_store_index()` or list mutations occur on one instance, it silently pollutes and mutates all other registry instances.

### Reproduction

```python
from litellm.vector_stores.vector_store_registry import VectorStoreIndexRegistry, LiteLLM_ManagedVectorStoreIndex

# Create two independent instances using default arguments
reg1 = VectorStoreIndexRegistry()
reg2 = VectorStoreIndexRegistry()

print(reg1.vector_store_indexes is reg2.vector_store_indexes) # True (shared object)

# Mutating reg1 modifies reg2:
reg1.vector_store_indexes.append(LiteLLM_ManagedVectorStoreIndex(index_name="test_index", ...))
print(len(reg2.get_vector_store_indexes())) # Unexpectedly returns 1 instead of 0
```

### Proposed Solution

Default to `None` and instantiate a new list per instance:

```python
class VectorStoreIndexRegistry:
    def __init__(
        self,
        vector_store_indexes: Optional[list[LiteLLM_ManagedVectorStoreIndex]] = None,
    ):
        self.vector_store_indexes: list[LiteLLM_ManagedVectorStoreIndex] = (
            vector_store_indexes if vector_store_indexes is not None else []
        )


class VectorStoreRegistry:
    def __init__(
        self,
        vector_stores: Optional[list[LiteLLM_ManagedVectorStore]] = None,
    ):
        self.vector_stores: list[LiteLLM_ManagedVectorStore] = (
            vector_stores if vector_stores is not None else []
        )
```

Happy to submit a PR with unit tests if this looks good!
author: Gracy769

title: Complexity/auto-router: fallbacks look up the router name, not the selected tier
body:
### What happened?

When a client calls a complexity/auto-router group (e.g. `smart-router` with `model: auto_router/complexity_router`), the pre-routing hook correctly selects a tier model (e.g. `tier1`). If that deployment then fails (402, 503, …), fallback lookup uses `kwargs["model"]`, which is still the original router name.

Result:

```
No fallback model group found for original model_group=smart-router.
Fallbacks=[{'tier1': ['backup-a', 'backup-b']}, {'tier2': [...]}]
```

The configured chain for the *selected* tier never runs, so a provider-level failure on the first hop of `tier1` is returned to the client instead of trying `backup-a` / `backup-b`.

This is the inverse of https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/27473 (alias pointing *at* the router; lookup stays on the alias). Here the client calls the **router itself**; lookup stays on the **router name** after the hook has already chosen a tier.

### Expected

Fallbacks should be resolved against the model the complexity router actually routed to (`tier1`), so `{'tier1': ['backup-a', 'backup-b']}` applies.

### Where

- `Router.async_get_available_deployment`: assigns `model = pre_routing_hook_response.model` locally only
- `Router.async_function_with_fallbacks_common_utils`: `original_model_group = kwargs.get("model")` — still the router name
- Seen on LiteLLM 1.96.2; likely all four strategy routers that share this hook (`complexity_router`, semantic `auto_router`, `adaptive_router`, `quality_router`)

### Workaround

Rewrite the request `model` to the selected alias in a proxy `async_pre_call_hook` before the router captures `original_model_group`.

### Suggested fix

After the pre-routing hook, also update the fallback lookup key (`kwargs["model"]`, or a dedicated field that `async_function_with_fallbacks_common_utils` reads) to `pre_routing_hook_response.model`, so `router_settings.fallbacks` is indexed by the selected tier rather than the router group.
author: oelmaier

title: is_web_search_tool(_chat_completion) misses {type:function, function:{name: web_search}} web-search shape
body:
## Enhancement / gap

`is_web_search_tool` (litellm/integrations/websearch_interception/tools.py:219) and the stricter `is_web_search_tool_chat_completion` (tools.py:154) match the OpenAI function-tool envelope `{"type": "function", "function": {"name": ...}}` **only** when the inner name is `litellm_web_search`.

Clients that send Anthropic-style web search over Chat Completions commonly use the same envelope with the plain name `web_search`:

```json
{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "web_search", "parameters": {...}}}
```

That shape is NOT detected, so on the chat-completions path the unrecognized tool falls through to the provider's tool mapper, which rejects the nameless `web_search` type with `Missing required parameter: name` (a 500) instead of the interception converting and running it.

## Suggested change

In both detectors' function-envelope branch, accept the conventional name too:

```python
if tool_type == "function" and "function" in tool:
    function_name = tool["function"].get("name", "")
    if function_name in (LITELLM_WEB_SEARCH_TOOL_NAME, "web_search"):
        return True
```

## Version

litellm 1.99.0 (rc.1 image).
author: mayank-affirm

title: websearch_interception chat-completions agentic follow-up misroutes model: 'LLM Provider NOT provided ... model=mantle/...'
body:
## Bug

After the `aws_region_name` kwarg collision (see #38828) is worked around, the chat-completions Web Search agentic follow-up fails again with:

```
litellm.BadRequestError: LLM Provider NOT provided. Pass in the LLM provider you are
trying to call. You passed model=mantle/anthropic.claude-sonnet
```

## Root cause

In `BaseLLMHTTPHandler._execute_chat_completion_agentic_plan` (litellm/llms/custom_httpx/llm_http_handler.py:5470):

```python
full_model_name = patch.model or model
if "/" not in full_model_name:
    full_model_name = f"{custom_llm_provider}/{full_model_name}"
```

For a catalog model deployed as `bedrock/mantle/anthropic.claude-sonnet-5` (Bedrock Mantle OpenAI-compatible path), `patch.model` already carries the provider prefix shape, and `custom_llm_provider` resolves to `mantle`. The result `mantle/anthropic.claude-sonnet-5` is not a routable LiteLLM provider/model string, so the follow-up `acompletion` raises `BadRequestError: LLM Provider NOT provided`.

The follow-up should preserve the original fully-qualified deployment string (`bedrock/mantle/anthropic.claude-sonnet-5`) rather than re-prefixing a model that already embeds its provider path.

## Repro

1. Deploy a model via `bedrock/mantle/<model>` (Bedrock Mantle OpenAI-compatible endpoint) with `websearch_interception` enabled.
2. POST `/v1/chat/completions` with `stream: true` and an interceptable web-search tool.
3. With the `aws_region_name` collision (#38828) patched/avoided, the follow-up raises the provider-resolution BadRequestError.

## Version

litellm 1.99.0 (rc.1 image, gateway enterprise split).
author: mayank-affirm

title: websearch_interception chat-completions agentic follow-up crashes: acompletion() got multiple values for keyword argument 'aws_region_name'
body:
## Bug

When `websearch_interception` intercepts a **Chat Completions** request that triggers the agentic Web Search loop, the follow-up model call crashes with:

```
LiteLLM.AgenticHookError: Exception in chat completion agentic hooks:
litellm.main.acompletion() got multiple values for keyword argument 'aws_region_name'
```

after which the handler returns a non-stream `ModelResponse` and the proxy's SSE generator crashes with:

```
TypeError: 'async for' requires an object with __aiter__ method, got ModelResponse
```

## Root cause

`BaseLLMHTTPHandler._execute_chat_completion_agentic_plan` (litellm/llms/custom_httpx/llm_http_handler.py:5498) issues the follow-up as:

```python
return await litellm.acompletion(
    model=full_model_name,
    messages=patch.messages,
    **optional_params_for_followup,
    **kwargs_for_followup,
)
```

`optional_params_for_followup` is built from the method's `optional_params` arg (+ `patch.optional_params`), and `kwargs_for_followup` from the method's `kwargs` arg (+ `patch.kwargs`). On a Bedrock route, BOTH source dicts carry `aws_region_name` (and the other AWS connection params), so the double-splat passes the same keyword twice and Python raises before the callee runs.

The interception callback (`WebSearchInterceptionLogger._build_chat_completion_request_patch`) rebuilds `patch.kwargs`/`patch.optional_params` from the original request and copies the provider connection keys into both, so the merge cannot dedup them.

## Repro

1. Configure a Bedrock chat model (e.g. `bedrock/mantle/anthropic.claude-sonnet-5`) with `websearch_interception` enabled and an AgentCore/search backend.
2. POST `/v1/chat/completions` with `stream: true` and a web-search tool that the interception converts (e.g. `{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "web_search", ...}}` after detection broadening — see linked issue for that gap).
3. The agentic follow-up raises the kwarg-collision TypeError.

## Suggested fix

Before the `litellm.acompletion(...)` call in `_execute_chat_completion_agentic_plan`, drop any key present in both `optional_params_for_followup` and `kwargs_for_followup` from one of them (keep the `optional_params` value), or otherwise merge the two dicts with explicit precedence instead of a bare double-splat.

## Version

litellm 1.99.0 (rc.1 image, gateway enterprise split).
author: mayank-affirm

title: [Feature]: vertex_ai Gemini embeddings silently fuse list inputs into one vector — add per-input fan-out option or warning
body:
### What happened?

Calling `/v1/embeddings` on a **`vertex_ai/` route** with a **list input** returns **only one embedding**, while `usage.prompt_tokens` (and the billed cost) covers **all** inputs. The request returns HTTP 200, so callers silently lose N-1 vectors and are charged for all N inputs.

The same request through the **`gemini/` (AI Studio) route** for the same underlying model fans out correctly (N inputs → N vectors).

### Reproduction

Proxy config (LiteLLM proxy `v1.92.0-stable`):

```yaml
  - model_name: emb-vertex
    litellm_params:
      model: vertex_ai/gemini-embedding-2
      vertex_project: <project>
      vertex_location: global
      vertex_credentials: os.environ/VERTEX_CREDENTIALS
  - model_name: emb-aistudio
    litellm_params:
      model: gemini/gemini-embedding-2
      api_key: os.environ/GEMINI_API_KEY
```

Request (identical for both):

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:4000/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "<model>", "input": ["alpha", "beta", "gamma"]}'
```

### Observed

| Route | vectors returned | usage.prompt_tokens | x-litellm-response-cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| `vertex_ai/gemini-embedding-2` | **1** (dim 3072) | 4 (all inputs) | 8e-07 |
| `gemini/gemini-embedding-2` | **3** (dim 3072) | 3 | 6e-07 |

The vertex route's `prompt_tokens_details` shows `text_tokens: 4`, i.e. tokens for all three inputs were sent and billed, but `data` contains a single embedding (which also means the one returned vector may be computed over concatenated/merged content rather than the first input alone).

### Expected

`vertex_ai/` embeddings with `input: [a, b, c]` should return one embedding per input, matching the OpenAI contract and the `gemini/` route's behavior.

### Impact

- Silent data loss: batch text embedding callers get 1 vector for N inputs with a 200 status.
- Overbilling relative to output: tokens/cost are logged for all N inputs.

### Notes

- Verified on proxy `v1.92.0-stable`.
- Diffing `litellm/llms/vertex_ai/vertex_embeddings/transformation.py` and `litellm/llms/vertex_ai/gemini_embeddings/batch_embed_content_transformation.py` between `v1.92.0` and `v1.98.0` shows only typing/cosmetic changes, so this looks unfixed as of v1.98.0 (not re-tested empirically on v1.98.0).
- Possibly related but distinct: #35092 (Batch API jsonl row shape), #35636 (multimodal response keeps only first embedding), #35626 (router token-count exception on list input).

### LiteLLM version

v1.92.0-stable
author: snigdhokdas

title: [Bug]: Cost Optimization total adds non-additive savings metrics
body:
## Check for existing issues

- [x] I searched the existing issues and checked that this is not a duplicate.

## What happened?

Severity: Medium

The Cost Optimization page calculates `Total saved` by adding compression, prompt-caching, and auto-router savings. Auto-router savings compares a cache-aware selected cost with a cache-aware baseline and includes cache-switch cost. Prompt-caching savings is a separate counterfactual against disabling caching on the selected model.

Those values are not additive. Their sum has no defined counterfactual and can count the same caching effect twice.

Expected: avoid the sum or use a sequential decomposition in which each request cost is attributed once.

## User Flow

Before a (hypothetical) fix: an operator sees `Total saved` exceed the saving against the auto-router baseline.

1. A developer sends `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` through an auto-router on traffic that also uses prompt caching and receives `200 OK`.
2. The operator opens `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=cost-optimization` and sees separate prompt-caching and auto-router savings cards.
3. The page adds both cards into `Total saved`, although each uses a different counterfactual.

After a (hypothetical) fix: the page does not present a non-additive sum as one dollar saving.

1. A developer sends `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` through the same auto-router on traffic that also uses prompt caching and receives `200 OK`.
2. The operator opens `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=cost-optimization` and sees separate prompt-caching and auto-router savings cards.
3. The page labels them as alternative views or shows a sequentially attributed total backed by one documented baseline.

## Proof the bug occurs

Setup: Cost Optimization page with one daily metrics row. No provider request or credentials are required.

Version or commit: `d517397005cbb87fd39a82a9d643a00fc015b66d`

```text
actual selected-model cost with caching: $6
selected-model cost without caching:     $10
cache-aware auto-router baseline cost:   $12
prompt-caching savings:                  $4  ($10 - $6)
auto-router savings:                     $6  ($12 - $6)
UI Total saved:                          $10 ($4 + $6)
```

The `$10` total implies a nonexistent `$16` counterfactual, while the displayed auto-router baseline is `$12`.

`useSavingsTotals` in `ui/litellm-dashboard/src/components/shared/SavingsTiles.tsx` sets `total` to `compression + caching + autorouter`.

## Suggested fix

Remove the combined headline unless all drivers use sequential attribution. If a total is required, define one counterfactual and give compression, caching, and routing non-overlapping marginal contributions.

Regression tests should verify totals for traffic using multiple drivers and document the accounting identity.

## What part of LiteLLM is this about?

UI Dashboard

## What LiteLLM version are you on?

Commit `d517397005cbb87fd39a82a9d643a00fc015b66d`
author: mubashir1osmani

title: [Bug]: Auto-router savings and benchmarks omit classifier cost
body:
## Check for existing issues

- [x] I searched the existing issues and checked that this is not a duplicate.

## What happened?

Severity: Medium

LLM-based complexity routing records `classifier_cost`, but that cost is not subtracted from auto-router savings. The classifier is logged as an internal sub-call and intentionally excluded from the auto-router session rollup, so benchmark actual spend omits it too.

This overstates net savings and understates routed spend.

Expected: savings are net of classifier cost, and benchmark routed spend includes that cost once.

## User Flow

Before a (hypothetical) fix: an operator using an LLM classifier sees gross model savings presented as net savings.

1. The operator configures a complexity router with an LLM classifier.
2. A developer sends `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` with the router model and receives `200 OK` after a paid classifier call selects a tier.
3. The operator requests `GET https://litellm-domain/auto_router/benchmarks` and sees routed spend without the classifier charge and saved spend without that charge deducted.

After a (hypothetical) fix: the same benchmark reports complete workflow cost and net saving.

1. The operator configures the same complexity router with an LLM classifier.
2. A developer sends `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` with the router model and receives `200 OK` after a paid classifier call selects a tier.
3. The operator requests `GET https://litellm-domain/auto_router/benchmarks` and sees routed spend including the classifier charge once and saved spend reduced by the same amount.

## Proof the bug occurs

Setup: local checkout with an LLM-classifier routing decision containing numeric `classifier_cost`. No provider request is required to reproduce the rollup arithmetic.

Version or commit: `d517397005cbb87fd39a82a9d643a00fc015b66d`

```text
single-model baseline cost: $0.030
selected model cost:        $0.010
classifier cost:            $0.005

observed spend:          $0.010
observed saved_spend:    $0.020
observed baseline_spend: $0.030

expected spend:          $0.015
expected saved_spend:    $0.015
expected baseline_spend: $0.030
```

The decision records `classifier_cost` in `complexity_router.py`, while `build_autorouter_turn_transaction` records only the served request spend in `litellm/proxy/db/autorouter_session_rollup.py`.

## Suggested fix

Subtract numeric classifier cost from per-request auto-router savings. Add it to the main request's session spend while continuing to exclude the internal classifier row, so it is counted once and `baseline_spend = spend + saved_spend` remains true.

Regression tests should cover priced, zero-cost, unpriced, malformed, and heuristic-only classifiers, plus multi-turn rollups.

## What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

## What LiteLLM version are you on?

Commit `d517397005cbb87fd39a82a9d643a00fc015b66d`
author: mubashir1osmani

title: [Bug]: Explicit free cache reads are charged at the full input rate
body:
## Check for existing issues

- [x] I searched the existing issues and checked that this is not a duplicate. Issues #37117 and #37284 do not cover explicit zero cache-read rates in baseline pricing.

## What happened?

Severity: Medium

An explicit `cache_read_input_token_cost: 0.0` is treated as missing because the baseline cache-rate check uses `bool(rate)`. The calculation moves cache-read tokens into ordinary text input and charges the full input rate.

This overstates savings for cache-capable providers or deployments where reads are free.

Expected: numeric zero is a valid price. Only an absent rate should trigger ordinary input fallback.

## User Flow

Before a (hypothetical) fix: an operator with free cache reads sees savings overstated by the baseline's full input charge.

1. The operator configures a cache-capable baseline deployment with `cache_read_input_token_cost: 0.0`.
2. A developer sends `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` for a continuing cached conversation and receives `200 OK`.
3. The operator opens `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=cost-optimization` and sees the cached prompt charged at the baseline's ordinary input rate.

After a (hypothetical) fix: the same cached prompt is priced at the configured free read rate.

1. The operator configures the same cache-capable baseline deployment with `cache_read_input_token_cost: 0.0`.
2. A developer sends `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` for a continuing cached conversation and receives `200 OK`.
3. The operator opens `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=cost-optimization` and sees the cached prompt priced at `$0.00` on the baseline arm.

## Proof the bug occurs

Setup: local checkout with a custom baseline pricing record and recorded cached usage. No provider request or credentials are required.

Version or commit: `d517397005cbb87fd39a82a9d643a00fc015b66d`

```text
baseline input rate:      $0.001/token
baseline cache-read rate: $0.000/token
cached prompt:             20,000 tokens

expected savings: $1.973
reported savings: $21.973
overstatement:     $20.000
```

`_baseline_cache_rate_keys` in `litellm/proxy/spend_tracking/savings.py` converts the configured rate to `bool`, so both `None` and `0.0` take the missing-rate path.

## Suggested fix

Distinguish absence from explicit zero with an `is not None` check. Use `supports_prompt_caching` where needed to distinguish unsupported caching from supported caching with no separate charge.

Regression tests should cover absent, positive, and explicit zero read and write rates.

## What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

title: [Bug]: Adaptive and quality routers omit metadata required for savings
body:
## Check for existing issues

- [x] I searched the existing issues and checked that this is not a duplicate.

## What happened?

Severity: High

Standalone adaptive and quality routers do not record a savings baseline or whether a request is the first turn of a conversation. Complexity routing records both.

Without a global `autorouter_savings_baseline_model`, savings remain off and are stored as zero. With a global override, the missing conversation field defaults to continuing, so a first turn can receive a false cache-switch penalty.

Expected: every routing strategy records the baseline and conversation shape required by the shared savings calculation.

## User Flow

Before a (hypothetical) fix: an operator uses a standalone adaptive or quality router, but its savings are absent or penalized as a cache switch.

1. The operator configures a standalone adaptive or quality router without a global savings baseline override.
2. A developer sends the first `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` for a new conversation and receives `200 OK`.
3. The operator opens `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=cost-optimization` and sees `$0.00`; if a global override is added, the first turn is priced as though the conversation were already warm.

After a (hypothetical) fix: the same router reports a derived baseline and identifies the first turn.

1. The operator configures the same standalone adaptive or quality router without a global savings baseline override.
2. A developer sends the first `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` for a new conversation and receives `200 OK`.
3. The operator opens `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=cost-optimization` and sees savings against the derived baseline with no false cache-switch penalty.

## Proof the bug occurs

Setup: local checkout with standalone adaptive and quality routing decisions. No provider request or credentials are required to reproduce the metadata handoff.

Version or commit: `d517397005cbb87fd39a82a9d643a00fc015b66d`

```text
adaptive fields: router_model_name, router_type, routed_model, cause, request_type
quality fields:  router_model_name, router_type, routed_model, cause, tier, score, signals
missing from both: savings_baseline_model, savings_baseline_deployment_id, conversation_continuing

adaptive savings without global override: None -> stored as $0.00
quality savings without global override:  None -> stored as $0.00
```

The decisions in `adaptive_router.py` and `quality_router.py` omit fields consumed by `autorouter_savings_for_request`.

## Suggested fix

Share baseline derivation and conversation-shape instrumentation across complexity, adaptive, and quality routers. Record the baseline model, baseline deployment ID when available, and an explicit `conversation_continuing` boolean.

Regression tests should exercise first and continuing turns for all strategies, with a derived baseline and with the global override.

title: [Bug]: Derived auto-router baseline underprices models with missing cache rates
body:
## Check for existing issues

- [x] I searched the existing issues and checked that this is not a duplicate. Issues #37117 and #37284 do not cover derived baseline selection.

## What happened?

Severity: High

The default auto-router baseline ranks hardest-tier deployments with a cache-heavy reference request. When a candidate has no cache-read or cache-write rate, those reference buckets are priced as free. Request-time savings uses different semantics and charges an unsupported cache bucket as ordinary input.

An expensive deployment can therefore rank as nearly free, causing every later request to use the wrong baseline.

Expected: reference ranking and request-time savings use the same missing-cache-rate semantics.

## User Flow

Before a (hypothetical) fix: an operator leaves the savings baseline unset, and the dashboard derives the wrong deployment from the hardest tier.

1. The operator configures an auto-router hardest tier containing one deployment with ordinary input pricing but no cache rates and another with explicit cache rates.
2. A developer sends `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` with the auto-router model and receives `200 OK`.
3. The operator opens `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=cost-optimization` and sees savings measured against the lower-cost deployment rather than the most expensive deployment the router could select.

After a (hypothetical) fix: the same pool derives its baseline with consistent cache semantics.

1. The operator configures the same auto-router hardest tier containing one deployment with ordinary input pricing but no cache rates and another with explicit cache rates.
2. A developer sends `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` with the auto-router model and receives `200 OK`.
3. The operator opens `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=cost-optimization` and sees savings measured against the deployment with the highest normalized reference cost.

## Proof the bug occurs

Setup: local checkout. Two deployment pricing records were ranked with the built-in 20,000-input and 1,000-output reference usage. No provider request or credentials are required.

Version or commit: `d517397005cbb87fd39a82a9d643a00fc015b66d`

```text
candidate A: input $0.001/token, output $0.000001/token, cache rates absent
candidate B: input/cache/output $0.00001/token
reference: 19,000 cache reads, 1,000 cache writes, 1,000 output

candidate A effective reference cost: $20.001
candidate B reference cost:           $0.210
derived baseline: candidate B
```

Candidate A is ranked with its missing cache buckets priced as free, although request-time calculation charges them at its ordinary input rate.

The mismatch is between `_REFERENCE_REQUEST` and `_priced` in `litellm/router_strategy/savings_baseline.py` and request-time normalization.

## Suggested fix

Normalize reference usage for each candidate before pricing it. Missing cache-read or cache-write rates should move those tokens into ordinary text input, using one shared helper with request-time savings.

Regression tests should rank candidates with missing read rates, missing write rates, explicit zero rates, and complete cache rates.

title: [Bug]: Auto-router savings conflates model identity with deployment identity
body:
## Check for existing issues

- [x] I searched the existing issues and checked that this is not a duplicate. Issues #37117 and #37284 concern other pricing paths.

## What happened?

Severity: High

Auto-router savings compares only provider and canonical model names when deciding whether the baseline and selected targets are the same. Two differently priced deployments of one model therefore report `$0.00`. Conversely, one Azure deployment represented by an alias on one side and its base model on the other can report a false loss.

The request path resolves both deployment IDs and pricing records, but the IDs are not passed into the final identity comparison.

Expected: use deployment IDs for identity when available, with canonical model identity only as a fallback.

## User Flow

Before a (hypothetical) fix: an operator routes between two differently priced deployments of the same model, but the dashboard reports no saving.

1. The operator configures an auto-router whose baseline and selected targets use the same provider model but have different deployment IDs and negotiated rates.
2. A developer sends `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` with the auto-router model and receives `200 OK` from the cheaper deployment.
3. The operator opens `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=cost-optimization` and sees `$0.00` auto-router savings although the cheaper deployment cost less.

After a (hypothetical) fix: the same request is compared by deployment identity and reports the negotiated-rate saving.

1. The operator configures the same auto-router whose baseline and selected targets use the same provider model but have different deployment IDs and negotiated rates.
2. A developer sends `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` with the auto-router model and receives `200 OK` from the cheaper deployment.
3. The operator opens `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=cost-optimization` and sees baseline deployment cost minus selected deployment cost.

## Proof the bug occurs

Setup: local checkout with deterministic usage and deployment pricing records. No provider request or credentials are required.

Version or commit: `d517397005cbb87fd39a82a9d643a00fc015b66d`

```text
usage: 20,000 input tokens, 1,000 output tokens
baseline: deployment A, anthropic/claude-opus-5, negotiated high rates
selected: deployment B, anthropic/claude-opus-5, negotiated low rates
expected savings: $26.973
reported savings: $0.000
```

A second reproduction using one Azure deployment as an alias on the selected side and its base model on the baseline side returned `-$0.023` instead of `$0.000`.

The equality check in `litellm/proxy/spend_tracking/savings.py` receives model identities but no deployment IDs, even though its caller has both IDs.

## Suggested fix

Pass baseline and selected deployment IDs into the savings calculation. If both exist, compare IDs. Otherwise fall back to canonical provider/model equality. Keep deployment-specific model information for pricing.

Regression tests should cover different IDs for the same canonical model, the same ID represented by alias and base model, and the no-ID fallback.

title: [Bug]: DeepInfra usage.estimated_cost and service_tier are ignored — priority-tier traffic under-reported by 1.5x
body:
### What happened?

DeepInfra returns its own cost and the delivered service tier in the chat completion response body, but LiteLLM ignores both and prices the request from `model_prices_and_context_window.json` at base rates. For traffic served at DeepInfra's `priority` tier, this under-reports cost by exactly 1.5×.

This is inconsistent with LiteLLM's own handling of OpenRouter, where `usage.cost` is read from the response and used as the authoritative cost.

**DeepInfra response body** (via the proxy, `model_list` entry `deepinfra/Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B`):

```json
{
  "usage": {
    "completion_tokens": 5,
    "prompt_tokens": 11,
    "total_tokens": 16,
    "estimated_cost": 8.775e-06
  },
  "service_tier": "priority"
}
```

LiteLLM reported `x-litellm-response-cost: 5.85e-06` for that request — i.e. `11 × 1e-07 + 5 × 9.5e-07`, the base map rates, ignoring that priority was delivered.

### Reproduction

Two requests, identical prompt and `max_tokens`, differing only in requested tier. Both returned 11 prompt / 5 completion tokens, so they are directly comparable:

| Requested `service_tier` | `service_tier` in response | `x-litellm-response-cost` | DeepInfra `usage.estimated_cost` | Ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `priority` | `priority` | 5.85e-06 | **8.775e-06** | **1.500** |
| `default` | `default` | 5.85e-06 | 5.85e-06 | 1.000 |

LiteLLM charges the same in both cases. DeepInfra's own figure differs by the documented 1.5× priority multiplier.

Note the base rates in the cost map are correct — `deepinfra/Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B` at `1e-07` / `9.5e-07` matches DeepInfra's `estimated_cost` exactly at `default` tier. The gap is solely the tier surcharge.

### Two related gaps

**1. `usage.estimated_cost` is not consumed.**

`litellm/llms/openrouter/chat/transformation.py` extracts `usage.cost` into `_hidden_params["additional_headers"]["llm_provider-x-litellm-response-cost"]`, which `response_cost_calculator` then short-circuits on. `litellm/llms/deepinfra/chat/transformation.py` has no equivalent — `DeepInfraConfig` extends `OpenAIGPTConfig` without overriding `transform_response`, so the field is dropped. Confirmed by the absence of any `llm_provider-x-litellm-response-cost` header on DeepInfra responses.

**2. `service_tier` does not affect cost-key selection for DeepInfra.**

`_get_service_tier_cost_key` in `litellm/litellm_core_utils/llm_cost_calc/utils.py` resolves suffixed keys such as `input_cost_per_token_priority` generically, and the DeepInfra entries in the cost map carry no `_priority` keys — so even a correct plumbing path would currently fall back to base rates. The response body reports the **delivered** tier, which is the right signal to key off (the requested tier can differ, since DeepInfra falls back to real-time when priority cannot be served, and bills accordingly).

### Suggested fix

Consuming `usage.estimated_cost` the way OpenRouter's `usage.cost` is consumed seems strictly better than adding `_priority` variants to the cost map: it is the provider's own number, it tracks the delivered tier automatically, and it does not require maintaining a multiplier or per-tier rates as DeepInfra's pricing changes.

Happy to open a PR for the transformation change if that direction is agreeable.

### Impact

Any deployment setting `service_tier: priority` on DeepInfra routes under-reports spend by 1.5× systematically. Where LiteLLM's spend tracking drives budgets, this means budgets are effectively 1.5× larger than configured for that traffic.

### Relevant log output

```
# priority (config default)
x-litellm-response-cost = 5.85e-06
x-litellm-response-cost-original = 5.85e-06
x-litellm-response-cost-input = 1.1e-06
x-litellm-response-cost-output = 4.75e-06
llm_provider-x-request-id = RO0KBKY1JqZyJsrnWnk53TSf
# no llm_provider-x-litellm-response-cost header present
# response body usage.estimated_cost = 8.775e-06, service_tier = "priority"
```

Yes

v1.98.0 (`ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database:1.98.0`)

title: [Bug]: Bedrock Converse rejects tool `custom` field ("tools.0.custom.strict: Extra inputs are not permitted") for cross-region inference profile Claude models
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

Calling a Bedrock-hosted Claude model (a cross-region inference profile ID, e.g. bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5) through litellm.acompletion with a custom/freeform tool definition (the kind the OpenAI Agents SDK sends for tools like apply_patch) fails with:

`litellm.exceptions.BadRequestError: litellm.BadRequestError: BedrockException - {"message":"The model returned the following errors: tools.0.custom.strict: Extra inputs are not permitted"}`

The tool dict includes a top-level custom key (e.g. custom: `{"strict": None})`. Bedrock does not accept this key at all, so the request is rejected outright instead of being forwarded with that field stripped.

Expected behavior: the request should succeed the same way it does against Anthropic's own API directly — i.e. any provider-specific extra fields under custom should be dropped before the tool list is sent to Bedrock, regardless of which internal code path builds the request for a given model ID.

### User Flow

Before a (hypothetical) fix: a developer running an agent against Bedrock gets a hard crash instead of a response

1. The developer configures their agent (via the OpenAI Agents SDK's LiteLLM model wrapper) to use model `bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5`, with a custom freeform tool registered (e.g. an apply_patch tool)
2. They run the agent, which sends a chat request with "stream": true and a tool list where one tool entry carries a `"custom": {"strict": null}` field alongside its name/description
3. Instead of a streamed response, the call immediately fails with a 400-style error whose body reads `"tools.0.custom.strict: Extra inputs are not permitted"`
4. The developer's agent run crashes with this error surfaced in their terminal/logs, and no assistant output is ever produced for that turn

After a (hypothetical) fix: the same agent run streams back a normal response

1. Same setup: model `bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5`, same custom tool registered
2. The developer runs the agent, which sends the identical request (same tool list, same custom field present)
3. The request succeeds; SSE chunks stream back containing the assistant's text and/or tool-call output as normal
4. The agent run completes and the developer sees the expected assistant response / tool invocation in their app, with no error

(No security/authorization consequence — this is a request-validation bug, not an access-control one.)

### Proof the bug occurs

Config / SDK setup the request ran with:

python
### env vars (non-secret ones kept, credentials redacted)
### AWS_REGION_NAME=us-east-1
### AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=<redacted>
### AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=<redacted>

> import litellm
> 
> tools = [
>     {
>         "type": "custom",
>         "name": "apply_patch",
>         "description": "Apply a unified diff patch to the workspace.",
>         "custom": {"strict": None},
>     }
> ]
> 
> await litellm.acompletion(
>     model="bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5",
>     messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}],
>     tools=tools,
>     stream=True,
> )

Version / commit: **_`litellm==1.90.1 (per uv.lock)`_**, called via agents.extensions.models.litellm_model.LitellmModel → agents.models.LitellmModel.stream_response → litellm.acompletion(..., stream=True)

Output:
`
litellm.exceptions.BadRequestError: litellm.BadRequestError: BedrockException - {"message":"The model returned the following errors: tools.0.custom.strict: Extra inputs are not permitted"}
`
Only SDK-level acompletion usage was exercised here (equivalent to /v1/chat/completions) — this was not run through the proxy's /v1/responses or /v1/messages endpoints, so proof for those endpoints isn't included.

SDK (litellm Python package)

author: gourab9817

title: [Bug]: proxy `--debug` is click-bound to the generic `DEBUG` env var — any unrelated shell `DEBUG=...` silently enables debug logging
body:
**What happened**

The proxy CLI binds its `--debug` flag to the bare environment variable `DEBUG` (`proxy_cli.py:413`, `envvar="DEBUG"` — verified on 1.83.13). `DEBUG` is one of the most overloaded env names in existence (build systems, JS tooling, random shell profiles). We hit it with a leftover `DEBUG=release` from an unrelated toolchain: the proxy silently came up in debug logging mode.

**Why it matters**

- Debug logging at the proxy tier is high-volume and can put request/response payloads into logs — turning it on by accident is a privacy/perf hazard, not just noise.
- It's silent: nothing tells you WHY logging is verbose; we only found it by reading the click options.
- Click treats any non-empty value as truthy for a `is_flag` option, so even `DEBUG=0`-style values from other tools can trip it.

**Repro**

```bash
DEBUG=release litellm --config config.yaml --port 4000   # comes up in debug mode
unset DEBUG; litellm --config config.yaml --port 4000    # normal
```

**Suggested fix**

Namespace it: `LITELLM_DEBUG` (and `LITELLM_DETAILED_DEBUG` for the `--detailed_debug` option at line 421, same pattern), optionally keeping the bare names for one deprecation cycle with a startup warning when the value comes from the environment rather than the flag.

**Version**: litellm 1.83.13, Linux, proxy mode with a config file.

Our workaround: `unset DEBUG` in the launcher script before exec.
author: erdholion

title: [Bug]: Anthropic /v1/messages streaming leaks the backend model id in message_start (non-streaming returns the requested model)
body:
## What happened?

For a model routed through the Anthropic `/v1/messages` passthrough (a deployment opted into `model_info.supported_endpoints: ["/v1/messages"]`, backend speaking the Anthropic Messages shape), the response `model` field disagrees between streaming and non-streaming:

- **Non-streaming** — the proxy rewrites the response `model` to the requested model name (the client's alias / model_group).
- **Streaming** — the `message_start` event passes the **backend's model id** through unchanged, with no rewrite.

**Expected:** streaming should return the requested model name too, matching non-streaming. The two response shapes should agree on `model`.

## User Flow

1. Client (Claude Code) sends `POST /v1/messages` with `"model": "<alias>"`, `stream: true`.
2. The client reads the response `model` (`message_start.message.model`) and persists it as the conversation's model.
3. Because the streaming path returns the backend model id instead of the alias, the client persists the backend id.
4. On session resume the client does not recognize the backend id (it is neither the configured model name nor a known model) and warns `Session model <backend-id> could not be restored`, then falls back to the configured model.

## Proof the bug occurs

Same model, only `stream` differs.

Non-streaming returns the requested name:
```bash
curl -s "$PROXY/v1/messages" -H "x-api-key: $KEY" -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \
  -d '{"model":"my-alias","max_tokens":40,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
# -> {"model":"my-alias", ...}
```

Streaming passes the backend id through:
```bash
curl -sN "$PROXY/v1/messages" -H "x-api-key: $KEY" -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \
  -d '{"model":"my-alias","max_tokens":40,"stream":true,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
# -> event: message_start
# -> data: {"type":"message_start","message":{"model":"<backend-model-id>", ...}}
```

Location: `litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/messages/streaming_iterator.py` forwards chunks unchanged (`_convert_chunk_to_sse_format` does not rewrite `model`), while the non-streaming path (`transform_anthropic_messages_response`) sets the response model to the requested model. Checked `main` as well — the streaming iterator still does not rewrite `model`, so this is not yet fixed.

## What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

## What LiteLLM version are you on ?

v1.98.0
author: kalavt

title: [Feature]: Add merge-safe authority for user metadata with hidden SCIM roots
body:
## Environment

- LiteLLM: `v1.98.0`
- Source commit: `d8f71d7bdbd7c9873d98293f83d64c6db72847e6`
- Database-backed user management with SCIM-managed metadata
- Relevant endpoints: `/user/info`, `/v2/user/info`, `/user/list`, and `/user/update`

## Problem

A declarative client cannot safely manage ordinary user metadata without risking deletion of directory-owned metadata.

LiteLLM persists SCIM enterprise attributes, entitlements, and roles inside the user's `metadata` column. The generic user read endpoints intentionally remove these roots through `_redact_scim_enterprise_metadata`:

- `scim_enterprise`
- `scim_entitlements`
- `scim_roles`

However, an explicit `metadata` value sent to `/user/update` becomes a replacement value for the metadata column. `prepare_metadata_fields` preserves the existing metadata only when the caller omits `metadata`; when metadata is supplied, it preserves only explicitly reserved fields such as `service_account_id`, not the hidden SCIM roots or arbitrary vendor-owned siblings.

This creates a lost-update/data-loss hazard:

1. A user row contains SCIM-owned roots plus caller-owned custom metadata.
2. `/user/info`, `/v2/user/info`, and `/user/list` return only the filtered custom subset.
3. A client changes one custom metadata key and sends the complete value it was able to read.
4. The whole-column update can remove hidden SCIM or other unobservable sibling data.

There is no complete admin read for this column, metadata-specific PATCH/merge operation, revision/ETag, or conditional update that lets the client preserve values it is not allowed to observe.

## Requested contract

Please provide at least one safe management path:

### Preferred: server-side metadata patch/merge

- Update selected JSON keys without replacing unmentioned roots.
- Define recursive versus top-level merge behavior.
- Define explicit key deletion, `{}`, and `null` semantics.
- Preserve SCIM/directory-owned roots unless the caller uses an appropriately authorized SCIM-specific operation.
- Return the resulting observable metadata plus a revision or otherwise support authoritative confirmation.

### Alternative: complete privileged read plus compare-and-swap

- Expose the exact complete metadata column only to an explicit privileged role.
- Include a revision/ETag.
- Require that revision on whole-column replacement so concurrent or hidden changes fail rather than being lost.

A safe fix does not need to expose directory-only values to ordinary users; server-side merge that protects those roots is sufficient.

## Why this matters

The Terraform provider shipped lossless, ownership-aware JSON bridges for key, organization, project, team, and observable model dictionaries. `litellm_user.metadata_json` remains deliberately blocked because read-modify-write would silently discard API-only data. The provider retains the existing legacy behavior rather than claiming unsafe ownership.

Provider tracking issue: https://github.com/ncecere/terraform-provider-litellm/issues/218

## Suggested validation

Add DB-backed tests covering:

- SCIM-owned roots plus arbitrary custom metadata;
- changing, adding, and deleting one custom key;
- preservation of hidden siblings;
- explicit null/empty/full-clear behavior;
- concurrent update rejection or merge correctness;
- admin and non-admin read/update roles; and
- round-trip behavior through `/user/info`, `/v2/user/info`, and `/user/list`.
author: ncecere

title: [Bug]: /budget/update returns 500 for valid structured model_max_budget objects
body:
## Environment

- LiteLLM: `v1.98.0`
- Source commit: `d8f71d7bdbd7c9873d98293f83d64c6db72847e6`
- Database-backed proxy using PostgreSQL
- Endpoint: `POST /budget/update`

## Problem

`BudgetNewRequest.model_max_budget` is typed as `dict[str, BudgetConfig]` and the endpoint documentation shows structured entries such as:

```json
{
  "budget_id": "<existing budget UUID>",
  "model_max_budget": {
    "openai/gpt-4o-mini": {
      "max_budget": 100.0,
      "budget_duration": "1d",
      "tpm_limit": 100000,
      "rpm_limit": 100000
    }
  }
}
```

The request passes the `GenericBudgetConfigType` shape expected by `validate_model_max_budget`, but v1.98 returns HTTP 500 when this structured value is sent through `/budget/update` instead of persisting the update or returning a bounded validation error.

The update handler passes `budget_obj.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)` directly to `BudgetRepository(...).table.update`. This path appears not to normalize the nested `BudgetConfig` values into the JSON representation expected by the database update.

Scalar budget fields on the same endpoint do not establish whether a structured model-budget update committed, and retrying after a 500 is unsafe for declarative clients.

## Expected behavior

For an Enterprise-enabled deployment:

1. A valid `dict[str, BudgetConfig]` should be serialized and persisted by `/budget/update`.
2. `/budget/info` and parent management reads should return the same structured values authoritatively.
3. The API should define whether `{}` clears all model entries, `null` leaves the value unchanged or clears it, and how one model entry is removed.
4. Invalid nested objects should return a deterministic 4xx response rather than 500.

## Why this matters

The Terraform provider currently has incompatible legacy representations across key, project, budget, and tag resources. A compatibility-safe structured representation is designed, but update and clear support cannot be enabled while the authoritative budget endpoint returns 500 for valid objects. Doing so could publish false state or retry an uncertain mutation.

Provider tracking issue: https://github.com/ncecere/terraform-provider-litellm/issues/223

## Suggested validation

Add DB-backed tests for:

- one and multiple structured model entries;
- integer TPM/RPM limits and finite budgets;
- duration aliases accepted by `BudgetConfig`;
- read-after-update identity and value confirmation;
- `{}`, `null`, omission, one-entry removal, and full clear;
- malformed entries returning 4xx; and
- response-loss/readback behavior after a committed update.
