title: cache_control_injection_points on /v1/messages lands as a stray top-level field instead of on a message, for long multi-turn tool-calling conversations (regression/gap in #31778)
body:
**Related:** #30293 (original bug), fixed by #31778 (merged 2026-07-01)

### Environment
- LiteLLM version: `v1.96.0` (proxy, pinned Docker image, released 2026-08-10 — well after #31778)
- Provider: Bedrock (`bedrock/eu.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5`, `bedrock_converse`)
- Route: native `/v1/messages` (Anthropic Messages format), reached via `anthropic/<model>` from an OpenAI-SDK-based client (n8n's Instance AI Assistant)

### Model config
```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: bedrock/eu.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5
    litellm_params:
      model: bedrock/eu.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5
      aws_region_name: eu-central-1
      cache_control_injection_points:
        - location: message
          role: system
        - location: message
          role: user
          index: -1
        - location: message
          role: user
          index: -2
```

### What happened

I confirmed #31778 is present in this version — `AnthropicCacheControlHook.apply_to_anthropic_messages_request()` exists in the pinned image's source and looks structurally correct (splits `system`/`messages`, handles both string and list-of-content-block message shapes).

However, on real traffic — a long, multi-turn, tool-heavy agentic conversation (an AI assistant that calls many tools per turn: file writes, node lookups, workflow builds, etc., each producing `tool_result` messages) — only the `system`-role breakpoint is ever actually applied. The `index`-based breakpoints are not.

Inspecting the raw outgoing request JSON directly, `cache_control` appears **exactly twice**:
1. Correctly inside `system[0].cache_control` (works every time, `cache_read_input_tokens` stays a stable, durable value across turns and even across days).
2. As a **stray, invalid top-level field on the request body itself** — `{"cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}}` sitting next to `tool_choice`/`output_config`, not attached to any message or content block. Anthropic's schema has no such top-level field; it's silently ignored by the API.

Result: `cache_creation_input_tokens` and (for anything beyond the system prompt) `cache_read_input_tokens` are `0` on every single request we've inspected — the message-indexed breakpoints have never once produced a real cache write in this deployment, despite being resolved (no "index out of bounds" warning in logs) and despite #31778's own test passing for a trivial single-turn case.

### Reproduction difference from #31778's test

#31778's proof-of-fix uses a single-turn request: one system string, one plain-text user message. Our conversations are long multi-turn tool loops — by the time an `index: -1`/`-2` breakpoint is evaluated, the target message is typically a `tool_result`-type content block several turns into the conversation, not a simple first-turn user string. I haven't been able to isolate the exact trigger further without instrumenting the proxy directly, but the `system`-role breakpoint (role-based resolution) works reliably in the same requests where the `index`-based ones (absolute-index resolution) don't — suggesting the two resolution paths inside `apply_to_anthropic_messages_request`/`_apply_message_injections` diverge for this shape of request.

### Expected behavior
`index`-based message breakpoints should attach `cache_control` to the target message's content block, the same way the `role`-based system breakpoint correctly does, regardless of conversation length or tool-result-heavy message shapes.

### Actual behavior
`cache_control` for `index`-based breakpoints ends up as an invalid top-level request field and is dropped by the Anthropic API, silently disabling caching for anything beyond the system prompt.

title: [Bug]: Intermittent ~16.7s time-to-first-byte (TTFB) on streaming Anthropic /v1/messages requests, not reproducible against Bedrock directly
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

Streaming `/v1/messages` requests through LiteLLM show a bimodal time-to-first-byte: most
runs return the first byte in about 2 seconds, matching direct Bedrock, but a subset
consistently take about 16.7 seconds, clustered tightly with nothing in between. The same
request sent directly to Bedrock (bypassing LiteLLM entirely) is fast on every run.

Five back-to-back identical requests (Anthropic Messages format, model
`us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5`, adaptive thinking,
`output_config.effort: max`, `stream: true`, headers and body shaped to match a real Claude
Code request) against each target:

| Target | Run 1 | Run 2 | Run 3 | Run 4 | Run 5 | min | max | mean | median | stdev |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bedrock direct (`bedrock-runtime.<region>.amazonaws.com/model/<id>/invoke-with-response-stream`) | 1.965s | 1.789s | 1.727s | 1.728s | 1.539s | 1.539 | 1.965 | 1.750 | 1.728 | 0.153 |
| Through LiteLLM (`http://localhost:4000/v1/messages`) | 2.131s | 16.840s | 16.757s | 2.257s | 16.663s | 2.131 | 16.840 | 10.930 | 16.663 | 7.975 |

Bedrock direct is fast and stable on every run (stdev 0.15s). Through LiteLLM, 3 of 5 runs
exceed a 10-second threshold, and the slow runs land within 0.2s of each other
(16.66-16.84s), which points at a specific added delay, timeout, or retry path rather than
generic overhead or model-side variance.

Expected: every request through LiteLLM should have a time-to-first-byte close to the
direct-Bedrock baseline, with no bimodal split.


### User Flow


Before a (hypothetical) fix: a Claude Code user occasionally waits roughly 15 seconds
longer than usual before the first token of a streaming reply appears, with no way to
predict which turns will be slow.

1. They run Claude Code with adaptive thinking at effort `max`, against a model routed
   through LiteLLM at `http://localhost:4000/v1/messages`.
2. They send the same prompt several times in a row in the same session.
3. On some turns, Claude Code's own `[API:timing] first byte after ...ms` debug log reports
   around 2000ms; on other turns it reports around 16000-17000ms, with no turns landing in
   between.
4. Sending the exact same request body directly to Bedrock's
   `invoke-with-response-stream` endpoint, bypassing LiteLLM, is fast (under 2 seconds) on
   every attempt, so the user has no way to tell in advance whether the next turn through
   LiteLLM will be fast or roughly 8x slower.

After a (hypothetical) fix: the same user sees a consistently fast first token on every
turn, matching what they get by hitting Bedrock directly.

1. They run Claude Code with adaptive thinking at effort `max`, against the same model
   routed through LiteLLM at `http://localhost:4000/v1/messages`.
2. They send the same prompt several times in a row in the same session.
3. Every turn's `[API:timing] first byte after ...ms` debug log reports close to 2000ms,
   matching the direct-Bedrock baseline.
4. The bimodal split disappears: no turn takes 16+ seconds when the direct-Bedrock request

title: cache_control breakpoint census ignores `tools` on the chat/completions path, so injection can exceed Anthropic's 4-block cap
body:
### What happened

`AnthropicCacheControlHook` counts the client's existing `cache_control` breakpoints before injecting its own, to stay under Anthropic's four-block limit. On the **`/v1/messages` path** that census includes `tools`. On the **chat/completions path** it does not, so a client that marks a tool definition can be pushed over the cap.

### Where

Checked on `v1.98.0` (latest release at time of writing) and `v1.100.0-dev.2`.

The `/v1/messages` path stands down when the client already marked anything, tools included — `_request_has_cache_control(messages, system, tools)`:

```python
if tools is not None:
    return any(
        isinstance(tool, dict)
        and (
            tool.get("cache_control") is not None
            or (isinstance(tool.get("function"), dict) and tool["function"].get("cache_control") is not None)
        )
        for tool in tools
    )
```

Its own docstring states the reason:

> Tools count: they are a breakpoint the client can mark, they count toward the provider's four-block limit, and caching only the tool definitions is a common pattern, so injecting alongside them can exceed the cap.

The chat/completions entry point does not apply that reasoning. `get_chat_completion_prompt` never calls `_should_stand_down`, and the census it uses looks only at system blocks and messages:

```python
# v1.100.0-dev.2
@staticmethod
def _count_request_cache_breakpoints(messages: Iterable[object], system: object = None) -> int:
    system_blocks: Final = (
        sum(1 for block in system if _carries_cache_breakpoint(block)) if isinstance(system, list) else 0
    )
    return system_blocks + sum(AnthropicCacheControlHook._count_cache_control_blocks(msg) for msg in messages)
```

`reserved_blocks` reserves a slot only for configured `location: tool_config` points — it does not account for `cache_control` the client put on a tool itself:

```python
reserved_blocks: Final = (
    1 if not openai_dialect and any(p.get("location") == "tool_config" for p in remaining_points) else 0
)
```

On `v1.98.0` the same holds with `used_blocks = sum(_count_cache_control_blocks(msg) for msg in messages)`.

### Why it matters

With `cache_control_injection_points` configured for a model, a request carrying:

- 1 `cache_control` on a tool definition, and
- 3 `cache_control` marks in `messages`

is censused as 3 of 4, so an injection point still applies and the request reaches the provider with **5** breakpoints — `messages` 4 + `tools` 1 — which Anthropic rejects.

This is reachable in practice: Claude Code sends a marked tool alongside its own message-level breakpoints, and routing Anthropic models through an OpenAI-shaped provider (e.g. OpenRouter) puts that traffic on the chat/completions path rather than `/v1/messages`.

### Reproduction

Model config:

```yaml
- model_name: claude-example
  litellm_params:
    model: openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-4.8
    cache_control_injection_points:
      - location: message
        role: system
      - location: message
        index: -1
```

Send a chat/completions request where `tools[-1]` carries `{"cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}}` and three messages already carry their own `cache_control`. The hook injects on top of that; the outgoing request has five blocks.

**Honest scope note:** this is from reading the code on the two versions above, not from a reproduced 400 against the live API. The census is demonstrably tools-blind on that path; whether a given request tips over the cap depends on how many marks the client already sent.

### Suggested fix

Make the chat/completions path use the same accounting the `/v1/messages` path already does — either:

1. pass `tools` into the census so client-marked tools count toward `used_blocks`, or
2. call `_should_stand_down(points, messages, system, tools)` in `get_chat_completion_prompt`, matching `_judged_configured_points`.

Option 2 keeps the two paths behaviourally identical, which seems to be the intent of the existing docstring.
author: xandr0s

title: [Bug]: Token usage logged as 0 for Responses API WebSocket mode (_aresponses_websocket), breaking cost tracking for Agent CLI traffic
body:
### Issue / Context
When deploying LiteLLM in an organization for developers using **Agent CLIs (e.g. Cursor, Codex, custom agents)** communicating via the **Responses API WebSocket endpoint** (`/v1/responses`, `_aresponses_websocket`), token usage is always logged as **0** (`prompt_tokens=0, completion_tokens=0, total_tokens=0`).
This prevents organizations from tracking costs and enforcing spend budgets on WebSocket traffic.

### Root Cause
1. In native Responses WebSocket mode, the raw list of forwarded stream events is passed to `logging_obj.dispatch_success_handlers(self.messages)`.
2. `normalize_logging_result` in `litellm_logging.py` lacks a handler for `CallTypes.aresponses_websocket`, so the event list is not normalized into a response object and collapses to an empty dict `{}`.
3. Consequently, `StandardLoggingPayload` and spend tracking records receive 0 tokens.
4. Additionally, existing proposed fixes for this issue simply sum the top-level 3 counters (`input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `total_tokens`) into a plain dict, discarding `input_tokens_details` (`cached_tokens`) and `output_tokens_details` (`reasoning_tokens`), which corrupts prompt caching discounts and reasoning cost calculations.

### Expected Behavior
- Responses API WebSocket sessions should log provider token usage extracted from terminal events (`response.completed`, `response.incomplete`).
- Detailed token breakdowns (`cached_tokens`, `reasoning_tokens`, etc.) must be preserved and combined across turns in the session so accurate costs and usage are recorded.

title: [Bug]: Key regenerate/update/delete fail with "cannot execute UPDATE in a read-only transaction" when DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA is set (access-group sync runs UPDATE via query_raw)
body:
### Check for existing issues

I searched the existing issues and this is not a duplicate. The closest, #35757, is about read-replica routing serving virtual-key **auth reads** (revoked keys still working / new keys rejected during lag). This report is a different defect: the access-group sync helpers added in v1.98.0 route **writes** (`UPDATE`) to the read-only replica, which the replica rejects outright. Related: PR #36843 and PR #36825, and feature request #38351.

### What happened?

After upgrading from **v1.97.0 → v1.98.0**, virtual-key **regeneration fails consistently**, and key **update/delete** become unreliable, on any deployment configured with a read replica (`DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA`, e.g. an Aurora reader endpoint).

The proxy returns:

```
Error regenerating key: ERROR: cannot execute UPDATE in a read-only transaction
```

(PostgreSQL `SQLSTATE 25006`, `read_only_sql_transaction`.)

**Root cause (traced in code + confirmed against a live 1.98.0 proxy):**

1. PR #36843 added `litellm/proxy/management_helpers/access_group_key_sync.py`. It mirrors key↔access-group membership using statements like:
   ```sql
   UPDATE "LiteLLM_AccessGroupTable"
   SET "assigned_key_ids" = array_append(array_remove(array_remove("assigned_key_ids", $1), $2), $2)
   WHERE $1 = ANY("assigned_key_ids")
   RETURNING "access_group_id"
   ```
   These `UPDATE ... RETURNING` statements are executed through Prisma **`query_raw`** (because the code needs the `RETURNING` rows).

2. `sync_key_regeneration_access_group_membership` runs its repoint `UPDATE` **unconditionally** on every regenerate (no access-group short-circuit), so regeneration hits this path every time. `sync_key_access_group_membership` (create/update/delete) runs its `UPDATE` whenever `access_group_ids` are involved.

3. `litellm/proxy/db/routing_prisma_wrapper.py` classifies `query_raw` as a **read** and routes it to the reader:
   ```python
   _MODEL_READ_METHODS: Final = frozenset({... "query_raw"})
   _TOP_LEVEL_READ_METHODS: Final = frozenset({"query_first", "query_raw"})
   ...
   def __getattr__(self, name):
       if name in _TOP_LEVEL_READ_METHODS:
           return getattr(self.read_target, name)   # -> the read replica
   ```

4. When `DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA` is set, `self.read_target` is the read-only replica. The replica rejects the `UPDATE` with `cannot execute UPDATE in a read-only transaction`.

5. In `_execute_virtual_key_regeneration`, the new token is written to the **writer** (`VerificationTokenRepository(...).table.update(...)`) **before** the failing `sync_key_regeneration_access_group_membership(...)` call. So the token is silently rotated, then the request errors out. The caller never receives the new key, keeps the old one, and every subsequent `GET /key/info`, `POST /key/{old}/regenerate`, and `POST /key/delete` on the stale token returns **`404 "Key not found" / "No keys found"`**. The key becomes orphaned and unmanageable via the API.

The same anti-pattern exists in `access_group_team_sync.py` (PR #36825): `_ATTACH_SQL` / `_DETACH_SQL` `UPDATE ... RETURNING` run via `query_raw` for the team write paths.

**Why it is version- and topology-specific** (A/B tested across environments):

| Topology | v1.97.0 | v1.98.0 |
|---|---|---|
| With `DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA` (Aurora reader) | ✅ works | ❌ fails |
| No read replica (writer only) | ✅ works | ✅ works |

v1.97.0 has no sync helper, so no `UPDATE` is ever sent via `query_raw`. Without a read replica, `query_raw` goes to the writer and the `UPDATE` succeeds. The read replica is required for the bug to fire, but the trigger is the v1.98.0 code.

**Expected:** key regenerate/update/delete succeed with a read replica configured; access-group membership writes go to the writer.

### User Flow

**Before a (hypothetical) fix:** a developer using our internal key-management portal (which drives the LiteLLM management API) clicks "Regenerate" on their virtual key, gets an error, and from then on the key can no longer be viewed, regenerated, or revoked.

1. On the portal key page they click **Regenerate key**. The portal sends `POST https://<litellm-proxy>/key/{old_key}/regenerate` with the master key.
2. The response is a **500** whose error text is `cannot execute UPDATE in a read-only transaction`. The portal shows "regeneration failed" and keeps displaying the old key.
3. Server-side the key's token has actually been rotated, so the old key the portal still holds no longer exists.
4. They retry, or click **View** / **Revoke**. The portal sends `POST /key/{old_key}/regenerate`, `GET /key/info?key={old_key}`, or `POST /key/delete` for `{old_key}` — every one now returns **404** (`Key not found` / `No keys found`).
5. The key is orphaned: it cannot be regenerated, inspected, or revoked through the API, so the user cannot recover or clean it up.

**After a (hypothetical) fix:** the same "Regenerate" click succeeds and returns the new key.

1. On the portal key page they click **Regenerate key**. The portal sends `POST https://<litellm-proxy>/key/{old_key}/regenerate`.
2. The response is **200** with the new key string.
3. The portal shows the new key; subsequent `GET /key/info` and `POST /key/delete` for that key work normally, and the key remains manageable.

Availability consequence: before a fix, any user who regenerates a key with a read replica configured loses the ability to manage that key at all (it is rotated but unrecoverable through the API). After a fix, regeneration is atomic from the user's seat and the key stays manageable.

### Proof the bug occurs

**Config / setup the proxy ran with** (non-sensitive env kept, secrets redacted):

- `DATABASE_URL = postgresql://<redacted>@<writer-endpoint>/litellm` (primary / writer)
- `DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA = postgresql://<redacted>@<reader-endpoint>/litellm` (Aurora **reader** endpoint — read-only)
- No Redis; 3 proxy pods. The bug reproduces on a single pod too. Any read-only Postgres hot standby as the replica reproduces it.

**Version:** `v1.98.0` (`ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-non_root:1.98.0`)

**Command (from the app that manages keys; equivalent bare curl):**

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "https://<litellm-proxy>/key/<key>/regenerate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <master_key>"
```

**Full server output (live proxy, `--detailed_debug`-equivalent JSON logs):**

```json
{"message": "Error regenerating key: ERROR: cannot execute UPDATE in a read-only transaction", "level": "ERROR", "timestamp": "2026-08-28T13:16:11.606896", "component": "LiteLLM Proxy", "logger": "key_management_endpoints.py:5067"}
{"message": "Exception: ERROR: cannot execute UPDATE in a read-only transaction", "level": "ERROR", "timestamp": "2026-08-28T13:16:11.612747", "component": "LiteLLM Proxy", "logger": "utils.py:6557"}
```

Cascade after the silent rotation — the same key can no longer be inspected, regenerated, or deleted (token abbreviated):

```json
{"message": "Exception: Key not found in database", "level": "ERROR", "logger": "key_management_endpoints.py:3675 (info_key_fn)"}
{"message": "Error regenerating key: 404: {'error': 'Key 4ab637…99195 not found.'}", "level": "ERROR", "logger": "key_management_endpoints.py:5067"}
{"message": "litellm.proxy.proxy_server.delete_verification_tokens(): Exception occured - 404: {'error': 'No keys found'}", "level": "ERROR", "logger": "key_management_endpoints.py:4236"}
```

Regenerating with the read replica **unset** (writer-only) makes the identical request succeed, and rolling back to **v1.97.0** with the same read-replica topology also succeeds — isolating the change to the v1.98.0 sync helpers.

### Suggested fix

Route these membership writes to the **writer** rather than through `query_raw`:

- In `access_group_key_sync.py` and `access_group_team_sync.py`, run the `UPDATE ... RETURNING` statements via `execute_raw` (writer-routed in `RoutingPrismaWrapper`), or explicitly target the writer client for the raw statement, instead of `query_raw`.
- More generally, `query_raw` being unconditionally classified as a read in `routing_prisma_wrapper.py` is unsafe for raw `UPDATE/DELETE ... RETURNING`; any raw mutation that needs `RETURNING` must not be routed to the reader.

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

### What LiteLLM version are you on?

v1.98.0 (regression introduced between v1.97.0 and v1.98.0; `access_group_key_sync.py` / `access_group_team_sync.py`, PRs #36843 and #36825)

title: supports_openai_prompt_cache_breakpoint's provider gate excludes bedrock_mantle, which genuinely supports the same dialect
body:
#37628 added dialect gating for the OpenAI `prompt_cache_breakpoint` feature. `AnthropicCacheControlHook._targets_openai_prompt_cache_breakpoint` does two checks in sequence:

1. `supports_openai_prompt_cache_breakpoint(model)` — model-map flag first (`supports_prompt_cache_breakpoint` in `litellm.model_cost`), falling back to a GPT-version regex.
2. `(custom_llm_provider or _resolve_provider(model)) == "openai"` — an unconditional provider-name check, applied regardless of how check 1 resolved.

I've verified live that AWS Bedrock's `bedrock_mantle` provider (routing an OpenAI-shaped request body to a Bedrock-hosted GPT-5.6-class model, e.g. `litellm_params.model = "bedrock_mantle/openai.<model>"`) genuinely honors `prompt_cache_breakpoint` end-to-end:

- Cold call with a ~2500-token cached system prefix and an explicit `prompt_cache_breakpoint`: response usage reports `cache_write_tokens: 2514` / `cache_creation_tokens: 2514`.
- Repeat call, same prefix, same `prompt_cache_key`: response usage reports `cached_tokens: 2514` — a real cache hit, not a passthrough no-op.
- Cost in both cases matches the model's cache-write/cache-read rates exactly.

`litellm.get_llm_provider("bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6")` resolves `custom_llm_provider` to `bedrock_mantle`, not `openai`. So even if an operator sets `supports_prompt_cache_breakpoint: true` explicitly on that model's cost-map entry (check 1 passes), check 2 still unconditionally returns `False` — the explicit, per-deployment-string flag can't override the coarse provider-name check.

**Ask**: let the model-map flag be authoritative when explicitly set, rather than layering an unconditional provider check on top of it. Since `litellm.model_cost` entries are already keyed per exact deployment string (e.g. `bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-sol` has its own entry, distinct from `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`), an explicit `supports_prompt_cache_breakpoint: true` on that specific entry is a more precise signal than a generic `custom_llm_provider == "openai"` string match — it already says "this exact deployment speaks the dialect," which is exactly what the provider check is trying to approximate less precisely. Concretely: skip the provider-name/host check when `_has_model_map_entry(model)` is true and the flag is explicitly set (only fall back to the provider/host heuristic when there's no explicit model-map entry to trust). Happy to share more repro detail or send a PR if that's useful.
author: deepanshululla

title: fix(gemini): do not inject temperature for Gemini 3 models when omitted
body:
### Problem

`VertexGeminiConfig.map_openai_params` currently adds `temperature = 1.0` for every Gemini 3.x model when the caller omitted it. `GoogleAIStudioGeminiConfig` inherits the same mapping, so this affects both Google AI Studio and Vertex AI routes.

That fallback now conflicts with Google's migration guidance: Gemini 3.6 already does not support `temperature`, `top_p`, or `top_k`; migrations to Gemini 3.7 must strip those sampling parameters from generation configs.

Google guidance: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/latest-model#choosing-the-right-model

### Proposed change

Remove the final Gemini-3 absent-temperature fallback in `VertexGeminiConfig.map_openai_params`:

```python
# Set default temperature to 1.0 for Gemini 3 models if not specified
if VertexGeminiConfig._is_gemini_3_or_newer(model):
    if "temperature" not in optional_params:
        optional_params["temperature"] = 1.0
```

Preserve the mapping of explicitly supplied `temperature`, `top_p`, and `top_k`; this only changes the absent-parameter path.

### Regression coverage

Please replace the existing positive default-temperature contract with transformation-level assertions that both the `gemini` and `vertex_ai` routes leave `generationConfig.temperature` absent when the input has no sampling parameters, while retaining an explicit-temperature case.

I can submit a PR once the requested direction is confirmed.

title: [Bug]: `encoding_format` cannot be suppressed when proxying embeddings through `custom_llm_provider="openai"`, breaking any 2-hop LiteLLM→LiteLLM chain
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

We run two chained LiteLLM proxies: proxy A has a model entry `model: openai/<model>` with `api_base` pointing at proxy B, which talks to Bedrock directly. This is the standard way to chain two LiteLLM proxies over the OpenAI-compatible surface.

For any embedding model where the Bedrock-backed proxy B reports **zero** supported OpenAI params (e.g. `amazon.titan-embed-text-v1`, whose Bedrock API genuinely has no format parameter), calling that model through proxy A always fails with a 400 rejecting `encoding_format`, no matter what the client sends, and no matter how proxy A is configured. We expected that if omit `encoding_format` entirely from my request, and/or set `LITELLM_DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_ENCODING_FORMAT=none` on proxy A, the field would not be forwarded to proxy B, but it always is, with a different default value depending on which knob is set.

Calling proxy B directly (bypassing proxy A), with the same model and a client request that omits `encoding_format` entirely, succeeds. This confirms the injection happens inside proxy A's own server process, specifically on the `openai`-provider embedding code path, not anywhere on proxy B or Bedrock itself.

### Check for existing issues
  - Related churn over this exact parameter, none of which cover the two-hop case: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/25388, https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/25428, https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/25698, https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/26976

### User Flow

Before a fix: a developer's app calls an embedding model through their org's edge LiteLLM proxy (which itself forwards to a second, Bedrock-backed LiteLLM proxy) and always gets a 400, even though the same call works when pointed directly at the second proxy

1. They send `POST https://proxy-a/v1/embeddings` with `{"model": "amazon.titan-embed-text-v1", "input": "hello world"}` (no `encoding_format` field at all)
2. The response is `400 Bad Request`, body containing `"litellm.UnsupportedParamsError: bedrock does not support parameters: {'encoding_format': 'float'}, for model=amazon.titan-embed-text-v1"`
3. Their platform team sets `LITELLM_DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_ENCODING_FORMAT=none` on proxy A's deployment and restarts it
4. They resend the identical `POST https://proxy-a/v1/embeddings` request, it still 400s, now complaining about `{'encoding_format': 'base64'}` instead of `'float'`
5. They point their app directly at `POST https://proxy-b/v1/embeddings` with the identical body, this succeeds with `200 OK` and a real embedding vector, confirming proxy B and Bedrock are not the problem

After a fix: the same request through proxy A succeeds identically to calling proxy B directly

1. The developer sends `POST https://proxy-a/v1/embeddings` with `{"model": "amazon.titan-embed-text-v1", "input": "hello world"}`
2. The response is `200 OK` with a `data[0].embedding` array, matching what `POST https://proxy-b/v1/embeddings` already returns today for the same input

### Proof the bug occurs

Config proxy A ran with:

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: amazon.titan-embed-text-v1
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/amazon.titan-embed-text-v1
      api_key: os.environ/PROXY_B_KEY
      api_base: https://<proxy-b-host>
```

Config proxy B ran with:

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: amazon.titan-embed-text-v1
    litellm_params:
      model: bedrock/amazon.titan-embed-text-v1
      aws_region_name: eu-central-1
```

Version: v1.98.0 on both proxies (also confirmed on v1.91.5)

Commands and output (captured live against the two-hop chain described above):

```
# Direct to proxy B, bypassing proxy A, encoding_format genuinely absent from the JSON body:
$ curl -s -X POST https://proxy-b/v1/embeddings \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $PROXY_B_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"amazon.titan-embed-text-v1","input":"hello world"}'
{
    "model": "amazon.titan-embed-text-v1",
    "data": [{"embedding": [0.7265625, -0.0703125, 0.34765625, "... 1536 floats total ..."], "index": 0, "object": "embedding"}],
    "object": "list",
    "usage": {"completion_tokens": 0, "prompt_tokens": 2, "total_tokens": 2, "completion_tokens_details": null, "prompt_tokens_details": null}
}
# 200 OK - works

# Through proxy A -> proxy B, default config, encoding_format omitted by the caller:
$ curl -s -X POST https://proxy-a/v1/embeddings \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $PROXY_A_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"amazon.titan-embed-text-v1","input":"hello world"}'
{
    "error": {
        "message": "litellm.BadRequestError: OpenAIException - Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': \"litellm.UnsupportedParamsError: bedrock does not support parameters: {'encoding_format': 'float'}, for model=amazon.titan-embed-text-v1. To drop these, set `litellm.drop_params=True` or for proxy:\n\n`litellm_settings:\n drop_params: true`\n\", 'type': 'None', 'param': None, 'code': '400'}}",
        "type": null,
        "param": null,
        "code": "400"
    }
}
# 400 Bad Request

# Same request, after setting LITELLM_DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_ENCODING_FORMAT=none on proxy A and restarting it:
$ curl -s -X POST https://proxy-a/v1/embeddings \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $PROXY_A_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"amazon.titan-embed-text-v1","input":"hello world"}'
{
    "error": {
        "message": "litellm.BadRequestError: OpenAIException - Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': \"litellm.UnsupportedParamsError: bedrock does not support parameters: {'encoding_format': 'base64'}, for model=amazon.titan-embed-text-v1. To drop these, set `litellm.drop_params=True` or for proxy:\n\n`litellm_settings:\n drop_params: true`\n\", 'type': 'None', 'param': None, 'code': '400'}}",
        "type": null,
        "param": null,
        "code": "400"
    }
}
# 400 Bad Request - note the value changed from 'float' to 'base64': the env var stopped
# proxy A's own default, but the OpenAI SDK client proxy A uses internally then applied its
# own default instead

# Same request, all three mitigations applied at once: drop_params: true set for this model,
# LITELLM_DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_ENCODING_FORMAT=none set on proxy A, and the caller's own request
# genuinely omits encoding_format entirely:
$ curl -s -X POST https://proxy-a/v1/embeddings \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $PROXY_A_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"amazon.titan-embed-text-v1","input":"hello world"}'
{
    "error": {
        "message": "litellm.BadRequestError: OpenAIException - Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': \"litellm.UnsupportedParamsError: bedrock does not support parameters: {'encoding_format': 'base64'}, for model=amazon.titan-embed-text-v1. To drop these, set `litellm.drop_params=True` or for proxy:\n\n`litellm_settings:\n drop_params: true`\n\", 'type': 'None', 'param': None, 'code': '400'}}",
        "type": null,
        "param": null,
        "code": "400"
    }
}
# 400 Bad Request - still fails with the SDK's 'base64' default, even with drop_params: true
# already set for this model. _check_valid_arg raises for models reporting zero supported
# params before drop_params logic is ever consulted, so drop_params cannot rescue this case
# either - none of the three mitigations, individually or combined, produce a request that
# reaches Bedrock with encoding_format genuinely absent.
```

Root cause, for reference: two independent default-injection points stack on the `custom_llm_provider == "openai"` (and `"litellm_proxy"`) embedding path:

`litellm/main.py`, `embedding()` (~line 6232 in v1.98.0, ~6022 in v1.91.5):

```python
if encoding_format is not None:
    optional_params["encoding_format"] = encoding_format
else:
    env_fmt = get_secret_str("LITELLM_DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_ENCODING_FORMAT")
    if env_fmt is not None and env_fmt.strip().lower() == "none":
        optional_params.pop("encoding_format", None)
    else:
        _default_fmt = optional_params.get("encoding_format") or env_fmt or "float"
        if _default_fmt.strip().lower() == "none":
            optional_params.pop("encoding_format", None)
        else:
            optional_params["encoding_format"] = _default_fmt
```

`litellm/llms/openai/openai.py`, `embedding()`/`aembedding()` (~line 1256 / ~1186):

```python
data = {"model": model, "input": input, **optional_params}
...
raw_response = await openai_aclient.embeddings.with_raw_response.create(**data, timeout=timeout)
```

Even when `LITELLM_DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_ENCODING_FORMAT=none` successfully pops `encoding_format` from `optional_params` in `main.py`, the resulting `data` dict is unpacked directly into the OpenAI Python SDK's `Embeddings.create(**data)`, and the SDK itself independently defaults `encoding_format` to `"base64"` whenever the kwarg isn't explicitly passed. Turning off either defaulting layer just lets the other one inject a value instead, and there's no configuration that results in the field being genuinely absent once a request passes through this code path, which is why calling proxy B directly (bypassing this code path entirely) is the only thing that works.

Possible fix: in `litellm/llms/openai/openai.py`, avoid unpacking a caller-absent `encoding_format` into the OpenAI SDK's high-level `.create(**data)` call, either pass the SDK's own "not given" sentinel in a way that suppresses its default too, or construct the raw embeddings request body/HTTP call directly instead of going through `openai_aclient.embeddings.create()`, so a genuinely-absent field can be represented and forwarded to the next hop.

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

v1.98.0

### Twitter / LinkedIn details

_No response_

title: [Bug]: custom_prometheus_metadata_labels are never populated on the failure and fallback metrics
body:
### What happened?

`custom_prometheus_metadata_labels` is honoured on the success path but never populated on the
failure- and fallback-side metrics. A configured label such as `caller` exports the literal
string `"None"` on exactly the series it is most needed on.

`PrometheusMetricLabels.get_labels()` appends the configured labels to the *declared* label set
of every metric, so the label exists everywhere. Only two emitters fill it:

| emitter | fills `custom_metadata_labels` | metrics it emits |
|---|---|---|
| `async_log_success_event` | yes | `litellm_proxy_total_requests_metric` (success) |
| `async_log_failure_event` | yes | `litellm_llm_api_failed_requests_metric` |
| `async_post_call_failure_hook` | **no** | `litellm_proxy_failed_requests_metric`, `litellm_proxy_total_requests_metric` (failure) |
| `set_llm_deployment_failure_metrics` | **no** | `litellm_deployment_failure_responses` |
| `log_success_fallback_event` | **no** | `litellm_deployment_successful_fallbacks` |
| `log_failure_fallback_event` | **no** | `litellm_deployment_failed_fallbacks` |

This looks like the tail of the migration in #27268 ("Fix Prometheus custom metadata label
counts"), which moved `async_log_failure_event` and `_set_virtual_key_rate_limit_metrics` onto
the keyword-label factory and "the same combined requester/auth/spend metadata extraction used
by successful request metrics". The four emitters above were not covered.

Worth distinguishing from that PR's symptom: the emitters it fixed were *raising*
`ValueError: Incorrect label count` because they emitted positionally. These four do not raise
— they use the label factory correctly and simply pass no value, so the label is filled with
`None`. Same omission, quieter failure. #38494 is another instance in the same family
(`increment_deployment_cooled_down`, still positional).

### User Flow

A proxy fronts several internal tasks that share one model group. Each request carries
`x-litellm-spend-logs-metadata: {"caller": "<task>"}`, and the proxy is configured with
`custom_prometheus_metadata_labels: ["caller"]`.

Before (today):
1. The operator opens their dashboard and splits gateway spend by task. It works — every
   successful call is attributed.
2. Calls start failing. The operator splits the failure rate the same way.
3. Every failure series comes back labelled `caller="None"`. There is no way to tell which task
   the failures belong to; the model group is shared, so it cannot separate them either.

After (expected):
1. Same dashboard, same split.
2. Calls start failing.
3. The failure series carry the same task names the success series do, and the operator can see
   which task is absorbing the failures.

### Proof the bug occurs

```python
import litellm
litellm.custom_prometheus_metadata_labels = ["caller"]

from prometheus_client import REGISTRY
from litellm.integrations.prometheus import (
    PrometheusLogger,
    get_custom_labels_from_metadata,
    _get_combined_custom_metadata_from_standard_logging_payload,
)

standard_logging_object = {
    "model_id": "resolved-deployment-id",
    "model_group": "my-model-group",
    "api_base": "https://example.com",
    "metadata": {"spend_logs_metadata": {"caller": "my-task"}},
}
request_kwargs = {
    "model": "my-model",
    "exception": Exception("upstream 503"),
    "litellm_params": {"custom_llm_provider": "vertex_ai", "metadata": {}},
    "standard_logging_object": standard_logging_object,
}

# The value is available from the payload the emitter already holds:
combined = _get_combined_custom_metadata_from_standard_logging_payload(standard_logging_object)
print("available:", get_custom_labels_from_metadata(combined))

# But the emitted series does not carry it:
PrometheusLogger().set_llm_deployment_failure_metrics(request_kwargs)
for metric in REGISTRY.collect():
    if metric.name == "litellm_deployment_failure_responses":
        for sample in metric.samples:
            print("emitted caller:", sample.labels.get("caller"))
            break
```

On a clean `litellm==1.98.0`:

```
available: {'caller': 'my-task'}
emitted caller: None
```

The exported value is the literal text `"None"` — the same stringification described in #38531.

### Suggested fix

`set_llm_deployment_failure_metrics` already holds `standard_logging_payload`, so it is a local
change. Verified to turn `caller="None"` into `caller="my-task"` with nothing else altered:

```diff
                 tags=standard_logging_payload.get("request_tags", []),
                 client_ip=client_ip,
                 user_agent=user_agent,
+                custom_metadata_labels=get_custom_labels_from_metadata(
+                    metadata=_get_combined_custom_metadata_from_standard_logging_payload(
+                        standard_logging_payload
+                    )
+                ),
             )
```

The other three emitters need the same value derived from what they hold, and there is a trap:
they carry *raw request* metadata, and passing that straight to
`get_custom_labels_from_metadata` returns `{}` — the configured key sits under
`spend_logs_metadata`, which only the payload-shaped helper flattens. Both fallback emitters
already build `standard_metadata` via
`StandardLoggingPayloadSetup.get_standard_logging_metadata`, so
`_get_combined_custom_metadata_from_standard_logging_payload({"metadata": standard_metadata})`
resolves correctly (verified). `async_post_call_failure_hook` does not build one today and
would need to.

Of the four, `set_llm_deployment_failure_metrics` is the self-contained one — it already has
the payload in scope — if a fix wants to start small.

Proxy

Present on `main`; reproduced on v1.98.0

title: [Bug]: cohere.embed-english-v3 missing from Bedrock embedding param-support dispatch
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

Calling `/v1/embeddings` against Bedrock model `cohere.embed-english-v3` fails with a 400, rejecting `encoding_format` as an unsupported parameter, even when the client never explicitly set that parameter, since the OpenAI SDK sends `encoding_format="float"` by default on every embeddings call. `drop_params: true` does not help.

I expected `cohere.embed-english-v3` to behave like `cohere.embed-multilingual-v3`, which accepts the same default without error, both are served by the same Bedrock Cohere Embed API and, on the LiteLLM side, the same `BedrockCohereEmbeddingConfig` transformation class already declares support for `encoding_format`. `cohere.embed-english-v3` is simply never routed to that class.

### Check for existing issues
  - Closest prior issue: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/9066, fixed, but only for `cohere.embed-multilingual-v3`.
  - Same shape of bug on a different provider: [#33173](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/33173) / https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/33179 (Vertex AI)

### User Flow

Before a (hypothetical) fix: a developer building a RAG pipeline configures `cohere.embed-english-v3` as their embedding model and cannot get a single embedding back

1. They send `POST https://<proxy>/v1/embeddings` with `{"model": "cohere.embed-english-v3", "input": "hello world"}` using the standard OpenAI Python SDK (`client.embeddings.create(...)`)
2. The response is `400 Bad Request` with body containing `"litellm.UnsupportedParamsError: bedrock does not support parameters: {'encoding_format': 'float'}, for model=cohere.embed-english-v3"`
3. They add `drop_params: true` to their proxy's `litellm_settings` and restart, the same request still returns the same 400

After a (hypothetical) fix: the same request returns a normal embedding vector

1. The developer sends the same `POST https://<proxy>/v1/embeddings` with `{"model": "cohere.embed-english-v3", "input": "hello world"}`
2. The response is `200 OK` with a `data[0].embedding` array of 1024 floats, matching what `cohere.embed-multilingual-v3` already returns today for the same input shape

### Proof the bug occurs

Config the proxy ran with (single hop, proxy talking directly to Bedrock):

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: cohere.embed-english-v3
    litellm_params:
      model: bedrock/cohere.embed-english-v3
      aws_region_name: eu-central-1
  - model_name: cohere.embed-multilingual-v3
    litellm_params:
      model: bedrock/cohere.embed-multilingual-v3
      aws_region_name: eu-central-1
litellm_settings:
  drop_params: true
```

Version: v1.98.0 (also confirmed on v1.91.5)

Commands and output (captured live against a single-hop, Bedrock-backed proxy, `drop_params: true` already set):

```
$ curl -s -X POST https://<proxy>/v1/embeddings \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $LLM_PROXY_API_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"cohere.embed-multilingual-v3","input":"hello world"}'
{
    "model": "cohere.embed-multilingual-v3",
    "data": [{"embedding": [0.004131317, 0.04748535, "... 1024 floats total ..."], "index": 0, "object": "embedding", "type": "float"}],
    "object": "list",
    "usage": {"completion_tokens": 0, "prompt_tokens": 2, "total_tokens": 2, "completion_tokens_details": null, "prompt_tokens_details": null}
}
# 200 OK - works

$ curl -s -X POST https://<proxy>/v1/embeddings \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $LLM_PROXY_API_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"cohere.embed-english-v3","input":"hello world"}'
{
    "error": {
        "message": "litellm.BadRequestError: OpenAIException - Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': \"litellm.UnsupportedParamsError: bedrock does not support parameters: {'encoding_format': 'float'}, for model=cohere.embed-english-v3. To drop these, set `litellm.drop_params=True` or for proxy:\n\n`litellm_settings:\n drop_params: true`\n\", 'type': 'None', 'param': None, 'code': '400'}}",
        "type": null,
        "param": null,
        "code": "400"
    }
}
# 400 - same request, same proxy, drop_params: true already set - still fails
```

Root cause, for reference (from `litellm/utils.py`, `get_optional_params_embeddings()`, the `custom_llm_provider == "bedrock"` branch):

```python
elif custom_llm_provider == "bedrock":
    if "amazon.titan-embed-text-v1" in model:
        object = litellm.AmazonTitanG1Config()
    elif "amazon.titan-embed-image-v1" in model:
        object = litellm.AmazonTitanMultimodalEmbeddingG1Config()
    elif "amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0" in model:
        object = litellm.AmazonTitanV2Config()
    elif "cohere.embed-multilingual-v3" in model or "cohere.embed-v4" in model:
        object = litellm.BedrockCohereEmbeddingConfig()
    elif "twelvelabs" in model or "marengo" in model:
        object = litellm.TwelveLabsMarengoEmbeddingConfig()
    elif "nova" in model.lower():
        object = litellm.AmazonNovaEmbeddingConfig()
    else:  # unmapped model
        supported_params = []
        _check_valid_arg(supported_params=supported_params)
        final_params = {**kwargs}
        return final_params
```

`cohere.embed-english-v3` matches none of the `elif` branches and falls into the `else` catch-all (`supported_params = []`), even though `BedrockCohereEmbeddingConfig.get_supported_openai_params()` (`litellm/llms/bedrock/embed/cohere_transformation.py`) already returns `["encoding_format", "dimensions"]` and would handle it correctly if english-v3 were routed there. Suggested fix: broaden the `elif` to `"cohere.embed" in model` so it covers english-v3 and any future Cohere Bedrock embedding model IDs, not just multilingual-v3/v4.

### The Feature

LiteLLM Proxy should preserve and pass-through the background parameter when forwarding image generation requests for gpt-image-2 to OpenAI and Azure OpenAI endpoints, instead of dropping it.

### User Flow

Before this feature (today):
Users sending image generation requests with the `background` parameter to LiteLLM Proxy dead-end because LiteLLM strips the parameter, preventing users from customizing the background of generated images.

After this feature (ideal user flow):
Users sending image generation requests with the `background` parameter to LiteLLM Proxy will successfully have the parameter passed to the provider, yielding images with the requested background style.

1. User sends a `POST /v1/images/generations` request to LiteLLM Proxy on `http://localhost:4000/v1/images/generations` with body containing `{"model": "gpt-image-2", "prompt": "a futuristic car", "background": "transparent"}`.
2. LiteLLM preserves and forwards the `background` parameter to Azure/OpenAI.

title: [Bug]: Vertex AI / Gemini 3+ silently drops google_search grounding when request contains function tool
body:
#### Check for existing issues
- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

#### What happened?
When sending a `/v1/chat/completions` request targeting a Gemini 3+ model (such as `vertex_ai/gemini-3.7-flash` or `gemini-3.5-flash`), LiteLLM unconditionally drops the search grounding tool (`google_search`, `googleSearch`, or `web_search_options`) if the client payload also specifies custom function declarations in `tools`. This issue was also reported in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/38648

As a result, Gemini 3+ requests lose search grounding and reply using only static training memory, despite the model family having native upstream support for multi-tool calling and search grounding in a single request

The dropping logic was originally introduced in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/23337 because older Gemini models (Gemini 1.5 and 2.x) returned a `400 BadRequestError: Unable to submit request because Multiple tools are supported only when they are all search tools` on Vertex AI when mixing tool types. However, Google officially supports Tool Combination starting in Gemini 3. LiteLLM should only drop search tools on pre-Gemini 3 models to prevent legacy 400 errors, and preserve both tool sets when targeting Gemini 3+ models

##### Official Upstream Sources
- Google GenAI SDK (https://github.com/googleapis/python-genai for Python and https://github.com/googleapis/genai-js for TypeScript): passing `GenerateContentConfig(tools=[{"google_search": {}}, my_func])` serializes to `[{"functionDeclarations": [...]}, {"googleSearch": {}}]` in the request body
- Vertex AI REST API reference (https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/model-reference/gemini) and Vertex AI Grounding documentation (https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/grounding/overview): Gemini 3+ endpoints accept sibling tool objects in `tools` and return grounded output alongside function calling

#### User Flow
Before a (hypothetical) fix: a client application sending both custom function declarations and Google Search grounding to a Gemini 3+ model receives an ungrounded response because search tools are stripped before forwarding to Vertex AI

1. The client sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with model `vertex-gemini-3.7`, a prompt asking for live exchange rates, a function tool `get_weather`, and a search tool `{"google_search": {}}`
2. The proxy responds with HTTP 200 containing a message generated solely from static training memory (stating it lacks real-time data or citing outdated rates)
3. The response JSON lacks search grounding attributes, and search tools are never invoked

After a (hypothetical) fix: the same client request retains both function calling capabilities and search grounding upstream on Gemini 3+ models

1. The client sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with model `vertex-gemini-3.7`, a prompt asking for live exchange rates, a function tool `get_weather`, and a search tool `{"google_search": {}}`
2. The proxy sends both the `functionDeclarations` tool object and the `googleSearch` tool object to Vertex AI
3. The proxy responds with HTTP 200 containing live, up-to-date grounded financial rate data

#### Proof the bug occurs

Config / setup the proxy ran with:

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: vertex-gemini-3.7
    litellm_params:
      model: vertex_ai/gemini-3.7-flash
      vertex_location: global
      vertex_credentials: "/path/to/vertex-sa.json"
```

Proxy startup command:
```bash
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --detailed_debug --port 4000
```

Version or commit:
`litellm_internal_staging` at `d8b1e7ba17`

Commands and their full output:

##### Test 1: Grounding only (Baseline - Works)
```bash
curl -s -X POST "http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "vertex-gemini-3.7",
    "messages": [
      {
        "role": "user",
        "content": "What is the exact EUR to HUF exchange rate today?"
      }
    ],
    "tools": [
      {
        "google_search": {}
      }
    ]
  }' | jq '.choices[0].message.content'
```

Output:
```json
"The live exchange rate for Euro to Hungarian Forint (EUR/HUF) is approximately 364.80 to 365.10 HUF per EUR."
```

##### Test 2: Mixed Function Tools + `google_search` (Bug Reproduction)
```bash
curl -s -X POST "http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "vertex-gemini-3.7",
    "messages": [
      {
        "role": "user",
        "content": "What is the exact EUR to HUF exchange rate today?"
      }
    ],
    "tools": [
      {
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
          "name": "get_weather",
          "description": "Get current weather for a city",
          "parameters": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
              "location": { "type": "string" }
            },
            "required": ["location"]
          }
        }
      },
      {
        "google_search": {}
      }
    ]
  }' | jq '.choices[0].message.content'
```

Proxy log output:
```text
LiteLLM:WARNING vertex_and_google_ai_studio_gemini.py: Vertex AI models older than Gemini 3 do not support mixing function declarations with search tools (googleSearch, enterpriseWebSearch, urlContext, googleSearchRetrieval) in the same request. Dropping search tools and keeping function declarations.
```

Output:
```json
"I do not have access to real-time financial market data to provide the exact exchange rate for today. Please check a live financial service."
```

title: [Bug]: Editing max_budget/budget_duration (UI or /key/update) leaves existing budget_limits window stale — auth still enforces the old limit (429)
body:
## Bug Description

Editing a key's (or team's) `max_budget` / `budget_duration` — via the Admin UI **or** `POST /key/update` — updates the top-level `max_budget`/`budget_duration` fields but leaves any **existing `budget_limits` array untouched**. The auth path (`_virtual_key_multi_budget_check` in `auth_checks.py`) enforces **only** the `budget_limits` windows, so the key keeps being rejected with the *old* limit/duration even though the UI and the DB top-level fields show the new budget.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a key with a budget, e.g. `POST /key/generate` with `{"key_alias": "c1", "max_budget": 5.0, "budget_duration": "7d"}` (with `STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True`).
   - DB `LiteLLM_VerificationToken.budget_limits` now contains `[{"reset_at": "...", "max_budget": 5.0, "budget_duration": "7d"}]`.
2. Later, raise the budget via the Admin UI (Team or Key → edit budget) to `max_budget: 20.0`, `budget_duration: "30d"`.
3. Observe:
   - `GET /key/info` and the DB row show `max_budget = 20.0`, `budget_duration = "30d"` ✓
   - But `LiteLLM_VerificationToken.budget_limits` **still contains** the old `7d / $5.00` window.
4. Call `/v1/chat/completions` with the key → `HTTP 429`:
   `{"error": {"message": "ExceededBudget: Key over 7d budget. Spend=$5.0065, Limit=$5.00", "type": "budget_exceeded", "code": "429"}}`

## Expected Behavior

Updating `max_budget`/`budget_duration` should either:
- propagate to the existing `budget_limits` window(s) (update the matching window's `max_budget`/`budget_duration`), **or**
- clear `budget_limits` so the top-level fields become the enforced budget.

The UI showing a new budget while the auth path enforces a phantom old one is a footgun: the change appears applied everywhere except the one place that actually gates requests.

## Actual Behavior

`budget_limits` stays frozen at creation-time values. The key remains blocked at the old limit even after:
- the UI/DB update,
- `POST /key/update` re-asserting `max_budget` + `budget_duration` (top-level only),
- a full container restart (it's a DB value, not a cache).

Only explicitly passing the corrected window in `budget_limits` on `POST /key/update` unblocks it:
```json
{"key": "<token>", "max_budget": 20.0, "budget_duration": "30d",
 "budget_limits": [{"reset_at": "2026-09-01T00:00:00+00:00", "max_budget": 20.0, "budget_duration": "30d"}]}
```

## Environment

- LiteLLM version: 1.98.0 (main-latest build, 2026-08)
- `STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True`, Redis usage cache enabled (`coordination_redis`)
- Proxy run with `litellm --port 4000` + `CONFIG_FILE_PATH`
- DB: Postgres

## Related

- #28205 (empty `budget_limits: []` not clearing windows — same dual-store gap, different symptom)
- #35364 (reset_at rewritten on every update — the inverse direction of the same dual-store confusion)

title: [Bug]: team model access is enforced at request time but not at /key/generate, and /key/update validates the pre-update model list
body:
### What happened?

Team model access is enforced at request time but not at key creation time, and the two paths disagree in a way that is easy to hit and hard to diagnose.

Given a team whose `models` list does **not** include `gpt-4o`:

**1. `/key/generate` accepts a model outside the team catalog.**

```bash
curl -X POST $PROXY/key/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"team_id":"team-b","key_alias":"probe","models":["gpt-4o"],"duration":"5m"}'
# -> 200 OK, key issued
```

**2. Using that key fails, correctly:**

```bash
curl -X POST $PROXY/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ISSUED_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"ok"}]}'
# -> 403 {"message":"team not allowed to access model. This team can only access
#          models=['claude-3-5-haiku','llama-3.1-8b',...].
#          Tried to access gpt-4o","type":"team_model_access_denied"}
```

So a key can be provisioned in a state where it can never be used. The failure only surfaces to the end user, at request time, long after whoever created the key has moved on.

**3. `/key/update` *does* validate — but against the key's current models, not the ones being set in the same call.**

Moving an existing key into a more restrictive team fails even when the request also narrows `models` to a subset the team allows:

```bash
# key currently declares 17 models; team allows 11 of them
curl -X POST $PROXY/key/update -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER_KEY" \
  -d '{"key":"'"$K"'","team_id":"team-a","models":["gpt-4o-mini","gpt-4o", ...11 allowed...]}'
# -> 403 team_model_access_denied, naming a model from the *old* list
```

The workaround is two sequential calls — first narrow `models`, then set `team_id` — which works but is not documented and is not obvious from the error message.

### Expected behaviour

Consistency between the three paths. Any of these would resolve it:

- `/key/generate` validates `models` against the team catalog and rejects with `team_model_access_denied`, matching request-time behaviour; and
- `/key/update` validates against the *resulting* state when `models` and `team_id` are supplied together, rather than the pre-existing model list.

If validating at creation is intentionally avoided (e.g. to allow provisioning before a team catalog is finalised), documenting that — and documenting the two-step update — would still remove most of the surprise.

### Relevant log output

_See the three curl exchanges above; all reproduced against a clean install._

Yes

v1.98.0

title: [Bug]: SearXNG search adapter turns HTTP 429/503 into a successful empty result
body:
### What happened?

The SearXNG search adapter builds a `SearchResponse` from `raw_response.json()` without ever checking the HTTP status code. When the SearXNG instance answers `429` or `503`, the JSON body has no `results` key, so `response_json.get("results", [])` yields an empty list and the caller receives a perfectly successful response with zero results.

The practical consequence is that a retryable provider failure becomes indistinguishable from "the query genuinely matched nothing". Any fallback logic built on top of search tools never fires, because nothing upstream ever sees a failure.

`litellm/llms/searxng/search/transformation.py`, in `transform_search_response`:

```python
response_json: Final = raw_response.json()

# Transform results to SearchResult objects
# Note: SearXNG doesn't natively support limiting results via API params
# It returns ~20 results per page by default
results: Final = []
for result in response_json.get("results", []):
```

The HTTP handlers that call this do not invoke `raise_for_status()` either, so there is no other place where the status is inspected.

### Relevant log output

Reproducing with a SearXNG instance that returns 429:

```
POST /v1/search  ->  200 OK
{"results": [], "query": "...", "number_of_results": 0}
```

Expected: a retryable error surfaced to the caller, so that fallback between configured search tools can happen.

### Suggested fix

Check the status before parsing, and raise through the provider's own error class so the existing retry/fallback machinery classifies it:

```python
if not 200 <= raw_response.status_code < 300:
    raise self.get_error_class(
        error_message=f"SearXNG search provider returned HTTP {raw_response.status_code}",
        status_code=raw_response.status_code,
        headers=dict(raw_response.headers),
    )

response_json = raw_response.json()
```

Deliberately not echoing the upstream body into the error message, since it can contain the original query.

Happy to open a PR with this if the approach looks right.

title: [Bug]: chatgpt provider strips parallel_tool_calls — Codex Responses-Lite (gpt-5.6-*) requests always 400
body:
### What happened?

Routing OpenAI Codex CLI (>= 0.144) through the LiteLLM proxy with the `chatgpt/` provider works for `gpt-5.5` / `gpt-5.4`, but **every request to `gpt-5.6-sol` (and other `gpt-5.6-*` models) fails with a hard 400** when the client's Responses-Lite header reaches the backend.

Codex >= 0.144 uses the new "Responses Lite" transport for `gpt-5.6-*`: it adds the header `x-openai-internal-codex-responses-lite: true` and sets `parallel_tool_calls: false` (+ `reasoning.context: "all_turns"`) in the body. With `forward_client_headers_to_llm_api: true` on the proxy, that header is forwarded to `chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses` — but `ChatGPTResponsesAPIConfig.transform_responses_api_request` filters the outgoing body through an `allowed_keys` whitelist that does **not** include `parallel_tool_calls`:

https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.98.0/litellm/llms/chatgpt/responses/transformation.py#L55-L97

So the client's explicit `parallel_tool_calls: false` is stripped, the backend sees the Lite header with an effective default of `true`, and rejects the request.

### Reproduction (through a proxy with the chatgpt provider configured)

```bash
curl -sS -X POST http://<proxy>/v1/responses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-openai-internal-codex-responses-lite: true" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-5.6-sol","input":[{"role":"user","content":"Say ok"}],
       "parallel_tool_calls":false,"reasoning":{"context":"all_turns"},
       "tools":[{"type":"function","name":"noop","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{}}}]}'
```

Result — even though the client body carries `parallel_tool_calls: false`:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "X-OpenAI-Internal-Codex-Responses-Lite requires `parallel_tool_calls` to be false.",
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "param": "parallel_tool_calls",
    "code": "unsupported_value"
  }
}
```

The identical request **without** the header succeeds, confirming the param is stripped in between.

### Expected behavior

- `parallel_tool_calls` (a documented Responses API param, already present in `ResponsesAPIOptionalRequestParams`) should pass through to the codex backend.
- When the Responses-Lite header is present, the transformation should satisfy the Lite contract (`parallel_tool_calls: false`, `reasoning.context: "all_turns"`) — codex 0.144.x can omit the reasoning object on a metadata race (openai/codex#33496) and the backend rejects that omission the same way.

Related ecosystem reports of the same contract: openai/codex#31882, openai/codex#31150, icoretech/codex-pooler#134.

### What version are you on?

`ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:main-stable` (v1.98.0); the whitelist is unchanged on current `main`.

I have a fix with regression tests ready and will open a PR referencing this issue.

title: [Bug]: /v1/messages stream answers 200 with message_start and an SSE error chunk when the fallback also fails before content
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

When a streaming `/v1/messages` request fails before any content and the router falls over to the configured fallback, the fallback's stream is forwarded to the client as it arrives. If that fallback also fails before producing content, the client has already received a `200 OK` and a `message_start` frame, and the failure then arrives as a `data: {"error": ...}` SSE chunk instead of the JSON error response with a real status code it would have gotten had no fallback run at all

The primary attempt already holds its lifecycle frames (`message_start`, `ping`, empty `content_block_start`) back until real content arrives, precisely so that a pre-content failure can still turn into a clean error response. The fallback attempt does not apply the same hold-back, so a double failure leaks the fallback's `message_start` onto the wire. Since #38606 this shape is also reachable for providers that raise their errors instead of emitting an Anthropic SSE `error` event (Bedrock, transport drops), so it will show up during a real multi-region outage rather than only on Anthropic's `overloaded_error` events

Expected: when both the primary and its fallback fail before any content, the client gets the same JSON error and status code it gets when the primary fails with no fallback configured, and the `x-litellm-attempted-fallbacks` header reflects the attempt that was made

### User Flow

Before a (hypothetical) fix: an operator with a primary and a fallback deployment behind one model group sees a double outage come back as a `200 OK` stream that dies on an error chunk, so clients keying off the status code treat it as a successful request

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with `"stream": true` and `"model": "bedrock-claude-doublefail"`, whose primary and fallback deployments are both unreachable
2. The response starts with `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`, `content-type: text/event-stream`, and `x-litellm-attempted-fallbacks: 0`
3. An `event: message_start` frame arrives carrying the fallback's message id
4. The stream then ends with `data: {"error": {"message": "serviceUnavailableException ...", "code": "503"}}` and no `message_stop`
5. Their SDK raises an API error from inside the stream iterator; the SDK's own status-code retries never fire because the response was a 200

After a (hypothetical) fix: the same double outage comes back as the error response it is

1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with `"stream": true` and `"model": "bedrock-claude-doublefail"`
2. The response is `HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable` with `content-type: application/json` and `x-litellm-attempted-fallbacks: 1`
3. The body is `{"error": {"message": "serviceUnavailableException ...", "code": "503"}}`, the same shape a primary-only failure returns
4. Their SDK retries the request on the 503 the way it does for every other 5xx

### Proof the bug occurs

A real double outage cannot be scheduled, so both deployments point at a local endpoint standing in for the Bedrock runtime that sends a real `message_start` event-stream frame and then a `serviceUnavailableException` exception frame, which is byte-for-byte what Bedrock sends when it sheds load mid-stream. Everything else is the real proxy, booted with `--num_workers 2`

Config / setup the proxy ran with:

```yaml
model_list:
- model_name: bedrock-claude-doublefail
  litellm_params:
    model: bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0
    aws_region_name: us-east-1
    aws_access_key_id: FAKEPRIMARYKEY
    aws_secret_access_key: FAKEPRIMARYSECRET
    aws_bedrock_runtime_endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:34820
- model_name: bedrock-claude-fake-fallback
  litellm_params:
    model: bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0
    aws_region_name: us-east-1
    aws_access_key_id: FAKEPRIMARYKEY
    aws_secret_access_key: FAKEPRIMARYSECRET
    aws_bedrock_runtime_endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:34820
router_settings:
  fallbacks:
  - bedrock-claude-doublefail:
    - bedrock-claude-fake-fallback
general_settings:
  master_key: sk-1234
litellm_settings:
  drop_params: true
```

Version or commit: 406db3fccf (PR #38606 tip at the time; the shape predates it for Anthropic `overloaded_error` events)

Commands and their full output:

```
$ curl -sS -i -N http://127.0.0.1:37572/v1/messages -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "content-type: application/json" -d '{"model":"bedrock-claude-doublefail","max_tokens":64,"stream":true,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly one word: pong"}]}'
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 01:30:40 GMT
server: uvicorn
x-litellm-call-id: 24340a08-d743-4e36-bb77-c5f6309a4b7c
x-litellm-model-name: bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0
x-litellm-version: 1.100.0
x-litellm-model-group: bedrock-claude-doublefail
x-litellm-attempted-retries: 0
x-litellm-attempted-fallbacks: 0
cache-control: no-cache
x-accel-buffering: no
content-type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

event: message_start
data: {"type": "message_start", "message": {"id": "msg_fake", "type": "message", "role": "assistant", "model": "us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0", "content": [], "stop_reason": null, "usage": {"input_tokens": 10, "output_tokens": 1}}}

data: {"error": {"message": "serviceUnavailableException {\"message\": \"fake upstream injected serviceUnavailableException mid-stream\"}", "type": "None", "param": "None", "code": "503"}}
```

For comparison, the same request against a model group with no fallback configured returns the clean error response the double failure should also produce:

```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
content-type: application/json
x-litellm-attempted-fallbacks: 0

{"error":{"message":"serviceUnavailableException {\"message\": \"fake upstream injected serviceUnavailableException mid-stream\"}","type":"None","param":"None","code":"503"}}
```

### What a fix PR should look like

In the router's `/v1/messages` mid-stream fallback attempt, hold the fallback stream's lifecycle frames back the same way the primary attempt already does (buffer until a content delta or the pre-content cap, then flush), so a fallback that fails before content propagates as an exception with nothing on the wire and the proxy answers with the JSON error and status code. While there, have the retries and fallbacks headers describe the attempt that actually answered. Cover it with a unit test where the fallback stream yields `message_start` and then raises, asserting nothing was yielded and the original error reached the caller, and QA it against a live two-worker proxy with the double-failure config above plus the real-fallback config from #38606 to show the successful fallback path still streams the same frames

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

1.100.0 (commit 406db3fccf)

### What happened?

title: [Bug]: /v1/messages prices Together deployments by their alias, so a size marker in the alias bills the size bucket
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

On the proxy's `/v1/messages` route, a Together AI deployment is priced by its public alias instead of the model it maps to. When the alias contains a parameter-size marker (`30b`, `70b`, ...), Together's size-bucket fallback picks that up and the `x-litellm-response-cost` header (and the `x-litellm-key-spend` header derived from it) bills the request at the bucket rate, ignoring the model's registry entry and its cache read price. The identical deployment on `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/responses` bills the registry rate. Expected: all three routes bill `together_ai/meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B` at its registry rates ($0.35/M input, $0.04/M cached input, $1.50/M output) whatever the alias is called

Observed at the tip of #38280 (dbadee7210), which makes registry pricing win over the size bucket on the other two routes. Before that PR every route billed the bucket, so the alias problem was invisible

### User Flow

Before a (hypothetical) fix: the cost header on `/v1/messages` disagrees with the same request on `/v1/chat/completions` for one Together deployment

1. A proxy admin adds `model_name: muse-glimmer-30b` mapping to `together_ai/meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B`
2. A developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "muse-glimmer-30b"` and a ~13k token prompt; the header reads `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0045726` (12996 x $0.35/M + 16 x $1.50/M)
3. They send the same prompt to POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with `"model": "muse-glimmer-30b"`; the header reads `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0101216` for 12636 input tokens (12636 x $0.80/M + 16 x $0.80/M, the 21.1B-41B size bucket), more than double the chat completions rate for fewer tokens
4. They send the `/v1/messages` request again; the usage block shows no cache read tokens and the header is unchanged, so a cache hit is never billed at the $0.04/M cached rate on this route

After a (hypothetical) fix: the same `/v1/messages` request bills the registry rates

1. A proxy admin adds `model_name: muse-glimmer-30b` mapping to `together_ai/meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B`
2. A developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "muse-glimmer-30b"` and a ~13k token prompt; the header reads `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0045726`
3. They send the same prompt to POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with `"model": "muse-glimmer-30b"`; the header reads `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0044466` (12636 x $0.35/M + 16 x $1.50/M), the same rate as chat completions
4. They send the `/v1/messages` request again; cached input tokens are billed at $0.04/M like they are on the other routes

### Proof the bug occurs

Config / setup the proxy ran with (`LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True`, `--num_workers 2`, `TOGETHER_API_KEY` set in the environment):

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: muse-glimmer-30b
    litellm_params:
      model: together_ai/meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B
      api_key: os.environ/TOGETHER_API_KEY

general_settings:
  master_key: sk-lit5972-test
```

Version or commit: dbadee7210 (tip of #38280 merged into litellm_internal_staging 67c7b97fd2), `x-litellm-version: 1.100.0`

Commands and their full output. `muse_chat.json` is `{"model": "muse-glimmer-30b", "messages": [{"role": "system", "content": "<~13k token corpus>"}, {"role": "user", "content": "Reply with the word ready and nothing else."}], "max_tokens": 16}`; `muse_messages.json` carries the same corpus as `system` with `"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "..."}]` and `"max_tokens": 16`

```
$ curl -s -D - -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:42191/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-lit5972-test' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @muse_chat.json | grep -i 'x-litellm-response-cost:\|x-litellm-model-name'
x-litellm-model-name: together_ai/meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B
x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0045726
usage: {"completion_tokens": 16, "prompt_tokens": 12996, "total_tokens": 13012, "prompt_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 0, "created_cache_tokens": 12992}}

$ curl -s -D - -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:42191/v1/messages -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-lit5972-test' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @muse_messages.json | grep -i 'x-litellm-response-cost\|x-litellm-model-name\|x-litellm-key-spend'
x-litellm-model-name: together_ai/meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B
x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0101216
x-litellm-response-cost-input: 0.0101088
x-litellm-key-spend: 0.0101216
usage: {"input_tokens": 12636, "output_tokens": 16}
```

12636 x 0.80/M + 16 x 0.80/M = 0.0101216 is exactly the `together-ai-21.1b-41b` bucket; the registry rate for the same tokens is 12636 x 0.35/M + 16 x 1.50/M = 0.0044466. With `--detailed_debug` the proxy logs `selected model name for cost calculation: together_ai/meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B` (cost 0.0044466) for the inner chat call and then `selected model name for cost calculation: together_ai/muse-glimmer-30b` (cost 0.0101216) for the messages response, and the second value is the one that reaches the header
