title: [Bug]: GET /v1/models/{model_id} returns 404 for any model name containing a slash
body:
## Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

## What happened?

A model group whose name contains a slash, which is the normal shape for OpenRouter style and other provider prefixed names, is listed by `GET /v1/models` under that exact id but cannot be retrieved at `GET /v1/models/{model_id}`. The gateway answers `404 {"detail":"Not Found"}`, which is the same body it returns for a URL it does not serve, so a client cannot tell the model apart from a missing endpoint.

Percent encoding the slash does not help, the encoded form comes back 404 as well.

I expected retrieve to accept any id that the listing hands out, the way the OpenAI API does. The same request works for model names without a slash, so the failure follows the name and not the configuration.

#32770 reports the same shape of failure on `GET`/`DELETE /fallback/{model}` and the fix proposed there does not reach this route.

## User Flow

Before a (hypothetical) fix: a developer pointing an OpenAI compatible client at the gateway cannot confirm that a slash named model exists, so their client treats it as unavailable

1. They send GET http://litellm-domain/v1/models with their key and get one entry back, `"id": "mistralai/mistral-7b-instruct"`
2. Their client retrieves that exact id, GET http://litellm-domain/v1/models/mistralai/mistral-7b-instruct
3. The gateway answers `404` with `{"detail":"Not Found"}`, the same body it gives for a URL it does not serve
4. They retry with the slash percent encoded, GET http://litellm-domain/v1/models/mistralai%2Fmistral-7b-instruct, and get the same `404`
5. They try the unversioned form, GET http://litellm-domain/models/mistralai/mistral-7b-instruct, and get the same `404`
6. Their client marks the model unavailable and never sends it a request, although POST http://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "mistralai/mistral-7b-instruct"` routes to the provider normally

After a (hypothetical) fix: the same client gets the model back and carries on

1. They send GET http://litellm-domain/v1/models with their key and get one entry back, `"id": "mistralai/mistral-7b-instruct"`
2. Their client retrieves that exact id, GET http://litellm-domain/v1/models/mistralai/mistral-7b-instruct
3. The gateway answers `200` with the model object carrying `"id": "mistralai/mistral-7b-instruct"`, matching what the listing advertised
4. The percent encoded form returns the same `200` and the same body
5. The unversioned form returns the same `200` and the same body
6. Their client proceeds to POST http://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with that model

## Proof the bug occurs

Config the proxy ran with:

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: mistralai/mistral-7b-instruct
    litellm_params:
      model: openrouter/mistralai/mistral-7b-instruct
      api_key: os.environ/OPENROUTER_API_KEY
  - model_name: gpt-4o-mini
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-4o-mini
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY

general_settings:
  master_key: sk-1234
```

Env vars: `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=sk-1234`, plus `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_KEY` set to placeholder values. Neither models endpoint calls a provider, so no real key is needed to reproduce this. The chat completion at the end is there only to show the same model name routes fine, and it reaches OpenRouter and comes back with a real provider 401 for the placeholder key

Commit the proof was captured at: `4fd7a73` on `litellm_internal_staging`

Started with:

```
CONFIG_FILE_PATH=config.yaml LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=sk-1234 \
  python -m uvicorn litellm.proxy.proxy_server:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4000
```

Commands and their full output:

```
$ curl -s http://localhost:4000/v1/models -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" | jq -c
{"data":[{"id":"mistralai/mistral-7b-instruct","object":"model","created":1677610602,"owned_by":"openai"},{"id":"gpt-4o-mini","object":"model","created":1677610602,"owned_by":"openai","mode":"chat","max_input_tokens":128000,"max_output_tokens":16384}],"object":"list"}

$ curl -s -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n" http://localhost:4000/v1/models/gpt-4o-mini -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234"
{"id":"gpt-4o-mini","object":"model","created":1677610602,"owned_by":"openai","mode":"chat","max_input_tokens":128000,"max_output_tokens":16384}
HTTP 200

$ curl -s -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n" http://localhost:4000/v1/models/mistralai/mistral-7b-instruct -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234"
{"detail":"Not Found"}
HTTP 404

$ curl -s -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n" "http://localhost:4000/v1/models/mistralai%2Fmistral-7b-instruct" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234"
{"detail":"Not Found"}
HTTP 404

$ curl -s -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n" http://localhost:4000/models/mistralai/mistral-7b-instruct -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234"
{"detail":"Not Found"}
HTTP 404

$ curl -s -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n" http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"model\": \"mistralai/mistral-7b-instruct\", \"messages\": [{\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"hi\"}]}"
{"error":{"message":"litellm.AuthenticationError: AuthenticationError: OpenrouterException - {\"error\":{\"message\":\"Missing Authentication header\",\"code\":401}}. Received Model Group=mistralai/mistral-7b-instruct\nAvailable Model Group Fallbacks=None","type":null,"param":null,"code":"401"}}
HTTP 401
```

The listing advertises `mistralai/mistral-7b-instruct`, the slash free `gpt-4o-mini` retrieves at `200`, and every form of the slashed id comes back `404`. The last call shows the same slashed name routing to the provider without trouble

title: [Bug]: anthropic_messages drops plaintext reasoning across tool-call replay
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I searched existing issues and did not find this plaintext chat-completions round-trip failure.

### What happened?

`anthropic_messages()` does not preserve plaintext reasoning state across its Anthropic ↔ chat-completions adapter when an assistant tool-call turn is replayed:

1. On the request path, an Anthropic `thinking` block is left only in the internal `thinking_blocks` field rather than restored as top-level `reasoning_content` on the chat assistant message.
2. On the response path, an explicitly present `reasoning_content: ""` is dropped because the adapter treats the field by truthiness, even when the same assistant turn contains tool calls.

These are presence-sensitive protocol fields. Fireworks documents that interleaved thinking/tool use must replay the prior `reasoning_content`, and DeepSeek documents the same requirement for thinking-mode tool calls:

- https://docs.fireworks.ai/guides/reasoning
- https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/thinking_mode/

This is distinct from #26916, which concerns Anthropic thinking being serialized as visible OpenAI Responses `output_text`. This report concerns plaintext reasoning state crossing the Anthropic/chat-completions adapter in both directions.

### Minimal reproduction

No provider credentials or network call are required.

```python
from litellm.llms.anthropic.experimental_pass_through.adapters.transformation import (
    LiteLLMAnthropicMessagesAdapter,
)
from litellm.types.utils import ModelResponse, Usage

adapter = LiteLLMAnthropicMessagesAdapter()

request = {
    "model": "fireworks_ai/accounts/fireworks/models/deepseek-v4-pro",
    "messages": [
        {
            "role": "assistant",
            "content": [
                {"type": "thinking", "thinking": "  preserve me  ", "signature": ""},
                {
                    "type": "tool_use",
                    "id": "call_1",
                    "name": "lookup",
                    "input": {"q": "x"},
                },
            ],
        }
    ],
}
translated, _ = adapter.translate_anthropic_to_openai(request)
assistant = translated["messages"][0]
print(assistant)
assert assistant["reasoning_content"] == "  preserve me  "

response = ModelResponse(
    id="chatcmpl-test",
    model="accounts/fireworks/models/deepseek-v4-pro",
    choices=[
        {
            "index": 0,
            "finish_reason": "tool_calls",
            "message": {
                "role": "assistant",
                "content": "",
                "reasoning_content": "",
                "tool_calls": [
                    {
                        "id": "call_1",
                        "type": "function",
                        "function": {
                            "name": "lookup",
                            "arguments": '{"q":"x"}',
                        },
                    }
                ],
            },
        }
    ],
    usage=Usage(prompt_tokens=1, completion_tokens=1, total_tokens=2),
)
blocks = adapter._translate_openai_content_to_anthropic(response.choices)
print(blocks)
assert blocks[0] == {"type": "thinking", "thinking": "", "signature": None}
```

### Observed output

The first assertion fails because the translated assistant contains `thinking_blocks` but no `reasoning_content`:

```python
{
    "role": "assistant",
    "content": None,
    "thinking_blocks": [
        {
            "type": "thinking",
            "thinking": "  preserve me  ",
            "signature": "",
            "cache_control": {},
        }
    ],
    "tool_calls": [
        {
            "id": "call_1",
            "type": "function",
            "function": {"name": "lookup", "arguments": '{"q": "x"}'},
        }
    ],
}
```

If execution continues, the response translation contains no thinking block:

```python
[
    {"type": "text", "text": ""},
    {
        "type": "tool_use",
        "id": "call_1",
        "name": "lookup",
        "input": {"q": "x"},
        "provider_specific_fields": None,
    },
]
```

### Expected behavior

- A plaintext Anthropic `thinking` block should become `reasoning_content` on the chat-completions assistant message with its exact value, including whitespace.
- An explicitly present empty `reasoning_content` on an assistant tool-call response should remain representable in the Anthropic response shape so the next request can replay it.
- A fully empty non-tool assistant response should remain omitted; the empty carrier is significant here because it accompanies tool calls.
- Provider transforms may remove internal `thinking_blocks` before wire, but must retain `reasoning_content`.

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

SDK (`litellm` Python package), `anthropic_messages()` chat-completions adapter.

### LiteLLM version

`1.95.0`
author: roni-frantchi

title: [Bug]: LangSmith tracing 400s with "trace_id does not match first part of dotted_order"
body:
## Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. (#7140 is the closest but covers child-run `dotted_order` with a `parent_run_id`. This is a root-run `trace_id != run_id` mismatch, no parent involved.) ## What happened? With LangSmith tracing enabled in the proxy config, requests that carry a session/trace header have every run batch rejected by LangSmith with a 400. No trace for those requests lands in LangSmith. Plain requests without such a header land fine. Langfuse (enabled side by side) works throughout. Likely cause: `_ensure_required_ids` in `litellm/integrations/langsmith.py` mints a fresh `run_id` when the request has no `id`, but only defaults `trace_id` to `run_id` when `trace_id` is *also* missing. When a request carries one of the headers LiteLLM maps to `metadata["trace_id"]`, the proxy honors it while generating a new `run_id`. For a root run LangSmith requires `trace_id == run_id`, so the payload is rejected. https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/ef84494d52c6708e4e9f4a54ce551a265995ad8f/litellm/integrations/langsmith.py#L170-L181 `metadata["trace_id"]` is derived from headers in `get_chain_id_from_headers` (`litellm/proxy/litellm_pre_call_utils.py`), which accepts `x-litellm-trace-id`, `x-litellm-session-id`, and any `x--session-id` header whose value looks like a session id. That last rule is what makes this hit real users without them ever setting a `trace_id` - for example, Claude Code through ngrok sends a constant `x-claude-code-session-id` for the whole session, so every run in the session carries the same `trace_id` while each gets a fresh `run_id`. ## User Flow Before a (hypothetical) fix: a developer who turns on LangSmith tracing in the proxy gets no traces in LangSmith for requests that carry a session id header. 1. They set the LangSmith API key and project in the proxy environment, enable LangSmith tracing in the proxy config, and start the proxy. 2. They send `POST https:///v1/chat/completions` with a model name and a message, their client (e.g. Claude Code) attaching a session id header. 3. The proxy returns a 200 with the completion content. 4. They open their LangSmith project. No trace appears for that request. 5. The proxy log shows LangSmith's API rejecting the run with a 400. After a (hypothetical) fix: the same request produces a trace in LangSmith. 1. Same proxy config and LangSmith keys. 2. Same `POST https:///v1/chat/completions` with the same model, message, and session id header. 3. The proxy returns a 200. 4. A trace for that request appears in the LangSmith project, and the proxy log shows no 400. ## Proof the bug occurs Config / setup the proxy ran with: ```yaml # litellm-config.yaml (excerpt) litellm_settings: success_callback: ["langfuse", "langsmith"] ``` Env vars set on the proxy: `LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY`, `LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY`, `LANGFUSE_HOST`, `LANGSMITH_API_KEY`, `LANGSMITH_PROJECT`, `LANGSMITH_BASE_URL` (values redacted; `LANGSMITH_BASE_URL=https://apac.api.smith.langchain.com`). Version or commit: `v1.97.0` (image `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:main-stable`). The `_ensure_required_ids` logic is byte-identical in `v1.96.2`. Commands and their full output: All three LLM endpoints are affected. Each was sent with its own `x-litellm-trace-id` so the runs can be told apart, and each returned 200 to the caller before LangSmith rejected the run on the next batch flush.
POST /v1/chat/completions - command and 400 ```bash podman compose up -d curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "x-litellm-trace-id: 3097ec42-c4f6-4634-b481-15d7bf99f792" \ -d '{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' ``` ``` LiteLLM:ERROR: langsmith.py:432 - Langsmith HTTP Error: 400 - {"error":"Bad request: invalid 'dotted_order': trace_id 3097ec42-c4f6-4634-b481-15d7bf99f792 does not match first part of dotted_order a0af48ee-e01a-4d99-9f06-b0685b3f5ec0 for run_id:a0af48ee-e01a-4d99-9f06-b0685b3f5ec0 trace_id:3097ec42-c4f6-4634-b481-15d7bf99f792 dotted_order:20260818T100130082650Za0af48ee-e01a-4d99-9f06-b0685b3f5ec0 parent_run_id:"} ```
POST /v1/messages - command and 400 ```bash curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "x-litellm-trace-id: 7a92dd42-656b-4665-a3e6-fb618b035a2a" \ -d '{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","max_tokens":16,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' ``` ``` LiteLLM:ERROR: langsmith.py:432 - Langsmith HTTP Error: 400 - {"error":"Bad request: invalid 'dotted_order': trace_id 7a92dd42-656b-4665-a3e6-fb618b035a2a does not match first part of dotted_order 4c364ee4-212c-4a57-a763-ee37495b3a78 for run_id:4c364ee4-212c-4a57-a763-ee37495b3a78 trace_id:7a92dd42-656b-4665-a3e6-fb618b035a2a dotted_order:20260818T102348430265Z4c364ee4-212c-4a57-a763-ee37495b3a78 parent_run_id:"} ```
POST /v1/responses - command and 400 ```bash curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/responses \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "x-litellm-trace-id: bf259ae6-936a-497d-ac6f-f9588f7c6540" \ -d '{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","input":"hi"}' ``` ``` LiteLLM:ERROR: langsmith.py:432 - Langsmith HTTP Error: 400 - {"error":"Bad request: invalid 'dotted_order': trace_id bf259ae6-936a-497d-ac6f-f9588f7c6540 does not match first part of dotted_order 6b5e4199-e9ee-47c8-ac5c-cb24e58f2a5a for run_id:6b5e4199-e9ee-47c8-ac5c-cb24e58f2a5a trace_id:bf259ae6-936a-497d-ac6f-f9588f7c6540 dotted_order:20260818T102443557144Z6b5e4199-e9ee-47c8-ac5c-cb24e58f2a5a parent_run_id:"} ```
The same request without the `x-litellm-trace-id` header lands cleanly on every one of those endpoints. Shown here for `/v1/chat/completions`, verified against the LangSmith API:
Headerless control - the run lands, id == trace_id ```bash # headerless request curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' # resolve the project to its session id curl -s "$LANGSMITH_BASE_URL/api/v1/sessions?name=$LANGSMITH_PROJECT&limit=1" \ -H "x-api-key: $LANGSMITH_API_KEY" | jq -r '.[0].id' # # the headerless run is present: id == trace_id, success, no error curl -s -X POST "$LANGSMITH_BASE_URL/api/v1/runs/query" \ -H "x-api-key: $LANGSMITH_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"id":["7d6658d2-e861-42c6-98b1-d0937e3f9cfa"]}' \ | jq -r '.runs[] | [.id, .trace_id, .status, .error, .dotted_order]' # ["7d6658d2-e861-42c6-98b1-d0937e3f9cfa","7d6658d2-e861-42c6-98b1-d0937e3f9cfa","success",null,"20260818T100034808837Z7d6658d2-e861-42c6-98b1-d0937e3f9cfa"] # the run_id from the /v1/chat/completions 400 above never lands - no run exists for it curl -s -X POST "$LANGSMITH_BASE_URL/api/v1/runs/query" \ -H "x-api-key: $LANGSMITH_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"id":["a0af48ee-e01a-4d99-9f06-b0685b3f5ec0"]}' | jq -r '.runs | length' # 0 ```
Only requests carrying one of the session/trace headers trip the 400. ## What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ## What LiteLLM version are you on ? `v1.97.0` ## Twitter / LinkedIn details _(optional, leave blank)_

title: [Bug]: /v1/responses omits required reasoning_tokens for Gemini responses without thoughts, breaking Codex clients
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

LiteLLM v1.97.0 emits an invalid OpenAI Responses API `response.completed` event when a Gemini response contains text tokens but no thinking tokens.

For `vertex_ai/gemini-3.7-flash`, a simple request with `reasoning.effort: "low"` can legitimately return no Gemini `thoughtsTokenCount`. LiteLLM still creates `usage.output_tokens_details` from the text-token count, but omits `reasoning_tokens`:

```json
"output_tokens_details": {
  "text_tokens": 1
}
```

OpenAI's Responses schema requires `reasoning_tokens` inside `output_tokens_details`. Codex consequently terminates the stream with:

```text
stream disconnected before completion: failed to parse ResponseCompleted: missing field `reasoning_tokens`
```

Expected:

```json
"output_tokens_details": {
  "reasoning_tokens": 0,
  "text_tokens": 1
}
```

If the provider reports a real reasoning-token count, LiteLLM should preserve it. If the provider reports no thinking-token count, the Responses API serializer should emit `reasoning_tokens: 0`.

This appears related to #31759 and #32837. PR #32837 intentionally omits `reasoning_tokens` when the provider value is absent, but that produces a response incompatible with the OpenAI Responses schema whenever other output-token details are present.

References:
- https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/31759
- https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/32837
- https://github.com/openai/openai-python/blob/main/src/openai/types/responses/response_usage.py
- https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/codex-api/src/sse/responses.rs

### User Flow

Before a hypothetical fix: a developer runs Codex through a LiteLLM Responses API endpoint backed by Gemini 3.7 Flash, and the completed response cannot be parsed.

1. The developer sends `POST https://<litellm-host>/v1/responses` with model `gemini-3.7-flash`, streaming enabled, reasoning effort `low`, and a simple text prompt.
2. The live Gemini provider completes the request without using thinking tokens.
3. The developer receives a `response.completed` SSE event whose `usage.output_tokens_details` contains `text_tokens` but no `reasoning_tokens`.
4. Codex displays `failed to parse ResponseCompleted: missing field reasoning_tokens` and retries or aborts instead of completing the task.

After a hypothetical fix: the same request completes successfully and remains schema-compatible when Gemini uses no thinking tokens.

1. The developer sends the same `POST https://<litellm-host>/v1/responses` request with the same model and inputs.
2. The live Gemini provider completes the request without using thinking tokens.
3. The developer receives a `response.completed` SSE event whose `usage.output_tokens_details` contains both `text_tokens` and `reasoning_tokens: 0`.
4. Codex parses the completed response and finishes the task without retrying or aborting.

### Proof the bug occurs

Config / setup:
- LiteLLM Proxy v1.97.0
- model alias: `gemini-3.7-flash`
- provider model: `vertex_ai/gemini-3.7-flash`
- no model-level `reasoning_effort` or thinking override
- live Vertex AI provider call
- authorization value redacted

Command:

```bash
curl --no-buffer https://<litellm-host>/v1/responses \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "model": "gemini-3.7-flash",
    "input": "Return exactly: ok",
    "max_output_tokens": 64,
    "reasoning": {"effort": "low"},
    "stream": true
  }'
```

Relevant fields from the final SSE event:

```text
data: {
  "type": "response.completed",
  "response": {
    "status": "completed",
    "model": "gemini-3.7-flash",
    "usage": {
      "input_tokens": 4,
      "input_tokens_details": {
        "cached_tokens": 0,
        "text_tokens": 4
      },
      "output_tokens": 1,
      "output_tokens_details": {
        "text_tokens": 1
      },
      "total_tokens": 5
    }
  }
}
```

Codex output:

```text
stream disconnected before completion: failed to parse ResponseCompleted: missing field `reasoning_tokens`
```

Provider comparison from the same live proxy using Gemini `generateContent` with `thinkingLevel: LOW`:

- `gemini-3.7-flash` returned no `thoughtsTokenCount`, which is valid for a request where the model used no thinking tokens.

author: franzudev

title: [Bug]: provider_budget_config reports budget_reset_at ~57 years in the future without Redis
body:
### What happened?

With `provider_budget_config` and **no Redis configured**, `GET /provider/budgets` reports a `budget_reset_at` roughly 57 years in the future, so a monthly budget effectively never resets.

Config:

```yaml
router_settings:
  provider_budget_config:
    openrouter:
      budget_limit: 5
      time_period: 30d
```

Response:

```json
{"providers":{"openrouter":{"budget_limit":5.0,"time_period":"30d",
 "spend":4.8888e-06,"budget_reset_at":"2083-05-04T16:04:00.635943+00:00"}}}
```

Same result with `time_period: 1mo` (`2083-05-05T15:39:32`), so it is not specific to the period format. Today's date when this was captured: 2026-08-18.

### Root cause

`async_get_ttl` means different things in the two cache backends, and `_get_current_provider_budget_reset_at` assumes the Redis meaning:

- `RedisCache.async_get_ttl()` returns **remaining seconds** (Redis `TTL`).
- `InMemoryCache.async_get_ttl()` returns `self.ttl_dict.get(key)` — and `ttl_dict` stores an **absolute expiry timestamp**: `self.ttl_dict[key] = time.time() + float(kwargs["ttl"])` (`litellm/caching/in_memory_cache.py`).

`litellm/router_strategy/budget_limiter.py`:

```python
if self.dual_cache.redis_cache:
    ttl_seconds = await self.dual_cache.redis_cache.async_get_ttl(spend_key)
else:
    ttl_seconds = await self.dual_cache.async_get_ttl(spend_key)

if ttl_seconds is None:
    return None

return (datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta(seconds=ttl_seconds)).isoformat()
```

Without Redis, `ttl_seconds` is an absolute unix timestamp (~1.79e9), so the result is `now + ~56.7 years` — which matches the observed 2083.

The budget limit itself works; only the reported reset time (and therefore the reset window for in-memory deployments) is wrong.

### Suggested fix

Either make `InMemoryCache.async_get_ttl` return remaining seconds like the Redis backend does, or convert at the call site:

```python
ttl_seconds = await self.dual_cache.async_get_ttl(spend_key)
ttl_seconds = ttl_seconds - time.time()   # in-memory stores absolute expiry
```

The first option is preferable — `async_get_ttl` returning different units per backend is a trap for any other caller.

### Relevant log output

```
LiteLLM.LoggingError: [Non-Blocking] Exception occurred while success logging
  File ".../litellm/router_strategy/budget_limiter.py", line 412, in async_log_success_event
    raise ValueError("custom_llm_provider is required")
ValueError: custom_llm_provider is required
```

Separate but related observation while testing the same feature: every request through a `pass_through_endpoints` route raises the above in `budget_limiter.async_log_success_event`, so pass-through traffic is not counted toward provider budgets at all. Happy to file that separately if useful.

No

v1.97.0

author: sashalab

title: [Bug]: Auth-stage failure spend logs (budget_exceeded) drop x-litellm-spend-logs-metadata even though the header is present
body:
## Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

## What happened?

`x-litellm-spend-logs-metadata` is documented to attach caller metadata to spend logs, and it works for successful calls and for post-auth failures (invalid model name, unsupported params, blocked model — all keep the metadata). But when a request is rejected during **auth** — most importantly `budget_exceeded` — the failure spend-log row is written with `"spend_logs_metadata": null`, even though the header is present on the rejected request.

Mechanism (from reading the proxy source): the header is only consumed by `LiteLLMProxyRequestSetup.add_litellm_metadata_from_request_headers` (`litellm/proxy/litellm_pre_call_utils.py`), which runs inside `add_litellm_data_to_request` **after** `user_api_key_auth` succeeds. Auth-stage exceptions (`BudgetExceededError`, invalid key, etc.) go through the auth failure logging path, which builds the failure `SpendLogsPayload` without ever consulting the request headers — so the caller's metadata is dropped for exactly those rows.

Impact: deployments that put a gateway in front of the proxy tag every request with `x-litellm-spend-logs-metadata` (e.g. `{"my_request_id": "..."}`) to join the client-facing request id to spend-log rows. Budget rejections are the most common customer-visible failure in prepaid setups, and they are precisely the rows that lose the join key. The customer holds a request id from the response, but the corresponding spend-log row cannot be found by it.

Reproduced on `v1.91.1` and `v1.97.0` (`litellm-database` images). Fully self-contained repro below (no provider key needed).

## Steps to Reproduce

`config.yaml` (mock model, absurd per-token cost so one call exceeds any small budget):

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: mock
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/mock
      api_key: mock
      mock_response: "ok"
      input_cost_per_token: 1.0
      output_cost_per_token: 1.0
```

Start the proxy:

```bash
docker network create litellm-repro
docker run -d --name litellm-repro-pg --network litellm-repro \
  -e POSTGRES_DB=litellm -e POSTGRES_USER=litellm -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=litellm \
  postgres:17-alpine
docker run -d --name litellm-repro --network litellm-repro -p 127.0.0.1:14001:4000 \
  -e DATABASE_URL=postgresql://litellm:litellm@litellm-repro-pg:5432/litellm \
  -e LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=sk-repro-master -e LITELLM_SALT_KEY=sk-repro-salt \
  -e STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True \
  -v "$PWD/config.yaml:/app/config.yaml:ro" \
  docker.litellm.ai/berriai/litellm-database:v1.97.0 --config /app/config.yaml --port 4000
```

Run the two-call sequence (identical header on both calls):

```bash
BASE=http://127.0.0.1:14001
KEY=$(curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/key/generate" \
  -H 'authorization: Bearer sk-repro-master' -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"key_alias":"budget-repro","models":["mock"],"max_budget":0.01}' | jq -r .key)

# call 1: succeeds, accrues spend (~30 USD at 1.0/token) far above max_budget
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "call1=%{http_code}\n" -X POST "$BASE/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -H 'x-litellm-spend-logs-metadata: {"my_request_id":"req_success_1"}' \
  -d '{"model":"mock","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'

sleep 20  # wait for the spend batch writer

# call 2: rejected at auth with 429 budget_exceeded
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "call2=%{http_code}\n" -X POST "$BASE/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -H 'x-litellm-spend-logs-metadata: {"my_request_id":"req_rejected_2"}' \
  -d '{"model":"mock","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'

sleep 15  # wait for the failure row

curl -sS "$BASE/spend/logs/v2?start_date=2026-08-18%2000:00:00&end_date=2026-08-19%2000:00:00&page=1&page_size=10" \
  -H 'authorization: Bearer sk-repro-master' | \
  jq '.data[] | {request_id, status, spend, spend_logs_metadata: .metadata.spend_logs_metadata}'
```

Observed output (v1.97.0):

```json
{
  "request_id": "6796b7ea-088d-4ade-8e82-cb7df540642d",
  "status": "failure",
  "spend": 0.0,
  "spend_logs_metadata": null
}
{
  "request_id": "chatcmpl-49bfbc9b-93f2-40d8-b836-bfc913386980",
  "status": "success",
  "spend": 30.0,
  "spend_logs_metadata": {
    "my_request_id": "req_success_1"
  }
}
```

## Expected behavior

The `failure` row for the budget-rejected request should carry `"spend_logs_metadata": {"my_request_id": "req_rejected_2"}` — the header is on the request, and post-auth failure rows already preserve it. The auth failure logging path should parse `x-litellm-spend-logs-metadata` (same `safe_json_loads` treatment as `_get_spend_logs_metadata_from_request_headers`) before building the failure `SpendLogsPayload`.

Related but distinct: #35068 covers post-call failures losing `call_type`/router metadata from the `litellm_metadata` bucket; this issue is about auth-stage failures never reaching the header-parsing step at all.

## LiteLLM version

Reproduced on `docker.litellm.ai/berriai/litellm-database:v1.91.1` and `:v1.97.0`.
author: samzong

title: [Bug]: PUT /v1/mcp/server silently nulls authorization_url, token_url, oauth2_flow when delegate_auth_to_upstream=true
body:
### What happened?

When an MCP server is configured with `auth_type: oauth2`, `oauth2_flow: authorization_code`, and `delegate_auth_to_upstream: true`, any subsequent update via `PUT /v1/mcp/server` silently discards `authorization_url`, `token_url`, and `oauth2_flow` — even when those exact fields are explicitly present with non-null values in the request body. The response (and the persisted record, confirmed via a follow-up `GET /v1/mcp/server`) always comes back with these three fields set to `null`.

This breaks the Admin UI's own "Authorize & Fetch Token" convenience button (used to fetch a test token for a server's Tools tab), since that feature depends on `authorization_url`/`token_url` being present. It fails with:

\`\`\`
{"detail":"MCP server authorization url is not configured. OAuth endpoint discovery against the configured server url did not resolve it; the url may be misconfigured. Check the proxy logs for 'MCP OAuth' warnings from server load, verify the server url, or set Authorization URL and Token URL manually, or set Issuer to discover them from the identity provider (RFC 8414)."}
\`\`\`

Setting `issuer` instead (for RFC 8414 discovery) does not help either — discovery does not appear to run on-demand, and `authorization_url`/`token_url` remain `null` regardless.

Importantly, this only affects the UI test button. The actual delegated/passthrough OAuth flow works correctly for real traffic: a client that authenticates against the upstream IdP directly and passes its own bearer token via `x-mcp-<server_name>-authorization`, alongside a valid LiteLLM virtual key in `Authorization`, successfully reaches the upstream MCP server and receives a real tool list. So the runtime behavior of `delegate_auth_to_upstream` is sound — only the persisted config for `authorization_url`/`token_url`/`oauth2_flow` is being wiped on save.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create/register an MCP server with `auth_type: oauth2`, `oauth2_flow: authorization_code`, `authorization_url`, `token_url`, and `delegate_auth_to_upstream: true`.
2. Send a `PUT /v1/mcp/server` with the full server object, explicitly including `authorization_url`, `token_url`, and `oauth2_flow: "authorization_code"` (and `issuer` cleared to `""`):

\`\`\`bash
curl -X PUT 'https://your-litellm-proxy.example.com/v1/mcp/server' \
  -H 'authorization: Bearer <admin-key>' \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  --data-raw '{
    "server_id": "<server_id>",
    "server_name": "example_mcp_server",
    "url": "https://your-mcp-server.example.com/mcp",
    "transport": "http",
    "auth_type": "oauth2",
    "oauth2_flow": "authorization_code",
    "issuer": "",
    "authorization_url": "https://your-idp.example.com/realms/your-realm/protocol/openid-connect/auth",
    "token_url": "https://your-idp.example.com/realms/your-realm/protocol/openid-connect/token",
    "delegate_auth_to_upstream": true,
    "oauth_passthrough": false,
    "dcr_bridge": false
  }'
\`\`\`

3. Inspect the response, or immediately follow up with `GET /v1/mcp/server` and find the same `server_id`.

### Expected behavior

`authorization_url` and `token_url` should be persisted exactly as submitted, and `oauth2_flow` should remain `"authorization_code"`.

### Actual behavior

The response (and subsequent GET) shows:

\`\`\`json
{
  "issuer": "",
  "authorization_url": null,
  "token_url": null,
  "oauth2_flow": null,
  "delegate_auth_to_upstream": true
}
\`\`\`

All three fields are nulled despite being explicitly sent as non-null in the request.

### Relevant log output

N/A on our end — we don't have access to the proxy's server-side logs in this deployment, only client-observable request/response pairs (above).

### Are you a ML Ops Team?

No

### What LiteLLM version are you on?

v1.97.0

### Twitter / LinkedIn details

_No response_
author: skvasanth-nyai

title: DeepSeek V4 Pro and Flash prices are stale — the flat rate no longer matches the provider at any hour
body:
Searched existing issues first: #31606 already tracks the *schema* side of this (time-based pricing support). This one is only about the **data being stale** — reporting it separately since the current values are wrong regardless of how #31606 is resolved.

### What's wrong

DeepSeek moved to time-of-day pricing on 2026-08-16 16:00 UTC and raised both bands. `model_prices_and_context_window.json` still carries the previous flat rate, so today it matches the provider at **no hour of the day** — it is not the off-peak price and not the peak price.

Current entries:

| key | input | output | cache hit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` | $0.435 | $0.87 | $0.003625 |
| `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` | $0.14 | $0.28 | $0.0028 |

Published at https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing — which is already the `source` set on both entries:

| model | band | input | output | cache hit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| V4 Pro | off-peak | $0.66 | $1.98 | $0.022 |
| V4 Pro | peak | $1.32 | $3.96 | $0.044 |
| V4 Flash | off-peak | $0.22 | $0.66 | $0.007 |
| V4 Flash | peak | $0.44 | $1.32 | $0.014 |

Peak is 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 UTC; every other hour is off-peak, at half the peak rate.

All figures are USD per 1M tokens, read off the provider page on 2026-08-17.

### Why I'm not just opening a PR

Picking the replacement value is the part #31606 exists for: with a single scalar, off-peak understates cost during the 7 peak hours and peak overstates it during the other 17. That tradeoff looks like a maintainer call, so I'd rather not pick it in a drive-by PR.

Happy to send the PR immediately once you say which band to use as the interim value — or to add both bands under new keys if #31606 is heading that way.

### One detail worth not losing

Cache reads are the sharpest part of this change and the easiest to miss next to the headline numbers: V4 Pro went from $0.003625 to $0.022 per 1M off-peak, a 6x. Possibly interacts with #28854 (`input_cost_per_token_cache_hit` reported as a dead field), since both DeepSeek entries set it.
author: mrenzo20

title: [Feature]: Bump Granian from 2.7.4 to 2.8.1 in the published proxy
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

There is no open or closed issue/PR for Granian 2.8.x. The last Granian bump was Dependabot [#28538](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/28538) (`2.5.7` → `2.7.4`, closed unmerged) and the security bundle [#29208](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/29208) that landed `2.7.4`.

### The Feature

Please evaluate and bump the Granian version shipped with the official proxy images / PyPI package from **2.7.4 to 2.8.1**.

`pyproject.toml` already allows `granian>=2.7.4,<3.0`, so 2.8.1 is in range. The published lock and images still ship **2.7.4**.

Granian **2.8.1** was released 2026-08-05 ([release](https://github.com/emmett-framework/granian/releases/tag/v2.8.1)). OSV reports no CVEs on 2.7.4 or 2.8.1 — this is not a security fire drill. The last LiteLLM Granian bump *was* CVE-driven (`CVE-2026-42544` / `CVE-2026-42545` in #29208), which is why I am asking here instead of sending a lockfile-only PR.

**Please review Granian 2.8.0 breaking changes before bumping** ([2.8.0 notes](https://github.com/emmett-framework/granian/releases/tag/v2.8.0)):

- Linux multi-worker + respawn now requires kernel ≥ 5.14 **and** `net.ipv4.tcp_migrate_req` enabled.
- Non-configurable backpressure on streamed / iterable ASGI responses (can change `/v1/chat/completions` streaming memory vs throughput).
- Worker loop / shutdown refactors (relevant if `--max_requests_before_restart` is in use).
- WSGI environ priority change (should not affect the ASGI proxy path).

2.8.1 itself is a patch on top of that: ASGI websocket performance regression fix, `PyFutureAwaitable` interface fix, RSGI websocket close, relaxed atomics.

I can send a lockfile PR if you want the bump after this review.

### User Flow

Before this feature (today): an operator who starts the official proxy with Granian gets 2.7.4 and cannot pick up the 2.8.1 server without rebuilding the image themselves.

1. They deploy `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database:1.97.0` (or `pip install litellm==1.97.0`) and start the proxy with `--run_granian` plus TLS.
2. They send `GET https://<litellm-host>/health/liveliness` with HTTP/2. It returns `HTTP/2 200`, `server: granian`, body `"I'm alive!"`.
3. The same URL over HTTP/1.1 also returns `200` and `server: granian`.
4. They have no supported way to run Granian 2.8.1 on that official image. Workaround is a custom image / fork of the lockfile.

After this feature (ideal user flow): the same official image ships Granian 2.8.1 after the 2.8.0 behavior is reviewed.

1. They deploy the next official image / PyPI release and start the proxy with the same `--run_granian` plus TLS.
2. They send the same `GET https://<litellm-host>/health/liveliness` with HTTP/2. It still returns `HTTP/2 200`, `server: granian`, body `"I'm alive!"`.
3. The same URL over HTTP/1.1 still returns `200` and `server: granian`.
4. Streamed `POST https://<litellm-host>/v1/chat/completions` with `"stream": true` still completes with SSE `data:` chunks and a normal `[DONE]` (this is the 2.8.0 backpressure check).
5. If they use worker respawn (`--max_requests_before_restart`), workers still recycle without dropping the listener.

### How far you got

Config / setup the proxy ran with:

- Image: `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database:1.97.0`
- Started with `--run_granian` and in-guest TLS
- Public host: `https://llm.kubetee.ai`

Version or commit:

- LiteLLM `1.97.0` (`stable/1.97.x`)
- Granian inside that image: `2.7.4`
- Constraint already in tree: `granian>=2.7.4,<3.0`

Commands and their full output, up to the step that dead-ends:

```
$ curl -sS -D - --http2 --max-time 15 https://llm.kubetee.ai/health/liveliness
HTTP/2 200
content-length: 12
content-type: application/json
x-frame-options: DENY
content-security-policy: frame-ancestors 'none'
x-content-type-options: nosniff
server: granian
date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 22:24:58 GMT

"I'm alive!"
```

```
$ curl -sS -D - --http1.1 --max-time 15 https://llm.kubetee.ai/health/liveliness
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-length: 12
content-type: application/json
x-frame-options: DENY
content-security-policy: frame-ancestors 'none'
x-content-type-options: nosniff
server: granian
date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 22:25:00 GMT

"I'm alive!"
```

What stopped me there:

HTTP/2 and HTTP/1.1 both work on 2.7.4. The missing piece is only the official 2.8.1 bump. I did not open a lockfile PR because 2.8.0 has breaking changes that need a maintainer look (streaming backpressure + Linux `tcp_migrate_req` / multi-worker respawn), and because `.github/dependabot.yaml` currently watches GitHub Actions only, so Dependabot will not open this.

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

### LiteLLM is hiring a founding backend engineer, are you interested in joining us and shipping to all our users?

No
author: pamanseau

title: [Bug]: OAuth2 client_credentials MCP servers never receive client_id/client_secret at runtime — token endpoint always rejects with 400
body:
### What happened?

Registering an MCP server with `auth_type: oauth2` / `oauth2_flow: client_credentials` results in `tools/list` failing 100% of the time with:

```
misconfigured: OAuth2 client_credentials grant rejected: token endpoint returned HTTP 400
```

This happens **regardless of how the server is configured** — via the REST API (`POST /v1/mcp/server` with a nested `credentials: {client_id, client_secret}` object) or via `config.yaml`'s `mcp_servers:` block (with either `os.environ/VAR` or literal values). In every case the token endpoint (a real, independently-verified-working Keycloak `client_credentials` grant) rejects the request, which points to litellm sending an empty or malformed `client_id`/`client_secret`.

### Root cause (traced in source, not guessed)

1. **`LiteLLM_MCPServerTable` (`schema.prisma`) has no `client_id` / `client_secret` columns** — only an encrypted `credentials Json?` blob:

   ```prisma
   model LiteLLM_MCPServerTable {
     server_id    String  @id @default(uuid())
     ...
     credentials  Json?   @default("{}")
     ...
   }
   ```

2. The runtime OAuth2 resolver builds its config from **flat fields on the `MCPServer` Pydantic model**:

   `litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/outbound_credentials/adapter.py`:
   ```python
   config=ClientCredentialsConfig(
       client_id=server.client_id,
       client_secret=SecretStr(server.client_secret) if server.client_secret else None,
       token_url=server.token_url,
       ...
   )
   ```

3. **Nothing in the codebase ever copies the decrypted `credentials` blob into `server.client_id` / `server.client_secret`.** Searched the whole `mcp_server` package for any `client_id=<decrypted value>` assignment feeding into an `MCPServer(...)` construction used by the OAuth2 resolver — there is none. `decrypt_credentials()` is only used for master-key rotation (`rotate_mcp_server_credentials_master_key`) and DCR client storage, never to populate the resolver's config.

   Result: for any server persisted through the database (which is every server registered via the REST API, and — because `general_settings.store_model_in_db: true` is a very common production setting — effectively every `config.yaml`-defined server too), `server.client_id` / `server.client_secret` are **always `None`** at the point the token request is built. Keycloak (or any spec-compliant IdP) correctly returns `400 invalid_request`/`invalid_client` for a `client_credentials` grant with an empty `client_id`.

4. Separately, **`config.yaml`'s `mcp_servers:` loader does not resolve `os.environ/VAR`** for `client_id`/`client_secret`, unlike `model_list.litellm_params`:

   `litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/mcp_server_manager.py`:
   ```python
   client_id=server_config.get("client_id", None),
   client_secret=server_config.get("client_secret", None),
   ```
   This is a plain dict `.get()` — no `get_secret()` / env-var indirection. The [MCP OAuth docs](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/mcp_oauth) show `client_id: os.environ/MCP_CLIENT_ID` as the documented pattern, but it is silently taken as a literal string, so the literal text `os.environ/MCP_CLIENT_ID` gets sent to the token endpoint instead of the resolved secret.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Register (via REST API or `config.yaml`) an MCP server:
   ```yaml
   mcp_servers:
     my_server:
       url: "https://my-mcp-server.example.com/mcp"
       transport: http
       auth_type: oauth2
       oauth2_flow: client_credentials
       client_id: "<a real, working client_id>"
       client_secret: "<its real secret>"
       token_url: "https://idp.example.com/protocol/openid-connect/token"
   ```
2. Independently confirm the same `client_id`/`client_secret`/`token_url` succeed with a plain `curl -d grant_type=client_credentials&client_id=...&client_secret=...` — they do (200, valid token).
3. Call `tools/list` against the proxy's `/mcp/` endpoint for this server.
4. Observe `"status": "internal", "http_status": 500"` in `_meta.litellm.ai/server_outcomes`, and in the proxy logs:
   ```
   Failed to get tools from server my_server: 500: misconfigured: OAuth2 client_credentials grant rejected: token endpoint returned HTTP 400
   ```
5. Confirm the grant mechanics themselves are fine by calling litellm's own `_prepare_grant` / `post_client_credentials_grant` directly with the identical config object (bypassing the server-record load path) — this **succeeds** and returns a valid access token. The bug is specifically in how the persisted/config-loaded `MCPServer` record's credentials reach that function, not in the grant logic itself.

### Expected behavior

`client_id`/`client_secret` provided at registration time (via API `credentials` object or `config.yaml`, with or without `os.environ/` indirection) should reach the actual token request unchanged.

### Suggested fix

- Add `client_id`/`client_secret` columns to `LiteLLM_MCPServerTable` (or decrypt+unpack the `credentials` blob into the `MCPServer.client_id`/`client_secret` fields at every read path that feeds `_client_credentials_spec`), and/or
- Apply the same `get_secret()`/`os.environ/` resolution used for `model_list` to the `mcp_servers:` config.yaml loader for `client_id`, `client_secret`, and any other credential-shaped field.

### Environment

- **LiteLLM version**: `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:main-stable`, image pulled/deployed 2026-08-10 (prod) — well after the March 2026 fix for #24522, so this is not that issue.
- **What part of LiteLLM is this about?**: MCP Gateway / OAuth2 `client_credentials`
- Reproduced independently on two separate deployments (Azure Container Apps and an OpenShift-hosted instance with `store_model_in_db: true`), both via REST API registration and via `config.yaml`.

### Related issues

Not a duplicate of #24522 (concurrent stateless teardown — different traceback, different mechanism). Possibly related in spirit to #22755 ("Unable to list MCP tools with OAuth through the UI Dashboard", closed `not_planned`) and #15957, which describe the same outward symptom (OAuth-protected MCP tool listing fails) without this root cause having been identified.

---

## Bug 2: `true_passthrough`/`oauth_delegate` MCP sessions time out despite the upstream call itself completing in milliseconds

### What happened?

As an alternative to `client_credentials` (see Bug 1), we tested `auth_type: oauth_delegate` (`true_passthrough`), where litellm is supposed to forward the caller's own bearer token verbatim (via the `x-mcp-{alias}-authorization` header) instead of minting its own. `tools/list` against this server times out inside litellm.

### Root cause (traced in source)

- `litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/outbound_credentials/resolver.py`, `_passthrough(self, subject)` (~line 163) forwards `subject.inbound_token` verbatim to the upstream MCP server — this part is correct and matches the caller-supplied-credential design we wanted.
- `litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/mcp_server_manager.py` (~line 4200) wraps the actual `client.list_tools()` call in `anyio.fail_after(MCP_TOOL_LISTING_TIMEOUT)`. In our reproduction, this consistently fires before the upstream ever responds.
- We isolated the upstream call from litellm's session/connection handling entirely: a standalone script (`debug_passthrough.py`), running inside the same cluster network as litellm and using the same caller token forwarded the same way, hit the internal MCP URL directly and got back **`HTTP 200` in `0.04s`**. The upstream server, network path, and token are all fine — the timeout is happening somewhere in litellm's own MCP client/session plumbing between accepting the passthrough token and actually completing the `list_tools()` round trip.

### Expected behavior

`tools/list` over a `true_passthrough`/`oauth_delegate` MCP server should complete in roughly the same time as a direct call to the upstream (tens of milliseconds in our environment), not hit `MCP_TOOL_LISTING_TIMEOUT`.

### Environment

Same as Bug 1 (OpenShift-hosted litellm instance, `store_model_in_db: true`).

### Status

This is reported with less certainty than Bug 1 — we have not yet traced the exact point inside litellm's session/connection setup where the delay is introduced (as opposed to Bug 1, which we traced to an exact missing assignment). Flagging it here because it blocks the architecturally-preferred alternative to Bug 1.

---

## Bug 3: `client_credentials` grant requests every scope advertised by the realm's discovery document, instead of only the client's assigned scopes

### What happened?

With Bug 1's root cause fixed locally (server record correctly populated with a real, independently-verified-working `client_id`/`client_secret`), the *live* litellm instance's `client_credentials` requests to our IdP (Keycloak) still fail — but with a different, more specific error surfaced in the IdP's own audit log (not visible from litellm's side, only from the token endpoint's server-side logs):

```
error="invalid_request", reason="Invalid scopes: basic uma_protection Custom_Scope a2a-chat-ia-mcp-audience roles phone microprofile-jwt openid web-origins offline_access acr email service_account profile address", grant_type="client_credentials", client_auth_method="client-secret", username="service-account-<client>"
```

Client authentication itself **succeeds** here (Keycloak resolves the service-account user, confirming the secret is valid) — the request fails only because of the `scope` parameter litellm sends. The requested scope list is unusually large and includes scopes that are not, and could never sensibly be, assigned to this specific client (`microprofile-jwt`, `web-origins`, `acr`, several other realm-wide default/optional scopes). This looks like litellm is requesting the full `scopes_supported` list from the IdP's OIDC discovery document (`/.well-known/openid-configuration`) rather than a scope the operator configured (or no `scope` parameter at all, which is valid per RFC 6749 §4.4.2 and lets the IdP apply the client's default scopes).

### Expected behavior

The `client_credentials` grant should either omit `scope` entirely (letting the IdP apply the client's configured default scopes, which is spec-compliant and what a plain `curl` grant with no `scope` param does successfully against the same client/IdP), or send only an operator-configured scope list — never every scope advertised by discovery metadata.

### Environment

Same as Bug 1/2.

### Related issues

Not yet searched for a matching open issue — flagging here since it was discovered as a direct consequence of investigating Bug 1.

**Update: Bug 3 also breaks the interactive `authorization_code` flow, not just `client_credentials`**

Confirmed this is not specific to `client_credentials`. Registering a second server with `oauth2_flow: authorization_code` (same `client_id`, plus an `issuer` so LiteLLM does RFC 8414 discovery instead of using manually-set `authorization_url`/`token_url`) and hitting LiteLLM's own `/{server_name}/authorize` endpoint produces a `307` redirect to the IdP's `/auth` endpoint whose `scope` query param is the **exact same** full discovery scope list:

```
Invalid scopes: basic uma_protection Custom_Scope a2a-chat-ia-mcp-audience roles phone microprofile-jwt openid web-origins offline_access acr email service_account profile address
```

i.e. once `issuer` is set for discovery, LiteLLM builds this over-broad `scope` value for **every** OAuth2 flow it drives (both the M2M token request and the interactive `/authorize` redirect), not just `client_credentials`. Same root cause, hits both the token-request call site and the `/authorize` redirect builder.

This was confirmed via a real interactive login attempt — the actual Keycloak login page itself surfaces `Invalid scopes` (same string as the token-endpoint audit log entry seen with `client_credentials`), which rules out this being a `client_credentials`-only or backend-log-only artifact.

author: armando-sepulveda

title: [Bug]: Batch spend is permanently lost when a client status poll records the terminal state before the batch cost job's next cycle
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

Closest neighbors, neither a duplicate: #37156 covers the cost poller retiring terminal batches unbilled when the poller itself sees the terminal transition (fixed by #37205), and #37153 covered the stale sweep's handling of completed unprocessed rows. This issue is the remaining ordering: the client sees the terminal transition first

### What happened?

When a client polls GET /v1/batches/{batch_id} through the proxy while waiting for a cancelled or failed batch to finalize, the proxy records the provider's terminal status the moment the client sees it. The background batch cost job skips batches already recorded as cancelled or failed, so it never revisits that batch and the spend for its completed requests is never written

PR #37205 makes the cost job bill any terminal batch with an output file, but only when the job notices the terminal transition itself. A polling client (the normal OpenAI SDK pattern) checks every few seconds while the job's default interval is one hour, so the client effectively always stamps the terminal status first and the spend is still lost. In the reproduction below the job's last look at the batch was 9 seconds before the provider finalized; the client's next poll landed first, and nine subsequent job cycles plus a full proxy restart never billed the 86 completed requests

Expected: the completed portion of a cancelled or failed batch is billed regardless of whether the client or the background job sees the terminal status first

### User Flow

Before a (hypothetical) fix: a developer cancels an in-progress batch and polls it through the gateway until it finalizes; the gateway serves the partial results but never records any spend for them

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files with purpose=batch and target_model_names to upload their requests JSONL
2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches with the returned input_file_id and the batch starts at the provider
3. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id}/cancel and get HTTP 200; the batch shows status cancelling while in-flight requests keep completing
4. They poll GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id} every few seconds, the way the OpenAI SDK polling helpers do; about 25 minutes later a poll returns status cancelled with a populated output_file_id and request_counts.completed 86
5. GET https://litellm-domain/v1/files/{output_file_id}/content returns HTTP 200 with 86 result lines carrying real token usage
6. GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs?request_id={batch_id} shows only the $0 batch-creation row and GET https://litellm-domain/key/info shows spend 0.0, permanently: hours of cost-job cycles and even a gateway restart never bill it

After a (hypothetical) fix: the same polled batch is billed for its completed work within one cost-job cycle

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files with purpose=batch and target_model_names to upload their requests JSONL
2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches with the returned input_file_id and the batch starts at the provider
3. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id}/cancel and get HTTP 200; the batch shows status cancelling while in-flight requests keep completing
4. They poll GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id} every few seconds; about 25 minutes later a poll returns status cancelled with a populated output_file_id and non-zero request_counts.completed
5. GET https://litellm-domain/v1/files/{output_file_id}/content returns HTTP 200 with the completed result lines
6. Within one cost-job cycle GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs?request_id={batch_id} gains a batch-retrieval row with the real cost and token counts of those completed requests, and GET https://litellm-domain/key/info shows the matching non-zero spend

### Proof the bug occurs

Config / setup the proxy ran with:

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: gpt-5.4-mini-batch
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-5.4-mini
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY
    model_info:
      mode: batch
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
```

Env: `LITELLM_LICENSE` set (the batch cost job is enterprise), `PROXY_BATCH_POLLING_INTERVAL=120` (short enough to observe many job cycles; the default 3600 makes the race even more certain), fresh Postgres DB

Version or commit: `b34cbb18e2` (the tip of PR #37205's branch, so the #37156 fix is already included; the base branch without #37205 loses the spend on every ordering, not just this one)

Commands and their full output (key redacted; live proxy on localhost:49726, real OpenAI batch API):

1. Create a key with a user_id, upload a 2000-request JSONL, create the batch:
   ```bash
   KEY=$(curl -s http://localhost:49726/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"key_alias":"lit5663-clobber","user_id":"lit5663-user","models":["gpt-5.4-mini-batch"]}' | jq -r .key)
   FILE=$(curl -s http://localhost:49726/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -F purpose=batch -F 'target_model_names=gpt-5.4-mini-batch' -F file=@cancelleg2.jsonl | jq -r .id)
   BATCH=$(curl -s http://localhost:49726/v1/batches -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"input_file_id\":\"$FILE\",\"endpoint\":\"/v1/chat/completions\",\"completion_window\":\"24h\"}" | jq -r .id)
   ```
2. Poll `GET /v1/batches/$BATCH` through the proxy every 2-3 s (the SDK pattern). At the first in_progress poll with completed 32, cancel through the proxy: `curl -s -X POST "http://localhost:49726/v1/batches/$BATCH/cancel" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"` returns HTTP 200 with status cancelling
3. Keep polling; ~25 min later (provider batch_6a836d8e1c30819090dd7133000d6a6f, cancelled_at 14:08:31 PDT) the first cancelled poll shows `"status": "cancelled"`, a populated output_file_id, `"request_counts": {"total": 2000, "completed": 86, "failed": 0}`
4. `GET /v1/files/{output_file_id}/content` returns HTTP 200 with 86 JSONL result lines totaling 1634 prompt + 344 completion = 1978 tokens of real completed work
5. Across six cost-job cycles: `curl -s "http://localhost:49726/spend/logs?request_id=$BATCH" -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER"` shows only the $0 `acreate_batch` row, `spend/logs?request_id=${BATCH}_batch_cost` returns `[]`, and `/key/info` reports `"spend": 0.0`
6. Restarting the proxy on the same DB and waiting three more cycles changes nothing: still no `aretrieve_batch` row, key spend still 0.0. The exclusion is durable state, not a warm-cache artifact

Timing detail from the proxy log: the cost job examined this batch on every one of its 22 cycles while the batch was non-terminal (last at 14:08:25), the client's poll recorded cancelling -> cancelled at 14:08:34, and none of the nine subsequent cycles examined the batch again

### What a fix PR should look like

Two workable shapes, either is fine:

- Include provider-terminal statuses in the cost job's pickup so a row stamped cancelled/failed with an output file and not yet billed still gets billed once. This needs an upgrade guard (for example a created_at cutoff) so pre-existing terminal rows from before the fix do not get retroactively billed as one spike on deploy, and it should mind the poll-page slots (MAX_OBJECTS_PER_POLL_CYCLE) so old rows cannot starve new ones
- Alternatively, keep the retrieve/cancel path from stamping a terminal status onto a not-yet-billed row (stamp it only once spend has been written, letting the cost job see the transition itself)

The regression test belongs in tests/proxy_unit_tests/test_check_batch_cost.py: simulate the retrieve-first ordering (row already carrying the provider's terminal status, batch_processed false, output file present) and assert the job still bills it exactly once

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

litellm_internal_staging @ f04b1dad plus PR #37205 (b34cbb18e2)
author: mateo-berri

title: No renewal path when an upstream grant has neither expires_in nor refresh_token
body:
## Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

## The Feature

When an upstream token response carries neither `expires_in` nor `refresh_token`:

- the access envelope gets `MAX_ENVELOPE_TTL_SECONDS` (3600), since
  `_envelope_ttl_seconds(None)` returns the cap, and
- no refresh envelope is minted, because `discoverable_endpoints.py` skips that
  step when the response has no `refresh_token`.

The result is that the client has no renewal path at all. Recovery is a full
interactive `authorization_code` flow, roughly every hour, for the lifetime of
the integration.

Some providers issue access tokens that do not expire, and signal that by omitting
`expires_in`. Nothing on the wire distinguishes this from "expires, lifetime
unstated", so the gateway assumes the latter. We are not asking it to assume
otherwise. The problem is what happens next: for this shape of grant there is no
bounded renewal mechanism, only re-authorization.

Two mechanisms already exist and neither reaches this case.

**The upstream 401 relay.** For `is_oauth_delegate` servers,
`mcp_server_manager` relays an upstream 401 as `MCPUpstreamAuthError` so callers
turn it into a 401 with the upstream's own `WWW-Authenticate` and re-run the OAuth
flow. The comment states the intent: only a 401 is a re-auth signal, and it is the
caller's to resolve. That is the right design, but the access envelope's own `exp`
fires first, so the upstream is never asked and the relay never runs. The gateway's
locally chosen expiry pre-empts the provider's own answer.

**The refresh envelope.** #32980 added refresh envelopes and scoped them to grants
returning a `refresh_token`:

> A new refresh envelope is re-issued only when the upstream returns a new refresh token, so the design mirrors the upstream authorization server's own rotation policy rather than reinventing it: against a rotating upstream the client rotates and the upstream detects reuse of a retired token; against a non-rotating upstream the original refresh envelope stands until its bounded TTL.

That covers a non-rotating upstream, which keeps its refresh envelope for the
14-day bound. It does not cover an upstream that returns no refresh token at all,
which gets no envelope and therefore no bound other than the 1h access cap.

We are not asking for the access cap to be raised or removed. The constant's own
docstring anticipates that argument and rejects it:

> Hard ceiling on ACCESS envelope lifetime [...] matching the 1h lifetime of the
> BYOK session bearer this module's signing approach is borrowed from: a client-held
> credential should never outlive a bounded window even when the upstream token does.

We think that is correct. The cap does not bound the provider's token, it bounds
the client-held bearer, and its value is that a leaked envelope dies on its own
without requiring the principal's access to be revoked wholesale. "The provider
says the token does not expire" is not an answer to envelope theft. Nor would
dropping the expiry work mechanically, since `exp` is a required claim on open.

Give this grant shape the same treatment the 14-day refresh bound already
represents: when the upstream returns neither `expires_in` nor `refresh_token`,
mint a refresh envelope sealing the access token, and let the `refresh_token`
grant re-mint a fresh 1h access envelope from the sealed grant.

This seems to fit the reasoning already documented on
`MAX_REFRESH_ENVELOPE_TTL_SECONDS`:

> A refresh envelope only renews the short-lived access envelope, and each renewal re-validates the sealed litellm key (revocation gates it) and is re-minted with a fresh window, so the practical bound is idle time, not a fixed session.

Both properties hold here. The credential is presented only back to the token
endpoint rather than held as a bearer for upstream calls, and each renewal
re-validates the sealed identity. The 1h client-held access cap is untouched,
revocation still gates every renewal, and hourly interactive re-authorization
becomes a 14-day idle bound.

One honest caveat: the current refresh path unwraps the sealed refresh token and
POSTs `grant_type=refresh_token` upstream, so this needs a distinct arm that
re-mints from the sealed grant without an upstream call, not a straight reuse of
the existing flow.

A per-server override for the access cap would also solve our immediate problem
and is a smaller change, since `MAX_ENVELOPE_TTL_SECONDS` is read only by
`envelope.py` and has no config field or environment variable today. We suggest it
second because it needs an operator to declare provider behavior correctly, and
because it weakens the client-held-bearer bound that the docstring above is
protecting. If you did prefer this shape, `MAX_REFRESH_ENVELOPE_TTL_SECONDS` is a
same-shaped sibling that an override should probably cover too.

Happy to send a PR for either direction.

## User Flow

Before this feature (today):

- Someone authorizes an MCP server once through the gateway and starts working.
- Roughly an hour later the credential is gone. There is no renewal path, so the
  only way back is the full interactive authorization flow.
- That repeats every hour, for as long as they use the integration.

After this feature:

- Someone authorizes once. Renewal happens against the token endpoint without
  their involvement.
- Interactive re-authorization is needed only after a long idle period, bounded by
  the existing 14-day refresh window, rather than hourly.

## How far you got

Config / setup the proxy ran with:

```yaml
mcp_servers:
  example_server:
    url: https://mcp.example.com/mcp
    transport: http
    auth_type: oauth_delegate
    dcr_bridge: true
```

Version or commit:

1.97.0

Commands and their full output, up to the step that dead-ends:

Complete the DCR flow against the server above, against an upstream whose token
response includes neither `expires_in` nor `refresh_token`. The token response
returns an access envelope and no `refresh_token` field. There is no further
command to run: no refresh grant exists to renew with, so the flow dead-ends at
re-authorization once the access envelope reaches its `exp`.

What stopped me there:

The client has no renewal path and must repeat the interactive `authorization_code` flow roughly every hour.

## What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

title: Bridge envelope admission returns a bare 401 where the gateway session path returns an invalid_token challenge
body:
## Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

## What happened?

`MCPRequestHandler` has two admission arms for a cryptographically valid
credential that can no longer be admitted, for example because it has expired.
They handle the same condition differently.

`_admit_gateway_session` fails closed with an RFC 9728 challenge via
`_gateway_dcr_challenge`, including RFC 6750 `error="invalid_token"` when a bearer
was presented. Its own comment explains why:

> A cryptographically valid bearer whose referenced user is now missing or SCIM-deactivated is an invalid_token at the requested scope: relay the RFC 9728 challenge so the DCR client re-authorizes, matching the SessionBearerInvalid arm, instead of a bare 401 with no WWW-Authenticate.

`_admit_dcr_bridge_delegate`, in the same class, raises
`HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="Invalid or expired credential")` on its
`BridgeEnvelopeInvalid() | NotBridgeEnvelope()` arm. No `WWW-Authenticate` header,
so it never reaches the challenge helper that the sibling arm uses.

Without a challenge a client has no machine-readable signal telling it where to
re-authorize, so recovery has to be driven by hand even though the client is
capable of re-running the flow.

This also seems inconsistent with the mode's own intent. For
`is_oauth_delegate` servers, `mcp_server_manager` already relays an upstream 401
as `MCPUpstreamAuthError` specifically so callers can turn it into a 401 with the
upstream's `WWW-Authenticate` and re-run the OAuth flow, and `server.py` converts
that to a 401 preserving the challenge. So challenge-driven re-authorization is
the intended recovery path for this mode. The envelope admission arm is the one
place in that chain that drops it.

Three merged PRs have closed the same kind of gap in neighboring paths: #30124
(surface upstream challenges for delegated OAuth), #31921 (surface `tools/list`
auth failures as a 401 challenge on single-server routes), and #32741 (surface
rejected delegate-auth upstream tokens as a connect-time 401, whose verification
output shows the `error="invalid_token"` challenge being relayed). The bridge
envelope arm arrived with #32824 and did not get the same treatment, so this looks
like an oversight rather than a deliberate exception.

Related but distinct: #36358 reports a different defect in the same bridge mode,
where the injected upstream credential is discarded on tool calls. That one is
about egress after a successful admission. This one is about the response when
admission fails.

## User Flow

Before:

- Someone uses an MCP client that connects through the proxy. Their credential
  eventually reaches its expiry.
- The next request fails with a 401 that carries no challenge, so the client has no
  way to discover where to re-authorize. It surfaces a generic failure instead.
- The person has to work out for themselves that re-authorization is what is
  needed, then re-run the login by hand.

After:

- The 401 carries a challenge, so the client discovers the authorization server and
  re-runs the flow.
- The person either keeps working or is prompted once by their client, rather than
  diagnosing an opaque error.

## Proof the bug occurs

Config / setup the proxy ran with:

```yaml
mcp_servers:
  example_server:
    url: https://mcp.example.com/mcp
    transport: http
    auth_type: oauth_delegate
    dcr_bridge: true
```

Version or commit:

1.97.0

Commands and their full output:

1. Configure an MCP server in `dcr_bridge` + `oauth_delegate` mode and complete
   the DCR flow so the client holds an access envelope.
2. Wait for the envelope to pass its `exp`, or tamper with it.
3. Send any request to the server's MCP route with that envelope as the bearer.

Observed: `401` with body `{"detail":"Invalid or expired credential"}` and no
`WWW-Authenticate` response header.

Expected: `401` carrying a `WWW-Authenticate` challenge, as the gateway session
path returns for the equivalent condition. Concretely,
`_admit_dcr_bridge_delegate` would emit an `invalid_token` challenge on an expired
or otherwise unusable envelope, matching `_admit_gateway_session`.

Scope note: this would fix the REST and connect-time paths. It would not by itself help a
tool call that fails mid-session, because as `server.py` notes, the MCP session
manager serializes handler exceptions as JSON-RPC errors, so a mid-session tool
call cannot emit a raw 401 with a `WWW-Authenticate` header and degrades to an
`isError` result instead. That looks like a separate limitation rather than part
of this inconsistency.

Happy to send a PR if the direction is agreeable.

title: [Bug]: POST /reload/model_cost_map is not reliably propagated to all proxy replicas
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

`POST /reload/model_cost_map` does not reliably propagate a refreshed model-cost map to every LiteLLM Proxy replica.

In a three-replica deployment, calling **Reload Price Data** through the load-balanced Admin UI caused `/model/info` to alternate between old and new metadata. Twenty identical requests returned the stale value 17 times and the refreshed value 3 times.

This can make model capability metadata, token limits, and pricing depend on which replica serves a request. Clients that cache `/model/info` can then retain stale capabilities after hitting an outdated replica.

The implementation appears to use a lossy shared boolean as an event:

1. The endpoint refreshes the serving process's `litellm.model_cost` and writes `force_reload: true` to `model_cost_map_reload_config`.
2. Background polling processes observe that flag.
3. The first process that consumes it reloads its local map and writes `force_reload: false`.
4. Replicas that poll afterward see `false` and remain stale.

If DB model synchronization is disabled, the other replicas do not consume the flag at all. Redis does not distribute `litellm.model_cost`; the map remains process-local.

Expected behavior: after a successful manual reload, every running proxy replica should converge on the same model-cost-map generation.

This is separate from the custom-pricing defects tracked in #30081, although its production report independently notes the same multi-replica behavior: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/30081#issuecomment-5030843840

The multi-pod reload feature was introduced by #13470: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/13470

A durable implementation could store a monotonically increasing reload generation in shared storage. Each process would retain its last applied generation and reload whenever the shared generation is newer, without any process clearing the event for the others.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run LiteLLM Proxy with at least three replicas sharing the same database and with `STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True`.
2. Set `LITELLM_MODEL_COST_MAP_URL` to a controllable valid model-cost-map URL and start all replicas with version A of that map.
3. Publish version B at the same URL with a recognizable metadata change.
4. Call `POST /reload/model_cost_map` once through the load-balanced Service, or use **Reload Price Data** in the Admin UI.
5. Wait longer than the background polling interval.
6. Query each pod directly using `/public/litellm_model_cost_map` or authenticated `/model/info`.
7. Observe that only the serving pod and, depending on polling order, at most one additional pod has version B. At least one replica can remain on version A.

The same problem is even more direct with `STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=False`: only the serving process reloads.

### Relevant log output

```shell
requests 1-17: supports_reasoning = null
request 18:    supports_reasoning = true
request 19:    supports_reasoning = null
request 20:    supports_reasoning = true
```

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

v1.95.0

title: CustomStreamWrapper erases the remembered model when an Azure chunk carries model=None
body:
## Summary

In `litellm/litellm_core_utils/streaming_handler.py`, the Azure branch of
`chunk_creator` does:

```python
if isinstance(chunk, BaseModel) and hasattr(chunk, "model"):
    # for azure, we need to pass the model from the original chunk
    self.model = getattr(chunk, "model", self.model)
```

The `getattr` default only applies when the attribute is **missing**. When the attribute
exists and is `None` — which is what the Responses-API bridge produces — `self.model` is
overwritten with `None`, discarding the request model the wrapper stored at construction.
The comment states the intent is to *pass along* the model; the effect is to erase it.

## Impact

Every downstream consumer that reads the model from the stream loses it. In our case
(Google ADK + LiteLLM against Azure OpenAI), `LlmResponse.model_version` became `None`, the
field was dropped by `exclude_none` when the SSE event was serialized, and 100% of token
usage in our evaluation runs was recorded as unattributed — so per-model cost and
attribution silently stopped working. Nothing errors; the numbers just quietly lose their
label.

## Reproduction

Any deployment routed through the Responses bridge shows it. With LiteLLM 1.84.x:

```python
import asyncio
from litellm import acompletion

async def main():
    stream = await acompletion(
        model="azure/<a gpt-5.6 deployment>",
        api_key=..., api_base=..., api_version="<a Responses-capable version>",
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with OK."}],
        # tools + reasoning_effort together are what select the Responses bridge
        tools=[{"type": "function", "function": {
            "name": "unused", "description": "unused",
            "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {}}}}],
        reasoning_effort="medium",
        stream=True, stream_options={"include_usage": True},
    )
    async for chunk in stream:
        print(repr(getattr(chunk, "model", "<ABSENT>")))

asyncio.run(main())
```

Observed: every chunk prints `None`. The equivalent non-streaming call returns a populated
`model`, because the non-streaming Responses transformer sets it from the request.

## Suggested fix

Guard on truthiness rather than attribute presence, so a null chunk model leaves the
remembered request model intact:

```python
chunk_model = getattr(chunk, "model", None)
if chunk_model:
    self.model = chunk_model
```

Alternatively (or additionally), have the Responses→chat translator propagate the
request/response model onto every `ModelResponseStream` it emits. The guard above is the
smaller and more general correction, since it also protects any other provider path that
emits a null model on a chunk.

## Environment

- litellm 1.84.x (pinned range `>=1.84.0,<1.85.0`)
- Provider: Azure OpenAI, `azure/` prefix, Responses-API bridge selected by tools +
  `reasoning_effort`
- Consumer: google-adk 1.33.0 (`LiteLlm.generate_content_async`, streaming branch)
