title: [Bug]: Ollama: get_runtime_model_info ignores the request's api_base and falls back to localhost:11434, adding ~8s of silent connect timeouts per completion
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

### What happens

Every `litellm.completion()` against an Ollama server on a non-default host pays
**two ~4s TCP connect timeouts before the model is ever asked anything.** The
failure is swallowed by a bare `except`, so it does not surface as an error — it
looks like a slow model.

`completion(model="ollama/...", api_base="http://my-host:30000", ...)` sends the
*completion* to the right host, but the model-info lookup on the same code path
resolves its own host independently:

```
litellm/main.py:5155      responses_api_bridge_check(...)
  -> utils.py             _get_model_info_helper(...)
    -> ollama/common_utils.py:219  OllamaModelInfo.get_model_info(...)
      -> ollama/common_utils.py:170  get_runtime_model_info(model, api_base=None)
```

`get_runtime_model_info` is called without the `api_base` the caller supplied,
so it falls through to the default (`common_utils.py:72`):

```python
@staticmethod
def get_api_base(api_base: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
    # env var OLLAMA_API_BASE or default
    return api_base or get_secret_str("OLLAMA_API_BASE") or "http://localhost:11434"
```

With nothing listening on `localhost:11434`, the POST to `/api/show` waits out
the connect timeout and raises, and `common_utils.py:191` turns that into a
silent default:

```python
except Exception:
    verbose_logger.debug("OllamaError: Could not get model info.")
    return { ... }
```

`verbose_logger.debug` means nothing is visible at default log levels.

### Measured

Ollama on `my-host:30000`; nothing on `localhost:11434`. One structured
completion, instrumented by wrapping `litellm.module_level_client.post`:

```
POST http://localhost:11434/api/show        -> ConnectError in 4.079s
POST http://localhost:11434/api/show        -> ConnectError in 4.066s
POST http://my-host:30000/api/show  -> 200 in 0.563s   <- the real one
```

Six of those on the first call in a process, two on every call after.
Per-call wall clock, mean of 5 warm reps:

|                               | without`OLLAMA_API_BASE` | with it          |
| ----------------------------- | -------------------------- | ---------------- |
| total                         | **10.37 s**          | **1.41 s** |
| ...of which generation        | 2.26 s                     | 1.30 s           |
| ...of which model-info lookup | **8.11 s**           | 0.10 s           |

The server is not slow — the same `/api/show` answers `curl` in **0.09 s**. The
8.11 s is entirely waiting on a host that is not there.

### Reproduce

Any machine with Ollama on a non-default host and **nothing** on
`localhost:11434`:

```python
import time, litellm

litellm.module_level_client.post = (
    lambda _p=litellm.module_level_client.post, *a, **kw: (
        print("POST", kw.get("url")), _p(*a, **kw))[1]
)

began = time.perf_counter()
litellm.completion(
    model="ollama/<your-model>",
    api_base="http://<your-ollama-host>:<port>",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}],
)
print(f"{time.perf_counter() - began:.2f}s")
```

Expected: one POST, to your host. Actual: three, two of them to
`localhost:11434`, and ~8s of the total spent failing to reach it.

Setting `OLLAMA_API_BASE` to the same value as `api_base` works around it
completely.

### Why this is worth fixing rather than documenting

1. **It is silent.** A bare `except` plus a `debug`-level log means the only
   symptom is latency, attributed to the model. It took a profiler to find —
   named timers around `litellm.completion` cannot see it, because it happens
   *inside* that call.
2. **`api_base` was supplied.** The caller did say where the server is; that
   value simply is not threaded to the lookup. This is not a missing
   configuration so much as configuration being dropped one frame down.
3. **The cost is disproportionate.** ~8s of dead time added to a ~2s generation
   is a 5x slowdown, and it scales with the number of calls — an agent loop
   making six phase calls per run pays it six times.

### The per-call path is a 4-line fix, and I have tested it

Everything below `responses_api_bridge_check` already accepts and forwards
`api_base` — `_get_model_info_helper` (`utils.py:5228`),
`OllamaModelInfo.get_model_info` (`common_utils.py:221`) and
`get_runtime_model_info` (`common_utils.py:172`) all take it. The only break is
the top frame, which neither accepts it nor passes it on, even though
`completion()` has it in scope at both call sites.

```diff
--- a/litellm/main.py
+++ b/litellm/main.py
@@ def responses_api_bridge_check(
 def responses_api_bridge_check(
     model: str,
     custom_llm_provider: str,
+    api_base: Optional[str] = None,
     web_search_options: Optional[OpenAIWebSearchOptions] = None,
     tools: Optional[List[Any]] = None,
@@ (inside responses_api_bridge_check)
         model_info = cast(
             dict,
-            _get_model_info_helper(model=model, custom_llm_provider=custom_llm_provider),
+            _get_model_info_helper(
+                model=model,
+                custom_llm_provider=custom_llm_provider,
+                api_base=api_base,
+            ),
         )
@@ main.py:5155 (completion)
         responses_api_model_info, model = responses_api_bridge_check(
             model=model,
             custom_llm_provider=custom_llm_provider,
+            api_base=api_base,
             web_search_options=web_search_options,
         )
@@ main.py:5391 (the second, later check)
             responses_api_model_info, model = responses_api_bridge_check(
                 model=model,
                 custom_llm_provider=custom_llm_provider,
+                api_base=api_base,
                 web_search_options=web_search_options,
```

Backwards compatible: the new parameter is optional and keyword-only in
practice, and `responses_api_bridge_check` has no callers outside `main.py`.

**Measured with that patch applied and `OLLAMA_API_BASE` deliberately unset**,
so only the patch can help:

```
rep 1  15.51s   (4 remaining localhost timeouts — see below)
rep 2   1.44s   all POSTs to the configured host
rep 3   1.06s   all POSTs to the configured host
```

### A second, separate path — cold start only

The four timeouts left in rep 1 come from somewhere else, and they are
`lru_cache`d so they only cost once per process:

```
cost_calculator.py:654  cost_per_token
  -> utils.py:5175      _cached_get_model_info_helper(model=..., custom_llm_provider=...)
    -> _get_model_info_helper -> ollama get_model_info(api_base=None)
```

`_cached_get_model_info_helper` accepts `api_base` too, but `cost_per_token`
has no `api_base` in scope to give it — the cost calculator is reached from the
logging layer with a response object rather than the request's kwargs. Threading
it there is a real change rather than a 1-line one, which is why I have split
it out. Its cost is bounded (~16s once per process, not per call), so the 4-line
patch above is the part that matters for throughput.

### Suggested fixes, roughly in order of preference

1. **Thread `api_base` through** — the 4-line patch above, which covers the
   per-call path. Happy to open it as a PR if that is useful.
2. **Do not silently swallow a connection failure.** Even keeping the fallback
   dict, `verbose_logger.warning` (not `debug`) with the URL and the elapsed
   time would have made this self-diagnosing.
3. **Cache the lookup per `(model, api_base)`.** Two identical `/api/show`
   requests per completion is wasteful even when the host is right — a warm
   run still spends ~0.10s per completion re-fetching immutable metadata.
4. **Short-circuit the fallback host.** If `api_base` was explicitly supplied
   for the completion and the lookup is about to use a *different* host, that is
   almost certainly not intended.

### Environment

- litellm 1.95.0
- instructor 1.15.4 (present, but not implicated — reproduces with plain
  `litellm.completion`)
- Python 3.14.3, Windows
- Ollama on a remote host, non-default port
[issue.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31105485/issue.md)



### User Flow

What happens
Every litellm.completion() against an Ollama server on a non-default host pays two ~4s TCP connect timeouts before the model is ever asked anything. The failure is swallowed by a bare except, so it does not surface as an error — it looks like a slow model.

### Proof the bug occurs

### Reproduce
Any machine with Ollama on a non-default host and nothing on localhost:11434
```
import time, litellm

litellm.module_level_client.post = (
    lambda _p=litellm.module_level_client.post, *a, **kw: (
        print("POST", kw.get("url")), _p(*a, **kw))[1]
)

began = time.perf_counter()
litellm.completion(
    model="ollama/<your-model>",
    api_base="http://<your-ollama-host>:<port>",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}],
)
print(f"{time.perf_counter() - began:.2f}s")
```


### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

SDK (litellm Python package)

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

litellm 1.95.0

title: [Bug]: chatgpt/* non-streaming chat completions fail with "Unknown items in responses API response: []" (streaming works)
body:
## Summary

For `chatgpt/*` routes using an existing valid ChatGPT OAuth `auth.json`, non-streaming chat completions regress after LiteLLM 1.88.1, while streaming continues to work.

The failure is reproducible on the same route, same auth, same prompt, and same container; changing only `stream=false` to `stream=true` changes the result.

## Version matrix

| LiteLLM version | `stream=false` | `stream=true` |
|---|---|---|
| 1.88.1 | PASS | PASS, but retry/fallback accounting headers are absent |
| 1.91.0 | FAIL | PASS |
| 1.96.2 | FAIL | PASS |

For 1.91.0 and 1.96.2, the non-streaming failure is:

```text
ChatgptException: Unknown items in responses API response: []
```

No 401/403 or token error is observed; authentication succeeds and the provider is reached.

## Minimal reproducer

Use a single model group backed by `chatgpt/gpt-5.4` with a valid OAuth `auth.json` exposed via `CHATGPT_TOKEN_DIR`, then send the same prompt twice:

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: repro-chatgpt
    litellm_params:
      model: chatgpt/gpt-5.4
```

Request 1:

```json
{
  "model": "repro-chatgpt",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply exactly: AUTH OK"}],
  "stream": false,
  "max_tokens": 16
}
```

Request 2: identical except:

```json
"stream": true
```

Observed on 1.96.2:

- `stream=false`: fails with `Unknown items in responses API response: []`
- `stream=true`: succeeds and returns the expected assistant content

The same split reproduces with `max_tokens` 16, 128, 256, and 1024, so this does not appear to be an output-budget issue.

## Additional observations

On 1.96.2, the streaming path is otherwise healthy:

- incremental SSE works
- usage is returned with `stream_options.include_usage`
- `x-litellm-attempted-retries` is present
- `x-litellm-attempted-fallbacks` is present
- tool-call streaming completes successfully

A controlled retry reports `x-litellm-attempted-retries: 1`, and a controlled fallback reports `x-litellm-attempted-fallbacks: 1`, so the accounting values reflect actual routing behavior.

## Suspected area

The observable exception comes from the non-streaming Responses transformation path in:

```text
litellm/completion_extras/litellm_responses_transformation/transformation.py
```

The relevant path converts `raw_response.output` to chat-completion choices and raises when no recognized output items can be recovered.

The check itself also exists in 1.88.1, where the same request succeeds. The regression therefore appears to be that `output_items` reaches this transform empty and recovery no longer reconstructs the provider response.

### Hypothesis, not confirmed root cause

The ChatGPT backend may still deliver the payload in an SSE-like form for this path, with non-streaming behavior depending on recovery from the raw/logged response. If that recovery stopped receiving or reconstructing the raw output after 1.88.1, it would explain why streaming remains healthy while non-streaming fails.

This is only a hypothesis; the reproducible version split and stream/non-stream behavior above are the measured facts.

## Expected behavior

The same `chatgpt/*` route and OAuth authentication should work for both streaming and non-streaming requests, as it does in LiteLLM 1.88.1.

author: icsy7867

title: [Bug]: MCP auto-execute (require_approval "never") hijacks client-side tool_use from agentic clients like Claude Code, breaking all non-MCP tools with "Error executing tool"
body:
## What happened?

A model configured with an MCP tool reference using `require_approval: "never"` (so the proxy auto-executes it server-side) is deployed behind an agentic client that sends its own tools in the same request, such as Claude Code sending Read/Bash/Edit. The auto-execute loop takes over the entire tool_use turn and tries to execute every tool_use block the model emits, including the client's own non-MCP tools. Those tools are not in the MCP server map, so the proxy raises a KeyError that gets swallowed into `Error executing tool: '<tool_name>'` and fed back to the model. The model retries, fails again, and eventually gives up. From the client's perspective all of its native tools (Read, Bash, etc.) are broken for any request routed to that model

What I expected: when `require_approval: "never"` is set, the proxy should auto-execute only the MCP tools it injected. A tool_use whose name does not resolve to a known MCP server should be passed through to the client unchanged so the client can execute it locally, the way a normal tool_use turn works when no MCP tool is present

## User Flow

Before a fix

1. A user creates a virtual key and a team in the LiteLLM proxy UI, then registers an HTTP MCP server (say `image_understand`) and grants the team access to it
2. The user attaches the MCP tool to a model via the model's LiteLLM Params, e.g. `{"tools": [{"type": "mcp", "server_url": "litellm_proxy/mcp/image_understand", "require_approval": "never"}]}`
3. The user points an agentic client (Claude Code) at `POST /v1/messages` on the proxy, using that model and that virtual key. The client sends its own tools (Read, Bash, Edit, ...) alongside whatever the proxy injects
4. The model decides to call Read on a local file. The proxy's auto-execute loop intercepts that tool_use, fails with `Error executing tool: 'Read'`, and returns the error text to the model instead of handing the tool_use back to the client
5. The model retries with Bash, gets `Error executing tool: 'Bash'`, and eventually stops with a message saying the tools are unavailable. The user sees tool call failures and the client's native tooling is dead for that model

After a fix

1. Same setup as above: MCP server registered, team granted access, MCP tool attached to the model with `require_approval: "never"`
2. The user points Claude Code at `POST /v1/messages` with that model and key, sending its own tools
3. The model calls Read on a local file. The proxy recognizes Read is not one of its MCP tools, returns the tool_use block to the client in the response, and lets the client execute it locally
4. When the model calls the injected MCP tool (`image_understand`), the proxy auto-executes it server-side as before and feeds the result back
5. Both the client's native tools and the injected MCP tool work in the same turn

## Proof the bug occurs

I verified the root cause by reading the current main branch (v1.98.0-dev.2). I was not able to capture a full Claude Code trace against my own proxy in time for this report, so the proof below is the code path plus the user-visible symptom. I can add a full end-to-end curl reproduction if the maintainers want one

Config / setup: a model with an MCP tool attached via LiteLLM Params

```json
{"tools": [{"type": "mcp", "server_url": "litellm_proxy/mcp/image_understand", "require_approval": "never"}]}
```

Version or commit: v1.98.0-dev.2 on main

Commands and their full output

The auto-execute loop in `litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/messages/mcp_handler.py` extracts every tool_use block without checking whether it belongs to an MCP server

```
# line 38-40
def _extract_tool_use_blocks(response):
    return tuple(block for block in _get_response_content(response) if block.get("type") == "tool_use")

# line 139-158 (abridged)
for _ in range(MAX_MCP_TOOL_USE_ITERATIONS):
    if _get_stop_reason(response) != "tool_use":
        break
    tool_use_blocks = _extract_tool_use_blocks(response)
    if not tool_use_blocks:
        break
    tool_results = await LiteLLM_Proxy_MCP_Handler._execute_tool_calls(
        tool_server_map=tool_server_map,
        tool_calls=list(tool_use_blocks),
        ...
    )
```

`tool_server_map` is built only from the injected MCP tools (in `_process_mcp_tools_without_openai_transform`). When `_execute_tool_calls` looks up a client-side tool name that is not in that map, it throws KeyError

```
# litellm/responses/mcp/litellm_proxy_mcp_handler.py line 675
server_name = tool_server_map[tool_name]
```

That KeyError is caught by the broad except at line 891-905 and turned into the user-visible error string

```
# line 891-905 (abridged)
except Exception as e:
    ...
    tool_results.append({
        "tool_call_id": tool_call_id,
        "result": f"Error executing tool: {e}",
        "name": tool_name,
    })
```

So a model emitting `tool_use` for `Read` produces `Error executing tool: 'Read'`, which matches what I observed in the proxy spend logs and what Claude Code surfaced as "tool call failed"

The symptom from the agentic client side (Claude Code talking to the proxy over `/v1/messages`): the model attempts Read on a file that exists, gets `Error executing tool: 'Read'` back, tries Bash, gets `Error executing tool: 'Bash'`, then tells the user it cannot read files or run commands. A plain curl client that sends no tools of its own works perfectly against the same model, because then every tool_use resolves to an MCP tool. This is why the bug is specific to agentic clients that bring their own tools

## What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

## What LiteLLM version are you on ?

v1.98.0-dev.2

title: Gemini native custom api_base sends system_instruction instead of canonical systemInstruction
body:
### Description

When using the native Gemini provider with a custom `api_base`, a request containing an OpenAI-style `system` message is serialized with the snake_case JSON key `system_instruction`.

Some Gemini-compatible proxies parse this as a duplicate protobuf optional/oneof assignment and return HTTP 400:

```text
Invalid value at 'request' (oneof), oneof field '_system_instruction' is already set.
Cannot set 'system_instruction'
```

The same endpoint accepts the canonical Gemini REST JSON key `systemInstruction`.

### LiteLLM versions

Reproduced with:

- 1.91.0
- 1.96.2 (latest available from PyPI when tested)

Python 3.13.14 on Windows.

### Minimal reproduction

```python
import litellm

litellm.completion(
    model="gemini/gemini-3.6-flash",
    api_base="https://<custom-gemini-base>/v1beta",
    api_key="<key>",
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are a concise assistant."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "Reply with exactly: ok"},
    ],
    max_tokens=512,
)
```

Actual result: HTTP 400 with the protobuf oneof error above.

A user-only request succeeds, so the failure is specifically triggered when LiteLLM extracts a system message.

### Request-body comparison

Sending this directly to `/v1beta/models/<model>:generateContent` succeeds with HTTP 200:

```json
{
  "systemInstruction": {
    "parts": [{"text": "You are a concise assistant."}]
  },
  "contents": [
    {"role": "user", "parts": [{"text": "Reply with exactly: ok"}]}
  ]
}
```

Changing only the key to snake_case reproduces HTTP 400:

```json
{
  "system_instruction": {
    "parts": [{"text": "You are a concise assistant."}]
  },
  "contents": [
    {"role": "user", "parts": [{"text": "Reply with exactly: ok"}]}
  ]
}
```

### Suspected source

In `litellm/llms/vertex_ai/gemini/transformation.py`, the request transformer currently sets:

```python
data["system_instruction"] = system_instructions
```

### Expected behavior

For native Gemini REST requests, serialize the system-instruction field using the canonical JSON name `systemInstruction`. This remains accepted by the Gemini REST endpoint and improves compatibility with custom native Gemini endpoints that do not safely handle the snake_case alias.
author: scarletkc

title: [Bug]: Gemini TTS via /v1/audio/speech is never spend-tracked on the proxy (no spend log, key spend stays 0)
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

Gemini text-to-speech requests sent through the proxy's `POST /v1/audio/speech` return audio (200) but never show up in spend logs, never increment the virtual key's spend, and never count against budgets. OpenAI TTS through the same endpoint, same proxy, and same key is tracked fine, so this is specific to the Gemini path (and, by the same mechanism, any TTS provider that is served by translating the speech request into a chat completion under the hood)

Expected: a `gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts` call priced at $0.30/M in and $2.50/M out shows a spend-log row with `call_type: aspeech` and non-zero `spend`, and the key's `spend` moves, exactly like `openai/tts-1` does

Root cause, for whoever picks this up: the speech entrypoint takes `metadata` as a named argument, then builds the litellm params it hands to the speech-to-completion bridge from the remaining kwargs, so `metadata` arrives there as `None`. The bridge spreads those params into the inner completion call while reusing the outer request's logging object, and the completion call overwrites that shared object's `metadata` with `None`. By the time the proxy's spend callback runs it finds no key, user, or team on the request and skips the write. Debug logs show it directly: the Gemini call logs `user_api_key None, user_id None, team_id None, end_user_id None`, the OpenAI call right after it logs the hashed key

### User Flow

Before a (hypothetical) fix: a developer whose app generates speech with Gemini through the gateway sees every call at $0 and their key budget never moves

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/speech with `{"model": "gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts", "input": "spend tracking check", "voice": "Kore"}` using their virtual key and get 200 with `audio/wav` bytes back
2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/speech with `{"model": "openai/tts-1", "input": "spend tracking check", "voice": "alloy"}` using the same key and get 200 with `audio/mpeg` bytes back
3. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs (or GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs) and only the OpenAI request is listed, at $0.00027; the Gemini request is missing entirely
4. GET https://litellm-domain/key/info with their key shows `"spend": 0.00027`, only the OpenAI call, so a max budget on that key never trips no matter how much Gemini audio they generate

After a (hypothetical) fix: both TTS calls are logged and billed to the key

1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/speech for `gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts` and get 200 with `audio/wav` bytes back
2. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/speech for `openai/tts-1` and get 200 with `audio/mpeg` bytes back
3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs lists both requests, the Gemini one with `call_type: aspeech` and non-zero spend computed from its input and audio output tokens
4. GET https://litellm-domain/key/info shows the key's `spend` as the sum of both calls, and a key max budget now trips on Gemini audio too

### Proof the bug occurs

Config the proxy ran with (`GEMINI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, and `DATABASE_URL` set in the environment, `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True`):

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts
    litellm_params:
      model: gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts
      api_key: os.environ/GEMINI_API_KEY
  - model_name: openai/tts-1
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/tts-1
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY
general_settings:
  master_key: sk-1234
```

Version or commit: `litellm_internal_staging` at 7a5b98e6a9 (v1.98.0), booted with `python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port 41873 --detailed_debug`

Commands and their full output (real Gemini and OpenAI calls):

```
$ KEY=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:41873/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"key_alias":"tts-spend-repro-3"}' | jq -r .key)

$ curl -s -o speech.wav -D - -X POST http://localhost:41873/v1/audio/speech -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts","input":"spend tracking check","voice":"Kore"}' | grep -i -E "^HTTP|x-litellm-call-id|content-type"
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-litellm-call-id: ab71b16a-e469-437f-8859-562e1c8cb3ef
content-type: audio/wav
$ ls -la speech.wav | awk '{print $5" bytes"}'
154170 bytes

$ curl -s -o speech.mp3 -D - -X POST http://localhost:41873/v1/audio/speech -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"openai/tts-1","input":"spend tracking check","voice":"alloy"}' | grep -i -E "^HTTP|x-litellm-call-id|content-type"
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-litellm-call-id: 6dcf0e92-9d26-43c6-9999-ede7aaaecaf1
content-type: audio/mpeg

$ sleep 15; curl -s "http://localhost:41873/spend/logs" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" | jq -c '.[] | {request_id, model, call_type, spend}'
{"request_id":"6dcf0e92-9d26-43c6-9999-ede7aaaecaf1","model":"openai/tts-1","call_type":"aspeech","spend":0.00027}

$ curl -s "http://localhost:41873/key/info" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" | jq -c '.info | {key_alias, spend}'
{"key_alias":"tts-spend-repro-3","spend":0.00027}

$ curl -s "http://localhost:41873/v1/model/info" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" | jq -c '.data[] | {model_name, input_cost_per_token: .model_info.input_cost_per_token, output_cost_per_token: .model_info.output_cost_per_token}'
{"model_name":"gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts","input_cost_per_token":3E-7,"output_cost_per_token":0.0000025}
{"model_name":"openai/tts-1","input_cost_per_token":null,"output_cost_per_token":null}
```

So the Gemini model is priced, the call succeeded, and the spend log has only the OpenAI row. The proxy's own debug log for the two calls, in order:

```
01:56:54 - LiteLLM Proxy:DEBUG: proxy_track_cost_callback.py:249 - user_api_key None, user_id None, team_id None, end_user_id None
01:56:56 - LiteLLM Proxy:DEBUG: proxy_track_cost_callback.py:249 - user_api_key d628805a57f5b935deab509bb849d9e7761e27681d714c191eee3336135a1f10, user_id None, team_id None, end_user_id None
```

The same happens with the master key and with the newer `gemini/gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview` (checked at #36788's head 32917b07fc)

### What a fix PR should look like

- `litellm/main.py`, `speech()`: pass the named `metadata` (and the other named args the bridge needs) into `get_litellm_params(...)` so the litellm params handed to `speech_to_completion_bridge_handler.speech` carry the request metadata instead of `None`; alternatively have `litellm/endpoints/speech/speech_to_completion_bridge/transformation.py` `transform_request` read `metadata` off the logging object's existing litellm params and forward it, so the inner completion never clobbers what the outer request set
- Whichever way, make sure the outer `aspeech` success handler ends up with the request's `metadata` and a non-zero `response_cost` in its kwargs, since the proxy's cost callback reads both from there
- Regression test in a new `tests/test_litellm/endpoints/speech/speech_to_completion_bridge/test_handler.py` (no mapped test exists yet for the bridge; `tests/test_litellm/test_main.py` also works for the `speech()` side): call `aspeech` for a `gemini/...-tts` model with `metadata={"user_api_key": "..."}` and a mocked completion, assert the success callback's `kwargs["litellm_params"]["metadata"]` still holds `user_api_key`; a second assertion that the same holds for the OpenAI path keeps the two in lockstep
- Out of scope: pricing of TTS models (already correct in `/v1/model/info`), and the `x-litellm-response-cost` header, which is empty for every `/v1/audio/speech` call and can be its own follow-up
- Proof for the fix PR: the exact commands above against a live proxy at the fix commit, showing a Gemini row in `/spend/logs` with `call_type: aspeech` and non-zero `spend`, and `/key/info` `spend` equal to the sum of both calls

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

litellm_internal_staging @ 7a5b98e6a9 (v1.98.0)

title: [Bug]: SCIM PATCH/PUT/DELETE /Users/{id} leave the in-memory user cache stale
body:
## Problem

The SCIM v2 user endpoints (`PATCH /scim/v2/Users/{id}`, `PUT /scim/v2/Users/{id}`, `DELETE /scim/v2/Users/{id}`) currently only write to `litellm_usertable` and do not refresh or invalidate the in-memory user cache used by `get_user_object` (which is keyed on the literal `user_id` per `auth_checks.py:1641`). The very next auth check that hits the cache serves the pre-mutation user, so:

- `PUT` (full replace, e.g. an email or role change) does not take effect on auth until the management-object TTL expires.
- `PATCH` (e.g. deactivation via `active: false`) does not take effect on auth until the TTL expires — even though the same PATCH has already called `_set_user_keys_blocked` to block the user's keys, the cached `LiteLLM_UserTable` still reports the user as active.
- `DELETE` does not invalidate the cached `user_id` entry, so a same-user `POST /user/new` reusing the same ID would read a stale `user_email` / `metadata` / `teams` snapshot from the cache.

## Why this matters

SCIM is the standard protocol for IdP-driven user sync (Okta, Azure AD, OneLogin, JumpCloud, etc.). Operators using an IdP-driven deployment expect a SCIM-driven deactivation or rename to take effect immediately on the proxy. Without cache invalidation, the stale read is silently served on every request for the TTL window — and in a multi-pod deployment, the window extends across replicas.

This is the same multi-prefix cache Achilles heel pattern already fixed in:
- #35565 (cycle 9): `/team/block` and `/team/unblock`
- #36817 (cycle 12): SCIM `PATCH/PUT/DELETE /Groups/{id}`

The `/Users` surface was missed in #36817 because the user cache key shape is different from the team cache key shape. The team cache is dual-keyed (`team_id:{id}` + `team_alias:{alias}`); the user cache is single-keyed on the literal `user_id`. Same defect class, different code path.

## Current behavior

`PUT /scim/v2/Users/{id}` updates the DB row, returns the new SCIM user shape, and leaves `user_api_key_cache[user_id]` unchanged.

## Expected behavior

`PUT` and `PATCH` should call `_refresh_cached_user(updated_user, ...)` after the database write. `DELETE` should invalidate the cache (not refresh, since the user no longer exists) by clearing both halves of the dual cache (local LRU + Redis) for the `user_id` key. `POST /scim/v2/Users` (`create_user`) needs no cache work — the user is new, not yet in cache.

## Proposed solution

Add a `_refresh_cached_user` helper in `litellm/proxy/auth/auth_checks.py` (mirrors the existing `_refresh_cached_team` at `team_endpoints.py:153`). Import it into `litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/scim/scim_v2.py` and call it from the 3 mutating endpoints.

Pin with regression tests in `tests/test_litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/scim/test_scim_v2_endpoints.py` in a new `TestScimUserCacheInvalidation` class (mirrors cycle 12's `TestScimGroupCacheInvalidation`).

## Alternatives considered

1. Inline the cache write in each endpoint (no helper). Rejected: scatters cache-management knowledge across 3 endpoints, easy to miss on a future SCIM endpoint addition.
2. Reuse `_refresh_cached_team`. Rejected: cache key shape (`user_id` literal vs `team_id:{id}`) and model type (`LiteLLM_UserTable` vs `LiteLLM_TeamTableCachedObj`) differ.

## Scope

One source file (`scim_v2.py`, ~25 lines), one helper file (`auth_checks.py`, ~15 lines), one test file (3 tests, ~250 lines).

## Acceptance criteria

- `update_user` calls `_refresh_cached_user` exactly once with the post-mutation row.
- `patch_user` calls `_refresh_cached_user` exactly once with the post-mutation row.
- `delete_user` calls `user_api_key_cache.delete_cache(key=user_id)` AND `proxy_logging_obj.internal_usage_cache.dual_cache.async_delete_cache(key=user_id)` (gated on `proxy_logging_obj is not None`).
- 3 new regression tests pass; each is verified to fail without the source fix.
- Pre-existing SCIM test suite stays green.

## Backward compatibility

No API surface change. Internal cache-management only.

## Risks

- `_refresh_cached_user` is a new helper. If a future SCIM endpoint mutates `litellm_usertable` without calling it, the same defect recurs. Mitigation: cross-reference in the new issue body so future contributors see the pattern.

title: Prisma engine watchdog treats ECHILD from waitpid as engine death and forces a reconnect
body:
### The code

`litellm/proxy/utils.py`, the thread that waits on the Prisma query engine:

```python
def _waitpid_thread_func(self, pid, loop):
    """Note: uvloop/libuv may reap the child first via waitpid(-1, WNOHANG)
    in its SIGCHLD handler. In that case our waitpid raises ChildProcessError.
    we still notify the event loop because the engine is dead either way."""
    try:    os.waitpid(pid, 0)
    except ChildProcessError: pass
    except OSError:           pass
    loop.call_soon_threadsafe(self._on_engine_death_from_thread, pid)
```

The comment states the reasoning: *"the engine is dead either way."*

We think that is not true. `ChildProcessError` is `ECHILD`, which means **"no
such child of mine"** — the child was reaped by someone else, or was never this
process's child, or was reparented away. None of those implies the process
exited.

That distinction is load-bearing here, because this proxy really does have
processes that are not its own children. In our container:

```
PID 1     litellm (the application)          S
PID 559   node-MainThread                    Z   ← never reaped
PID 1086  query-engine-de                    S   ← PPID 1, reparented
```

The Node process Prisma spawns to bootstrap the engine exits at startup and stays
a zombie for the pod's lifetime; the engine itself has been reparented. A
`waitpid` against a PID that is alive but no longer the caller's child is exactly
the case that raises `ECHILD`.

### The consequence

The notification is unconditional, and the receiver does not re-check liveness:

```python
def _on_engine_death_from_thread(self, dead_pid):
    if self._engine_confirmed_dead: return
    if dead_pid != self._engine_pid: return
    if self._consume_expected_death(dead_pid): return
    # ... engine_process_death + force reconnect
```

Three guards, none of which asks whether the process is running. The class
already has `_is_engine_alive()` (`os.kill(pid, 0)`), and this path never calls
it. So a spurious `ECHILD` and a real death produce byte-identical behaviour: a
forced reconnect that tears down a working connection.

### What we observed, and what we did not establish

We saw DB-backed admin endpoints (`/key/list`, `/spend/tags`, `/spend/logs`)
intermittently return `500` alongside these log lines:

```
prisma-query-engine PID 4220 exited (waitpid thread); triggering reconnect.
Attempting Prisma DB reconnect. reason=engine_process_death
prisma-query-engine PID 0 is dead; reconnecting.
```

**We cannot say the incident we saw was a spurious `ECHILD`.** The pod was
replaced before we could examine it, and our log retention did not cover that
namespace at the time. On the replacement pod the endpoints have been stable and
we have not reproduced it.

We are reporting the code path rather than the incident: it is reachable, and on
that path a live engine and a dead one are indistinguishable. The `PID 0 is dead`
line is suggestive — `_is_engine_alive()` treats `_engine_pid <= 0` as alive, so
a zeroed PID arriving on a death path looks anomalous — but we cannot tie it to
either branch without the pod.

### Suggested fix

One line, either way:

- Call `_is_engine_alive(pid)` before notifying on the `ECHILD` path, **or**
- Do not notify when `waitpid` *raised* — only when it *returned* a status.

Related: `_reap_all_zombies()` is only invoked on engine-death paths, never
periodically, which is why the startup zombie above survives for the life of the
pod. Not a bug on its own, but it is why the process table looks the way it does.

### Version

v1.90.0, PostgreSQL backend, container running the app as PID 1 with no init
process.

title: GET /spend/logs has no pagination and OOM-kills the proxy on a large LiteLLM_SpendLogs
body:
### What happens

`GET /spend/logs` with no query parameters fetches every row of
`LiteLLM_SpendLogs` into memory. On a table of ~110k rows (~371 MB on disk) this
exhausts the container and the kernel kills it:

```
reason   = OOMKilled
exitCode = 137
limit    = 4Gi
```

The proxy is unavailable for about a minute while it restarts. In our deployment
that proxy fronts all model traffic, so a single admin API call takes every model
in the cluster offline.

Version: **v1.90.0**, PostgreSQL backend.

### Why it is not avoidable by the caller

`view_spend_logs` accepts no pagination parameters at all — there is no `page`,
`limit`, or `page_size` in the signature, only filters that all default to
`None`:

```python
async def view_spend_logs(
    api_key:    Optional[str] = fastapi.Query(default=None, ...),
    user_id:    Optional[str] = fastapi.Query(default=None, ...),
    request_id: Optional[str] = fastapi.Query(default=None, ...),
    start_date: Optional[str] = fastapi.Query(default=None, ...),
    end_date:   Optional[str] = fastapi.Query(default=None, ...),
    summarize:  bool          = fastapi.Query(default=True,  ...),
    ...
)
```

and the query is issued with no row cap:

```python
data = await SpendLogsRepository(prisma_client).table.find_many(
    where=filter_query,
    order={...},
)
```

`find_many` is called without `take`. A caller who passes no filters therefore
cannot bound the result; the only way to stay safe is to know in advance not to
call the endpoint.

### The paginated endpoints already exist

`/spend/logs/v2` and `/spend/logs/ui` do the right thing:

```python
page:      int = fastapi.Query(default=1, ge=1)
page_size: int = fastapi.Query(default=50, description="Number of items per page", ge=1, le=100)
```

and the admin UI calls those, not the legacy path. So the unbounded behaviour is
isolated to the v1 endpoint — which is what makes this look like an oversight
rather than a design choice.

### Suggested fix

Any of these would close it; the first seems closest to existing behaviour:

1. Add `page` / `page_size` to `view_spend_logs` and pass `take`/`skip` through
   to `find_many`, mirroring the v2 endpoint.
2. Apply a server-side default cap (e.g. `take=1000`) when no `request_id` is
   given, and document that the endpoint truncates.
3. Deprecate `/spend/logs` in favour of `/spend/logs/v2` and have it return a
   `400` when called without filters, pointing at the paginated path.

### Reproducing

Populate `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` with a few hundred thousand rows, set a container
memory limit in the low gigabytes, then:

```
GET /spend/logs
Authorization: Bearer <master key>
```

The request does not return; the connection closes when the process is killed.

### Notes

- Retention does not fix this on its own. `maximum_spend_logs_retention_period`
  bounds growth over time, but a bursty workload can add tens of thousands of
  rows in a single day, so the table can cross the threshold within any
  retention window.
- We mitigated locally by blocking the exact path at the ingress. That is
  possible only because the UI uses the `/ui` and `/v2` variants; it is a
  workaround for an operator, not a fix.

title: [Bug]: Metadata-only model registration (e.g. mode) silently converts unknown-model cost errors into $0.00 — Router.__init__ triggers it
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. (Closest neighbors: my open PR #36561 fixes the *empty*-payload case of this and explicitly scopes this variant out; #28336 and #30198 are about pricing fields being dropped/overwritten, not about metadata-only registration converting errors into $0.)

### What happened?

Registering **metadata-only** model info (for example just `{"mode": "chat"}`, no pricing) for a model that is not in the cost map makes every later cost lookup for that model return **$0.00 instead of raising "this model isn't mapped yet."**

Expected: cost tracking for an unmapped model should stay loud (raise), or use real pricing — never silently bill $0. A metadata-only registration carries no pricing information, so it should not change whether the model is considered priceable.

This is easy to hit without calling `register_model` yourself: a `Router` deployment whose `model_info` carries any metadata (e.g. `mode`) but whose model isn't in the cost map does this on `Router.__init__`, process-wide.

### User Flow

**Before a (hypothetical) fix:** a team routing to a brand-new provider model sees their spend dashboard flatline at $0 for it, with no error anywhere.

1. The proxy admin adds a deployment to `config.yaml` with `model: deepinfra/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` (not yet in the public price catalog) and `model_info: {mode: chat}`, then starts the proxy.
2. A developer sends POST `https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` with that model; the request succeeds and a normal completion comes back.
3. They open `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs` — the request is logged at **$0.00 spend**. No warning, no error, on this and every subsequent request.
4. Monthly reconciliation against the provider invoice shows real charges the gateway never accounted for.

**After a (hypothetical) fix:** the same setup makes the missing price visible instead of silently billing zero.

1. The proxy admin adds the same deployment with the same `model_info: {mode: chat}` and starts the proxy.
2. A developer sends the same POST `https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions`; the completion comes back the same way.
3. `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs` shows the request with an explicit "pricing unknown for this model" marker (or real pricing, once the admin supplies `input_cost_per_token`/`output_cost_per_token` in `model_info`) — not a silent $0.00.
4. Reconciliation matches, because unpriced traffic was flagged the moment it happened.

### Proof the bug occurs

This is a pure cost-arithmetic path — no LLM provider call is involved in computing the cost, so the proof is a complete SDK transcript (the proxy's spend logging sits directly on this function). Captured at commit `09889e1986` on `litellm_internal_staging`, Python 3.13:

```
>>> litellm.completion_cost(model="deepinfra/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731", prompt="hi", completion="there")
raises Exception: This model isn't mapped yet. model=deepinfra/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731

>>> litellm.register_model({"deepinfra/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731": {"mode": "chat"}})  # metadata only, no pricing
>>> litellm.completion_cost(model="deepinfra/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731", prompt="hi", completion="there")
0.0
```

Same result through the Router path real configs hit (fresh process):

```
>>> before Router init:
raises Exception: This model isn't mapped yet. model=deepinfra/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731

>>> Router(model_list=[{"model_name": "my-deepseek",
...                     "litellm_params": {"model": "deepinfra/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731", "api_key": "sk-redacted"},
...                     "model_info": {"mode": "chat"}}])
>>> after Router init:
0.0
```

### Additional context

Verified mechanism (for whoever picks this up): the registration materializes a cost-map entry that carries no pricing keys, and the subsequent lookup treats key-existence as "mapped," synthesizing zero costs for the missing price fields. My #36561 guards the fully-empty-payload version of this; the metadata-only variant needs the fix at the cost-synthesis side instead, because metadata-only registration is legitimate for models that ARE in the built-in catalog. I'm happy to submit the PR for this once #36561 lands (I'm currently at what appears to be the per-author open-PR limit).

title: [Bug]: Admin UI session cookie is a non-HttpOnly JWT carrying the caller's proxy key
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

The Admin UI login sets a `token` cookie holding a JWT whose `key` claim is the caller's real proxy key, and the cookie is not marked `HttpOnly`. For a proxy admin signing in with `UI_USERNAME` / `UI_PASSWORD` or through SSO, that means a full-privilege `sk-...` key sits in `document.cookie`, readable by any script running on `/ui`, for the whole 8h cookie lifetime.

Two things make it worse than a normal session cookie:

The key keeps working outside the browser. Anything that can read the cookie can paste the decoded key into `curl` and mint new keys, read spend, or call models, with no session involved.

Logout does not revoke it. The dashboard clears cookies client-side, so a key that was copied before logout stays valid until its own expiry.

I would expect the browser to hold an opaque session identifier that the proxy resolves server-side, in an `HttpOnly` cookie, with a logout route that drops the session on the server.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the proxy with any config that sets a master key, for example

```yaml
model_list: []

general_settings:
  master_key: sk-1234
```

2. Log in the way the Admin UI does, and look at the cookie it sets

```
$ curl -si -X POST http://localhost:4000/login -d 'username=admin&password=sk-1234' | grep -i '^set-cookie'
set-cookie: token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjoiZGVmYXVsdF91c2VyX2lkIiwia2V5Ijoic2steHh4eHh4...<truncated>; Path=/; SameSite=lax
```

No `HttpOnly` flag, so `document.cookie` in the devtools console on http://localhost:4000/ui/ returns the same string.

3. Decode the middle segment

```
$ echo "$TOKEN" | cut -d. -f2 | base64 -d | python -m json.tool
{
  "user_id": "default_user_id",
  "key": "sk-<the admin's real proxy key>",
  "user_role": "proxy_admin",
  "login_method": "username_password",
  "auth_header_name": "Authorization",
  "server_root_path": "",
  "exp": 1786805817
}
```

4. Use that key from outside the browser

```
$ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_FROM_COOKIE" \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"key_alias":"minted-outside-the-browser"}'
{
  "key": "sk-...",
  "key_alias": "minted-outside-the-browser",
  "expires": null
}
```

5. Log out in the UI, then repeat step 4 with the same key; it still mints keys

### Relevant log output

```shell
POST /login HTTP/1.1" 303 See Other
POST /key/generate HTTP/1.1" 200 OK   # using the key decoded out of the login cookie
```

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

UI Dashboard

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

v1.98.0 (reproduced on `litellm_internal_staging` at 423b791ee0)

### Possible direction

I have a working change locally that swaps the JWT for an opaque `sso_<hex>` handle stored in the cache the `login_code` exchange already uses, delivered in an `HttpOnly` `SameSite=Lax` cookie, plus `/sso/session/me` for identity and `/sso/session/logout` for server-side revocation, with a credential-free `litellm_ui_session=1` marker so the dashboard can still tell a session exists. Happy to open a PR if that direction sounds right to you.
author: duhd-vnpay

title: [Bug]: completion(stream=True) silently drops reasoning-summary streaming for OpenAI reasoning models (79s of total silence)
body:
### What happened?

`litellm.completion(stream=True)` routes OpenAI reasoning models through Chat Completions, which sends nothing at all while the model thinks. `litellm.responses(stream=True)` uses the Responses API and streams `response.reasoning_summary_text.delta` throughout.

Same model, same reasoning effort, same prompt, measured 2026-08-12 on v1.96.2:

| surface | time to first byte | total | max inter-chunk gap | summary deltas |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `completion(stream=True)` | **79.1s** | 79.1s | **79.1s** | 0 |
| `responses(stream=True)` | **0.8s** | 76.5s | 17.2s | 1318 |

The first row is 100% silence — max inter-chunk gap equals total elapsed, because nothing arrives until everything arrives. Total time is nearly identical either way, so this isn't a speed difference, it's a visibility one.

**Why it matters — socket read timeouts.** Sizing a read timeout from observed inter-token gaps is the sane way to do it, and it works for every provider until you hit an OpenAI reasoning model, whose real gap is 79s where everything else is single-digit seconds. Then it times out mid-think. On the wire, a long think and a hung connection are indistinguishable.

**The silent part is the actual bug, more than the routing.** Nothing in the response indicates that summary streaming was dropped — no field, no warning, no flag. The stream says nothing for 79 seconds and then completes normally. There's no way to detect the condition and compensate; you have to already know.

### User Flow

Streaming a reasoning model through `completion()` in a pipeline that (a) shows progress to a user, or (b) sets a socket read timeout derived from observed inter-chunk gaps. Both are routine, and both break only for OpenAI reasoning models while working everywhere else.

### Proof the bug occurs

```python
import litellm, time

start = time.time()
first = None
for chunk in litellm.completion(
    model="gpt-5.5",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "<prompt requiring real reasoning>"}],
    reasoning_effort="high",
    stream=True,
):
    if first is None:
        first = time.time() - start
print(f"TTFB {first:.1f}s  total {time.time() - start:.1f}s")
# TTFB 79.1s  total 79.1s   <- nothing for 79.1s, then everything

# Same model, same effort, same prompt via responses(stream=True):
# TTFB 0.8s   total 76.5s   <- 1318 response.reasoning_summary_text.delta events,
#                              largest gap between any two chunks 17.2s
```

### Proposal

Either:

1. Route reasoning models from `completion()` to the Responses API when a summary is available, or
2. Surface the drop — any signal a caller can detect — and document the limitation prominently.

(2) alone would be enough here. Today the only way to learn about it is to measure both surfaces side by side.

### Prior art (checked before filing)

- #13780 asked for reasoning summaries through `/chat/completions` and was closed completed, but the resolution was `extra_body` param pass-through. That gets params *to* the Responses API; it doesn't make the default `completion(stream=True)` path stream summaries. Still 79.1s of silence on v1.96.2.
- #14117 ("Route Chat Completions to OpenAI Responses API for reasoning") was the routing fix for exactly this, closed unmerged 2026-02-24.

Since the routing option has been attempted and dropped once already, I'd happily take option 2.

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

v1.96.2

title: [Bug]: /model/info pricing metadata becomes worker-dependent after successful requests in v1.98.0
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I searched the open and closed issues before filing this report

The closest result I found was [#30484](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/30484), which mentions a completed team-scoped `/v1/model/info` consistency item. This report is a different failure mode: pricing fields in `/model/info` change according to the Uvicorn worker handling the request after successful model traffic, even without team filtering

### What happened?

After upgrading a live LiteLLM proxy from v1.96.0 to v1.98.0, repeated authenticated requests to `GET /model/info` stopped returning a stable model catalog

For the same caller, key, URL, configuration, and database state, one response contains built-in pricing fields while another response omits those fields for a different subset of models. In a 12-request sample, I observed seven distinct canonicalized pricing variants. The number of rows missing at least one checked pricing field ranged from 12 to 40

The behavior is process-local:

- A direct connection to a mature pod exposes two stable variants, matching its two Uvicorn workers
- Different pods converge on different affected subsets based on the successful requests handled by each process
- A fresh worker initially returns the expected pricing metadata
- Successful model requests cause the affected entries to lose pricing metadata in that worker
- Restarting workers clears the symptom temporarily, but it returns after normal traffic
- The public raw model cost map still contains the correct prices on the same affected worker

This does not appear to be a Redis race. The corruption reproduces in one Python process with no Redis or database, and the object being changed is returned by a process-local `functools.lru_cache`. Redis and the load balancer make the production symptom easier to notice, but neither is needed to trigger it

The affected fields are:

- `input_cost_per_token`
- `output_cost_per_token`
- `input_cost_per_character`
- `output_cost_per_character`
- `cache_read_input_token_cost`
- `cache_creation_input_token_cost`

Because `/model/info` strips `None` values before serializing the response, the corrupted fields are omitted rather than returned as explicit nulls

### User Flow

Before a hypothetical fix:

1. Send an authenticated `GET /model/info` request to display the available model catalog
2. Send successful chat completion requests through the same proxy
3. Repeat the authenticated `GET /model/info` request
4. Read pricing metadata that is present or absent depending on which worker served the catalog request

After a hypothetical fix:

1. Send an authenticated `GET /model/info` request to display the available model catalog
2. Send successful chat completion requests through the same proxy
3. Repeat the authenticated `GET /model/info` request
4. Read the same pricing metadata from every response regardless of which worker served the catalog request

### Proof the bug occurs

#### Live end-to-end setup

The production identifiers below are deliberately replaced. The observed topology and behavior are unchanged:

- Multiple Kubernetes replicas behind one HTTP load balancer
- Two Uvicorn workers per replica
- PostgreSQL-backed model configuration with `store_model_in_db` enabled
- Redis enabled for shared proxy features
- Real provider requests, not mocked responses
- LiteLLM v1.98.0
- Previous working version v1.96.0

Sanitized configuration:

```yaml
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
  store_model_in_db: true
```

Sanitized start command:

```bash
litellm --config /app/config.yaml --port 4000 --num_workers 2
```

Environment variable names used by the reproduction:

```bash
export PROXY_URL="https://proxy.example.com"
export LITELLM_KEY="<redacted>"
```

A successful request to a real configured deployment was used to exercise the normal success callback:

```bash
curl -sS "$PROXY_URL/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "model-a",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with OK"}],
    "max_tokens": 4
  }' |
jq '{
  request_succeeded: (.choices | length > 0),
  finish_reason: .choices[0].finish_reason
}'
```

Output:

```json
{
  "request_succeeded": true,
  "finish_reason": "stop"
}
```

The following samples only model names and three pricing fields, canonicalizes the result, and prints aggregate values so no deployment names or response data are disclosed:

```bash
sample_dir="$(mktemp -d)"

for i in $(seq 1 12); do
  curl -sS "$PROXY_URL/model/info" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_KEY" \
    > "$sample_dir/$i.json"
done

python3 - "$sample_dir" <<'PY'
import hashlib
import json
import pathlib
import sys

directory = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
files = sorted(directory.glob("*.json"))
fields = (
    "input_cost_per_token",
    "output_cost_per_token",
    "cache_read_input_token_cost",
)

digests = set()
missing_counts = []

for path in files:
    rows = json.loads(path.read_text())["data"]
    projection = []
    missing = 0

    for row in rows:
        info = row.get("model_info") or {}
        projection.append(
            {
                "model_name": row.get("model_name"),
                **{field: info.get(field) for field in fields},
            }
        )
        if any(info.get(field) is None for field in fields):
            missing += 1

    projection.sort(key=lambda item: str(item["model_name"]))
    encoded = json.dumps(
        projection,
        sort_keys=True,
        separators=(",", ":"),
    ).encode()
    digests.add(hashlib.sha256(encoded).hexdigest())
    missing_counts.append(missing)

print(f"samples={len(files)}")
print(f"unique_pricing_variants={len(digests)}")
print(f"missing_pricing_rows_min={min(missing_counts)}")
print(f"missing_pricing_rows_max={max(missing_counts)}")
PY
```

Output from the live v1.98.0 proxy:

```text
samples=12
unique_pricing_variants=7
missing_pricing_rows_min=12
missing_pricing_rows_max=40
```

A persistent connection pinned to one worker and a persistent connection pinned to the other worker returned the following representative row. The model identifier was replaced one-for-one, and numeric values were reduced to presence booleans:

```text
worker_a_model_info={"model_name":"model-a","input_cost_per_token_present":true,"output_cost_per_token_present":true,"cache_read_input_token_cost_present":true}
worker_b_model_info={"model_name":"model-a","input_cost_per_token_present":false,"output_cost_per_token_present":false,"cache_read_input_token_cost_present":false}
worker_b_raw_cost_map={"model_name":"provider/model-a","input_cost_per_token_present":true,"output_cost_per_token_present":true,"cache_read_input_token_cost_present":true}
```

This shows that the source cost map is intact while the derived cached model info is corrupted inside one worker

#### Deterministic single-process reproduction

This reproduction uses the v1.98.0 package, no HTTP server, no Redis, no database, no mocks, and no provider credentials. It selects a public cost-map entry with three populated pricing fields without printing the model name:

```python
import copy

import litellm
from litellm import Router
from litellm.types.router import Deployment, LiteLLM_Params, ModelInfo

FIELDS = (
    "input_cost_per_token",
    "output_cost_per_token",
    "cache_read_input_token_cost",
)

model_info_name, cost_entry = next(
    (name, info)
    for name, info in litellm.model_cost.items()
    if "/" in name
    and info.get("litellm_provider") == name.split("/", 1)[0]
    and all(info.get(field) is not None for field in FIELDS)
)
provider, provider_model = model_info_name.split("/", 1)

litellm.get_model_info.cache_clear()
before = copy.deepcopy(litellm.get_model_info(model=model_info_name))

deployment = Deployment(
    model_name="cache-repro",
    litellm_params=LiteLLM_Params(
        model=provider_model,
        custom_llm_provider=provider,
    ),
    model_info=ModelInfo(id="cache-repro"),
)

router = Router()
router.get_router_model_info(
    deployment=deployment,
    received_model_name="cache-repro",
)

after = litellm.get_model_info(model=model_info_name)
raw = litellm.model_cost[model_info_name]

def present(info):
    return tuple(info.get(field) is not None for field in FIELDS)

print("before_present=", present(before))
print("after_present=", present(after))
print("raw_map_present=", present(raw))
print(
    "same_cached_object=",
    after is litellm.get_model_info(model=model_info_name),
)
```

Output on v1.98.0:

```text
before_present= (True, True, True)
after_present= (False, False, False)
raw_map_present= (True, True, True)
same_cached_object= True
```

Clearing `litellm.get_model_info`'s cache restores the values until the same merge path runs again. Passing an equivalent plain dictionary with absent pricing keys does not erase the values, which isolates the trigger to the Pydantic deployment path with unset fields

### Root cause

The regression begins with [4de7a7443a](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/4de7a7443ac5506f422efb36e96387aaae185607), merged by [d0758a291c](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/d0758a291c9dd5405dd8310fd02bccdd5b8b87ff) in PR #36215

That change makes router `ModelInfo` inherit `MirroredPricingParams`, which declares the six pricing fields with defaults of `None`:

```python
class MirroredPricingParams(BaseModel):
    input_cost_per_token: float | None = None
    output_cost_per_token: float | None = None
    input_cost_per_character: float | None = None
    output_cost_per_character: float | None = None
    cache_read_input_token_cost: float | None = None
    cache_creation_input_token_cost: float | None = None
```

The existing router merge obtains an object from `litellm.get_model_info()` and mutates it in place:

```python
model_info = litellm.get_model_info(model=model_info_name)
user_model_info = deployment.get("model_info") or {}

if model_info is not None:
    model_info.update(cast(ModelInfo, user_model_info))

return model_info
```

At the same time, `litellm.get_model_info()` returns the object held by an LRU cache:

```python
@lru_cache(maxsize=DEFAULT_MAX_LRU_CACHE_SIZE)
def _cached_get_model_info(...):
    return _build_model_info(...)
```

The failure sequence is:

1. `litellm.get_model_info()` returns a mutable cached object containing valid built-in prices
2. A successful request invokes `Router.deployment_callback_on_success()`
3. The callback reaches `get_router_model_info()` with a Pydantic `Deployment`
4. Iterating the nested Pydantic `ModelInfo` includes the newly declared pricing fields even when they were never configured
5. `dict.update()` writes those `None` defaults over the valid prices in the cached object
6. Later `get_model_info()` calls in the same process return the already-mutated object
7. `/model/info` strips the `None` values, so the fields disappear from JSON
8. Each worker corrupts only the entries touched by requests routed through that process, producing worker-dependent responses

The same in-place update existed in v1.96.0, but router `ModelInfo` did not yet declare these mirrored pricing fields. Unset values therefore were not present during model iteration and did not overwrite the cached built-in values

### Suggested fix

The merge should both avoid mutating an object owned by the LRU cache and exclude unset or `None` Pydantic defaults:

```python
cached_model_info = litellm.get_model_info(model=model_info_name)
raw_user_model_info = deployment.get("model_info") or {}

if isinstance(raw_user_model_info, BaseModel):
    user_model_info = raw_user_model_info.model_dump(exclude_none=True)
else:
    user_model_info = {
        key: value
        for key, value in raw_user_model_info.items()
        if value is not None
    }

return {
    **cached_model_info,
    **user_model_info,
}
```

This preserves explicit non-null deployment overrides, keeps built-in prices when the deployment did not provide an override, and returns a fresh dictionary rather than modifying shared cached state

Suggested regression coverage:

1. A Pydantic `Deployment` with unset pricing fields must not change the object returned by later `litellm.get_model_info()` calls
2. Unset pricing fields must preserve built-in prices
3. Explicit non-null pricing overrides must still win
4. Dictionary and Pydantic deployment paths must produce equivalent merged metadata
5. Running the success callback must not change a later `/model/info` response
6. Two routers or workers processing different model subsets must still expose identical pricing metadata

A fix with regression tests has been validated locally and can be submitted as a PR

### Related independent reload finding

During diagnosis I also found a separate v1.98.0 DB-only reload edge case. It does not cause the `None` overwrite above, but it can add another source of model-cost-map inconsistency around startup or manual reloads

The schedule work in [9ea5cfce0e](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/9ea5cfce0edd365f722556d3d72960f1d60012ac) can cause a newly started process to perform a one-time model cost map swap when a persisted manual reload revision exists. A DB-only proxy constructs `Router()` before loading deployments, and router tracking currently depends on a truthy initial `model_list`. That router is therefore absent from `_live_routers`, so `reapply_runtime_model_cost_registrations()` cannot replay the dynamically loaded DB deployments after the swap

Registering every live Router, including an initially empty Router that is populated later, fixes that replay gap. I included this note to distinguish it from the primary cache-mutation regression and am happy to file it separately if maintainers prefer one root cause per issue

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

### What LiteLLM version are you on?

v1.98.0

title: [Bug]: A2A agent calls report "NoneType takes no arguments" instead of the "install a2a-sdk" error
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

---

### What happened?

`a2a-sdk` is an optional dependency. It ships in the `extra_proxy` extra, not in `proxy`, so the documented install `uv tool install 'litellm[proxy]'` leaves it out. Calling a registered A2A agent in that state returns

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"1","error":{"code":-32603,"message":"Internal error: NoneType takes no arguments"}}
```

The gateway already has a purpose built message for exactly this case, `Server error: 'a2a' package not installed. Please install 'a2a-sdk'.`, and it never reaches the caller. Neither the response nor the proxy log names the missing package, so an operator has no way to tell what to install

I expected the response to name `a2a-sdk`, which is what the gateway was built to say

Official Docker images install `extra_proxy` and are not affected. This reaches people who install the gateway with pip or uv and have not separately installed `a2a-sdk`

### User Flow

Before a (hypothetical) fix: an operator who installed the gateway the documented way calls their registered agent and gets an opaque Python error rather than being told which package is missing

1. They install the gateway with `uv tool install 'litellm[proxy]'`, then register an agent named `demo-agent` under the top level `agents` key in config.yaml
2. They start the gateway and confirm GET http://localhost:4000/health/liveliness returns 200
3. They send POST http://localhost:4000/a2a/demo-agent with a JSON-RPC `message/send` body
4. The call comes back HTTP 500 with `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"1","error":{"code":-32603,"message":"Internal error: NoneType takes no arguments"}}`
5. They check the gateway log and find only `Error invoking agent: NoneType takes no arguments`, repeated, naming no package, so they are left guessing what to install

After a (hypothetical) fix: the same call names the missing package, so the operator knows what to do next

1. They install the gateway with `uv tool install 'litellm[proxy]'`, then register an agent named `demo-agent` under the top level `agents` key in config.yaml
2. They start the gateway and confirm GET http://localhost:4000/health/liveliness returns 200
3. They send POST http://localhost:4000/a2a/demo-agent with a JSON-RPC `message/send` body
4. The call comes back HTTP 500 with `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"1","error":{"code":-32603,"message":"Server error: 'a2a' package not installed. Please install 'a2a-sdk'."}}`
5. They run `pip install "a2a-sdk>=1.1.0,<2.0"`, restart the gateway, and the same POST reaches their agent

### Proof the bug occurs

This path fails before any call to the registered agent or to an LLM provider, so no provider request is involved and there is nothing to bill

Config the proxy ran with, `a2a_config.yaml`:

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: gpt-4o-mini
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-4o-mini
      api_key: sk-placeholder-not-used-by-this-repro

agents:
  - agent_name: demo-agent
    agent_card_params:
      name: "Demo Agent"
      url: "http://localhost:10001"
      protocolVersion: "1.0"

general_settings:
  master_key: sk-1234
```

Env: `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True`, and `a2a-sdk` not installed (`pip uninstall a2a-sdk`)

Version: commit `423b791ee0`. Also reproduced on released `v1.96.2`

Start the proxy:

```
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config a2a_config.yaml --port 4000
```

Call the agent:

```
$ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/a2a/demo-agent \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"1","method":"message/send","params":{"message":{"role":"user","parts":[{"kind":"text","text":"hello"}],"messageId":"msg-1"}}}'

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"1","error":{"code":-32603,"message":"Internal error: NoneType takes no arguments"}}
[HTTP 500]
```

Proxy log for that request:

```
23:54:19 - LiteLLM Proxy:ERROR: a2a_endpoints.py:970 - Error invoking agent: NoneType takes no arguments
TypeError: NoneType takes no arguments
```

For comparison, the message the gateway is meant to return here, captured on the same proxy and the same request after making the missing-package check reachable:

```
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"1","error":{"code":-32603,"message":"Server error: 'a2a' package not installed. Please install 'a2a-sdk'."}}
[HTTP 500]
```

title: [Bug]: bedrock_mantle rejects max_tokens for Gemma models (google.gemma-4-*)
body:
### What happened?

Bedrock Mantle's OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint rejects the `max_tokens` parameter for `google.gemma-4-*` models, and there is no per-model handling in `BedrockMantleChatConfig` to work around it — the parameter is forwarded unchanged (like any other OpenAI-compatible provider) and Bedrock returns a 400-shaped error, which surfaces as `litellm.APIConnectionError`.

I also verified that the AWS docs' own sample-code parameter name for this model, `max_output_tokens` (the name used for Bedrock's native Converse/InvokeModel APIs), is **not** a valid substitute here either — it's simply not recognized on this OpenAI-compatible route at all. Omitting the parameter entirely is the only thing that succeeds.

### Relevant log output

```
litellm.APIConnectionError: Bedrock_mantleException - {"error":{"code":"unsupported_parameter","message":"Unsupported parameter: 'max_tokens' is not supported with this model.","param":"max_tokens","type":"invalid_request_error"}}
```

### Are you a ML Ops Team?

No

### What LiteLLM version are you on?

v1.97.0-dev (confirmed present on latest main as of 2026-08-14; also present on v1.93.0)

### Twitter / LinkedIn details

_No response_

### Reproduction

```python
from litellm.llms.bedrock_mantle.chat.transformation import BedrockMantleChatConfig

config = BedrockMantleChatConfig()
result = config.map_openai_params(
    non_default_params={"max_tokens": 50},
    optional_params={},
    model="google.gemma-4-31b",
    drop_params=False,
)
print(result)
# Actual: {'max_tokens': 50}  -- forwarded unchanged, will 400 against real Bedrock
# Expected: {} -- max_tokens should not be sent for this model family
```

Confirmed against the real Bedrock endpoint (not mocked), via a `bedrock_mantle/google.gemma-4-31b` deployment:

| Request body | Result |
|---|---|
| `max_tokens: 50` | `unsupported_parameter: max_tokens` |
| `max_output_tokens: 50` (AWS's native-API param name) | `unknown_parameter: max_output_tokens` — not recognized on this route at all |
| param omitted entirely | `200 OK` |

Also confirmed that setting `drop_params: true` at the config/router level does **not** work around this: `drop_params` only filters parameters that `get_supported_openai_params()` already declares unsupported client-side. Since `max_tokens` is a normal, generally-supported OpenAI param and `BedrockMantleChatConfig` doesn't override `get_supported_openai_params` to exclude it for Gemma, LiteLLM has no way to know ahead of time that Bedrock will reject it server-side.

### Proposed fix

`BedrockMantleChatConfig` (`litellm/llms/bedrock_mantle/chat/transformation.py`) should override `map_openai_params` to drop `max_tokens` (after the parent's existing `max_completion_tokens` → `max_tokens` rename) when the target model is a Gemma variant — following the same model-substring-exclusion pattern already used elsewhere in this file's neighborhood (e.g. `AmazonAnthropicClaudeConfig._needs_tool_workaround` in the Bedrock Invoke Anthropic transformation).

Happy to open a PR with this fix plus a regression test — have already verified it end-to-end against real Bedrock in a downstream fork. Will link the PR here.

title: AnthropicMessagesConfig.get_complete_url doesn't dedup trailing /v1 in api_base (yields /v1/v1/messages), unlike openai_like/deepseek siblings
body:
### What happened

`AnthropicMessagesConfig.get_complete_url` appends `/v1/messages` to a custom `api_base` without deduplicating a trailing `/v1`:

```python
# litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/messages/transformation.py (~line 227)
api_base = AnthropicModelInfo.get_api_base(api_base) or "https://api.anthropic.com"
if not api_base.endswith("/v1/messages"):
    api_base = f"{api_base}/v1/messages"
```

So a deployment resolving to `custom_llm_provider: anthropic` with `api_base: https://host/v1` produces `https://host/v1/v1/messages`, which 404s at the provider.

Every sibling Anthropic-messages config already handles this:

- `OpenAILikeAnthropicMessagesConfig.get_complete_url` (`litellm/llms/openai_like/messages/transformation.py`) does `rstrip("/")` → return if endswith `/v1/messages` → `removesuffix("/v1")` → append, with test coverage in `tests/test_litellm/llms/openai_like/messages/test_openai_like_anthropic_messages_transformation.py` asserting `https://host/v1 → https://host/v1/messages`.
- `DeepSeek`'s messages config (`litellm/llms/deepseek/messages/transformation.py`) has the same normalization.

Only the Anthropic config lacks it. Users hit this when pointing an `anthropic/`-prefixed model at an Anthropic-compatible gateway whose base already ends in `/v1` — see discussion #36651 for a real-world report (Claude Code → LiteLLM → Groq/NIM, where a misconfigured entry surfaces exactly this shape).

### Expected behavior

`api_base: https://host/v1` should yield `https://host/v1/messages`, consistent with the openai_like and deepseek configs.

### Proposed fix

Mirror the openai_like normalization in `AnthropicMessagesConfig.get_complete_url` (two lines), plus parametrized tests matching the openai_like test table. PR incoming.
