title: [Feature]: Publish floating minor-version Docker tags for patch-only updates (e.g. 1.89 → latest 1.89.x)
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### The Feature

## Summary

Please publish and maintain floating minor-version tags for the official LiteLLM Docker images, so operators can follow patch releases within a chosen minor release without automatically crossing into the next minor release.

For example:

- `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:1.89.5` → immutable/exact release
- `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:1.89` → floating tag pointing to the latest published `1.89.x`
- `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:1.90` → floating tag pointing to the latest published `1.90.x`

The same convention could be applied to the corresponding official database image where appropriate.

## Current behavior

LiteLLM publishes exact release tags, but a minor-family tag such as:
```yaml
services:
  litellm:
    image: ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:1.89
```
is not consistently available.

Docker/OCI registries do not perform semantic-version resolution themselves. Therefore an operator currently has to choose between:

1. pinning an exact patch version such as 1.89.5 and manually discovering/updating every patch release; or
2. following a broader moving channel such as main-stable, which can eventually move the deployment across minor releases.

I would like the middle option: follow maintenance releases automatically while deliberately holding the feature/minor release line.

## Desired behavior

When a patch release is published, for example:
```
v 1.89.6
```
the release workflow would also update this docker compose:
```
image: ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:1.89
```
to point to the newest release in the 1.89.x family.
Publishing 1.90.0 would create/update 1.90, but would NOT change 1.89.

## Conceptually:
```
1.89.5  ─┐
1.89.6   ├─ exact release tags
1.89.7  ─┘

1.89 → 1.89.7

1.90.0  ─┐
1.90.1   ├─ exact release tags
1.90.2  ─┘

1.90 → 1.90.2
```
Existing exact tags would remain available for operators requiring fully reproducible deployments.

## Example Docker Compose use case

An operator who deliberately wants to remain on the 1.89 release line could use:
```yaml
services:
  litellm:
    image: ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:1.89
```
Then:
```bash
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d
```

could consume a newly published 1.89.x maintenance release, but would never silently upgrade the deployment to 1.90.x.

Operators requiring immutable deployments could continue using:
```yaml
image: ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:1.89.5
```
## Scope

This request is specifically for publisher-maintained OCI/Docker tags.
(It is NOT a request for Docker Compose to interpret semantic-version ranges; as t.m.k. Docker does not provide that behavior for image tags.)



### User Flow


LiteLLM is infrastructure, and there is a useful operational distinction between accepting patch/maintenance updates and accepting a new minor release.

For a long-running LiteLLM Proxy deployment, I want to:

- receive maintenance and security fixes within a tested release line;
- avoid unnecessarily lagging behind on patch releases;
- deliberately review release notes before crossing a minor-version boundary;
- retain an easy rollback path;
- avoid depending on a broad moving tag that may introduce new functionality or behavioral changes.

This is particularly useful for self-hosted and production-style Docker Compose deployments where LiteLLM sits between persistent clients and several providers.

For example, my deployment uses LiteLLM as a central gateway for OpenWebUI and other clients, with PostgreSQL persistence and multiple upstream providers. A regression in provider behavior or database handling can affect all clients simultaneously. I therefore deliberately hold a known-good minor release line while still wanting maintenance fixes from that line.

Other container projects use floating minor tags successfully for this operational model. The desired contract is simple:

`1.89` = latest supported `1.89.x`

while:

`1.89.5` = exact release

This would complement rather than replace LiteLLM's existing exact and stable release channels.

If floating minor tags are intentionally not provided for release-engineering, reproducibility, or security reasons, documenting that policy and the recommended mechanism for tracking patch-only updates would also be valuable.

### How far you got

using docker compose,
```yaml
  litellm:
    image: ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:1.89
```
will fail to pull the latest subversion (1.89.5 right now) within the 1.89 minor version.

Only pinning the subversion will pull an image:
```yaml
  litellm:
    image: ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:1.89.5
```

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

_No response_

### LiteLLM is hiring a founding backend engineer, are you interested in joining us and shipping to all our users?

No

### Twitter / LinkedIn details

_No response_

title: [Feature]: Auto-detect context window (max_input_tokens) for LM Studio models from its native metadata API
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### The Feature

For self-hosted/local providers that expose their own richer model-metadata API (LM Studio's `/api/v0/models` and `/api/v1/models`, both distinct from the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/models` LiteLLM currently calls for discovery), LiteLLM never queries or surfaces the provider's own `max_context_length` into a model's `model_info.max_input_tokens`.

This affects every LM Studio model regardless of how it's added to LiteLLM — a manually written `model_list` entry, a model added via the Admin UI, or (once supported) a discovered wildcard model — because context window info for any model not in LiteLLM's built-in static cost map (`model_prices_and_context_window.json`) is simply never populated from anywhere. Since LM Studio models are arbitrary user-loaded local models, they can never be in that static map.

Concretely: LiteLLM's provider-discovery interface (`BaseLLMModelInfo.get_models()`) is `list[str]` — model IDs only, no channel for per-model metadata like context length even for providers that do query a richer endpoint. Fixing this requires both (a) querying an endpoint that has the data, and (b) a place in the model-info population path to put it.

### User Flow

Before this feature (today): a proxy admin adding an LM Studio model gets no context window info, and has no way to keep it in sync when they swap models locally

1. Admin adds `qwen/qwen3.6-35b-a3b` as a LiteLLM model pointing at their LM Studio server, either via `model_list` in `config.yaml` or the Admin UI "Add Model" form
2. They call `GET https://litellm-domain/v1/model/info` with their key
3. The model's entry shows `"max_input_tokens": null, "max_output_tokens": null` — LiteLLM has no idea the model supports a 262144-token context
4. Their workaround is to open LM Studio's own UI (or call its native API directly), read the context length off there, and hand-type it into `model_info.max_input_tokens` in their config — and remember to update it by hand every time they swap the loaded model or LM Studio changes the context settings

After this feature (ideal user flow): LiteLLM reflects the real context window LM Studio reports, with no manual step

1. Admin adds the same model the same way, with no extra config
2. They call `GET https://litellm-domain/v1/model/info`
3. The model's entry shows `"max_input_tokens": 262144` — LiteLLM asked LM Studio directly and used the real value
4. If they swap the loaded model in LM Studio for one with a different context size, the next model-info refresh reflects the new value with no manual edit

### How far you got

Config the proxy ran with (`config.yaml`, static entry, no discovery, no wildcards — deliberately using only currently-shipped LiteLLM behavior):

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: qwen3.6-35b-a3b
    litellm_params:
      model: lm_studio/qwen/qwen3.6-35b-a3b
      api_base: http://<lm-studio-host>:1234/v1
      api_key: os.environ/LM_STUDIO_KEY
```

Version: v1.96.2 (`docker.litellm.ai/berriai/litellm-database:latest`)

Commands and full output:

```bash
$ curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER_KEY" http://localhost:4000/v1/model/info | jq '.data[] | select(.model_name == "qwen3.6-35b-a3b") | .model_info | {max_input_tokens, max_output_tokens}'
{
  "max_input_tokens": null,
  "max_output_tokens": null
}
```

Meanwhile, calling LM Studio's own native API for the exact same model, at the same moment, shows the real answer LiteLLM never asked for:

```bash
$ curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $LM_STUDIO_KEY" http://<lm-studio-host>:1234/api/v0/models | jq '.data[] | select(.id == "qwen/qwen3.6-35b-a3b")'
{
  "id": "qwen/qwen3.6-35b-a3b",
  "object": "model",
  "type": "vlm",
  "publisher": "qwen",
  "arch": "qwen3_5_moe",
  "compatibility_type": "mlx",
  "quantization": "4bit",
  "state": "loaded",
  "max_context_length": 262144,
  "loaded_context_length": 34560,
  "capabilities": ["tool_use"]
}
```

LM Studio also exposes an even richer, newer native endpoint (`/api/v1/models`, distinct response shape — `{"models": [...]}` not `{"data": [...]}`) with the same `max_context_length` field plus `loaded_instances`, structured `quantization`, and `capabilities`:

```bash
$ curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $LM_STUDIO_KEY" http://<lm-studio-host>:1234/api/v1/models | jq '.models[] | select(.key == "qwen3.6-35b-unsloth-code-reasoning-deepseek-v4-pro-destilled-mlx")'
{
  "type": "llm",
  "publisher": "10Hen10",
  "key": "qwen3.6-35b-unsloth-code-reasoning-deepseek-v4-pro-destilled-mlx",
  "architecture": "qwen3_5_moe",
  "quantization": {"name": "4bit", "bits_per_weight": 4},
  "max_context_length": 262144,
  "format": "mlx",
  "capabilities": {"vision": false, "trained_for_tool_use": true}
}
```

What stopped me there: LiteLLM has no config option, discovery mechanism, or background refresh that queries either of LM Studio's native endpoints for `max_context_length`, and the discovery interface it does have for other providers (`BaseLLMModelInfo.get_models() -> list[str]`) has no field to carry per-model metadata even if it did.

title: [Bug]: check_provider_endpoint: true in config.yaml has no effect when STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

Setting `check_provider_endpoint: true` in `config.yaml` under `litellm_settings` has no effect on `/v1/models` wildcard expansion when `STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True`. Observed with `vertex_ai/*` — a provider explicitly listed as supported for model discovery in the [docs](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/model_discovery).

The setting works correctly without `STORE_MODEL_IN_DB` (no Postgres). With it enabled, the DB-stored `litellm_settings` row (written via the Admin UI or `/config/update`) silently takes precedence over `config.yaml`, and that row typically lacks `check_provider_endpoint` entirely — causing the runtime flag to remain at its default (`False`).

This is the same class of bug as #36533 (`max_budget` not applied from DB-stored config). The proxy's `_update_config_fields()` only applies `litellm_settings` keys listed in `LITELLM_SETTINGS_SAFE_DB_OVERRIDES` (`litellm/constants.py`). `check_provider_endpoint` is not on that allowlist, so even when `config.yaml` correctly sets it at initial startup, the value is effectively lost during the DB-overlay merge lifecycle.

Additionally, `VertexAIModelInfo.get_models()` (in `litellm/llms/vertex_ai/common_utils.py`) is a bare `raise NotImplementedError("Vertex AI models are not supported yet")` stub — so even if the config flag propagated correctly, Vertex AI discovery would still silently fail (the exception is caught and swallowed by `_get_valid_models_from_provider_api`). The [Model Discovery docs](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/model_discovery) list Vertex AI as a supported provider without noting this limitation.

### User Flow

Before a (hypothetical) fix: a proxy admin enabling model discovery with `STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True` sees only the literal wildcard

1. Admin writes `config.yaml` with `litellm_settings.check_provider_endpoint: true` and a `model_list` entry for `vertex_ai/*` with valid Vertex AI credentials
2. Admin starts the proxy with `STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True` and a Postgres database
3. Admin sends `GET http://localhost:4000/v1/models` with their master key
4. Response contains only `{"id": "vertex_ai/*"}` — no real Vertex AI models are listed
5. Admin checks DB: `SELECT param_value FROM "LiteLLM_Config" WHERE param_name = 'litellm_settings';` shows `{"drop_params": true}` — no `check_provider_endpoint` key
6. Admin removes `STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True` and restarts without a database — still no Vertex AI models discovered (second bug: the `get_models()` stub)

After a (hypothetical) fix: the config setting takes effect and models are discovered

1. Same `config.yaml`, same `STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True`, same Postgres database
2. `check_provider_endpoint: true` persists into the runtime regardless of what the DB-stored `litellm_settings` row contains
3. Admin sends `GET http://localhost:4000/v1/models` with their master key
4. Response contains real models discovered from the configured provider

### Proof the bug occurs

**Config:**

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: vertex_ai/*
    litellm_params:
      model: vertex_ai/*
      vertex_project: my-gcp-project
      vertex_location: us-central1

litellm_settings:
  check_provider_endpoint: true
```

**Version:** v1.98.0 (commit `423b791ee`, `litellm_internal_staging` branch)

**Bug 1 — config flag not propagated with STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True:**

DB-backed proxy with `STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True`:

```bash
$ curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" http://localhost:4000/v1/models | jq '.data[].id | select(startswith("vertex"))'
"vertex_ai/*"
# Only the literal wildcard — flag not in effect
```

Verified the runtime value from inside the running container:
```python
import litellm
print(litellm.check_provider_endpoint)  # False — should be True
```

DB row confirms the key is absent:
```sql
SELECT param_value FROM "LiteLLM_Config" WHERE param_name = 'litellm_settings';
-- {"drop_params": true, "cost_discount_config": {"vertex_ai": 0.05}}
-- No check_provider_endpoint key
```

**Bug 2 — VertexAIModelInfo.get_models() is a stub:**

```python
from litellm.llms.vertex_ai.common_utils import VertexAIModelInfo
VertexAIModelInfo().get_models()
# NotImplementedError: Vertex AI models are not supported yet
```

```python
from litellm.utils import get_valid_models
result = get_valid_models(check_provider_endpoint=True, custom_llm_provider="vertex_ai")
# WARNING: Error getting valid models: Vertex AI models are not supported yet
# result = []
```

### Related issues

- #36533 — same root cause for config propagation (DB-stored `litellm_settings` not applied), different key (`max_budget`)

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

v1.98.0

title: [Bug]: SSO and JWT email matching can take over an existing proxy admin
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate

### What happened?

When an SSO or JWT subject does not match an existing `user_id` or `sso_user_id`, LiteLLM falls back to a case-insensitive email lookup. A matching row is returned even if it already has a different `sso_user_id`, and LiteLLM schedules an update that overwrites that id with the new subject

The SSO path then inherits the matched row's stored role when the identity provider did not supply a LiteLLM role. The JWT path checks the matched row's role directly. A different identity-provider subject that can present an existing privileged email can therefore inherit `PROXY_ADMIN` and durably rebind the victim's `sso_user_id`

There is no shared requirement that the email claim is verified, no refusal when the row already has a different SSO subject, and no protection for administrative roles

Expected behavior is that email linking is allowed only for a verified email on an explicitly unlinked or invited row. A row already bound to another subject, especially a proxy admin, must not be silently rebound

### User Flow

Before a fix: a second identity-provider subject can become an existing proxy admin by presenting the same email

1. An administrator already has a LiteLLM dashboard account bound to SSO subject `admin-subject`
2. A different trusted identity-provider subject authenticates at `GET https://litellm-domain/sso/callback` with the administrator's email in its claims
3. LiteLLM misses by the new subject, finds the administrator row by email, and overwrites its `sso_user_id`
4. The new subject is redirected into `https://litellm-domain/ui/` with the stored `proxy_admin` role
5. The new subject can call `POST https://litellm-domain/key/generate` and other administrator routes
6. The original administrator can be locked out because their row is now bound to the different subject
7. The attacker can access other users' keys and management data that their original identity should never reach

After a fix: a subject mismatch cannot silently link to a privileged or already-bound row

1. The same administrator account remains bound to `admin-subject`
2. The different identity-provider subject authenticates with the same email claim
3. LiteLLM detects that the row is already bound to another subject, or that the email is not verified
4. `GET https://litellm-domain/sso/callback` returns a 403 or creates a separate non-admin user according to policy
5. The new subject cannot call `POST https://litellm-domain/key/generate`
6. The original administrator remains able to sign in with `admin-subject`
7. The second subject cannot read or modify any other user's management objects

### Proof the bug occurs

Config / setup:

```yaml
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
```

Enable Generic OIDC, SAML, or JWT auth. Existing database row:

```json
{
  "user_id": "admin-user",
  "user_email": "admin@example.test",
  "sso_user_id": "admin-subject",
  "user_role": "proxy_admin"
}
```

Version / commit:

```text
v1.98.0, commit 46ffc2ab7d4b29889b54f9ccefd78f995a0e53ff
```

Current shared fuzzy-link code:

```python
if response is None and user_email is not None:
    response = await user_table.find_first(
        where={"user_email": {"equals": user_email, "mode": "insensitive"}},
        include={"organization_memberships": True},
    )

    if response is not None and sso_user_id is not None:
        asyncio.create_task(
            user_table.update(
                where={"user_id": response.user_id},
                data={"sso_user_id": sso_user_id},
            )
        )
```

The repository's existing test encodes the unsafe rebinding contract. It starts with a row whose SSO id is `sso_123`, looks it up by email for `new_sso_456`, and expects the update to the new id

Audit command and output:

```shell
$ uv run --no-sync python -m pytest tests/proxy_unit_tests/test_auth_checks.py::test_get_fuzzy_user_object
============================== 1 passed ==============================
```

The current SSO role resolution uses the database role when the SSO response does not supply a LiteLLM role. The JWT auth builder also calls `get_user_object` with the presented subject and email, then treats a returned `PROXY_ADMIN` row as admin

A live third-party identity provider was not used because reproducing against a real account would modify authentication state. The test and source path confirm the email match, subject overwrite, and role inheritance without external side effects

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

v1.98.0, commit 46ffc2ab7d4b29889b54f9ccefd78f995a0e53ff

title: [Bug]: budget_limits reset clears Redis before reset_at commits (bypass only with disable_spend_logs)
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate

### What happened?

Rescoped on 2026-08-16 after re-validating against `litellm_internal_staging` at `973329e986`. The ordering defect is real and unchanged. The budget bypass I originally described does not occur under default configuration, and I have corrected that below

The multi-window budget reset path clears each Redis enforcement counter before it persists the window's new `reset_at` in PostgreSQL. `_reset_expired_window` zeroes the in-memory and Redis counter and mutates the local JSON, then returns; `reset_budget_windows` performs the database update afterwards. If that update fails, the database still says the old window is due while Redis reports zero spend for it

```python
spend_counter_cache.in_memory_cache.set_cache(key=counter_key, value=0.0)
if spend_counter_cache.redis_cache is not None:
    await spend_counter_cache.redis_cache.async_set_cache(
        key=counter_key,
        value=0.0,
    )
window["reset_at"] = compute_budget_reset_at(...).isoformat()
return True
```

Only after that helper returns does `reset_budget_windows` call:

```python
await VerificationTokenRepository(self.prisma_client).table.update(
    where={"token": row["token"]},
    data={"budget_limits": windows},
)
```

The same class documents the required opposite order for ordinary key, user, and team spend counters, in the `_invalidate_spend_counter` and `_reset_budget_common` docstrings, and pins it with `test_reset_does_not_zero_counter_when_db_write_fails`. That test covers only the key, user, and team path, not windows, which is why the inversion survives here

Expected behavior is commit first, then clear the enforcement counter only for a window whose `reset_at` advance succeeded, matching what the rest of the class already does

### Why this is not a budget bypass by default

`_virtual_key_multi_budget_check` passes `window_start=get_budget_window_start(w)` into `get_current_spend`, and because `window_start is not None` the `is_window` branch consults `_authoritative_floor_spend` on every window check rather than trusting the counter. `SpendCounterReseed.from_db` returns `None` for window counters by design, so it falls through to `window_from_spend_logs`, which re-aggregates the old window from `LiteLLM_SpendLogs`. The database still holds the old due `reset_at`, so `window_start` is the old window's start, the sum comes back at the full amount, `_repair_stale_spend_counter` raises the counter back, and the request is rejected

My original claim that the reservation path treats the Redis zero as a warm cache hit is literally true of `_is_spend_counter_cache_warm`, but that only affects reservation seeding, which is never reached because auth has already rejected. That hardening landed in `a8b94b9a87` on 2026-06-18, about two months before I filed this

The one configuration where the bypass is real is `disable_spend_logs: true`, or a spend-log retention window shorter than the budget window. `window_from_spend_logs` then returns `0.0` rather than `None`, that zero is treated as a verified authoritative floor, and the still-due window gets a second full budget

### User Flow

Before a fix, with spend logs disabled:

1. The user has a key with a `budget_limits` window of `$10/day`, has spent `$10`, and its `reset_at` is due
2. The reset job sets `spend:key:<token>:window:1d` to zero
3. The PostgreSQL update of `budget_limits.reset_at` times out, so the stored window is still due
4. The user sends `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` for a request costing `$1`
5. Spend logs are disabled, so the authoritative floor reads `0.0` and the request is admitted
6. The user can spend another `$9` in the same still-due window

After a fix, in every configuration:

1. The reset job computes the future `reset_at` but the PostgreSQL update times out
2. The counter is left untouched because the commit did not succeed
3. The same request is rejected against the still-exhausted old window
4. After a later successful database update, the counter is cleared for the new window

### Proof the bug occurs

Create a key or team whose `budget_limits` JSON contains a due window and whose Redis counter is at its maximum, then make the `budget_limits` update raise. The Redis zero is already written with no compensating action. With `general_settings.disable_spend_logs: true`, the next request against that window is admitted

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

Re-validated on `litellm_internal_staging` at `973329e986`. Originally filed against v1.98.0 at `46ffc2ab7d4b29889b54f9ccefd78f995a0e53ff`

title: [Bug]: Concurrent budget reset jobs erase spend from the new window
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate

### What happened?

Every proxy replica schedules `ResetBudgetJob.reset_budget`. The job reads due keys, users, and teams and later performs unconditional updates that set `spend=0` and advance `budget_reset_at`

There is no `PodLockManager` lock around the reset tick and no compare-and-swap condition on the old `budget_reset_at`. Two replicas can read the same due row. If replica A resets it, new-window traffic increments spend, and replica B then applies its stale reset, replica B erases the new-window spend from PostgreSQL and zeros the Redis counter

Both reset jobs report success. The affected key, user, or team appears to have a full budget even though it has already spent in the new window

Expected behavior is that one reset wins per entity and a stale second writer cannot erase spend recorded after that reset

### User Flow

Before a fix: a virtual-key user can spend past the new-window budget after two replicas reset the same key

1. The user has a virtual key with a `$10` daily budget and the previous window is due for reset
2. Two proxy replicas start their reset jobs and both read the key as due
3. Replica A commits the reset
4. The user sends `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` and receives 200 for a request costing `$2`
5. Replica B commits its stale `spend=0` update and clears the Redis counter
6. `GET https://litellm-domain/key/info` reports `spend: 0` for the new window
7. The user can send another `$10` of requests before receiving a budget rejection, exceeding the intended window by the erased amount

After a fix: only one reset can advance the due row and post-reset spend remains visible

1. The user has the same virtual key and due daily budget
2. Two proxy replicas start their reset jobs
3. One replica atomically advances the due row and the second updates zero rows
4. The user sends the same `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` and receives 200 for a `$2` request
5. `GET https://litellm-domain/key/info` reports `spend: 2`
6. A further `$8` reaches the budget, and a request that would exceed `$10` is rejected
7. Another user cannot consume budget headroom created by a stale reset

### Proof the bug occurs

Config / setup:

```yaml
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
```

Run at least two proxy replicas with `disable_reset_budget` unset. Give a key, user, or team a `budget_duration` and a due `budget_reset_at`

Version / commit:

```text
v1.98.0, commit 46ffc2ab7d4b29889b54f9ccefd78f995a0e53ff
```

Current reset tick:

```python
await self.reset_budget_for_litellm_keys()
await self.reset_budget_for_litellm_users()
await self.reset_budget_for_litellm_teams()
await self.reset_budget_for_litellm_budget_table()
await self.reset_budget_windows()
```

Current queued writes in `litellm/repositories/unit_of_work.py`:

```python
self.table.update(
    where={"token": token},
    data={"spend": 0, "budget_reset_at": budget_reset_at},
)
```

The user and team writes have the same unconditional shape. There is no lock acquisition in `reset_budget_job.py`, and the write does not require the row to remain due

The deterministic database ordering is:

```text
A: UPDATE spend=0, budget_reset_at=future
request: UPDATE spend = spend + 2
B: UPDATE spend=0, budget_reset_at=future
final spend: 0
```

A live two-pod proxy was not started during this audit. The lost update is the direct result of two unconditional successful writes around an increment

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

v1.98.0, commit 46ffc2ab7d4b29889b54f9ccefd78f995a0e53ff

title: [Bug]: CheckBatchCost can apply completed batch spend more than once
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate

### What happened?

The enterprise `CheckBatchCost` poller applies the full cost of a completed managed batch before it writes `batch_processed=true`. The spend side effect and the processed flag are not atomic, the flag update is not compare-and-swap, and the poller has no cross-pod lock

If the final managed-object update fails, the next poll selects the same `batch_processed=false` row and bills it again. If two proxy replicas select the row concurrently, both can emit spend before either writes the flag

The emitted success callback increments live Redis budget counters and queues SQL increments for key, user, team, organization, end-user, and daily spend. A duplicate spend-log request id does not roll those other increments back

Expected behavior is exactly-once accounting for each managed batch, including concurrent pollers and retry after a database timeout

### User Flow

Before a fix: a batch user is charged twice when two pollers reconcile the same completed batch

1. The user uploads JSONL with `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files` and receives a managed file id
2. The user creates a batch with `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches` and receives a managed batch id
3. The provider completes the batch once
4. Two proxy replicas poll the still-unprocessed managed row and each records the full batch cost
5. The user opens `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs` and sees duplicated or inconsistent batch accounting
6. `GET https://litellm-domain/key/info` reports spend increased by up to twice the provider cost
7. A later `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches` can be rejected because the duplicated increment exhausted the user's budget

After a fix: only one poller can claim and account for the completed batch

1. The user uploads the same JSONL and creates the same batch
2. The provider completes the batch once
3. Two proxy replicas attempt reconciliation
4. One replica atomically claims the managed row and the other observes that it is already claimed
5. `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs` shows one billed batch
6. `GET https://litellm-domain/key/info` increases by exactly the provider cost
7. Later batch creation is blocked only when real spend reaches the configured budget

### Proof the bug occurs

Config / setup:

```yaml
general_settings:
  proxy_batch_polling_interval: 3600
litellm_settings:
  require_managed_files: true
```

Two or more proxy replicas share the same `DATABASE_URL`. `PROXY_BATCH_POLLING_ENABLED` is left at its default enabled value

Version / commit:

```text
v1.98.0, commit 46ffc2ab7d4b29889b54f9ccefd78f995a0e53ff
```

Current control-flow order in `enterprise/litellm_enterprise/proxy/common_utils/check_batch_cost.py`:

```python
tracked = await self._track_completed_batch_cost(...)
processed_models.append(tracked)

update_data = {
    "status": "complete",
    "file_object": response.model_dump_json(),
}
update_data["batch_processed"] = True
await self.prisma_client.db.litellm_managedobjecttable.update(
    where={"id": job.id},
    data=update_data,
)
```

The update failure is logged and swallowed after the spend callback has run:

```python
except Exception as db_err:
    verbose_proxy_logger.error(
        f"CheckBatchCost: failed to mark job {job.id} complete in DB: {db_err}"
    )
```

The initial read is a normal `find_many` with `batch_processed=False`. There is no `PodLockManager`, processing lease, or conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE batch_processed=false` in this file

The audit confirmed the emit line precedes the mark line and that each tracking call creates a new callback context. A live provider batch was not submitted during this audit because that would incur external cost. The race and retry are deterministic from the persisted ordering above

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

v1.98.0, commit 46ffc2ab7d4b29889b54f9ccefd78f995a0e53ff

title: [Bug]: Helm upgrade rolls new proxy pods before the migration Job completes
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate

### What happened?

The published `helm/litellm-helm` chart defaults `migrationJob.enabled=true` and `migrationJob.hooks.helm.enabled=false`. The Deployment also forces `DISABLE_SCHEMA_UPDATE=true`, so application pods cannot migrate the database themselves

On `helm upgrade`, the migration Job is therefore an ordinary resource rather than a pre-upgrade hook. Helm can update the Deployment and start the new image before the Job has completed. The new Prisma client then queries columns introduced by that image while the database still has the previous release's schema

The default replica count is one. A normal schema-bearing upgrade can replace the only serving pod with an N+1 binary against an N schema. Readiness can still pass because it does not verify every ORM model column

Expected behavior is that schema expansion completes before any N+1 proxy replica starts serving. The componentized `helm/litellm` chart already uses a `pre-install,pre-upgrade` migration hook

This is not a duplicate of #7536, which reports an existing non-hook Job not being recreated, or #16190, which reports the migration Job starting before a newly deployed database is reachable

### User Flow

Before a fix: a Helm operator gets a Ready N+1 pod while the database still has the N schema

1. The operator runs `helm upgrade litellm oci://ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-helm --set image.tag=<N+1>` with the chart defaults
2. Kubernetes starts the N+1 Deployment pod with `DISABLE_SCHEMA_UPDATE=true`
3. The migration Job has not completed yet, but `GET https://litellm-domain/health/readiness` returns 200
4. The operator sends `GET https://litellm-domain/model/info` or `GET https://litellm-domain/key/list`
5. The request returns a database error for an N+1 column that does not exist yet
6. The same route starts working only after the migration Job finishes, or remains broken if that Job fails

After a fix: Helm completes the schema expansion before creating any N+1 proxy pod

1. The operator runs the same `helm upgrade` command with the same image and values
2. Helm runs the migration Job as a blocking pre-upgrade hook
3. The Job applies the N+1 migration and exits successfully
4. Kubernetes then starts the N+1 Deployment pod
5. `GET https://litellm-domain/health/readiness` returns 200 only after the compatible pod is running
6. `GET https://litellm-domain/model/info` and `GET https://litellm-domain/key/list` return 200 throughout the serving transition

### Proof the bug occurs

Config / setup:

```yaml
replicaCount: 1
migrationJob:
  enabled: true
  hooks:
    argocd:
      enabled: true
    helm:
      enabled: false
```

Version / commit:

```text
v1.98.0, commit 46ffc2ab7d4b29889b54f9ccefd78f995a0e53ff
```

Current template evidence:

```yaml
{{- if .Values.migrationJob.hooks.helm.enabled }}
helm.sh/hook: "pre-install,pre-upgrade"
helm.sh/hook-delete-policy: "before-hook-creation"
{{- end }}
```

The Deployment separately emits:

```yaml
{{- if .Values.migrationJob.enabled }}
- name: DISABLE_SCHEMA_UPDATE
  value: "true"
{{- end }}
```

With the default values, the Job has no Helm hook annotation and the proxy cannot close the schema gap. The generated Prisma models include additive fields such as `LiteLLM_Config.last_run_at` and `reload_revision`. Querying those fields against the previous schema produces PostgreSQL's `column does not exist` error

The audit reproduced the database half of the transition by removing those additive columns from a migrated disposable PostgreSQL database and issuing the N+1 SELECT list:

```sql
SELECT "param_name", "param_value", "last_run_at", "reload_revision"
FROM "LiteLLM_Config"
WHERE "param_name" = 'general_settings';
```

```text
ERROR: column "last_run_at" does not exist
```

A Kubernetes cluster was not available in this audit, so the Helm ordering itself was confirmed from rendered-resource conditions and Helm's ordinary-resource lifecycle rather than a live `helm upgrade`

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

v1.98.0, commit 46ffc2ab7d4b29889b54f9ccefd78f995a0e53ff

title: [Bug]: Required PR checks can pass when schema.prisma has no matching migration
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate

### What happened?

A pull request can change `schema.prisma` without adding equivalent SQL under `litellm-proxy-extras/litellm_proxy_extras/migrations`, and the required GitHub Actions path can still pass

The only test that asks Prisma whether the committed migration history produces the current datamodel is `tests/proxy_migration_tests/test_db_schema_migration.py`. It skips without `DATABASE_URL`, and no GitHub Actions unit job starts Postgres for it

The GitHub Actions substitute, `test_aaaaaschema_compatibility`, runs `git show main:schema.prisma` but does not check the command's exit status. The reusable unit workflow uses the default depth-1 checkout, so `main` is normally absent. The missing schema becomes an empty string, the old-model map becomes empty, and the test reports no breaking changes

Even with a full `main` ref, the test treats a newly added required field as informational. That is the common failure mode where the generated client expects a column that no migration creates

Expected behavior is a required pull-request check that applies all committed migrations to an empty PostgreSQL database and fails when `prisma migrate diff --from-url ... --to-schema-datamodel schema.prisma --exit-code` detects drift

### User Flow

Before a fix: a proxy operator upgrades to a release whose generated client expects a column that the shipped migrations never created

1. A maintainer merges a pull request after every required GitHub Actions check passes
2. The operator deploys that release and its migration Job completes because there is no new SQL migration to apply
3. The operator sends `GET https://litellm-domain/key/list` with an admin key
4. The proxy queries through the new generated client and returns a 500 database error because the expected column is missing
5. Requests that touch the affected model continue failing until the operator authors and applies corrective SQL

After a fix: the same incomplete schema pull request is blocked before an operator can deploy it

1. A maintainer opens the same pull request with a `schema.prisma` field and no matching SQL migration
2. The required migration-diff job creates an empty PostgreSQL database and applies every committed migration
3. Prisma reports datamodel drift and the pull request check fails
4. The maintainer adds the missing migration and the check passes
5. The operator upgrades and `GET https://litellm-domain/key/list` returns 200 against the migrated schema

### Proof the bug occurs

Config / setup:

```text
GitHub Actions reusable unit workflow: .github/workflows/_test-unit-base.yml
Checkout: actions/checkout with no fetch-depth override
Migration oracle: tests/proxy_migration_tests/test_db_schema_migration.py
```

Version / commit:

```text
v1.98.0, commit 46ffc2ab7d4b29889b54f9ccefd78f995a0e53ff
```

Deterministic evidence from the current tree:

```python
def get_schema_from_branch(branch: str = "main") -> str:
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "show", f"{branch}:schema.prisma"],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    )
    return result.stdout
```

The caller parses that returned string without checking `result.returncode`. On the depth-1 checkout shape used by the workflow, the audit reproduced:

```shell
$ git show main:schema.prisma
fatal: invalid object name 'main'

$ python -c 'from tests.proxy_unit_tests.test_db_schema_changes import get_schema_from_branch, parse_model_fields; print(repr(get_schema_from_branch("main"))); print(parse_model_fields(get_schema_from_branch("main")))'
''
{}
```

The actual migration oracle is explicitly disabled without a database:

```python
@pytest.mark.skipif(
    "DATABASE_URL" not in os.environ,
    reason="requires a postgres database (DATABASE_URL)",
)
```

The current GitHub Actions workflows do not set `DATABASE_URL` for that test. CircleCI has a PostgreSQL-backed `schema_migration_check`, but it is not the required GitHub Actions pull-request gate

This validation did not deploy a live proxy because the defect is in pull-request assurance. The production consequence follows when an incomplete schema change is merged and deployed

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Other

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

v1.98.0, commit 46ffc2ab7d4b29889b54f9ccefd78f995a0e53ff

title: [Bug] Databricks provider drops Anthropic prompt-cache token counts when streaming
body:
**LiteLLM version:** v1.96.0 (also reproduced on v1.90.2)
**Provider:** `databricks` (Azure Databricks Foundation Model API, Claude models)
**Model:** `system.ai.claude-opus-5`

## What happens

With `stream: false`, prompt-cache token counts are returned correctly.
With `stream: true`, `cache_creation_input_tokens` and `cache_read_input_tokens` are
absent from the usage object entirely — not zero, absent.

Because spend is computed from the usage object, every streamed Databricks request is
costed at the full input rate even when it was served from cache. For an
Anthropic-format agent client that always streams and relies on prompt caching, this
makes reported spend diverge sharply from actual provider cost.

Importantly, **caching itself works** — only the accounting is broken. See
"Caching is actually working" below.

## Reproduction

Identical payload, only `stream` differs. Fallbacks and retries disabled.

```python
body = {
    "model": "claude-opus",              # -> databricks/system.ai.claude-opus-5
    "max_tokens": 8,
    "system": [{"type": "text", "text": CORPUS,          # ~9.6k tokens
                "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}}],
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with OK."}],
    "disable_fallbacks": True,
    "num_retries": 0,
}
```

**Non-streaming — correct:**

```
1st (cold)   input_tokens=11   cache_creation_input_tokens=9603   cache_read_input_tokens=None
2nd (warm)   input_tokens=11   cache_creation_input_tokens=None   cache_read_input_tokens=9603
```

**Streaming — cache fields missing from every event:**

```
message_start   usage: {"input_tokens": 0,  "output_tokens": ...}
message_delta   usage: {"input_tokens": 11, "output_tokens": 1}
```

### Same-endpoint control, with `stream_options`

To rule out `stream_options` as the cause, the following ran against
`/v1/chat/completions` with `"stream_options": {"include_usage": true}` on both
providers — identical payload, identical proxy, only the provider differs:

```
anthropic  cold   prompt_tokens_details: {"cached_tokens": 0,     "text_tokens": 10, "cache_write_tokens": ...}
anthropic  warm   prompt_tokens_details: {"cached_tokens": 13304, "text_tokens": 10, "cache_write_tokens": ...}

databricks cold   (no prompt_tokens_details)   prompt_tokens: 7015
databricks warm   (no prompt_tokens_details)   prompt_tokens: 7015
```

The Anthropic provider is correct in both streaming and non-streaming modes.

Note also that **without** `stream_options: {"include_usage": true}` the Databricks
streaming response contains **no usage chunk at all**. Setting
`general_settings.always_include_stream_usage: true` restores the usage chunk but
still yields no cache fields — so the gap is in response parsing, not in the request
or in `stream_options` handling.

## Caching is actually working

A streamed request with `cache_control` was sent, then the same corpus was sent
non-streaming. The non-streaming call reported `cached_tokens: 13303` on its *first*
call — i.e. the preceding streaming request had populated the cache. So streaming
requests participate in caching normally; the tokens are simply never surfaced in the
usage object.

This means reported cost for streamed Databricks traffic is inflated relative to the
provider's actual metering.

## Cause

In `litellm/llms/databricks/chat/transformation.py`:

- **Line 643** (non-streaming) works only incidentally:
  ```python
  setattr(model_response, "usage", Usage(**completion_response["usage"]))
  ```
  The provider's whole `usage` dict is splatted into `Usage`, so cache keys survive
  because they happen to be present — not because they are handled.

- **Line 665**, `class DatabricksChatResponseIterator(BaseModelResponseIterator)`, has
  no equivalent. Grepping the entire `litellm/llms/databricks/` tree returns **zero**
  matches for `cache_creation`, `cache_read`, or `cached_tokens`, whereas
  `litellm/llms/anthropic/chat/transformation.py` handles them explicitly.

`DatabricksConfig` inherits from `AnthropicConfig`
(`class DatabricksConfig(DatabricksBase, OpenAILikeChatConfig, AnthropicConfig)`,
line 152), but the streaming response iterator is a separate class that does not
inherit Anthropic's usage parsing.

## Expected

`DatabricksChatResponseIterator` should extract `cache_creation_input_tokens` and
`cache_read_input_tokens` from streaming chunks and populate
`usage.prompt_tokens_details`, matching both the Anthropic provider and the Databricks
non-streaming path.

## Impact

Spend tracking is wrong for any streaming Databricks request that uses prompt caching
— which is every request from an Anthropic-format agent client. Cache-aware pricing
(`cache_read_input_token_cost`, `cache_creation_input_token_cost`) is configured on
the deployment and applied correctly on the Anthropic provider, but cannot take effect
here because the token counts never reach the cost calculator.

## Related

Separate bug in the same provider, filed as #36931 — the Databricks request path emits
LiteLLM's internal `thinking_blocks` field instead of Databricks' documented
`reasoning` content block, breaking multi-turn extended thinking. Independent of this
issue.
author: pokepoke81

title: [Bug] Databricks provider sends internal `thinking_blocks` field instead of the documented `reasoning` content block, breaking multi-turn extended thinking
body:
**LiteLLM version:** v1.96.0
**Provider:** `databricks` (Azure Databricks Foundation Model API)
**Models:** `system.ai.claude-opus-5`, `system.ai.claude-sonnet-5`

## What happens

Multi-turn conversations with extended thinking fail as soon as an assistant message
containing thinking content is replayed as history:

```
litellm.BadRequestError: DatabricksException - {"error_code":"BAD_REQUEST",
  "message":"{\"message\":\"messages.98.thinking_blocks: Extra inputs are not permitted\"}"}
```

The first turn always succeeds. The failing index tracks conversation length — it is
whichever message is the first assistant turn carrying thinking content.

## Cause

`litellm/llms/databricks/chat/transformation.py` (~line 499) extracts reasoning
content from Databricks responses into LiteLLM's internal `thinking_blocks`
representation. There is no corresponding conversion on the **request** path, so on
the next turn `thinking_blocks` is emitted as a message-level field. Databricks
validates strictly and rejects unknown message fields.

## This is not a Databricks limitation

Databricks accepts reasoning content on input. I verified the wire format empirically by
capturing a real reasoning block from `system.ai.claude-opus-5` and replaying it in each
candidate shape. Only one is accepted:

| Assistant content block shape | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `{"type": "thinking", "thinking": ..., "signature": ...}` (Anthropic native) | rejected, `Failed to parse ContentItem` |
| `{"type": "reasoning", "content": [{"type": "reasoning_text", ...}], "encrypted_content": ...}` | rejected, `Expecting one non-null Summary` |
| `{"type": "reasoning", "summary": [{"type": "summary_text", "text": ..., "signature": ...}]}` | **accepted** |
| message-level `thinking_blocks` (current behaviour) | rejected, `Extra inputs are not permitted` |

So the target format is a `reasoning` content block carrying a `summary` array:

```json
{
  "type": "reasoning",
  "summary": [
    { "type": "summary_text", "text": "...", "signature": "<opaque provider signature>" }
  ]
}
```

Note that Databricks' published docs for multi-turn reasoning describe
`content` / `reasoning_text` with `encrypted_content`, which the endpoint actively
rejects. The shape asserted by the existing test in
`tests/test_litellm/llms/databricks/chat/test_databricks_chat_transformation.py`
is the correct one, and matches what the provider's own response parsing already produces

The `signature` must be replayed unmodified. Dropping it loses the reasoning chain even
when the request is accepted

## Expected behaviour

On the request path, the Databricks provider should convert LiteLLM
`thinking_blocks` into the documented `reasoning` content block, mapping the
Anthropic thinking `signature` to `encrypted_content` so reasoning continuity is
preserved.

Note that **merely stripping `thinking_blocks` is only a partial fix**: it clears the
400 but discards the reasoning chain, which is the behaviour Databricks explicitly
describes as "the model can't reason over its earlier thinking."

## Control

The Anthropic provider round-trips thinking correctly in the same LiteLLM version,
with the same client and the same conversation — only the `databricks` provider
fails. So the round trip is clearly within LiteLLM's remit.

## Related prior issues

- **#15758** — same error. Closed by the reporter within a day, attributing it to
  Databricks (*"this is a Databricks issue and cannot be fixed with code"*). Per the
  documentation above, that attribution is incorrect and the bug is still present.
- **#9790** — feature request for exactly this, went stale and was auto-closed. The
  reporter there used `summary` / `summary_text`, which is not the documented schema
  either, so that failure was also a format mismatch rather than a missing feature.

## Reproduction

1. Configure a `databricks` deployment for `system.ai.claude-opus-5`.
2. Send a request with extended thinking enabled.
3. Append the assistant response, including reasoning content, to the message list.
4. Send a second request with that history → 400 as above.

## Environment note

Requests reach the endpoint via `/ai-gateway/mlflow/v1/chat/completions`. Separately
observed on the same models: `temperature`, `top_p`, and `top_k` are rejected with
400 by both `claude-opus-5` and `claude-sonnet-5` (Databricks documents this for
Sonnet 5 only). Not related to this bug, but relevant to anyone configuring these
deployments — `drop_params` handles it.
author: pokepoke81

title: [Bug]: Gemini reasoning/thinking content leaks into output_text for /responses with reasoning.effort=medium|high, breaking strict json_schema
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

Calling `litellm.responses()` for a Gemini model with a strict `json_schema` output format works correctly at `reasoning.effort="low"` (or unset), returning clean, schema-conformant JSON. Raising `reasoning.effort` to `"medium"` or `"high"` breaks this: the model's raw chain-of-thought narrative is returned as the `output_text` / message content instead of the requested JSON, and the `strict: true` json_schema constraint is effectively ignored.

Example actual output at `reasoning.effort="high"` (this is the full `output[0].content[0].text`, not a summary):

```
**My Approach to Crafting the JSON Response**

Okay, here's how I'm approaching this. The task is straightforward: generate a JSON response that
says "hello" and gives a score of 1. It needs to be perfectly formatted JSON and nothing else - no
extra text, no markdown, no comments, just valid, parseable...

[... continues for 400+ tokens of first-person reasoning narrative, sometimes including its own
markdown code fence with a correct JSON example buried in the middle, before or without ever
emitting the JSON as the actual final answer ...]
```

This strongly looks like the model's "thinking"/reasoning content is not being kept separate from the final answer content when Gemini is accessed through the Responses API surface (there's no native `litellm/llms/gemini/responses/` provider config - I believe this goes through a chat-completions-style bridge). For comparison, OpenAI's own reasoning models keep reasoning content out of the final message content (tracked only via `usage.output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`) - Gemini's thinking content is not being handled the same way here, and it also appears to override/ignore the requested strict `json_schema` format once reasoning is engaged at higher effort.

`reasoning_tokens` in the usage response does increase correctly with effort level (e.g. 0 at low, 225-400+ at medium/high), confirming the model *is* being asked to think more - the bug is specifically that that content ends up in the answer instead of being separated out, and that it overrides the structured-output constraint.

Reproduced identically on both **v1.90.0** and **v1.96.0** (six minor versions apart), so this isn't a recent regression - it looks like a long-standing gap in how Gemini's thinking output is handled via the Responses API bridge.

### Steps to Reproduce

```python
import litellm

schema = {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {"greeting": {"type": "string"}, "score": {"type": "number"}},
    "required": ["greeting", "score"],
    "additionalProperties": False,
}

for effort in ["low", "medium", "high"]:
    response = litellm.responses(
        model="gemini-3.5-flash",
        instructions="You are a helpful assistant. Respond only with JSON matching the schema.",
        input=[{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "input_text", "text": "Say hello and give a score of 1."}]}],
        max_output_tokens=512,
        reasoning={"effort": effort},
        text={"format": {"type": "json_schema", "name": "smoke_test", "strict": True, "schema": schema}},
        api_base="http://localhost:4000",  # a real LiteLLM Proxy instance, gemini-3.5-flash mapped to gemini/gemini-3.5-flash
        api_key="sk-...",
    )
    text = response.output[0].content[0].text
    print(effort, "-> valid JSON prefix:", text.strip().startswith("{"), "| len:", len(text))
```

Expected output:

```
low -> valid JSON prefix: True | len: ~40
medium -> valid JSON prefix: True | len: ~40
high -> valid JSON prefix: True | len: ~40
```

Actual output:

```
low -> valid JSON prefix: True | len: 41
medium -> valid JSON prefix: False | len: 1130
high -> valid JSON prefix: False | len: 1465
```

### Relevant log output

```shell
N/A - no error is raised; the response is returned successfully with status "completed", just
with reasoning prose as the content instead of the requested structured JSON.
```

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Responses API / Gemini provider

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

v1.96.0 (also reproduced on v1.90.0)

### Twitter / LinkedIn details

_No response_
author: Jeevan-threev

title: [Bug]: interactions.create() silently drops response_format when routed via litellm_proxy (Gemini)
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

When `USE_LITELLM_PROXY=true` (or `litellm.use_litellm_proxy=True`) is set process-wide, `litellm.interactions.create()` for a Gemini model silently loses its `response_format` (JSON schema / mime type constraint) with no error or warning, and the model falls back to free-text output.

Root cause, traced through the source:

1. `get_llm_provider()` (`litellm/litellm_core_utils/get_llm_provider_logic.py`) checks `LiteLLMProxyChatConfig._should_use_litellm_proxy_by_default()` **first, unconditionally**, before looking at any explicitly-passed `custom_llm_provider`. With `USE_LITELLM_PROXY=true` set, this forces `custom_llm_provider="litellm_proxy"` for *every* litellm call in the process, including `interactions.create()`.
2. `get_provider_interactions_api_config()` (`litellm/interactions/utils.py`) only recognizes `provider == "gemini"`. For `"litellm_proxy"` it returns `None`.
3. Back in `litellm/interactions/main.py`, when `interactions_api_config is None`, the call **silently bridges to `litellm.responses()`** via `LiteLLMResponsesInteractionsHandler` instead of raising or warning.
4. That bridge's request transform, `transform_interactions_request_to_responses_request()` (`litellm/interactions/litellm_responses_transformation/transformation.py`), maps `system_instruction`, `input`, `tools`, and parts of `generation_config` — but has **no handling for `response_format` at all**. It's dropped entirely, silently.

Net effect: a caller who explicitly requested strict JSON-schema output via the Interactions API gets back ordinary free-text (Gemini then wraps its answer in a markdown code fence, as it typically does without an explicit JSON constraint), with no exception and no log line indicating the constraint was dropped. This is especially easy to hit by accident: `USE_LITELLM_PROXY` is a reasonable thing to set globally so that `litellm.responses()`/`litellm.completion()` route through a self-hosted LiteLLM Proxy, but doing so silently breaks the Interactions API for the same process.

Confirmed present in every version I checked, `1.82.0` through the current latest `1.96.2` (checked wheel/sdist contents directly) — `litellm/llms/litellm_proxy/interactions/` does not exist in any of them, unlike `litellm/llms/litellm_proxy/{chat,responses,image_generation,image_edit,skills}/` which do.

### Steps to Reproduce

```python
import os
os.environ["USE_LITELLM_PROXY"] = "true"
import litellm

response = litellm.interactions.create(
    model="gemini-3.5-flash",
    system_instruction="Respond only with JSON matching the schema.",
    input=[{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "Say hello and give a score of 1."}]}],
    response_format={
        "type": "text",
        "mime_type": "application/json",
        "schema": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {"greeting": {"type": "string"}, "score": {"type": "number"}},
            "required": ["greeting", "score"],
        },
    },
    generation_config={"max_output_tokens": 512},
    api_base="http://localhost:4000",   # a real LiteLLM Proxy instance
    api_key="sk-...",                    # a valid virtual key for that proxy
)
```

Expected: request reaches the proxy's `/interactions`-equivalent handling (or, if unsupported, the fallback should still honor `response_format`), returning clean JSON.

Actual: request is silently rerouted to `/responses` with `response_format` dropped; the returned text is unconstrained free text (often markdown-fenced JSON, not raw JSON), and `json.loads()` on it fails intermittently depending on how the model chooses to format its answer.

### Relevant log output

```shell
# No warning/error is logged - the drop is completely silent. Confirmed via the local proxy's
# access log: with USE_LITELLM_PROXY=true, an interactions.create() call for a Gemini model never
# produces a "/interactions" (or equivalent) hit on the proxy - only "/responses" hits appear,
# confirming the silent bridge.
```

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy / Interactions API

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

v1.96.0 (also reproduced on v1.96.2; confirmed present via source inspection back through v1.82.0)

### Twitter / LinkedIn details

_No response_
author: Jeevan-threev

title: [Bug]: False BudgetExceededError under sustained load — 'Current cost' = max_budget + recent spend, no Redis, self-heals in ~2 min
body:
### What happened

During sustained batch runs (~100-130 requests over ~40 min, single client, mix of `/v1/ocr` Mistral passthrough, Gemini `generateContent` passthrough and Anthropic passthrough), the proxy starts returning `429 budget_exceeded` near the end of the run, with a reported `Current cost` that matches **no real aggregate**. The reported value is always `max_budget + (small recent spend)`, and the condition **self-heals in about 2 minutes** without any intervention: a retry with 15s/30s/60s backoff fails 3 times, then the 4th attempt succeeds.

We reproduced this on **v1.88.1** and again on **v1.96.2** after upgrading, and once earlier when our global cap was 20 instead of 50 — the phantom value tracked the cap each time.

### Occurrences

| Date | Proxy version | Configured cap | Error message excerpt | Real spend at that moment |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-07-01 | 1.88.1 | 20 (global) | `Budget has been exceeded! Current cost: 20.013879769999956, Max budget: 20` | a few cents that day |
| 2026-08-14 AM | 1.88.1 | 50 (key + global) | `Budget has been exceeded! Key=<hash> Current cost: 51.0512, Max budget: 50.0`, then `Current cost: 50.014505` on the two retries | key spend that day ~1.05 USD |
| 2026-08-14 PM | 1.96.2 | 50 (key + global) | `Budget has been exceeded! Key=<alias> (sk-...) Current cost: 50.024508499999996, Max budget: 50.0` | key spend that day ~1.1 USD |

In each case `Current cost - max_budget` equals the key's genuine recent spend (e.g. `51.0512 - 50 = 1.0512` ≈ the 1.05 USD actually spent by the run so far). It looks like an in-memory spend counter transiently gets seeded/inflated with the `max_budget` value itself.

### What the database said at the same time

Checked immediately around the 2026-08-14 AM occurrence:

- `LiteLLM_VerificationToken.spend` for the key: **1.07**
- `sum(spend)` in `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` for that key, last 30 days: **1.59**
- `sum(spend)` in `LiteLLM_SpendLogs`, all keys, all time: **24.90**
- No individual SpendLogs row above 0.04
- `/global/spend`: 4.24 / 50

Nothing anywhere near 50, and no row disappeared afterwards. The inflated value existed only in memory and was gone once the periodic DB resync ran (the 4th retry, ~2 min after the first 429, passed; `/key/info` afterwards reported the correct small spend).

### Setup

- Docker `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:main-stable`, **single instance**, **no Redis** (in-memory cache only)
- Postgres-backed (`database_url` set), default batch-write settings
- `litellm_settings`: `max_budget: 50`, `budget_duration: 30d`, `turn_off_message_logging: true`, `drop_params: true`, `telemetry: false`
- Virtual key with `max_budget: 50`, `budget_duration: 30d`, model ACL
- `router_settings`: `simple-shuffle`, `num_retries: 0`, `allowed_fails: 0`, `cooldown_time: 60`, cross-provider fallbacks configured
- Load pattern when it triggers: ~100+ requests spread over ~40 min through one virtual key, several requests in flight concurrently (bounded page-level concurrency). Light traffic (20 sequential probes) never triggers it.

### Expected behavior

Budget checks compare against actual spend. A request should not be rejected with `Current cost ≈ max_budget + real spend` while the durable stores all agree spend is ~2% of the cap.

### Possibly related

- #27735 (stale spend in BudgetExceededError while `/key/info` disagrees) — same symptom family, but our value is not stale, it is inflated by exactly `max_budget` and self-corrects
- #30460 (Redis counters inflating) — we run without Redis, so the in-memory path can inflate on its own

### Are you a ML Ops Team?

No

### What LiteLLM version are you on?

v1.96.2 (also reproduced on v1.88.1)

title: [Bug]: responses() crashes with TypeError 'int object is not iterable' when input is numeric instead of returning 400
body:
## Description

`litellm.responses()` crashes with `TypeError: 'int' object is not iterable` when `input` is a non-string, non-list type (e.g. integer, float, bool, None, dict). Instead of returning a clear validation error (HTTP 400), the TypeError propagates through `exception_type()` which has no `status_code`, falls through to `APIConnectionError`, and returns HTTP 500.

## Repro

```python
import litellm

response = litellm.responses(
    model="gpt-5.1",
    input=12345,  # integer instead of string or list
)
```

## Stack trace

```text
File "litellm/responses/main.py", line 588, in _apply_prompt_management_to_responses_call
    for item in input
TypeError: 'int' object is not iterable
```

## Root cause

In `litellm/responses/main.py`, `_apply_prompt_management_to_responses_call()` (both the async branch in `aresponses()` and the sync helper) checks only `isinstance(input, str)`:

```python
if isinstance(input, str):
    client_input = [{"role": "user", "content": input}]
else:
    client_input = [
        item
        for item in input  # ← crashes when input is not iterable
        if isinstance(item, dict) and "role" in item
    ]
```

When `input` is not a string, it assumes it is iterable. Non-string, non-list types (int, float, bool, None, dict) raise TypeError during `for item in input`.

## Expected behavior

Invalid `input` types should raise `BadRequestError` with a descriptive message (e.g. "input must be a string or list of input items, got int") so the proxy returns HTTP 400 instead of HTTP 500.

## Suggested fix

Add a type guard before iteration:

```python
if isinstance(input, str):
    client_input = [{"role": "user", "content": input}]
elif not isinstance(input, list):
    raise BadRequestError(
        message=f"'input' must be a string or list of input items, got {type(input).__name__}",
        model=model,
        llm_provider=custom_llm_provider or "unknown",
    )
else:
    client_input = [
        item
        for item in input
        if isinstance(item, dict) and "role" in item
    ]
```

This applies at two locations in `litellm/responses/main.py`:
1. The async prompt-management branch (line ~472)
2. The sync `_apply_prompt_management_to_responses_call` helper (line ~583)

## Impact

- Invalid client requests are misclassified as provider/system failures
- Client receives retryable-looking 500 instead of non-retryable 400
- LiteLLM retry/cooldown machinery may treat this as a deployment failure, which can amplify impact

## Environment

- LiteLLM version: v1.92.0 (observed in production; also present on current main)
- Endpoint: `POST /v1/responses` / `POST /responses`

title: [Bug]: `acount_tokens()` silently returns `total_tokens=0` for Vertex AI Gemini models
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

### What happened

`litellm.acount_tokens()` returns `total_tokens=0` with `error=False` for any
`vertex_ai/gemini-*` model when called with `messages` (the documented usage). The
messages are never sent to Vertex, and the failure is not surfaced — neither as an
exception, nor via the `error` flag, nor by falling back to local counting.

### Reproduction

Requires ADC for a project with Vertex AI enabled.

```python
import asyncio, os
import litellm

os.environ["VERTEXAI_PROJECT"] = "<your-project>"
os.environ["VERTEXAI_LOCATION"] = "us-central1"


async def main():
    result = await litellm.acount_tokens(
        model="vertex_ai/gemini-2.5-flash",
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello, how are you? " * 50}],
    )
    print(result.total_tokens, repr(result.tokenizer_type), result.error)


asyncio.run(main())
```

**Expected:** ~301 (the count Vertex's `:countTokens` returns for this text), with
`tokenizer_type` indicating the provider API — or, if provider counting is unavailable, the
documented local-tiktoken fallback.

**Actual:**

```
0 '' False
```

That the endpoint itself is reachable and correct with the same credentials, model and
location is easy to confirm — passing Gemini-format `contents` directly to the same handler
works:

```python
from litellm.llms.vertex_ai.count_tokens.handler import VertexAITokenCounter

await VertexAITokenCounter().acount_tokens(
    model="gemini-2.5-flash",
    contents=[{"role": "user", "parts": [{"text": "Hello, how are you? " * 50}]}],
    vertex_project=os.environ["VERTEXAI_PROJECT"],
    vertex_location="us-central1",
)
# {'totalTokens': 301, 'totalBillableCharacters': 800,
#  'promptTokensDetails': [{'modality': 'TEXT', 'tokenCount': 301}]}
```

### Root cause

Three things compound, all still present on `v1.96.2`:

1. **`messages` is never converted to `contents`.** `litellm/main.py::acount_tokens`
   unconditionally passes `contents=None` to the provider counter
   ([`main.py:8753`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.96.2/litellm/main.py#L8753)),
   leaving conversion to the provider.

2. **The Vertex Gemini branch ignores `messages`.**
   `VertexAITokenCounter.count_tokens`
   ([`llms/vertex_ai/common_utils.py:1100`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.96.2/litellm/llms/vertex_ai/common_utils.py#L1100))
   splits on `is_vertex_partner_model`. The partner-model branch (Claude on Vertex) forwards
   `messages=messages or []` and works correctly. The Gemini branch builds
   `{"model": ..., "contents": contents}` ([line 1174](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.96.2/litellm/llms/vertex_ai/common_utils.py#L1174))
   and never reads `messages`, so the request body posted is `{"contents": null}`
   ([`llms/gemini/count_tokens/handler.py:133`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.96.2/litellm/llms/gemini/count_tokens/handler.py#L133)).

3. **The empty response reads as a valid answer of zero.** Vertex accepts
   `{"contents": null}` with HTTP 200 and a response carrying no `totalTokens`, so
   `total_tokens=result.get("totalTokens", 0)`
   ([line 1183](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.96.2/litellm/llms/vertex_ai/common_utils.py#L1183))
   yields `0`. Because the result is non-`None` and `error` is falsy, `acount_tokens`
   returns it immediately and the local-tiktoken fallback is never reached.

The proxy endpoints are not an alternative path: `TokenCountRequest` exposes `contents` as a
separate field, i.e. Google-format callers are expected to supply `contents` themselves.
There is no `messages` → `contents` conversion anywhere in the token-counting code.

### Why the silent zero matters

The natural use of this API is a pre-flight guard against context-window overflow. A
silently-zero count inverts the guard: every payload appears to fit, and the overflow
surfaces later as a provider `400` on the real request. A raised exception, or the
documented fallback, would both be safe; returning `0` is not.

### Suggested fix

Convert in the Vertex Gemini branch, so the SDK and the proxy are both covered:

```python
else:
    from litellm.llms.vertex_ai.count_tokens.handler import VertexAITokenCounter
    from litellm.llms.vertex_ai.gemini.transformation import (
        _gemini_convert_messages_with_history,
    )

    if contents is None and messages is not None:
        contents = _gemini_convert_messages_with_history(messages=messages)
    ...
```

and treat a response without `totalTokens` as a failure rather than a zero, so the
documented local fallback is reached:

```python
    if result is not None and "totalTokens" in result:
        return TokenCountResponse(...)
    return None
```

### Related, lower priority

**`system` and `tools` are dropped on the Vertex Gemini path.** `acount_tokens` accepts both,
but the handler posts only `{"contents": ...}`. Vertex's `:countTokens` does honour the other
request fields — measured on `gemini-3.6-flash`, global endpoint:

| request body | `totalTokens` |
| --- | --- |
| `contents` only | 7 |
| `contents` + `systemInstruction` | 107 |
| `contents` + `tools` | 31 |

So an assembled prompt is under-counted by however much its system instruction and tool
declarations cost. Note that `_gemini_convert_messages_with_history` folds a `system` message
into the user `contents`, which counts the text but not the `systemInstruction` framing.

**The local fallback has no Gemini tokenizer.** `_select_tokenizer_helper`
([`utils.py:1945`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.96.2/litellm/utils.py#L1945))
special-cases cohere `command-r`, pre-`claude-3` Anthropic and llama-2/3; everything else
falls through to tiktoken `cl100k`. For Gemini that is substantially optimistic on
token-dense input, which is what makes the silent fallback in issue 3 above consequential.
Measured against the API on `gemini-3.6-flash`:

| input | `litellm.token_counter` (local) | Vertex `:countTokens` | error |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| prose, 72k chars | 17,939 | 19,344 | 7% optimistic |
| dense numeric, 1.0M chars | 528,006 | 959,999 | **45% optimistic** |

Documenting `local_tokenizer` as approximate-only for Gemini would help; a Gemini tokenizer
would help more.

### Environment

- litellm **1.82.3** — all behaviour above reproduced live against Vertex AI.
- litellm **1.96.2** (latest at time of writing) — verified by source inspection to be
  unchanged in all four locations cited; not run live.
- Python 3.12, Vertex AI Gemini via ADC (`gemini-2.5-flash` regional, `gemini-3.6-flash` and
  `gemini-3.7-flash` on the `global` endpoint — all three affected, all three counted
  correctly via the direct-`contents` workaround).


### User Flow

See above

### Proof the bug occurs

See above

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

SDK (litellm Python package)

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

v1.96.2

### Twitter / LinkedIn details

_No response_
