title: Mid-conversation system-role hoist invalidates the entire prompt-cache prefix (AnthropicMessagesConfig)
body:
## Summary

`AnthropicMessagesConfig._normalize_system_role_messages` (introduced in #33807) hoists mid-conversation `role: "system"` messages into the top-level `system` field for Claude models without `supports_mid_conversation_system` (pre-4.8 generation). This avoids the 400 those models throw on partner endpoints (Vertex, Azure Foundry, Bedrock Invoke) — but the hoist itself invalidates the entire cached prompt prefix on every turn a reminder appears, which is exactly the cost [mid-conversation system messages](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-system-messages) are designed to avoid.

## Why the hoist breaks caching

Per Anthropic's docs, prompt caching hashes the request prefix in order `tools` → `system` → `messages`, and a cache hit requires everything up to the breakpoint to match byte-for-byte. The `system` field sits early in that order, so any change to it — including appending a hoisted message — invalidates the cache for the system prompt *and every cached message after it*, not just the new content.

Current code (`litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/messages/transformation.py`, at `6a919aec6a` on `main`):

```python
else:
    hoisted = [m for m in messages if self._is_system_role_message(m)]
    remaining = [m for m in messages if not self._is_system_role_message(m)]
if hoisted:
    anthropic_messages_request["messages"] = remaining
system_content: Final = [
    block
    for source in (
        anthropic_messages_request.get("system"),
        *(m.get("content") for m in hoisted),
    )
    for block in self._as_system_content_blocks(source)
]
```

Every system-role message anywhere in `messages` gets pulled out and folded into `system` on every request (LiteLLM re-derives the downstream payload from the client's full history each call). The turn a *new* reminder first appears, `system`'s content changes for the first time since the last request — full cache miss on that call, reprocessing the entire prior conversation.

## Measured impact (real Vertex AI traffic, unflagged model)

| | current (hoist) | proposed (convert-in-place, see below) |
|---|---|---|
| Reminder-turn `cache_read_input_tokens` | 5265 | 6973 (full prior history preserved) |
| Reminder-turn `cache_creation_input_tokens` | 1746 | 60 |
| Follow-up turn `cache_read_input_tokens` | 7011 | 7033 |

Both variants return `200` — this isn't about the correctness fix from #33807, which works fine. It's specifically the caching side effect of *how* it avoids the 400.

## Proposed fix

Since the model itself can't accept `role: "system"` in `messages` at all (that's the actual constraint being worked around), and the hoist target (`system`) sits earlier in the cache hash than `messages`, moving the offending message *anywhere* in `system` will always cost the full prefix. Instead: for unflagged models, mutate the message's `role` to `"user"` **in place** (same position in `messages`) rather than moving it to `system`. Nothing before that position changes, so an existing cache breakpoint still hits; only the new message needs fresh processing — the same cost as any ordinary new turn.

I have this working as a local patch with the measurements above, happy to open a PR if that's useful. One tradeoff worth surfacing first: converting to `role: "user"` loses Claude's "system beats a conflicting user instruction" priority for that specific message, compared to a true system-role turn. For models that don't support the feature at all, there may not be a way to fully avoid that tradeoff — but it seemed worth confirming that's an acceptable direction before sending a PR, given it's a behavior change beyond just fixing the 400.

## Environment

- litellm `main` @ `6a919aec6a2a0c54cc6a2e6f67ff7b236a3a2573`
- Reproduced against real `vertex_ai/` Claude deployments (unflagged, pre-4.8 generation) with the Claude Agent SDK's `mid-conversation-system-2026-04-07` reminder shape
- Related: #33807 (introduced the current model-aware hoist), #31452 (earlier draft of the same base-class idea, predates #33807, does not address caching)

title: [Bug]: `_should_start_new_content_block` crashes on empty-`choices` chunk (`/v1/messages`, non-Anthropic backend)
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

`streaming_iterator.py`'s `_should_start_new_content_block` accesses `chunk.choices[0]` unconditionally. Some OpenAI-format backends send a usage-only chunk with `choices: []` near stream end. This chunk crashes the adapter.

### Traceback

```
IndexError: list index out of range
  File ".../litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/adapters/streaming_iterator.py", line 262, in __anext__
    should_start_new_block = self._should_start_new_content_block(chunk)
  File ".../litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/adapters/streaming_iterator.py", line 474, in _should_start_new_content_block
    if chunk.choices[0].finish_reason is not None:
       ~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^
IndexError: list index out of range
```

### Impact

Stream ends without `message_delta`/`message_stop`. Clients relying on final usage lose token-consumption tracking.

### Scope

Present on `main` as of this writing: `_should_start_new_content_block` has no `choices` length check, and `__next__`/`__anext__` independently re-derive `is_final_chunk = chunk.choices[0].finish_reason is not None` right after — same unguarded access, same crash.

### Reproduction

`/v1/messages`, `stream=true`, backend: GLM-5.1 via LiteLLM 1.83.14, `route_type=anthropic_messages`. Model-specific — MiniMax-M2.5 on the same proxy does not trigger it, so the empty-choices usage chunk is backend-dependent.

### Related

- #27928 — same unguarded-`choices[0]` pattern, same version (1.83.14), different call site (`streaming_handler.py::raise_on_model_repetition`). Confirms the pattern is not backend- or file-specific.
- #28884 — same pattern, Vertex Gemini.

### Suggested fix

Guard `chunk.choices` before indexing in `_should_start_new_content_block` (and the two `is_final_chunk` sites): treat empty `choices` as `should_start_new_block=False` / not final, and let any `usage` on that chunk flow through the existing `will_merge_into_held` path.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run LiteLLM proxy 1.83.14 with a GLM-5.1 model configured, routed via `/v1/messages` (route_type=anthropic_messages).
2. Send:
```
curl -N 'http://<litellm-host>:4000/v1/messages' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-...' \
  -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "glm-5.1",
    "max_tokens": 256,
    "stream": true,
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello in one sentence."}]
  }'
```
3. Observe: SSE stream emits message_start, content_block_start, content_block_delta(s), content_block_stop, then a typeless error event instead of message_delta/message_stop.

title: [Feature]: Lakera v2 guardrail: advisory mode (inject_system_message) instead of block/monitor on flagged content
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### The Feature

Add a third `on_flagged` action to the Lakera v2 guardrail (`litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/lakera_ai_v2.py`): `inject_system_message`. On a flag, instead of raising HTTP 400 (`block`) or silently allowing the request (`monitor`), this mode appends an advisory system message describing why the request was flagged and lets the real LLM call proceed. The LLM itself then decides whether to respond helpfully or decline, based on the flagged reason and its own judgment of the actual request.

The message-injection mechanism itself should be a shared, guardrail-agnostic helper on `CustomGuardrail` (not Lakera-only code), living next to the existing `raise_passthrough_exception` helper, since both represent generic strategies for handling a flagged request. `raise_passthrough_exception` short-circuits the LLM call entirely and returns a canned message; the new helper does the opposite: it lets the request through with an added note, and never blocks the LLM from seeing the underlying content.

### Motivation, pitch

Lakera today only supports `on_flagged: block` (hard fail every flagged request) or `monitor` (log only, no user-visible effect at all). Neither option fits a common need: a false-positive-prone detector such as prompt-injection heuristics that can trip on legitimate instructional language (for example, a support agent prompt that says "ignore the customer's previous request and start a new ticket"). With `block`, that legitimate request fails outright. With `monitor`, a genuinely malicious request sails through with no signal reaching the model at all.

An advisory mode gives a middle ground: the request proceeds, but the LLM is told the request was flagged and why, and can use its own judgment, similar to how a human reviewer would weigh a flagged item rather than auto-rejecting or ignoring the flag. This is especially useful for guardrails with a nonzero false-positive rate, where blocking outright causes real user friction but staying silent forfeits the LLM's ability to react to a real threat.

This does not overlap with the existing `passthrough` mechanism (`raise_passthrough_exception`, used by several other guardrails via their own `on_flagged_action` field), which short-circuits the LLM call entirely and returns a canned response without ever showing the model the actual request. The proposal here is the opposite: the model sees the full, unmodified request plus an advisory note, and decides how to proceed.

title: [Bug]: LoggingWorker strands its worker task and drops its queue when the event loop changes
body:
### What happened?

`LoggingWorker._ensure_queue` drops its worker task and queue when it sees a new event loop, without cancelling either. In a process with more than one event loop — a worker pool where each thread runs its own — the bound loop flips on every call from a different thread, so each flip strands the previous loop's `_worker_loop` task and discards whatever was queued on it.

Symptoms, all at ERROR:

```
Task was destroyed but it is pending!
task: <Task pending name='Task-2168' coro=<LoggingWorker._worker_loop() running at
  .../litellm/litellm_core_utils/logging_worker.py:121> wait_for=<Future pending ...>>
```

and, when the old loop has since closed:

```
RuntimeError: Event loop is closed
  File ".../litellm/litellm_core_utils/logging_worker.py", line 121, in _worker_loop
    task = await self._queue.get()
```

In a service running 5 worker threads at roughly 10 rps this produced about **0.4 records per request** — thousands per pod per day. Nothing functionally breaks, but a service whose error rate is almost entirely this cannot use error rate as a signal; an unrelated genuine failure sat hidden inside it for a while before we found it.

I believe this is the residual case behind #5559, #7255 and #8831. `LoggingWorker` fixed the original problem — tasks created by bare `asyncio.create_task` with no reference held — and `_running_tasks` does keep them alive correctly for a single loop. The multi-loop rebind path is what is left.

### The code

`litellm/litellm_core_utils/logging_worker.py`, unchanged on `main` as of today:

```python
# Check if we need to reinitialize due to event loop change
if self._queue is not None and self._bound_loop is not current_loop:
    verbose_logger.debug(
        "LoggingWorker: Event loop changed, reinitializing queue and worker"
    )
    # Clear old state - these are bound to the old loop
    self._queue = None
    self._sem = None
    self._worker_task = None      # still pending, never cancelled
    self._running_tasks.clear()   # ditto
```

Worth noting `LoggingWorker.stop()` cancels correctly and awaits the gather — it is specifically this branch that does not.

### Relevant log output

```
litellm 1.83.0, python 3.12.4
bound loop ids:            [4750435792, 4306022144]
rebound to a second loop:  True
queue still has a waiter:  <Queue maxsize=50000 _getters[1]>
stranded task reports:     3
```

`_getters[1]` shows the stranded task still parked on the abandoned queue.

### Twitter / LinkedIn details

_No response_

### Steps to reproduce

No API key or network needed. This drives `GLOBAL_LOGGING_WORKER` directly, the same way `litellm.utils._client_async_logging_helper` does on every async call.

```python
"""Two threads, each with its own event loop -- any worker-pool design."""

import asyncio
import gc
import sys
import threading
from importlib.metadata import version

from litellm.litellm_core_utils.logging_worker import GLOBAL_LOGGING_WORKER

strands: list[str] = []
bound_loops: list[int] = []


async def noop() -> None:
    pass


def collect_strand(_loop, context) -> None:
    if "destroyed" in context.get("message", ""):
        strands.append(context["message"])


def one_worker_thread() -> None:
    async def main() -> None:
        GLOBAL_LOGGING_WORKER.ensure_initialized_and_enqueue(async_coroutine=noop())
        await asyncio.sleep(0)  # let the worker task start
        bound_loops.append(id(GLOBAL_LOGGING_WORKER._bound_loop))

    loop = asyncio.new_event_loop()
    loop.set_exception_handler(collect_strand)
    asyncio.set_event_loop(loop)
    try:
        loop.run_until_complete(main())
    finally:
        loop.close()


for _ in range(2):
    thread = threading.Thread(target=one_worker_thread)
    thread.start()
    thread.join()

gc.collect()

print(f"litellm {version('litellm')}, python {sys.version.split()[0]}")
print(f"bound loop ids:            {bound_loops}")
print(f"rebound to a second loop:  {bound_loops[0] != bound_loops[1]}")
print(f"queue still has a waiter:  {GLOBAL_LOGGING_WORKER._queue}")
print(f"stranded task reports:     {len(strands)}")
```

### Possible fixes

**Cancel before dropping.** The obvious one, but awkward: `self._worker_task` belongs to a *different* loop that may not be running on this thread, so a bare `task.cancel()` is not safe. It needs `old_loop.call_soon_threadsafe(task.cancel)`, and that raises if the old loop is already closed — so it has to be guarded with `old_loop.is_closed()`. Doable, and it would still discard the queued callbacks.

**One worker per loop.** Keeps a worker per running loop instead of one global with a `_bound_loop`, so the rebind branch becomes unreachable: no cross-loop cancellation is ever needed and nothing queued is thrown away. This is what we ended up doing locally, by swapping `GLOBAL_LOGGING_WORKER` for a proxy that dispatches to a real `LoggingWorker` keyed weakly by `asyncio.get_running_loop()`. It has run clean in production — 282 requests across 4 distinct event loops, zero strands, where the same traffic previously produced them steadily.

Happy to open a PR for the second approach if that direction is welcome. One wrinkle worth flagging either way: `LoggingWorker.__init__` calls `atexit.register(self._flush_on_exit)`, which holds a strong reference — anything keeping workers per loop has to unregister it or they accumulate.

No

v1.83.0 (branch `main` carries the same code)

title: [Bug]: bedrock_mantle Responses: several Codex input-item types rejected wholesale, and the 400 is masked into an opaque 500
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

Follow-up to #36528 / PR #36530, which fixes `agent_message`. The same enumeration turned up more item types Mantle's `input` union doesn't accept. Filing separately so #36530 isn't held up. See also #36545 for the `tools`-side counterpart (reserved `functions` namespace).

### What happened?

I enumerated Codex input-item types against `bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-terra` one per request. These are rejected with `invalid request body: Invalid 'input': value did not match any expected variant` — byte-identical to the response for a made-up `{"type":"totally_bogus_item"}`, so Mantle's union simply lacks them:

| Item | Sent by |
| --- | --- |
| `function_call` with `encrypted_function_args` (instead of plaintext `arguments`) | Codex multi-agent v2 / subagents |
| `compaction`, `compaction_trigger`, `context_compaction` | Codex auto-compaction |
| `local_shell_call` | Codex shell tool |
| `tool_search_call`, `tool_search_output` | deferred tool loading |

Accepted, for contrast: `message` (incl. role `developer`/`system`), `additional_tools`, `function_call`/`function_call_output` (with or without a `namespace` field), `custom_tool_call`/`custom_tool_call_output`, `web_search_call`, `image_generation_call`, `reasoning` without `encrypted_content`.

`encrypted_function_args` is the practical one: it explains the "worked for an hour, then every request fails" reports. Once a subagent tool call lands in a thread's history, every later request replays it and fails. PR #36530 mentions `encrypted_content` on `agent_message` but does not touch `encrypted_function_args` on `function_call`.

**Second, separable problem:** Mantle returns a clean **400** with a precise message. LiteLLM wraps it in `MaskedHTTPStatusError`, re-raises as a 500 `APIConnectionError`, and retries twice — so a deterministic schema rejection looks like a flaky connection, and clients burn 3x tokens on it. The real message only exists in the gateway pod log; no request body is logged anywhere, and `/spend/logs` doesn't capture it either. Diagnosing this took a day of black-box probing that a passed-through 400 would have answered in one request.

**Expected:**

1. Normalize or drop these items in `transform_responses_api_request`, following the `_hoist_codex_additional_tools` / `_normalize_codex_agent_messages` pattern, with a `verbose_logger.warning` naming what was changed.
2. Don't mask upstream 4xx as 5xx — a validation error should surface as `BadRequestError` with the upstream message and should not be retried.

### Steps to Reproduce

POST to `/v1/responses` with `bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-terra`, one item at a time, e.g.:

```json
{"model":"gpt-5.6-terra","input":[
  {"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"hi"}]},
  {"type":"function_call","name":"exec","call_id":"call_1","encrypted_function_args":"gAAAA=="}]}
```

Each rejected type returns the variant error. Sanity check that validation runs before semantic checks: a plain `function_call` with no matching output returns the *different* error `No tool output found for function call`, so the variant responses above are genuine schema rejections, not side effects.

### Relevant log output

```shell
litellm.APIConnectionError: Bedrock_mantleException - {"error":{"code":"validation_error","message":"invalid request body: Invalid 'input': value did not match any expected variant","param":null,"type":"invalid_request_error"}}
Received Model Group=gpt-5.6-terra
```

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy — `litellm/llms/bedrock_mantle/responses/transformation.py`

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

v1.95.0, also present on main

title: [Bug]: bedrock_mantle rejects every Codex 0.147 request — hoisted namespace named 'functions' collides with a reserved Mantle namespace
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

Sibling case, same provider and same transform: #36528 / PR #36530 (`agent_message` input items). That one is about `input`; this one is about `tools`, and neither the issue nor the PR covers it.

### What happened?

Codex CLI 0.147 sends a code-mode `exec` tool wrapped in a `namespace` tool whose name is literally `functions`. `_hoist_codex_additional_tools()` correctly lifts it out of the `additional_tools` input item, and `namespace` is in `_BEDROCK_MANTLE_SUPPORTED_RESPONSE_TOOL_TYPES`, so it passes through verbatim to Mantle — which rejects the whole request:

```
invalid request body: Invalid Value: 'tools.namespace'.
User-defined namespace 'functions' collides with an existing tool namespace.
```

`functions` is reserved on the Mantle side. Codex 0.147 sends it on **every** request, so the model is completely unusable: 11 POSTs, 0 completions, retrying every ~6s. Codex 0.146.0 sent only a `collaboration` namespace and worked fine.

**Expected:** LiteLLM should not forward a namespace name the upstream reserves. Either rename it on the way out and map it back on the way in (`functions` -> e.g. `codex_functions`, reversed for tool calls in the response so call attribution survives), or fail fast with a clear `BadRequestError` naming the collision instead of letting it surface as an opaque 500. A rename is the only option that actually makes Codex 0.147 work, but it needs to be bidirectional.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure `bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-terra` with `use_openai_responses_path: true`.
2. POST to `/v1/responses` with a `namespace` tool named `functions`:

```json
{"model":"gpt-5.6-terra","input":[{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"hi"}]}],
 "tools":[{"type":"namespace","name":"functions","description":"js","tools":[{"type":"function","name":"exec","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{}}}]}]}
```

3. -> 500. Change **only** `"name":"functions"` to `"name":"my_ns"` -> 200. Any other name works.

### Relevant log output

```shell
litellm.APIConnectionError: Bedrock_mantleException - {"error":{"code":"validation_error","message":"invalid request body: Invalid Value: 'tools.namespace'. User-defined namespace 'functions' collides with an existing tool namespace.","param":null,"type":"invalid_request_error"}}
Received Model Group=gpt-5.6-terra
```

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy — `litellm/llms/bedrock_mantle/responses/transformation.py`

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

v1.95.0 (`ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-gateway:v1.95.0`), also present on main

title: [Bug]: Anthropic /v1/messages → Responses API transform drops tool_result blocks containing tool_reference
body:
### What happened

Claude Code's tool search (deferred MCP tool loading) fails on any model routed through the OpenAI Responses path. Every turn that calls `ToolSearch` dies with a 500 after retries.

```
litellm.APIConnectionError: Bedrock_mantleException - {"error":{"code":"validation_error",
"message":"No tool output found for function call call_7a07046543b355e08cd966b732ca925f.",
"param":null,"type":"invalid_request_error"}}. Received Model Group=gpt-5.6-sol
```

Retrying can't help — the payload is already malformed. The turn ends with `stop_reason=tool_use`.

### Root cause

When Claude Code's `ToolSearch` finds matches, the tool result is **not text**. It's a `tool_result` whose content is an array of `tool_reference` blocks:

```js
{ type: "tool_result", tool_use_id: id,
  content: matches.map(name => ({ type: "tool_reference", tool_name: name })) }
```

`tool_reference` is an Anthropic beta content block. The `/v1/messages` → Responses transform doesn't handle it, so the whole `tool_result` is dropped instead of degrading. The upstream request then contains a `function_call` with no matching `function_call_output`, and the provider rejects it.

Two things make this worth fixing rather than working around:

1. The block's *semantics* don't need to survive — only the item does. Claude Code already injects the discovered tool schemas into the `tools` array itself (`Dynamic tool loading: 5/567 deferred tools included`), so the reference block is a history marker. Rendering it as text is enough.
2. Dropping an item that carries a `tool_use_id` can never be correct on this path. Any unknown block type inside a `tool_result` should degrade, not delete.

This is visible in the type definitions. `litellm/types/llms/anthropic.py` defines `ToolReference` — "Reference to a tool that should be expanded from deferred tools" — but it belongs to no union. `AnthropicMessagesToolResultParam.content` accepts `str | Iterable[AnthropicMessagesToolResultContent | AnthropicMessagesImageParam | AnthropicMessagesDocumentParam]`, so a `tool_reference` block inside a `tool_result` cannot be represented. The tool-search *tool* types (`AnthropicToolSearchToolRegex`, `AnthropicToolSearchToolBM25`) are present, but not the blocks those tools return — so the search request is translatable and the search result is not.

### Environment

- LiteLLM `1.95.0` (chart `1.95.0` from `oci://ghcr.io/berriai/litellm/chart`)
- Claude Code `2.1.220`, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` pointed at the proxy
- `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=1` (required — Claude Code disables tool search on non-first-party hosts by default)
- ~20 MCP servers, 567 tools
- Behaviour still present on `main` as of this report (see the type definitions above); not tested on `1.96.0`

Route:

```yaml
- model_name: gpt-5.6-sol
  litellm_params:
    model: bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-sol
    aws_region_name: us-east-1
    aws_bedrock_project_id: os.environ/BEDROCK_MANTLE_PROJECT_ID
  model_info:
    mode: responses
    use_openai_responses_path: true
```

### Reproduction

1. Route a model through `use_openai_responses_path: true`.
2. Run Claude Code against the proxy with `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=1` and enough MCP servers to trigger deferral.
3. Ask for something that makes the model call `ToolSearch`.
4. The request carrying the tool result 500s with `No tool output found for function call <id>`.

### Suggested fix

In the Anthropic→Responses transform, map unknown `tool_result` content blocks to text rather than dropping them:

```python
# tool_reference (Anthropic advanced-tool-use beta) and any future unknown block
{"type": "text", "text": f"[Loaded tool: {block['tool_name']}]"}
```

and never emit a `function_call` without its `function_call_output`.

### Notes

- The beta-header allowlist in `anthropic_beta_headers_config.json` has no `bedrock_mantle` key, so `advanced-tool-use-2025-11-20` is dropped for this provider. That is arguably correct here, but it means the header cannot be used to gate the body transform.
- Same class of bug reported client-side against Bedrock in anthropics/claude-code#25212 (closed as duplicate). The proposed fix there is the same degradation, applied in the client.
- Related: #12404 incorrect `tool_result` block transform in the Anthropic unified endpoint.
- Possibly related, same provider: #36528 (Bedrock Mantle rejects Codex `agent_message` input items).

title: [Bug]: langfuse_otel never sets observation output for /v1/rerank (legacy langfuse callback does)
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

Searched for `langfuse_otel` with rerank, `langfuse.observation.output`, and `set_response_output_messages`. The closest hits are #25720 (duplicate traces on the same route, different symptom) and #30249 (missing `langfuse.observation.type`, fixed, and the attribute is present in my traces). I did not find anything covering a missing output attribute on rerank.

With `success_callback: ["langfuse_otel"]`, `/v1/rerank` spans reach Langfuse with Input and metadata set but Output always empty. Switch the callback to `langfuse` and Output appears. Nothing else changes.

This is not #25720, which is duplicate traces on the same route.

Two places in `langfuse_otel` can write an output attribute, and neither handles `RerankResponse`:

- `set_langfuse_otel_attributes` (`langfuse_otel.py:47`) delegates to `_utils.set_attributes` (`arize/_utils.py:411`), which calls `_set_response_attributes` (`arize/_utils.py:79`). Its six setters look for `choices`, images, audio, embeddings, structured outputs and usage. A rerank response carries `results`, so all six no-op.
- `_set_observation_output` (`langfuse_otel.py:125`, called at `:245`). The `hasattr(response_obj, "get")` guard passes, because `RerankResponse` defines `.get` (`types/rerank.py:76`), but the body only reads `choices` and `output`.

There is a method that would handle it: `set_response_output_messages` (`langfuse_otel_attributes.py:101`). `RerankResponse` is a `BaseModel` (`types/rerank.py:65`), so `get_output_content_by_type` would reach `model_dump_json()` and serialize it. It has no callers, and `arize/_utils.py:72-76` explains why: the live path goes through `_set_choice_outputs` instead.

The legacy callback covers this in one branch (`langfuse.py:401`):

```python
elif response_obj is not None and isinstance(response_obj, litellm.RerankResponse):
    output = response_obj.results
```

Input is not part of this report. `utils.py:970` sets `messages = kwargs.get("query")` for rerank call types, so the query is logged and documents are left out on purpose.

Expected: a rerank span carries its ranking result as output, the way the legacy callback already does.

### Suggested fix

Add a `results` branch to `_set_observation_output` (`langfuse_otel.py:125`), mirroring the legacy callback:

```python
results = response_obj.get("results", [])
if results:
    safe_set_attribute(
        span,
        LangfuseSpanAttributes.OBSERVATION_OUTPUT.value,
        safe_dumps(results),
    )
```

Calling `attributes.set_response_output_messages(span, response_obj)` from `set_attributes` when no type-specific setter matched would also work, and would cover other non-chat response shapes at the same time.

The newer mapper in `litellm/integrations/otel/` looks like it has the same gap, so a fix may want to cover both paths. `LangfuseMapper._BLOB_ATTRS` builds `langfuse.observation.output` from `output_messages` (`otel/mappers/utils.py:115`), which reads `data.choices_out` and nothing else, and `otel/model/payloads.py` defines no rerank span type. I have not run that path, so this part is from reading the source rather than from a reproduction.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Point the proxy at a rerank model with the OTEL callback:

```yaml
litellm_settings:
  success_callback: ["langfuse_otel"]

model_list:
  - model_name: my-reranker
    litellm_params:
      model: hosted_vllm/my-reranker
      api_base: http://my-reranker.internal/v1
      api_key: fake-api-key
    model_info:
      mode: rerank
```

2. Send a rerank request:

```bash
curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
        "model": "my-reranker",
        "query": "What is the capital of France?",
        "documents": ["doc a", "doc b", "doc c"],
        "return_documents": false
      }'
```

3. Open the trace in Langfuse. Input holds the query, metadata is populated, Output is empty.

4. Set `success_callback: ["langfuse"]` and repeat. Output is populated.

5. To check without a Langfuse instance, drive the attribute setter with a fake span. A chat call runs alongside as a control:

```python
from litellm.integrations.langfuse.langfuse_otel import LangfuseOtelLogger
from litellm.types.utils import ModelResponse, Choices, Message
from litellm.types.rerank import RerankResponse


class FakeSpan:
    def __init__(self):
        self.attrs = {}

    def set_attribute(self, key, value):
        self.attrs[key] = value

    def record_exception(self, e):
        self.attrs["__exception__"] = repr(e)


def make_slp(call_type, model):
    return {
        "id": "req-1",
        "call_type": call_type,
        "model": model,
        "custom_llm_provider": "hosted_vllm",
        "metadata": {"user_api_key_hash": None, "user_api_key_alias": None, "requester_metadata": {}},
        "model_parameters": {},
        "messages": None,
        "response": None,
    }


def run(label, kwargs, response_obj):
    span = FakeSpan()
    LangfuseOtelLogger.set_langfuse_otel_attributes(span, kwargs, response_obj)
    out = [k for k in span.attrs if "output" in k.lower()]
    print(f"{label}: output attrs = {out or 'NONE'}")
    return span


rerank_kwargs = {
    "model": "my-reranker",
    "call_type": "rerank",
    "optional_params": {},
    "litellm_params": {"metadata": {"trace_user_id": "u1", "session_id": "s1"}},
    "standard_logging_object": make_slp("rerank", "my-reranker"),
    "query": "What is the capital of France?",
    "documents": ["doc a", "doc b", "doc c"],
    # utils.py:970 -> rerank sets `messages` to the query string
    "messages": "What is the capital of France?",
}
r = run("RERANK", rerank_kwargs, RerankResponse(
    id="rr-1",
    results=[{"index": 2, "relevance_score": 0.98}, {"index": 0, "relevance_score": 0.41}],
    meta={"api_version": {"version": "1"}, "billed_units": {"search_units": 1}},
))

chat_kwargs = {
    "model": "my-chat-model",
    "call_type": "completion",
    "optional_params": {},
    "litellm_params": {"metadata": {"trace_user_id": "u1", "session_id": "s1"}},
    "standard_logging_object": make_slp("completion", "my-chat-model"),
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}],
}
run("CHAT (control)", chat_kwargs, ModelResponse(
    id="cc-1",
    choices=[Choices(index=0, message=Message(role="assistant", content="hello there"))],
    model="my-chat-model",
))

print("\nall attrs written for RERANK:")
for k, v in sorted(r.attrs.items()):
    print(f"  {k} = {str(v)[:120]}")
```

### Relevant log output

```shell
RERANK: output attrs = NONE
CHAT (control): output attrs = ['output.value', 'llm.output_messages.0.message.role', 'llm.output_messages.0.message.content', 'langfuse.observation.output']

all attrs written for RERANK:
  langfuse.observation.input = "What is the capital of France?"
  langfuse.observation.type = generation
  llm.is_streaming = False
  llm.model_name = my-reranker
  llm.provider = Unknown
  llm.request.type = rerank
  llm.response.id = rr-1
  metadata = {"user_api_key_hash": null, "user_api_key_alias": null, "requester_metadata": {}}
  openinference.span.kind = RERANKER
  session.id = s1
  user.id = u1


`openinference.span.kind = RERANKER` and `llm.request.type = rerank` are both set, so the span is recognised as a rerank call. Only the output mapping is missing.

For comparison, calling the legacy callback's `LangFuseLogger._get_langfuse_input_output_content` with the same `RerankResponse` does return an output:


RERANK (legacy langfuse callback)
  input  = 'What is the capital of France?'
  output = [{'index': 2, 'relevance_score': 0.98}, {'index': 0, 'relevance_score': 0.41}]


That return value is what the caller passes as `output=` into `_log_langfuse_v2`, so the ranking reaches the observation on the legacy path and not on the OTEL one.
```

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

v1.96.0

title: [Bug]: Bedrock Converse 400s on forced tool_choice + parallel_tool_calls (Claude 4.5+/Opus): conflicting tool_choice injected into additionalModelRequestFields
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

On Bedrock Converse with Claude 4.5+/Opus 4.6 models, a request that **forces a specific tool** (`tool_choice={"type":"function","function":{"name":...}}`) and also sets `parallel_tool_calls` fails with a 400 from Bedrock:

```
litellm.BadRequestError: BedrockException - {"message":"The additional field tool_choice/type conflicts with the existing field toolConfig.toolChoice.tool. Remove tool_choice/type and try again."}
```

This is the standard request shape emitted by OpenAI-protocol structured-output clients — e.g. LangChain's `ChatOpenAI.with_structured_output(schema, method="function_calling")` (forced tool + `parallel_tool_calls=false`) pointed at a LiteLLM proxy — so **any structured-output call through the proxy to a Bedrock Claude 4.5+/Opus model 400s deterministically**.

### Root cause

LiteLLM emits the forced tool choice **twice**, in two different dialects:

1. `map_openai_params()` correctly converts the forced choice to Bedrock-native `toolConfig.toolChoice.tool`.
2. Independently, the `parallel_tool_calls` handling (`converse_transformation.py`, ~line 894) builds
   ```python
   optional_params["_parallel_tool_use_config"] = {
       "tool_choice": {"type": "auto", "disable_parallel_tool_use": not value}
   }
   ```
   which `_merge_parallel_tool_use_config` injects into `additionalModelRequestFields` for any model with `supports_parallel_tool_use_config` — **without checking whether `toolConfig.toolChoice` already carries a forced tool**.

The Anthropic model on Bedrock then receives both `toolConfig.toolChoice.tool` and `additionalModelRequestFields.tool_choice{type: "auto", ...}` and rejects the request.

Captured Converse request body (via a logging mock at `aws_bedrock_runtime_endpoint`), litellm proxy v1.96.0:

```json
"toolConfig": {
  "tools": [ ... ],
  "toolChoice": {"tool": {"name": "ComplianceFindingResponse"}}
},
"additionalModelRequestFields": {
  "tool_choice": {"type": "auto", "disable_parallel_tool_use": true}
}
```

### Relationship to existing issues

- #22637 reports the same injection path; its symptom (`tool_choice.type: Field required`) was patched by #34347 (add `"type": "auto"`), which is precisely the `tool_choice/type` field named in the new conflict error. So #34347 fixed the missing-`type` symptom but created this conflict variant for forced-tool requests.
- #34420 / #29668 / #34888 cover the *toolless* leak of the same config; a tools-presence check does not help here since tools are present.

### Suggested fix

When the resolved `toolConfig.toolChoice` is a specific tool (or `any`), do not inject the auto-typed `tool_choice` block into `additionalModelRequestFields`. If `disable_parallel_tool_use` must be honored alongside a forced tool, emit a **single** Anthropic-style `tool_choice` (e.g. `{"type": "tool", "name": ..., "disable_parallel_tool_use": ...}`) in `additionalModelRequestFields` and omit `toolConfig.toolChoice`, so the two dialects never coexist.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Proxy config (no real AWS needed — point the runtime endpoint at any request-logging mock to see the malformed body; against real Bedrock you get the 400):

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: claude-opus
    litellm_params:
      model: bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-6-v1
      aws_region_name: us-east-1
```

2. Send an OpenAI-format request with tools + forced tool_choice + parallel_tool_calls:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "claude-opus",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "extract findings"}],
    "tools": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "Resp", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"findings": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}}}}}],
    "tool_choice": {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "Resp"}},
    "parallel_tool_calls": false
  }'
```

3. Bedrock returns 400: `The additional field tool_choice/type conflicts with the existing field toolConfig.toolChoice.tool.`

Equivalent LangChain client (the common real-world trigger):

```python
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
llm = ChatOpenAI(model="claude-opus", base_url="http://localhost:4000/v1", api_key="sk-1234")
llm.with_structured_output(MySchema, method="function_calling").invoke("extract findings")
```

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Both the SDK transformation (`litellm/llms/bedrock/chat/converse_transformation.py`) and the proxy.

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

Reproduced on v1.96.0 (latest stable). Affects v1.95.0+ with this exact error; older versions fail the same request shape with the pre-#34347 `tool_choice.type: Field required` variant. Also observed in production against a v1.95+ proxy deployment.

title: [Bug]: sensitive_data_routing documented but not recognized as guardrail
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

I’m trying to configure the sensitive_data_routing guardrail as described in the documentation:

https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/guardrails/sensitive_data_routing#configuration

Example:

```yaml
guardrails:
  - guardrail_name: "sensitive-data-routing"
    litellm_params:
      guardrail: sensitive_data_routing
      mode: "pre_call"
```

However, LiteLLM fails during startup with:

ValueError: Unsupported guardrail: sensitive_data_routing

The error originates from:

litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_registry.py

This also happens when using the latest LiteLLM Docker image.

It looks like the documentation exposes sensitive_data_routing as a supported Guardrails v2 integration, while the current guardrail registry does not register it.

Could you please confirm whether:

sensitive_data_routing is expected to be supported in the current release, or

the documentation is ahead of the released implementation?

Thanks!

### Steps to Reproduce

```yaml

  master_key: os.environ/PROXY_MASTER_KEY

model_list:
  - model_name: local-agent-rhoai
    litellm_params:

      regex_patterns:
        - 'pattern'
      sticky_session: true

litellm_settings:

title: [Bug]: DB-stored litellm_settings.max_budget is not applied after a proxy restart
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?
I need to enforce a single proxy-wide budget with a reset interval. The [budget documentation](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/users) describes `litellm_settings.max_budget` and `budget_duration` for this purpose.

In our production deployment, `config.yaml` is immutable for security reasons, so changing these settings requires rebuilding and redeploying the proxy. I then found the [database-backed configuration documentation](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/configs#configyaml-vs-database-settings), which says that with `STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True`, `/config/update` writes settings to `LiteLLM_Config` and the database value overrides `config.yaml` on startup.

Based on that documented behaviour, I used `POST /config/update` to store a new `litellm_settings.max_budget` value and restarted the proxy. The API returned `Config updated successfully`, and the database row was written correctly, but the proxy continued enforcing the value from `config.yaml`.

To make the active limit observable, I set `max_budget` to `0.00001` in `config.yaml`, stored `10` in the database through `/config/update`, and restarted the proxy. I then set the proxy-wide spend counter to `1.0`.

Because `1.0` is below the database limit but above the YAML limit, the request outcome shows which value is being enforced. The request is rejected:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
{"error":{"message":"Budget has been exceeded! Current cost: 1.0, Max budget: 1e-05", ...}}
```

The `Max budget` in that response is the `config.yaml` value, `0.00001`. No warning or diagnostic explains why the saved DB value is unused.

**Expected** — [Proxy Config → *config.yaml vs database settings*](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/configs#configyaml-vs-database-settings):

> On startup and on every config refresh, the proxy loads your `config.yaml` first and then overlays the database rows for `general_settings`, `router_settings`, `litellm_settings`, and `environment_variables`. The overlay is a deep merge in which the database value wins on any key that exists in both places, so editing that key in the YAML and restarting your pods will not change the running value.

For `litellm_settings.max_budget` the opposite happens: the YAML value wins, and restarting the pods is exactly what reapplies it.

---

### Steps to Reproduce

`max_budget` is used because `/global/spend` directly reports the runtime `litellm.max_budget`, making the mismatch easy to verify in one request.

1. Start v1.96.0 with Postgres and `STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True`.

   `docker-compose.yml`:

   ```yaml
   services:
     litellm:
       image: ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.96.0
       ports: ["4000:4000"]
       volumes: ["./config.yaml:/app/config.yaml:ro"]
       command: ["--config=/app/config.yaml", "--port=4000"]
       environment:
         DATABASE_URL: "postgresql://llmproxy:dbpassword9090@db:5432/litellm"
         STORE_MODEL_IN_DB: "True"
         LITELLM_MASTER_KEY: "sk-1234"
       depends_on:
         db: {condition: service_healthy}
     db:
       image: postgres:16
       environment:
         POSTGRES_DB: litellm
         POSTGRES_USER: llmproxy
         POSTGRES_PASSWORD: dbpassword9090
       healthcheck:
         test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -d litellm -U llmproxy"]
         interval: 5s
         retries: 10
   ```

   `config.yaml` (`budget_duration` is required, or startup aborts):

   ```yaml
   litellm_settings:
     max_budget: 0.00001
     budget_duration: 30d

   general_settings:
     master_key: sk-1234
   ```

   ```bash
   docker compose up -d
   ```

2. Confirm the proxy is using the file value:

   ```bash
   curl -s http://localhost:4000/global/spend -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234"
   # {"spend":null,"max_budget":1e-05}
   ```

3. Write a different value to the DB:

   ```bash
   curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/config/update \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"litellm_settings": {"max_budget": 10}}'
   # {"message":"Config updated successfully"}
   ```

4. Confirm it persisted:

   ```bash
   docker compose exec db psql -U llmproxy -d litellm \
     -c 'SELECT param_name, param_value FROM "LiteLLM_Config";'
   #  litellm_settings | {"max_budget": 10}
   ```

5. `docker compose restart litellm`

6. Read it back:

   ```bash
   curl -s http://localhost:4000/global/spend -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234"
   # {"spend":null,"max_budget":1e-05}   <-- still the config.yaml value; expected 10
   ```

7. Verify that the stale value is enforced on an actual LLM request. The proxy-wide spend counter is stored on the special `litellm-proxy-budget` aggregate user. Seed it above the YAML limit, then restart to clear the in-memory spend cache:

   ```bash
   docker compose exec db psql -U llmproxy -d litellm \
     -c "UPDATE \"LiteLLM_UserTable\" SET spend = 1 WHERE user_id = 'litellm-proxy-budget';"

   docker compose restart litellm
   ```

   After the proxy is ready, make a request. The budget check runs before model routing, so this does not require a real provider or a valid model:

   ```bash
   curl -sS -i -X POST http://localhost:4000/chat/completions \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"model":"nonexistent-repro-model","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"test"}]}'
   # HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
   # {"error":{"message":"Budget has been exceeded! Current cost: 1.0, Max budget: 1e-05",...}}
   ```

   The DB config still contains `max_budget: 10`, but request enforcement uses the value loaded from `config.yaml`, `0.00001`. `/global/spend` is useful here for exposing the runtime `litellm.max_budget`; its `spend` field comes from `MonthlyGlobalSpend`, while authentication reads proxy-wide spend from the `litellm-proxy-budget` aggregate user.


### Relevant log output

No error or stack trace is emitted for this issue. At DEBUG, the stored value is
read before startup completes but is not applied. Unrelated lines are omitted:

```shell
10:10:54 - LiteLLM Proxy:DEBUG: proxy_server.py:1064 - prisma_client: <litellm.proxy.utils.PrismaClient object at 0x7ec753ddef90>
...
10:10:54 - LiteLLM Proxy:INFO: utils.py:4040 - DB User Table - update succeeded user_id='litellm-proxy-budget' ... max_budget=1e-05 spend=0.0 ... budget_duration='30d' ...
10:10:54 - LiteLLM Proxy:DEBUG: proxy_server.py:6085 - param_name=litellm_settings, param_value={'max_budget': 10}
10:10:54 - LiteLLM Proxy:DEBUG: proxy_server.py:5492 - len new_models: 0
10:10:54 - LiteLLM Proxy:DEBUG: proxy_server.py:6085 - param_name=litellm_settings, param_value={'max_budget': 10}
...
10:10:55 - LiteLLM Proxy:INFO: proxy_server.py:8353 - APScheduler started with memory leak prevention settings: removed jitter, increased intervals, misfire_grace_time=3600
INFO:     Application startup complete.
```

The two `param_name=litellm_settings` lines surround the router update, placing both
DB reads inside the one-shot startup `add_deployment()` call rather than the periodic
job. The DB value `{'max_budget': 10}` is read and merged before startup completes, but
nothing afterwards applies it: `/global/spend` still reports the `config.yaml` value of
0.00001, and the 429 above still quotes that same value.

The DB user update in the same excerpt shows the opposite direction working: the proxy
writes the `config.yaml` value of 0.00001 onto the `litellm-proxy-budget` row during the
same startup.

### Root cause

Two paths during startup could apply a DB-sourced `max_budget`. Neither applies it to `litellm.max_budget`.

**1. The startup config load never merges the DB.**

`load_config()` calls `get_config()`, then applies each `litellm_settings` key to the `litellm` module. Its `max_budget` branch assigns `litellm.max_budget = float(value)`, and `_global_proxy_budget_check()` later enforces that module attribute. But `get_config()` merges the DB only behind:

```python
if prisma_client is not None and store_model_in_db is True:
    config = await self._update_config_from_db(...)
```

Both conditions are false at that point in a fresh startup. `prisma_client` is initialized only after `load_config()` returns. `store_model_in_db` still has its default value and is populated from file or environment later. The same ordering also prevents `general_settings.store_model_in_db: true` in the file from enabling this first DB merge, because that setting is processed later inside `load_config()`.

**2. Later in the same startup the merge does run, but the merged `max_budget` is not applied.**

Once the Prisma client exists, `initialize_scheduled_background_jobs()` makes a one-shot `add_deployment()` call to load existing models during startup. This is separate from the periodic `add_deployment_job`. The one-shot path reaches `get_config()` again through `_update_llm_router()`. Both guards now hold, so `_update_config_from_db()` runs and merges the `LiteLLM_Config` row into the returned dict.

The merged `litellm_settings` has several specialized consumers, but none applies `max_budget`:

- `_update_config_fields()` writes DB values to the `litellm` module only for keys in `LITELLM_SETTINGS_SAFE_DB_OVERRIDES`. `max_budget` is not among the 12.
- `_update_llm_router` explicitly consumes the callback-related `litellm_settings` keys through `_add_callbacks_from_db_config`, then uses `config_data` for `router_settings` and `general_settings`. It has no generic step that applies other merged `litellm_settings` module attributes such as `max_budget`.

The returned config therefore contains the DB value `max_budget: 10`, while the runtime `litellm.max_budget` remains `0.00001` from `config.yaml`.

The same startup ordering and application path are still present on `main` at commit `6a919aec6a` (`proxy_server.py:4317`, `proxy_server.py:4677`; the safe-overrides list in `constants.py` is unchanged).

### Questions

I can't tell from the code which side of this is intended, so I'd rather ask than send a PR against the wrong one.

**1. Should a DB-stored `litellm_settings.max_budget` override the YAML value after restart?** The documentation says the database wins during startup, but the initial config load cannot access the DB and the later `add_deployment()` path does not apply `max_budget`. My use case only requires the stored value to be loaded on startup. Is that behaviour supported, and if so, which startup path is intended to apply it?

**2. Is there a supported way to set the proxy-wide budget without editing `config.yaml`?** This is the practical problem behind the report: in our production deployment `config.yaml` is baked into the image and awkward to change after rollout, while the database and the management API are reachable. Everything I checked is a dead end:

- `litellm.max_budget` has no environment variable. It is a plain `float = 0.0` module default, unlike the environment-backed tunables in `constants.py`. The only `MAX_BUDGET` environment variable in the tree is `LITELLM_MAX_BUDGET_PER_SESSION_TTL`, which is unrelated.
- `POST /config/update` stores the value correctly, but the tested update and restart paths do not apply it to `litellm.max_budget`.
- The `litellm-proxy-budget` row in `LiteLLM_UserTable` has its own `max_budget` column and startup writes the `config.yaml` value into it, but enforcement never reads it back: `_fetch_global_spend_with_event_coordination()` takes only `proxy_budget_row.spend`, and `_global_proxy_budget_check()` compares that spend against `litellm.max_budget`. Editing the row's `max_budget` column changes nothing.
- Every other `max_budget` in `_types.py` is scoped to a key, user, team or model, not to the proxy.

If there's a supported path I've missed, that resolves the practical problem for us and only question 1 remains.

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

v1.96.0

### Twitter / LinkedIn details

_No response_

title: [Bug] MCP inference route `/mcp/{subpath}` misses trailing slash and multi-segment sub-paths, yielding a misleading "Only proxy admin" 403
body:
### What happened?

A virtual key with a non-admin role gets a misleading admin-management error when
calling an MCP server path with a trailing slash:

```
Only proxy admin can be used to generate, delete, update info for new
keys/users/teams. Route=/mcp/gitlab_mcp/. Your role=internal_user
```

The route is a data-plane MCP call, not key/user/team management. The message sends
you looking at RBAC config instead of at route matching, which is where the problem
actually is.

### Root cause

`LiteLLMRoutes.mcp_inference_routes` (`litellm/proxy/_types.py:474`) declares the
placeholder as `"/mcp/{subpath}"`, without the `:path` suffix.

`RouteChecks._route_matches_pattern` (`litellm/proxy/auth/route_checks.py:484-489`)
turns a placeholder into `[^:]+` when it ends in `:path`, and into `[^/]+` otherwise.
So `/mcp/{subpath}` compiles to `^/mcp/[^/]+$`, which does not match a trailing
slash nor a multi-segment sub-path.

`is_llm_api_route()` therefore returns `False`, and
`non_proxy_admin_allowed_routes_check()` falls through to
`_raise_admin_only_route_exception()` — hence the message about keys/users/teams.

Measured by calling the shipped matcher directly:

```
route                  is_llm_api_route
/mcp/my-server         True
/mcp/my-server/        False   <-- falls through to the admin-only branch
/mcp/my-server/mcp     False   <-- streamable-http transport sub-path
```

### Why the test suite is green

There *is* a parametrized regression test over the MCP inference routes
(`tests/test_litellm/proxy/auth/test_route_checks.py:459-472`), and it uses concrete
routes rather than the literal pattern. But the only `{subpath}` case it exercises is

```python
("/mcp/my-server", "POST"),  # matches the /mcp/{subpath} pattern
```

without a trailing slash — exactly the shape that works. The broken shapes are never
tested, so the suite passes with the defect in place.

### Suggested fix

One line: `"/mcp/{subpath}"` → `"/mcp/{subpath:path}"`.

This is the same idiom the sibling list already uses twelve lines below —
`mcp_management_routes` declares `"/v1/mcp/server/{path:path}"` — so it introduces no
new convention.

**It does not widen admin surface.** Everything admin-only under MCP lives under the
`/v1/mcp/` prefix (`mcp_management_routes`), which `^/mcp/...` never matches; and
multi-segment paths under `/mcp/` are already treated as inference
(`/mcp/tools/list`, `/mcp/tools/call` are explicit entries in the same list). The
existing test that asserts multi-segment admin sub-paths stay rejected
(`test_virtual_key_llm_api_routes_rejects_mcp_multi_segment_admin_subpaths`) targets
`/v1/mcp/server/...` and is unaffected.

Verified by patching the route list in-process and re-running the classifier:

```
route                            before   after
/mcp/my-server/                  False    True    <- fixed
/mcp/my-server/mcp               False    True    <- fixed
/mcp, /mcp/, /mcp/my-server      True     True    (unchanged)
/mcp/tools{,/list,/call}         True     True    (unchanged)
/v1/mcp/server/abc-123/approve   False    False   (guard holds)
/v1/mcp/server/oauth/session     False    False   (guard holds)
/key/generate, /user/new         False    False   (guard holds)
```

### Secondary: the error message

Independently of the route fix, a route that is simply not in the caller's scope
should not be reported as an admin key/user/team management route. Issue #36508
raises the same complaint for `pass_through_endpoints`, so the misleading message is
not specific to MCP.

### Version

Defect confirmed by reading `main` on 2026-08-11; reproduced on `v1.83.14-stable`.

title: [Bug]: Bedrock Mantle rejects Codex agent_message input items
body:
### What happened?

Codex tasks that delegate to subagents can fail when the parent task continues and replays the conversation through the Bedrock Mantle Responses API.

LiteLLM forwards Codex `agent_message` items in the Responses `input` array. Bedrock Mantle rejects that item type with:

```text
invalid request body: Invalid 'input': value did not match any expected variant
```

### Reproduction

Send a Responses request containing a Codex agent message:

```json
{
  "model": "openai.gpt-5.6-terra",
  "input": [
    {"type": "message", "role": "user", "content": [{"type": "input_text", "text": "Continue the task."}]},
    {
      "type": "agent_message",
      "id": "amsg_example",
      "author": "worker",
      "recipient": "parent",
      "content": [{"type": "input_text", "text": "The subtask is complete."}]
    }
  ]
}
```

Codex multi-agent v2 can also send an `encrypted_content` block alongside a readable `input_text` metadata block.

### Expected behavior

LiteLLM should adapt unsupported Codex-only history items to the Bedrock Mantle input schema, preserving readable agent text where possible and logging when encrypted content cannot be forwarded.

### Environment

- Provider: `bedrock_mantle`
- Endpoint: Responses API
- Affected traffic: Codex multi-agent follow-up requests

### Relevant log output

```text
Bedrock_mantleException: invalid request body: Invalid 'input': value did not match any expected variant
```
