title: [Bug]: Anthropic API reasoning_tokens always 0 under default thinking display — usage.output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens ignored (Claude Opus 5 / Fable 5)
body:
## Summary

On the direct Anthropic API path, `usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` is always 0 for Claude Opus 5 / Claude Fable 5 / Claude Sonnet 5 under their default thinking display, even when the model performed (and billed) extended thinking.

Root cause: `AnthropicConfig.calculate_usage` (litellm/llms/anthropic/chat/transformation.py, ~line 2255 in 1.88.1) estimates reasoning tokens by token-counting the returned `reasoning_content` text. On these models the API's default is `display: \"omitted\"`, so thinking blocks arrive with an empty `thinking` field — the estimate is always 0. Even under `display: \"summarized\"` the estimate counts the summary text, not the billed internal reasoning.

The Anthropic API now reports the authoritative count in `usage.output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens`, which `calculate_usage` never reads.

## Evidence

Raw Anthropic API response usage for a single `claude-opus-5` request with no thinking parameter (thinking on by default), 2026-08-08:

```json
{
  \"input_tokens\": 29,
  \"output_tokens\": 391,
  \"output_tokens_details\": { \"thinking_tokens\": 180 },
  \"service_tier\": \"standard\"
}
```

The same request through `litellm.completion` returns `completion_tokens=391` with `completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens=0`, while `message.thinking_blocks` is present (empty text + signature, per the default display).

## Impact

Any accounting or eval pipeline reading `reasoning_tokens` concludes these models never think. We hit this in a public benchmark: the per-model usage CSVs showed zero reasoning tokens for every Claude row, which masked a real serving-configuration issue until a reader questioned it.

## Proposed fix

In `calculate_usage`, prefer the provider-reported value when present:

```python
details = usage_object.get(\"output_tokens_details\") or {}
reasoning_tokens = details.get(\"thinking_tokens\")
if reasoning_tokens is None:
    # fall back to the existing estimate from visible reasoning_content
```

Related: #30099 reports the same estimate-from-text root cause on the Vertex AI path (redacted thinking on Opus 4.7/4.8); this issue covers the direct Anthropic API path, where the fix site is the anthropic chat transformation.

- litellm version: 1.88.1
- Models affected: claude-opus-5, claude-fable-5, claude-sonnet-5 (default display omitted); any model whose visible thinking text understates billed thinking
author: MaxGhenis

title: [Feature Request] Add Vertex AI RAG Engine as a vector store provider for /rag/ingest and vector_stores/search
body:
## Feature Description

Add Google Cloud **Vertex AI RAG Engine** as a first-class vector store provider, enabling the `/v1/rag/ingest` and `/v1/vector_stores/{vector_store_id}/search` endpoints to route to the Vertex AI RAG API.

## Motivation

We use LiteLLM Proxy as our enterprise AI gateway with `vector_store_registry` configured for multiple backends. Vertex AI RAG Engine is a fully managed RAG service from Google Cloud that handles:

- **Document ingestion** — PDF, text, GCS, Google Drive sources
- **Chunking & embedding** — managed internally using `text-embedding-005`
- **Vector search** — managed Vertex Vector Search backend
- **Corpus-level retrieval** — `retrieveContext` API

We currently have Vertex AI RAG declared in `vector_store_registry` with `custom_llm_provider: "vertex_ai"`, but there is **no runtime provider driver** to translate vector store calls into Vertex AI RAG API requests.

## Current Config (works for Azure, not for Vertex)

```yaml
vector_store_registry:
  - vector_store_name: "azure-ai-search"
    litellm_params:
      custom_llm_provider: "azure_ai"
      # ... works for search, ingest has separate gap

  - vector_store_name: "vertex-rag"
    litellm_params:
      custom_llm_provider: "vertex_ai"
      vertex_project: "my-project"
      vertex_location: "us-central1"
      vector_store_id: "5305882475833065472"  # RAG Corpus ID
      # ... no provider driver
```

## Required Support

### 1. Ingest (`/v1/rag/ingest`)
Register `vertex_ai` as an **IngestProvider** that routes to the Vertex AI RAG file import API.

**Key architectural note**: Vertex AI RAG manages its own chunking and embedding pipeline internally (using `text-embedding-005`). The client-side chunking/embedding pipeline should be **bypassed** for Vertex — raw files should be passed directly to the Vertex API.

**Vertex API**: `vertexai.rag.import_files()` or `vertexai.rag.upload_file()`
- Accepts: GCS URIs, local files, Google Drive links
- Handles: chunking (configurable `chunk_size`, `chunk_overlap`), embedding, indexing
- Supports: `LayoutParserConfig` and `LlmParserConfig` for layout-aware parsing

### 2. Search (`/v1/vector_stores/{vector_store_id}/search`)
Route `vector_store_search` calls to Vertex AI RAG retrieval API.

**Vertex API**: `vertexai.rag.retrieval_query()`
```python
response = vertexai_rag.retrieval_query(
    rag_resources=[RagResource(rag_corpus=corpus_name)],
    text=query,
    rag_retrieval_config=RagRetrievalConfig(top_k=top_k),
)
```

Returns ranked contexts with `source_display_name`, `text`, and `score`.

### 3. Authentication
Support `vertex_project`, `vertex_location`, and `vertex_credentials` from `litellm_params` — consistent with existing Vertex AI model support.

## API References

| Operation | Vertex AI RAG API | Python SDK |
|---|---|---|
| **Ingest** | `POST .../ragCorpora/{id}/ragFiles:import` | `vertexai.rag.import_files()` |
| **Search** | `POST .../ragCorpora/{id}:retrieveContext` | `vertexai.rag.retrieval_query()` |
| **Upload** | `POST .../ragCorpora/{id}/ragFiles:upload` | `vertexai.rag.upload_file()` |
| **List files** | `GET .../ragCorpora/{id}/ragFiles` | `vertexai.rag.list_files()` |
| **Delete** | `DELETE .../ragCorpora/{id}/ragFiles/{fileId}` | `vertexai.rag.delete_file()` |

Full docs: https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/model-reference/rag-api

## Benchmarks (from our testing)

We benchmarked Vertex AI RAG with clinical study documents (3 FDA PDFs, 120 pages, 1.5MB):

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Avg Latency | 774ms |
| Precision | 0.384 |
| Recall | **1.000** (perfect) |
| Errors | 0 |

## Current Workaround

We are building a custom provider adapter (similar pattern to custom LiteLLM providers) that intercepts vector store calls when `custom_llm_provider == "vertex_ai"` and routes them to the Vertex AI RAG Python SDK.

## Related

- **Dependency**: `google-cloud-aiplatform` (already a LiteLLM dependency for Vertex AI models)
- **Similar to**: Azure AI Search provider (`azure_ai`) — but Vertex handles its own embeddings server-side
- **Related issues**: We also reported the `/v1/rag/query` credential resolution bug (#35599) and Azure AI Search IngestProvider gap

## Context

Enterprise deployment using LiteLLM as an AI gateway for a pharmaceutical R&D platform, running multi-provider RAG across Azure AI Search, DocInsight, and Vertex AI RAG.
author: aaakinkunmi

title: pass_through_endpoints: include_subpath routes are auth-classified as management routes, so virtual keys get 401
body:
### What happened

A pass-through endpoint declared with `include_subpath: true` registers its `{subpath:path}` wildcard route correctly, but every **virtual key** is then rejected on it with a management-route error:

```
401 {"error":{"message":"Authentication Error, Only proxy admin can be used to generate, delete, update info for new keys/users/teams. Route=/orx/rerank. Your role=unknown. Your user_id=unknown","type":"auth_error"}}
```

The identical route **without** `include_subpath` accepts the same virtual key and works (200/202). So the flag that makes sub-paths reachable is also the flag that makes the route admin-only, which defeats the purpose: the reason to put a provider behind the proxy is per-consumer budgeted keys, and the master key must never be handed to a consumer.

### Why it matters

This is the only mechanism for proxying provider APIs whose resources live under a path — for example OpenRouter's asynchronous video generation, where you `POST /videos`, then `GET /videos/{jobId}` and `GET /videos/{jobId}/content`. Exact-path routes can serve the submit but not the poll, and a per-job route obviously cannot be declared. With `include_subpath` unusable by non-admin keys, the poll has to leave the proxy entirely — taking budget enforcement, logging and key auth with it.

### Reproduce

`config.yaml`:

```yaml
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  pass_through_endpoints:
    - path: "/orx"
      target: "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1"
      include_subpath: true
      headers:
        Authorization: "Bearer os.environ/OPENROUTER_API_KEY"
        content-type: application/json
```

```bash
# with a virtual key (sk-...) generated via /key/generate
curl -X POST $PROXY/orx/rerank -H "Authorization: Bearer $VIRTUAL_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"cohere/rerank-v3.5","query":"bee","documents":["a bee","a car"]}'
# -> 401 "Only proxy admin can be used to generate, delete, update info for new keys/users/teams"
```

Now remove `include_subpath: true`, change the path to the exact `/orx/rerank`, restart:

```bash
# same request, same key -> 200
```

Renaming the prefix does not change the behaviour, so it is the wildcard registration, not the path string.

### Expected

A pass-through route declared in `pass_through_endpoints` should be treated as an LLM/passthrough route for auth purposes whether or not `include_subpath` is set — i.e. a valid virtual key with access should be accepted, and `auth: false` should remain the way to opt out of auth entirely.

### Notes

`add_subpath_route()` registers `f"{path}/{{subpath:path}}"` with `Depends(user_api_key_auth)`, and the auth layer appears to fall through to its management-route branch for that shape (`Your role=unknown`), whereas the exact-path registration is recognised. Happy to test a patch against a self-hosted proxy — this is running in production here behind per-consumer budgeted keys.
author: coeur-de-loup

title: [Bug]: /v1/responses with background:true returns completed but empty output when using polling_via_cache
body:
## Description

  When using `/v1/responses` with `background: true` and `polling_via_cache: "all"`, the polling result returns `status:
  "completed"` but `output: []`, `text: null`, `usage: null`.

  ## Versions Affected

  - v1.91.0 and above (including v1.92.0, v1.95.0) ❌
  - v1.83.7 ✅ works correctly

  ## Root Cause

  PR #31499 introduced `_buffer_first_chunk_honoring_disconnect` which cancels the upstream LLM call when the client
  disconnects before the first chunk. In background polling mode, the client **intentionally** disconnects immediately after
  receiving the polling ID — this is expected behavior. However, this disconnect triggers the cancel logic, causing the
  upstream LLM call to be cancelled before the result is written to Redis cache.

  ## Config

  ```yaml
  litellm_settings:
    responses:
      background_mode:
        polling_via_cache: "all"
    cache: true
    cache_params:
      type: redis
  ```

  ## Steps to Reproduce

  ```bash
  # Step 1: POST with background: true
  curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/responses \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model": "gpt-3.5-turbo", "input": "say ok", "background": true}'
  # Returns: {"id": "litellm_poll_xxx", "status": "queued", ...}

  # Step 2: Poll result
  curl http://localhost:4000/v1/responses/litellm_poll_xxx
  # Returns: {"status": "completed", "output": [], "usage": null}  ← BUG
  ```

  ## Relevant Log Output

  ```
  create_response: client disconnected before first chunk, upstream LLM request cancelled
  background_streaming_task: response for {id} has no body_iterator; this may indicate a misconfiguration or provider error
  Recorded streaming client disconnect with error_code=499
  Updated polling state for {id}: status=completed, output_items=0
  Finished background streaming for {id}, status=completed, error=None, incomplete_details=None, output_items=0
  ```
## Proposed Fix (verified on v1.92.0)

The fix was verified by hotpatching a running v1.92.0 pod.

**Fix 1** — `litellm/proxy/response_polling/background_streaming.py`

Pass `request=None` to `base_process_llm_request` so the disconnect listener is not activated in background tasks:

```python
# Before (buggy)
response = await processor.base_process_llm_request(
    request=request,
    ...
)

# After (fix)
response = await processor.base_process_llm_request(
    request=None,  # background task — client disconnect should not cancel upstream
    ...
)
```

**Fix 2** — `litellm/proxy/common_request_processing.py`

Guard all `dict(request.headers)` calls against `None`:

```python
# Before
request_headers=dict(request.headers),

# After
request_headers=dict(request.headers) if request is not None else {},
```

Note: The exact fix may differ for v1.95.0 as the code structure may have changed, but the root cause is the same — `_buffer_first_chunk_honoring_disconnect` should not cancel upstream calls in background polling mode.

## Regression Introduced By

  PR #31499: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/31499
author: jackscchen

title: [Bug]: DB-less proxy 500s on batch create after the provider job already started, managed files hook dereferences prisma_client=None
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

On a proxy booted without `DATABASE_URL`, `POST /v1/batches` sends the create to the provider, the provider accepts and starts the job, and then the response to the caller is an HTTP 500 with `'NoneType' object has no attribute 'db'`. The job runs and bills, the caller gets no batch id to poll or cancel, and a retry starts a second paid job

The chain (line numbers at b6e3ff639c): `_add_proxy_hooks` (`litellm/proxy/utils.py:538-555`) instantiates every hook in `PROXY_HOOKS`, passing the module-global `prisma_client`, which is `None` with no database, into any constructor that asks for it, and registers the hook regardless. The enterprise managed-files hook, merged into `PROXY_HOOKS` via `ENTERPRISE_PROXY_HOOKS` (`litellm/proxy/hooks/__init__.py:56`, `enterprise/enterprise_hooks/__init__.py:11`), is the only hook whose constructor takes `prisma_client`, and it is typed non-optional (`enterprise/litellm_enterprise/proxy/hooks/managed_files.py:125-129`). Its `async_post_call_success_hook` calls `store_unified_object_id` unconditionally for every `LiteLLMBatch` response (`managed_files.py:1278`) and every `LiteLLMFineTuningJob` (`managed_files.py:1327`), and that method upserts through `self.prisma_client.db` (`managed_files.py:231`), so the `AttributeError` fires after the provider already accepted the job. `create_batch` runs this as `post_call_success_hook` (`litellm/proxy/batches_endpoints/endpoints.py:313`) and the exception surfaces as an opaque 500

Nothing here is Vertex-specific: any provider's batch create, and by the same call site any fine-tuning job create, hits this on a DB-less boot whenever the enterprise hooks are importable, which they are in the standard proxy image and dev installs. Found while QA'ing #35141, whose playbook preferred DB-less proxy legs and had to fall back to per-leg databases because of this

### User Flow

Today the money is spent at step 3 but the user is told the create failed:

1. Admin boots the proxy with a Vertex AI model in the config and no `DATABASE_URL`
2. User uploads the batch input with `POST /v1/files` (`purpose=batch`, `custom_llm_provider=vertex_ai`) and gets back a `gs://` file id
3. User creates the batch with `POST /v1/batches` using that id and `"custom_llm_provider": "vertex_ai"`, the provider accepts and starts the job, and the response is `500` with `{"error":{"message":"'NoneType' object has no attribute 'db'", ...}}`
4. The job runs to completion and bills, but the user never saw its id, so they cannot poll it, cancel it, or fetch its output, and retrying the create starts another paid job

After a fix, the same walk completes without a database:

1. Admin boots the same DB-less proxy
2. User uploads the input with `POST /v1/files` as before
3. `POST /v1/batches` returns `200` with the batch object (provider batch id, `"status": "validating"`)
4. User polls `GET /v1/batches/{id}?provider=vertex_ai` to `completed` and fetches the output; unified-id bookkeeping simply does not happen, the same as every other database-gated feature on a DB-less proxy

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Boot the proxy with a config containing a `vertex_ai/...` model with valid credentials and no `DATABASE_URL` anywhere in the environment
2. Upload an input file: `curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -F purpose=batch -F custom_llm_provider=vertex_ai -F file=@batch-input.jsonl`
3. Create the batch: `curl -sS -i -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/batches -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"input_file_id": "<id from step 2>", "endpoint": "/v1/chat/completions", "completion_window": "24h", "custom_llm_provider": "vertex_ai"}'`
4. Observe the 500, then observe in the proxy log that the provider job was created (status `validating`) before the hook raised

### Relevant log output

```shell
INFO: managed_files.py - Storing LiteLLM Managed batch object with id=9110789467874000896 in cache
ERROR: litellm.proxy.proxy_server.create_batch(): Exception occured - 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'db'
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "litellm/proxy/batches_endpoints/endpoints.py", line 313, in create_batch
    response = await proxy_logging_obj.post_call_success_hook(
  File "litellm/proxy/utils.py", line 2417, in post_call_success_hook
    raise e
  File "litellm/proxy/utils.py", line 2411, in post_call_success_hook
    callback_response = await callback.async_post_call_success_hook(
  File "enterprise/litellm_enterprise/proxy/hooks/managed_files.py", in async_post_call_success_hook
    await self.store_unified_object_id(
  File "enterprise/litellm_enterprise/proxy/hooks/managed_files.py", in store_unified_object_id
    await self.prisma_client.db.litellm_managedobjecttable.upsert(
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'db'
INFO: 127.0.0.1:60526 - "POST /v1/batches HTTP/1.1" 500 Internal Server Error
```

The LiteLLMBatch in the log carries the real provider batch id and `status='validating'`, so the job exists upstream. Reproduced on both legs of the #35141 QA (its base and head); the code path is unchanged on current staging

### What a fix PR should look like

The clean fix is registration, not guards inside the hook: in `_add_proxy_hooks` (`litellm/proxy/utils.py:538-555`), skip constructing and registering any hook whose constructor requires `prisma_client` when the global `prisma_client` is `None`. Today that is exactly the managed-files hook, the only constructor asking for it. Consumers already treat the hook as optional, `litellm/proxy/batches_endpoints/endpoints.py:685` checks `is not None` and `litellm/proxy/response_api_endpoints/endpoints.py:360-364` casts to `_PROXY_LiteLLMManagedFiles | None`, so an unregistered hook lands on existing code paths and a DB-less proxy simply has no managed-files layer. Do not instead sprinkle `if self.prisma_client is None: return` inside the hook: a half-running hook would still rewrite ids and enforce access checks against a database it does not have

Tests: extend `tests/test_litellm/proxy/utils/proxy_logging/test_lifecycle.py`, which already pins `_add_proxy_hooks`, with a regression test that a `prisma_client`-requiring hook is left out of `proxy_hook_mapping` and out of the registered callbacks when `prisma_client` is `None`, and registered as today when one is present

QA proof: boot a DB-less proxy with Vertex credentials, run the three curls above, and show `POST /v1/batches` returning 200 with the batch object and `GET /v1/batches/{id}?provider=vertex_ai` polling it to `completed`. Then rerun with `DATABASE_URL` set and show the managed row still landing in `LiteLLM_ManagedObjectTable`, so the DB-backed behavior is unchanged

title: [Bug]: Anthropic streaming tool_use is lost before internal tool-call chunks on v1.95.0
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I searched existing issues. #2435 is an older same-direction report that was closed as fixed in 2024. #25321 and #20711 cover different adapter directions or event shapes.

### What happened?

With LiteLLM 1.95.0, an Anthropic-compatible `/v1/messages` stream can contain a valid `tool_use`, but `litellm.completion(..., stream=True)` emits only content chunks and no `delta.tool_calls`.

This is not a model/tool-choice failure in the observed requests:

- Sending the exact Anthropic request body generated by LiteLLM directly to the same `/v1/messages` endpoint returns `thinking -> text -> tool_use`, with `stop_reason="tool_use"` and the expected tool name.
- Sending the same logical request through LiteLLM with `stream=False` preserves the function call.
- Calling `litellm.completion(stream=True)` directly, before any Responses API conversion, produces 163 chunks, zero chunks with tool calls, `finish_reason="stop"`, and ordinary message content.
- The behavior reproduced with both `claude-sonnet-5` and `claude-opus-5`, including Sonnet at two reasoning-effort settings.

Therefore the tool call is already lost while the native Anthropic SSE is converted into LiteLLM's internal streaming chunks. A downstream Responses stream adapter cannot recover it.

Expected behavior: the native `tool_use` block and its `input_json_delta` events should become a streamed tool call and survive `stream_chunk_builder` aggregation.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure an Anthropic or Anthropic-compatible endpoint that can return a required tool call with a `thinking -> text -> tool_use` content-block sequence.
2. Run the following call shape with LiteLLM 1.95.0:

```python
import os
import litellm

messages = [
    {"role": "system", "content": "Call submit_result exactly once."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Return value=1 using the required tool."},
]
tools = [{
    "type": "function",
    "function": {
        "name": "submit_result",
        "description": "Submit the result",
        "parameters": {
            "type": "object",
            "additionalProperties": False,
            "properties": {"value": {"type": "integer"}},
            "required": ["value"],
        },
        "strict": True,
    },
}]

stream = litellm.completion(
    model="anthropic/claude-sonnet-5",
    messages=messages,
    tools=tools,
    tool_choice="required",
    parallel_tool_calls=False,
    reasoning_effort="high",
    max_tokens=24000,
    temperature=1.0,
    stream=True,
    stream_options={"include_usage": True},
    api_key=os.environ["ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"],
    api_base=os.environ.get("ANTHROPIC_API_BASE"),
    num_retries=0,
    max_retries=0,
    timeout=900,
)

chunks = list(stream)
built = litellm.stream_chunk_builder(chunks=chunks, messages=messages)

print("chunks:", len(chunks))
print("chunks with tool calls:", sum(
    1 for chunk in chunks
    if getattr(chunk.choices[0].delta, "tool_calls", None)
))
print("built:", built.model_dump())
```

3. Confirm separately that the exact Anthropic wire request returns a native `tool_use`, while the LiteLLM chunks contain no `tool_calls`.

The short prompt above shows the minimized request shape. Our captured reproduction used a larger application prompt; I can provide a sanitized native SSE fixture if useful for a deterministic regression test.

### Relevant log output

```shell
LiteLLM streaming result:
chunk_count=163
chunks_with_tool_calls=0
finish_reason=stop
message_content_present=true
tool_names=[]

Native SSE content_block_start sequence for the exact generated request:
index=0 type=thinking
index=1 type=text
index=2 type=tool_use name=submit_controller_action
stop_reason=tool_use

LiteLLM non-streaming result for the same logical request:
output_types=[reasoning,message,function_call]
tool_names=[submit_controller_action]
```

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

SDK (litellm Python package). The same loss also propagates through the Proxy Responses endpoint.

### What LiteLLM version are you on?

1.95.0

title: [Bug]: DB proxy routes all GET /v1/batches through managed files, provider filter 500s and Vertex provider-side listing is unreachable
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

On a proxy with a database attached, `GET /v1/batches` is unconditionally routed through the enterprise managed-files hook before any provider routing runs (`litellm/proxy/batches_endpoints/endpoints.py:684-694` at 1bafdb3c93). The hook rejects any `provider` filter with a bare `Exception` (`enterprise/litellm_enterprise/proxy/hooks/managed_files.py:346-349`), and `handle_exception_on_proxy` turns that into an opaque HTTP 500

Two consequences:

- `GET /v1/batches?provider=...` and the `GET /{provider}/v1/batches` route (the path param binds to the same `provider` argument, `endpoints.py:614-632`) return a 500 `internal_server_error` for what is really an unsupported-parameter condition, indistinguishable from a gateway crash
- The endpoint's own provider fallback (SCENARIO 3, `endpoints.py:737-756`), which supports `vertex_ai` via `litellm.alist_batches` (`litellm/types/utils.py:3715`), is unreachable on these deployments. No proxy route reaches `VertexAIBatchPrediction.list_batches`, so provider-side Vertex batches (anything created outside this proxy) cannot be listed at all

Found while QA'ing #35141 (see "What the QA also turned up" there): the list-path error handling that PR touches could not be exercised end to end because the route dies before reaching the handler

### User Flow

Today the walk dead-ends at step 2:

1. Create a Vertex batch through the proxy, `POST /v1/batches` with `"custom_llm_provider": "vertex_ai"`, and get back a unified batch id
2. `GET /v1/batches?provider=vertex_ai` to see that batch alongside everything else Vertex has, and get `500` with `{"error":{"message":"Filtering by 'provider' is not supported when using managed batches.","type":"internal_server_error","param":"None","code":"500"}}`
3. Retry as `GET /vertex_ai/v1/batches`, and get the same 500, since the path param feeds the same argument
4. Read `internal_server_error` as a gateway outage and retry or escalate, when nothing is down and the request was simply carrying an unsupported filter
5. Drop the filter, `GET /v1/batches`, and get only rows this proxy created. Batch prediction jobs created from the console, gsutil, or another gateway never appear, and no other proxy route reaches Vertex's list API

After a fix, the same walk succeeds at step 2:

1. Create a Vertex batch through the proxy the same way
2. `GET /v1/batches?provider=vertex_ai` returns 200 with the provider-side listing from `litellm.alist_batches`, and the job created in step 1 is in it under its provider-side id
3. `GET /v1/batches` with no filter keeps returning the managed view, unchanged

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the proxy with `DATABASE_URL` set (the managed-files hook registers automatically, `litellm/proxy/hooks/__init__.py` merges `ENTERPRISE_PROXY_HOOKS`)
2. `curl -sS -i "http://localhost:4000/v1/batches?provider=vertex_ai" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234"`
3. Observe HTTP 500 instead of a listing or a 4xx

### Relevant log output

```shell
$ curl -sS -i "http://localhost:4000/v1/batches?provider=vertex_ai" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234"
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
{"error":{"message":"Filtering by 'provider' is not supported when using managed batches.","type":"internal_server_error","param":"None","code":"500"}}
```

Reproduced at both `0acca3e86a` (base of #35141) and that PR's head, litellm 1.97.0

### What a fix PR should look like

Scope it as endpoint routing, not as adding provider metadata to the managed-objects table (that larger design is sketched in the comment at `managed_files.py:343-345` and can stay future work)

- `litellm/proxy/batches_endpoints/endpoints.py`: gate the managed-files branch in `list_batches` on having no `provider` and no `target_model_names` (the hook rejects both identically, `managed_files.py:354-357`), so filtered requests fall through to the existing SCENARIO 2-alt and SCENARIO 3 handling. Roughly a one-condition change around line 685
- `enterprise/litellm_enterprise/proxy/hooks/managed_files.py`: keep both guards as defense in depth, but raise `HTTPException(status_code=400, ...)` instead of bare `Exception`, so any remaining direct caller gets a 4xx rather than a 500
- Tests: adjust `tests/enterprise/litellm_enterprise/proxy/hooks/test_managed_files.py::test_list_batches_from_managed_objects_table_provider_filter_raises_exception` and its `target_model_names` twin to expect the `HTTPException`; add an endpoint-level test that a provider-filtered list on a DB proxy routes to `litellm.alist_batches` rather than the hook. The `managed_filter_unsupported` carve-out in `tests/e2e/batches/test_batches_e2e.py:299-319` can then be simplified since the filtered list stops erroring
- Behavior note for the PR body: SCENARIO 3 returns raw provider batch ids without unified-id encoding, matching what DB-less proxies do today, and unfiltered listing must not change
- QA proof: on a DB proxy with Vertex credentials, `GET /v1/batches?provider=vertex_ai` returns 200 and reaches `VertexAIBatchPrediction.list_batches`, which also finally exercises the list-path error handling touched by #35141 end to end. `GET /v1/batches` unfiltered still returns the managed view

### What version of LiteLLM are you on?

1.97.0 (litellm_internal_staging, 1bafdb3c93)
author: mateo-berri

title: [Bug]: Anthropic streams bypass protocol-aware custom guardrail iterators
body:
## Problem

PR #35260 fixed #35257 by routing Anthropic `/v1/messages` streams through Unified Guardrail translation.

A custom guardrail can implement both `apply_guardrail()` and `async_post_call_streaming_iterator_hook()`, with its iterator already handling Anthropic SSE. The current dispatcher detects `apply_guardrail()` and reroutes the callback to the Unified path anyway, bypassing the custom streaming iterator.

## Current behavior

The Unified fallback collects the stream before yielding the first guarded response. A protocol-aware custom iterator therefore does not receive the stream incrementally.

## Impact

- TTFT can approach the full response duration.
- The response is retained in memory while it is collected.
- Incremental, windowed, or request-level passthrough behavior implemented by the custom iterator is ignored.

## Expected behavior

A custom guardrail that explicitly supports the current streaming protocol should retain its own streaming iterator. Guardrails without protocol support should continue using the Unified fallback.
author: ZXYxc

title: [Bug]: Responses API — reasoning items (incl. encrypted_content) are silently dropped for providers without a native ResponsesAPIConfig (anthropic, bedrock/converse, non-gpt databricks)
body:
### What happened?

When a **Responses API** request carrying `reasoning` items is routed to a provider that has **no native `ResponsesAPIConfig`** (`anthropic/`, `bedrock/converse/`, non-`gpt` `databricks/`), LiteLLM converts the request to that provider's chat dialect and **silently drops every reasoning item**, including `encrypted_content`.

Tool plumbing survives the conversion correctly — this is specifically about reasoning state.

The practical effect is that a reasoning model loses its reasoning across every tool-call turn and re-derives it from scratch. That is the exact penalty the Responses API exists to avoid ([OpenAI measures it at +5% on TAUBench and 40–80% better cache utilization](https://developers.openai.com/blog/responses-api)). Because nothing errors, a caller migrating to `/v1/responses` for reasoning persistence gets none of it on these providers and has no signal that anything was lost.

Interestingly, LiteLLM *does* translate the reasoning **effort knob** on this path — it emits `thinking: {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": 2048}` (or `additionalModelRequestFields.thinking` for Bedrock). So the request tells Claude to think fresh while discarding the prior thinking. That combination is arguably worse than dropping both, because it spends tokens re-deriving reasoning that was already paid for.

### Relevant log output / evidence

Measured by pointing `api_base` at a local HTTP server that records the request body. Config:

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: p-anthropic
    litellm_params:
      model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929
      api_key: sk-ant-fake
      api_base: http://127.0.0.1:9099
  - model_name: p-bedrock
    litellm_params:
      model: bedrock/converse/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0
      aws_access_key_id: AKIAFAKEFAKEFAKEFAKE
      aws_secret_access_key: fakefakefakefakefakefakefakefakefakefake
      aws_region_name: us-east-1
      aws_bedrock_runtime_endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:9099
general_settings:
  master_key: sk-probe-local
```

Request to `POST /v1/responses`:

```json
{
  "model": "p-anthropic",
  "reasoning": {"effort": "medium"},
  "input": [
    {"role": "user", "content": "Check CWE-79 then CWE-89 and summarize."},
    {"type": "reasoning", "id": "rs_001",
     "summary": [{"type": "summary_text", "text": "First I should look up CWE-79."}],
     "encrypted_content": "ENCRYPTED_BLOB_ONE"},
    {"type": "function_call", "call_id": "call_1", "name": "lookup", "arguments": "{\"cwe\":\"79\"}"},
    {"type": "function_call_output", "call_id": "call_1", "output": "XSS details"},
    {"type": "reasoning", "id": "rs_002",
     "summary": [{"type": "summary_text", "text": "Now CWE-89."}],
     "encrypted_content": "ENCRYPTED_BLOB_TWO"},
    {"type": "function_call", "call_id": "call_2", "name": "lookup", "arguments": "{\"cwe\":\"89\"}"},
    {"type": "function_call_output", "call_id": "call_2", "output": "SQLi details"}
  ],
  "tools": [{"type": "function", "name": "lookup", "description": "Look up a CWE",
             "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"cwe": {"type": "string"}},
                            "required": ["cwe"]}}]
}
```

What each provider actually receives upstream, counting how many of the two `encrypted_content` blobs survive:

| `litellm_params.model` | Upstream route | Reasoning blobs surviving | Tool pairs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` | `POST /responses` | **2 / 2** | intact |
| `azure/gpt-5.4-mini` | `POST /openai/responses?api-version=…` | **2 / 2** | intact |
| `databricks/pixee-gpt54-mini` | `POST /responses` | **2 / 2** | intact |
| `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5-…` | `POST /v1/messages` | **0 / 2** | intact |
| `bedrock/converse/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-…` | `POST /model/{id}/converse` | **0 / 2** | intact |
| `databricks/claude-sonnet-4-5` (no `gpt` in name) | `POST /chat/completions` | **0 / 2** | intact |

The reasoning `summary` text is dropped along with `encrypted_content`. Identical results on **v1.86.1** and **v1.95.0**.

### Root cause

`ProviderConfigManager.get_provider_responses_api_config` (`litellm/utils.py`, ~L8214) has no entry for `ANTHROPIC` or for `bedrock/converse`, so those requests take the chat-conversion fallback, and that conversion has no representation for a reasoning item.

The mapping exists, but only in the opposite direction: `LiteLLMAnthropicToResponsesAPIAdapter` (`litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/responses_adapters/transformation.py`) implements `translate_thinking_to_reasoning` for the Anthropic-in → Responses-out path. There is no Responses-in → Anthropic-out counterpart that replays a `reasoning` item as a `thinking` block with its `signature`.

### Suggested fix

Replay reasoning items as Anthropic `thinking` / Bedrock `reasoningContent` blocks, preserving the signature, rather than dropping them. Anthropic's extended thinking already has the matching concept, and pydantic-ai's native `AnthropicModel` does exactly this round-trip today (`BetaThinkingBlockParam` with `signature`), so there is a working reference for the shape.

If a full mapping is not desirable, **failing loudly would be better than dropping silently** — today there is no way for a caller to detect the loss.

Two related notes:

1. **Please consider capability-driven dispatch rather than model-name substrings.** The Databricks branch still gates on `if model and "gpt" in model.lower()`, so renaming a model silently changes the wire format and the fidelity of the request. `BEDROCK_MANTLE` in the same function already does this the better way, and the comment there states the principle explicitly: *"Both decisions are data-driven from the model's price-map entry, with no model-name logic."* Extending `mantle_supports_responses`-style capability lookup to the other providers would remove a whole class of surprise.
2. This is adjacent to #35677, which is a different symptom of the same hardcoded-model-name pattern on the Anthropic Responses path.

### Are you a ML Ops Team?

No

### What LiteLLM version are you on?

v1.86.1 and v1.95.0 (both reproduce)

---

*(Filed on Johnathan Gilday's behalf by Claude Code.)*
author: gilday

title: Azure GPT-5.6 terra/luna cost-map rows carry OpenAI's prices, not Azure's published meters
body:
## What is wrong

`azure/gpt-5.6-terra` and `azure/gpt-5.6-luna`, along with their `azure/us/` and `azure/eu/` data-zone siblings, currently hold OpenAI's direct post-cut prices. Azure never made that cut.

OpenAI reduced Terra by 20% and Luna by 80% on 2026-07-30. #35481 then applied the same reduction to the twelve Azure rows on 2026-08-05. Its stated basis was that "Azure global historically mirrors OpenAI global for these models"; the Azure link it cites is a Microsoft Foundry availability announcement, not a pricing page. @mihidumh raised exactly this objection in a comment on the merged PR the next morning ("Azure has not updated their pricing yet, this should be reverted for now"), and the change is still on `main` and `litellm_internal_staging` today.

## Evidence

Azure's public retail prices API is the authoritative list-price source, and it needs no authentication:

```bash
curl -sS -G "https://prices.azure.com/api/retail/prices" \
  --data-urlencode "currencyCode=USD" \
  --data-urlencode "\$filter=contains(productName,'Azure OpenAI') and armRegionName eq 'eastus2'"
```

Every GPT-5.6 meter still carries `effectiveStartDate` of 2026-07-01 as a single version, so there is no cut applied and none future-dated. The values are identical in `eastus2`, `westus3` and `swedencentral`, so this is not a regional anomaly. Global Standard rates, per 1M tokens:

| Model | Field | Azure meter | Cost map today | Error |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| terra | input | $2.50 | $2.00 | 20% under |
| terra | output | $15.00 | $12.00 | 20% under |
| terra | cache read | $0.25 | $0.20 | 20% under |
| luna | input | $1.00 | $0.20 | 5x under |
| luna | output | $6.00 | $1.20 | 5x under |
| luna | cache read | $0.10 | $0.02 | 5x under |

The relevant meter names are `5.6 terra ShortCo Inp Std Gl 1M Tokens` and siblings, where `Gl` is Global and `DZ` is Data Zone at exactly 1.1x, `Std` is Standard and `PP` is Priority Processing at exactly 2x, and `ShortCo`/`LongCo` are the base and above-272k tiers. Those exact 1.1x and 2x ratios hold across the whole family, which is a good indication the rows are live rather than stale. Sol was not cut by either vendor and is correct as it stands.

## Impact

Any Azure deployment of GPT-5.6 Terra or Luna under-reports spend by 20% and 80% respectively, silently, on every request. Luna is the worse case because the map bills a fifth of the real rate.

#35481 also added `test_generic_cost_per_token_azure_gpt56`, which asserts the incorrect Azure global and EU data-zone values. The wrong numbers are now test-locked, so a straight revert of the JSON alone will fail CI; the test needs correcting in the same change.

## The same root cause is about to land again in #35125

#35125 is open and adds the missing `cache_creation_input_token_cost` fields to all twelve Azure GPT-5.6 entries. The underlying gap is real, since Azure does publish cache-write meters and the map currently bills those tokens at zero. The Sol and base-alias values in that PR match Azure exactly, but the Terra and Luna values are OpenAI-derived in the same way as #35481:

| Key | Field | Azure meter | #35125 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `azure/gpt-5.6-terra` | cache write | $3.125 | $2.50 |
| `azure/gpt-5.6-terra` | cache write above 272k | $6.25 | $5.00 |
| `azure/gpt-5.6-luna` | cache write | $1.25 | $0.25 |
| `azure/gpt-5.6-luna` | cache write above 272k | $2.50 | $0.50 |

Separately, that PR derives the data-zone `_priority` cache-write fields with a 2.5x multiplier where Azure's Priority Processing meters are exactly 2x Standard, so `azure/us/gpt-5.6` and `azure/eu/gpt-5.6` come out at $17.1875 against a published $13.75, and the Sol rows likewise.

## Suggested fix

Restore the Terra and Luna token prices on all twelve Azure rows to the meter values in the first table, and correct `test_generic_cost_per_token_azure_gpt56` to match. For #35125, resource the Terra and Luna cache-write numbers from the `Cd Wr` meters and use 2x rather than 2.5x for the Priority Processing fields.

More generally, an OpenAI price change is not evidence about Azure. The retail prices API query above is cheap, unauthenticated and definitive, and it is worth making the standard check before porting any price movement onto an `azure/` row.

I am happy to open the PR for either part if that helps.
author: marty-sullivan

title: [Feature]: /ui/usage should persist selected time range and activity tab across page reload
body:
### The Feature

Persist the user's selection on the `/ui/usage` dashboard across a full page reload:
- The "Select Time Range" date picker (whether a relative preset like "Today"/"7d" or a custom range)
- The selected usage view (Global/Team/Tag/etc.) and the active tab within it (Cost/Model Activity/Key Activity/etc.)

Currently these all reset to defaults on every reload, and a relative preset like "Today" is computed once at page load and frozen, so it silently goes stale if the tab is left open across midnight.

### Motivation, pitch

Every time an admin reloads `/ui/usage` (or comes back to it later), they have to re-pick their date range and re-navigate to the tab they were looking at. This is a small but constant friction point for anyone who keeps the usage dashboard open and refreshes periodically.

While testing this, also found and fixed a related bug: the "Apply" button in the date-range picker never closes the dropdown in Safari, because `handleApply()` calls `requestIdleCallback()` (which Safari has never implemented) before closing it - the resulting exception silently skips the close. Included that fix in the same PR since it's the same component.

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

UI Dashboard

title: [Bug]: /ui/usage shows 0 tokens for rerank calls (hosted_vllm and other providers)
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

`/rerank` calls always show `prompt_tokens`/`completion_tokens`/`total_tokens` as `0` in `/ui/usage` and spend logs, for every rerank provider, not just `hosted_vllm`.

  Root cause: `RerankResponse` has no top-level `usage` field, only `meta.billed_units`/`meta.tokens`. `StandardLoggingPayloadSetup.get_usage_from_response_obj()` and `get_usage_as_dict()` in
  `litellm_core_utils/litellm_logging.py` only ever read `response_obj["usage"]`, so they silently return zeroed usage for rerank responses.

  Separately, `HostedVLLMRerankConfig._transform_response()` in `llms/hosted_vllm/rerank/transformation.py` only reads `response["usage"]`, but vLLM's `/rerank` endpoint (Cohere-compatible) returns
  usage under `response["meta"]` instead, so even the raw `RerankResponse.meta` ends up wrong for hosted_vllm.

  Expected: token counts from `meta.billed_units`/`meta.tokens` should show up in `/ui/usage`, same as `usage` does for chat/embeddings.

### Steps to Reproduce

 1. Configure a rerank model, e.g. `hosted_vllm/BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3`.
  2. `curl <proxy>/v1/rerank -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -d '{"model": "hosted_vllm/BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3", "query": "...", "documents": ["...", "..."]}'`
  3. Response includes real usage under `meta.billed_units.total_tokens`.

title: Uvicorn workers die silently during long SSE streams, taking every in-flight stream with them (v1.90.6, --num_workers 2)
body:
### What happens

With `--num_workers 2`, worker processes die and get respawned by the master
while long streaming completions are in flight. Every SSE stream that worker was
carrying dies in the same instant, client-side as an abruptly closed socket.

The container itself never restarts (`RestartCount=0`), the master process keeps
its original start time, and **nothing is written to the log** — it goes straight
from silence to the replacement worker's `register_model` sequence.

### Evidence

Over 20 days of persisted client-side attempts, 75 mid-stream disconnects. They
are not independent: **53 of 75 happen within one second of the previous one.**
Grouped into 2-second windows they form ~20 bursts:

| Burst start (UTC) | Sockets killed | Window |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-07-28 13:50:30 | 9 | 18 ms |
| 2026-08-02 11:57:55 | 7 | 42 ms |
| 2026-08-03 14:43:46 | 7 | 8 ms |
| 2026-08-06 11:17:51 | 6 | 62 ms |
| 2026-08-07 09:45:54 | 5 | 700 ms |

Nine sockets in eighteen milliseconds is not a network fault.

Correlated on the server for the last burst — process start times tell the story:

| Process | RSS | Started (UTC) |
|---|---|---|
| master `litellm --num_workers 2` | 616 MB | **05:17:38** |
| worker 1 | 697 MB | **09:45:43** |
| worker 2 | 673 MB | **09:46:59** |

Timeline: worker 1 dies at 09:45:43 and is respawned immediately; the client sees
5 sockets die at 09:45:54; the replacement finishes `register_model` at 09:46:03;
worker 2 then dies at 09:46:59 and is respawned at 09:47:19.

### Not memory

This was my first hypothesis and it is ruled out: no container memory limit,
`OOMKilled=false`, nothing in `dmesg` or the kernel journal, 4.6 GiB free on the
host, load average 0.02. Workers sit at ~700 MB each, container at 1.93 GiB of
7.75 GiB available.

### Environment

- `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database:v1.90.6`, Docker, Ubuntu 24.04, 2 vCPU / 8 GB
- `--num_workers 2`, `LITELLM_MODE=PRODUCTION`, `LITELLM_LOG=ERROR`
- `store_model_in_db: False`, config-file driven, ~50 models mostly routed through
  OpenRouter
- Streaming completions lasting 4 to 10 minutes (long HTML generations)

### Why it matters

Short completions are essentially unaffected — models answering in seconds show a
0% disconnect rate through the same gateway that shows 29.5% for a long-running
model. The disconnect rate tracks **exposure time**, so this hits long streaming
workloads specifically.

### Questions

1. Does the master apply any heartbeat/timeout to its workers that a worker busy
   with several multi-minute SSE streams could miss?
2. Is there a way to have a dying worker log its cause at `LITELLM_LOG=ERROR`?
   Right now the death is completely silent, which makes this very hard to
   diagnose without taking the proxy down to raise the log level.
3. Is `--num_workers` expected to be safe with long-lived SSE connections, or
   should long-streaming deployments run a single worker?

Happy to run with `LITELLM_LOG=INFO` and attach logs — tell me what you need
captured and I will schedule the restart.

title: [Bug]: Batch/Files upload loses model/deployment routing when forwarded to a second LiteLLM proxy
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

Uploading a file for the Batch API fails when one LiteLLM proxy is configured with a model deployment whose `api_base` points at a second LiteLLM proxy (a chained-proxy setup). The request that reaches the second proxy is a bare `/v1/files` upload with no `target_model_names` and no `model`, so it cannot be routed to the correct backend deployment on the second proxy.

**Setup:** proxy A has `gpt-4.1-batch` configured with `litellm_params.model: openai/gpt-4.1-batch` pointing at proxy B's `api_base`. Client uploads with `client.files.create(file=..., purpose="batch", extra_body={"target_model_names": "gpt-4.1-batch"})` against proxy A. This is the documented managed-files pattern and works fine against a single proxy.

Traceback confirms the request reaches proxy A's managed-files hook correctly (enterprise license, `target_model_names` present):

```
files_endpoints.py:route_create_file -> managed_files_obj.acreate_file
managed_files.py:create_file_for_each_model -> llm_router.acreate_file
router.py:create_file_for_deployment -> litellm.acreate_file
files/main.py:acreate_file -> openai/openai.py:acreate_file
openai_client.files.create(**create_file_data)
```

The bug is in `router.py::create_file_for_deployment` (`Router._acreate_file`): it builds the downstream `litellm.acreate_file(**{**data, "custom_llm_provider": custom_llm_provider, ..., **kwargs_copy})` call from only the deployment's static `litellm_params` plus the original `file`/`purpose` kwargs. It never forwards `target_model_names` or the resolved model into the downstream request.

As a result, proxy B receives a bare upload, `custom_llm_provider` defaults to `"openai"` (the `Form` default in `files_endpoints.py::create_file`), and proxy B has no way to know which of its own deployments the file was meant for. If proxy B has no matching model/provider hint, it raises `files_settings is not set, set it on your config.yaml file.` (from `get_files_provider_config`). If a `files_settings` fallback entry is added on proxy B keyed to whatever provider it defaults to, credentials attach but the request still goes to the wrong endpoint shape for the actual target deployment (e.g., an OpenAI-shaped `/v1/files` call against an Azure-backed deployment returns a 404), because the original deployment identity was never recoverable.

## Expected behavior

`create_file_for_deployment` should forward `target_model_names` (or the resolved model) to the downstream `acreate_file` call, e.g. via `extra_body`, so a second-hop LiteLLM proxy can route the upload to the correct deployment using the same managed-files mechanism, instead of falling back to a bare default provider.

## Related issues

https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/31867 documents the same class of bug for chat completions: `LiteLLMProxyChatConfig.transform_request()` silently drops internal routing metadata (`tags`, `litellm_session_id`) when one LiteLLM proxy forwards to another LiteLLM proxy as its backend. This issue is the Batch/Files equivalent, in a different code path (`router.py::create_file_for_deployment` rather than `litellm_proxy/chat/transformation.py`).

### Steps to Reproduce

We reproduced this with a minimal repro chain (self-hosted Proxy A -> self-hosted Proxy B (intermediate proxy) -> Azure, Azure-only, no third-party proxy involved) and confirmed each stage:

1. No `files_settings` on the intermediate proxy: `files_settings is not set`.
2. `files_settings` keyed to a provider that doesn't match the bare upload's resolved provider: `api_key client option must be set` (fallback entry never selected).
3. `files_settings` keyed to match: credentials attach, but the intermediate proxy issues an OpenAI-shaped request against an Azure endpoint: `404 Resource not found`.

### Relevant log output

```shell
Error code: 500 - {'error': {'message': 'files_settings is not set, set it on your config.yaml file.', 'type': 'None', 'param': 'None', 'code': '500'}}



Error code: 500 - {'error': {'message': 'The api_key client option must be set either by passing api_key to the client or by setting the OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable', 'type': 'None', 'param': 'None', 'code': '500'}}



Error code: 404 - {'error': {'code': '404', 'message': 'Resource not found'}}
```

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

`v1.91.3` (also confirmed unfixed in `v1.95.0`)

### Twitter / LinkedIn details

_No response_

title: [Bug]: Router pre-call context-window check blocks the event loop (sync token_counter on async path)
body:
### What happened?

`Router.async_get_healthy_deployments` calls the **sync** `_pre_call_checks`, which calls `_count_pre_call_check_tokens` -> `litellm.token_counter` (tiktoken) directly on the event loop.

With `enable_pre_call_checks=True` and deployments that declare `max_input_tokens`, every async completion blocks the loop for the duration of the count. Measured on our side: ~91ms @ 200k tokens, ~454ms @ 1M tokens, and up to 2.6s stalls in production (all other coroutines starved, incl. health/liveness).

Call chain at `v1.97.0`:

```
async_get_available_deployment      litellm/router.py:10812
  -> async_get_healthy_deployments  litellm/router.py:10676
     -> self._pre_call_checks(...)  litellm/router.py:10765   # sync call from async
        -> _count_pre_call_check_tokens  litellm/router.py:10207
           -> litellm.token_counter      # tiktoken, sync
```

#31497 helped by skipping the count when no deployment has `max_input_tokens` and counting at most once, but when a limit *is* configured the count still runs on the loop. #26193 tracks the same class of problem at a different call site (`stream_chunk_builder` / `count_reasoning_tokens`).

### Proposed fix

tiktoken's Rust extension releases the GIL, so a thread offload gives real parallelism. Precompute once in the async entry and pass it into the sync filter:

```python
# router.py, async_get_healthy_deployments
input_tokens = None
if self.enable_pre_call_checks and (messages is not None or input is not None):
    input_tokens = await asyncio.to_thread(
        self._count_pre_call_check_tokens, messages, input, instructions
    )

healthy_deployments = self._pre_call_checks(
    ...,
    input_tokens=input_tokens,   # new optional kwarg
)
```

`_pre_call_checks` gains `input_tokens: Optional[int] = None` and skips its own counting when the value is provided. Sync `get_available_deployment` (`:11349`) is unchanged and keeps counting inline.

Alternative with the existing helper: `await asyncify(self._count_pre_call_check_tokens)(...)` (`litellm/litellm_core_utils/asyncify.py`).

No public API break; one optional kwarg.

### Workaround we use today

Monkey-patching `Router._count_pre_call_check_tokens` + both async getters to precompute via `asyncio.to_thread` and stash in a `ContextVar`. Works, but we'd rather drop it. Happy to open a PR if the shape above looks right.

- `disable_token_counter=True` is not equivalent (it disables context-window pre-filtering too).

### Relevant log output

```shell
Event loop heartbeats during pre-call check (18 expected):
  sync token_counter : 1/18   (loop starved)
  asyncio.to_thread  : 19/18  (loop responsive)
```

### Are you a ML Ops Team?

Yes

### What LiteLLM version are you on?

v1.95.0 (also present at v1.97.0 / HEAD)

### Twitter / LinkedIn details

_No response_

title: [Bug]: LiteLLM 1.94.0 — Bug reports
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

# LiteLLM 1.94.0 — Bug reports (GitHub issue drafts)

Self-hosted LiteLLM proxy, multi-provider routing. Environment for all reports:

- **LiteLLM**: 1.94.0
- **Python**: 3.12
- **OS**: RHEL / Enterprise Linux 9.8 (`5.14.0-687.15.1.el9_8.x86_64`)
- **OpenSSL**: 3.5.5
- **DB**: PostgreSQL (Prisma client)
- **Config**: `store_model_in_db: true`; model groups back multiple deployments across providers (Zhipu / iFlytek / Volcengine Ark), exposed via the Anthropic pass-through endpoint `/v1/messages`.

Each section below is a self-contained issue draft (title + body) that can be pasted into a new GitHub issue. Issues are ordered by impact/relevance to us. Items 1–2 below (issues A and B) are the ones we most want fixed upstream.

---

## Issue A — Failed requests don't record which upstream deployment was selected (SpendLogs `api_base` / `model_id` / `model_group` empty on failures)

### Title
Failed LLM requests don't record the selected upstream deployment in `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` (`api_base`, `model_id`, `model_group` are empty on failure rows)

### What happened
For a model group backed by multiple deployments across providers, a **failed** request produces a `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` row whose `api_base`, `model_id`, and `model_group` columns are all empty. There is no way to tell which upstream deployment/provider actually returned the error. **Successful** requests on the same path populate these columns correctly, so the information is available at call time — it is simply not persisted on the failure path.

Measured on our instance (last 2 days), same pass-through model group family:

| model (SpendLogs.model) | rows | rows with `api_base` | rows with `model_id` | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `anthropic/GLM-5.2` (mostly success) | 898 | 898 | 898 | populated ✅ |
| `anthropic/GLM-5` (all failures)   | 58  | 0   | 0   | empty ❌ |

### Expected behavior
A failed request should record the same deployment-routing fields a successful request records: `api_base`, `model_id` (the selected deployment's `model_info.id`), and `model_group`. This is essential for operating a multi-provider proxy — when an upstream returns 4xx/5xx, operators must be able to find *which* deployment was hit.

### Reproduction
1. Configure a model group (e.g. `anthropic/GLM-5`) backed by ≥2 deployments pointing at different upstream Anthropic-compatible endpoints (different `api_base` / credential per deployment).
2. Send a request through the Anthropic pass-through endpoint that one upstream will reject with a 4xx (e.g. an upstream whose gateway doesn't recognize the model name → HTTP 400).
3. Inspect the resulting `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` row:

```sql
SELECT "startTime", model, api_base, model_id, model_group,
       metadata->'error_information'->>'error_message' AS err
FROM "LiteLLM_SpendLogs"
WHERE metadata->'error_information' IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY "startTime" DESC LIMIT 5;
```

Observed: `api_base`, `model_id`, `model_group` are `''`. The upstream URL is only recoverable from the proxy log's `MaskedHTTPStatusError ... for url 'https://<upstream>/v1/messages'` traceback line — not from the DB.

### Root cause
1. `LiteLLM_ErrorLogs` is a dead table. It exists in the Prisma schema (`litellm/proxy/schema.prisma`, model `LiteLLM_ErrorLogs`, with `api_base`, `model_group`, `litellm_model_name`, `model_id`, `request_kwargs`, `exception_type`, `exception_string`, `status_code`) and has a Pydantic model (`litellm/models/spend_logs.py`), but **no code anywhere in the package ever inserts into it** (no `.create()` / `.upsert()` / `INSERT INTO "LiteLLM_ErrorLogs"`). It is always 0 rows, so the error dashboards in `spend_management_endpoints.py` that `SELECT` from it always return empty.
2. Errors are actually persisted in `LiteLLM_SpendLogs.metadata.error_information`, written by `ProxyTrackCostCallback.async_post_call_failure_hook` → `DBSpendUpdateWriter.update_database` → `get_logging_payload` (`litellm/proxy/spend_tracking/spend_tracking_utils.py`).
3. `get_logging_payload` reads the three columns from the failure-path kwargs:
   - `api_base = litellm_params.get("api_base", "")`  (spend_tracking_utils.py ~L426)
   - `model_id = metadata.get("model_info", {}).get("id", "")`  (~L310)
   - `model_group = metadata.get("model_group", "")`  (~L311)
4. On the failure path, `async_post_call_failure_hook` (`litellm/proxy/hooks/proxy_track_cost_callback.py`, ~L50–177) rebuilds the spend-log kwargs from the **proxy-level** `request_data`, and only lifts `model` and `custom_llm_provider` from the logging object (~L128–133). It does **not** lift `api_base`, `model_info`, or `model_group` — even though they are present on the logging object (`logging_obj.litellm_params`).
5. The logging object **is** reachable on the failure path: `base_process_llm_request` sets `data["litellm_logging_obj"]` (`common_request_processing.py` ~L1248), the Anthropic endpoint passes `data` as `request_data` to `post_call_failure_hook` (`anthropic_endpoints/endpoints.py` ~L189–190), and `update_database(kwargs=request_data)` → `get_logging_payload(kwargs=request_data)` therefore has `kwargs["litellm_logging_obj"]` available. `LiteLLMLoggingObj.pre_call` populates `model_call_details["litellm_params"]["api_base"]` (`litellm_core_utils/litellm_logging.py` ~L923), and the router sets `model_info` / `model_group` on `litellm_params`.

So the data exists; it is just not copied into the spend-log kwargs on failures. (Note the existing `# [TODO] migrate completely to sl payload. currently missing pass-through endpoint data` comment in `get_logging_payload`.)

### Suggested fix (upstream)
In `async_post_call_failure_hook`, mirror the existing `model`/`custom_llm_provider` lift and also copy `api_base`, `model_info`, and `model_group` from `litellm_logging_obj.litellm_params` (or `model_call_details["litellm_params"]`) into `request_data["litellm_params"]` / its `metadata` before `update_database` runs. Guard for `litellm_logging_obj is None`.

Alternatively (or additionally): actually write to `LiteLLM_ErrorLogs` (the table is purpose-built with exactly these columns but is currently never populated).

### Workaround
Monkey-patch `get_logging_payload` to lift the three fields from `kwargs["litellm_logging_obj"]` before the original runs (fallback-on-empty only, so the success path is untouched). Happy to share the patch.

---

## Issue B — ChatGPT subscription Responses API streaming returns 400 `"Stream must be set to true"`

### Title
ChatGPT subscription provider: streaming `POST /v1/responses` (`stream=true`) returns 400 `"Stream must be set to true"`; non-streaming works

### What happened
Using a ChatGPT subscription model through the Responses API, a **streaming** request fails:

```
litellm.BadRequestError: ChatgptException - {"detail":"Stream must be set to true"}
Received Model Group=chatgpt/gpt-5.5
```

- Failing request: `POST /v1/responses` with `model="chatgpt/gpt-5.5"`, `stream=true`.
- LiteLLM's upstream request path is `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses`.
- The same request with `stream=false` succeeds (200).
- The model is configured with `model_info.mode = "responses"`, `blocked = false`.
- This is **not** a config issue: non-streaming `/v1/responses` correctly sends `stream=true` to the ChatGPT backend and LiteLLM aggregates the SSE into a normal Responses JSON. Only the client-facing streaming path is broken.

### Expected behavior
`POST /v1/responses` with `stream=true` should return 200 with an SSE body (`data: …`).

### Reproduction
```bash
curl -sS -o /tmp/r.out -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST http://<proxy>:4000/v1/responses \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"chatgpt/gpt-5.5","input":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply exactly ok"}],"stream":true}'
# 400, body: {"detail":"Stream must be set to true"}
```
With `"stream":false` → 200.

### Root cause
In 1.89.0–1.94.0, the ChatGPT provider's Responses streaming path triggers a 400 from the ChatGPT Codex Responses backend. The non-streaming path correctly forwards `stream=true` to the backend and aggregates SSE; the streaming path does not.

### Files
```
litellm/llms/custom_httpx/llm_http_handler.py
litellm/llms/chatgpt/responses/transformation.py
```

### Workaround
Monkey-patch: for `custom_llm_provider == "chatgpt"` with Responses `stream=true`, route through LiteLLM's already-working non-httpx-stream Responses path and synthesize SSE back to the client via `CachedResponsesAPIStreamingIterator`. Other providers, non-streaming Responses, and `/chat/completions` are unaffected. (Status as of 1.94.0: patch logic still effective; we could not capture a 200 positive case because the ChatGPT account hit `usage_limit_reached`, but the error is the rate-limit error, not the `400 Stream must be set to true` regression.)

---

## Issue C — `pip install --upgrade litellm` does not regenerate the Prisma client → login & key creation fail with `FieldNotFoundError`

### Title
After `pip install --upgrade litellm`, login (`POST /v2/login`) and key creation (`/key/generate`) return 500 with `prisma.errors.FieldNotFoundError` until `prisma generate` is run manually

### What happened
After upgrading LiteLLM via `pip install --upgrade litellm`, the first login or key creation fails:

```
prisma.errors.FieldNotFoundError: Could not find field at `upsertOneLiteLLM_VerificationToken.create.project_id`
```

Login failing means the entire admin UI is inaccessible. (Upstream has a same-shape report: #19238, their field was `organization_id`.)

### Root cause
`pip install --upgrade litellm` replaces LiteLLM's Python code and the schema source (`litellm/proxy/schema.prisma`, and since 1.93.0 `litellm_proxy_extras/schema.prisma`), but does **not** regenerate the Prisma client (the generated `prisma/` package under `site-packages`: `models.py`, `actions.py`, `schema.prisma`, embedded engine datamodel). The stale client's `models.py`/`schema.prisma` *appear* to contain the new field, but the generated internals (actions/partials/engine datamodel) are inconsistent with the new schema, so the engine's loaded datamodel is missing the field and `upsert … create <field>` raises `FieldNotFoundError`.

This is **not** a missing column or a missing migration: the DB table has the column, the schema source has the field, and a fresh minimal probe recognizes the field (which bypasses the inconsistency and is misleading during triage). The reliable signal is that the generated client's mtime predates the upgrade.

### Reproduction
```bash
pip install --upgrade litellm==1.94.0
# restart proxy, then:
curl -sS -o /tmp/kg.out -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST http://<proxy>:4000/key/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <master_key>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"models":[]}'
# 500; log shows FieldNotFoundError on project_id
```

### Expected behavior
`pip install --upgrade litellm` should leave the proxy in a working state, or print a clear post-install step. Operators should not have to know to run `prisma generate` against LiteLLM's bundled schema after every upgrade.

### Workaround / manual fix
```bash
export DATABASE_URL="postgresql://…/litellm"
prisma generate --schema="$(python3.12 -c 'import litellm,os;print(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(litellm.__file__),"proxy","schema.prisma"))')"
# then restart; /key/generate -> 200
```
Note: 1.94.0 ships prisma-python 0.15.0 (client format changed), so a client generated under an older prisma-python breaks again even if the LiteLLM version didn't change the schema.

### Suggested fix
Ship a pre-generated, version-matched Prisma client in the wheel, or run `prisma generate` as a post-install hook against the bundled schema, or fail fast at startup with a clear "run prisma generate" message instead of `FieldNotFoundError` mid-request.

---

## Issue D — Prisma query-engine binary missing `rhel-openssl-3.5.x` variant on EL9 / OpenSSL 3.5 → `NotConnectedError` on startup

### Title
On RHEL/EL9 with OpenSSL 3.5, prisma-python 0.15.0 looks for `prisma-query-engine-rhel-openssl-3.5.x` which `@prisma/engines` does not ship → proxy cannot start

### What happened
After upgrading to 1.94.0 (which brings prisma-python **0.15.0** + Prisma engine **5.17.0**), the proxy fails to start:

```
prisma.engine.errors.NotConnectedError: Not connected to the query engine
```
(the underlying error is `prisma.engine.errors.BinaryNotFoundError`).

### Root cause
prisma-python 0.15.0 derives the query-engine binary variant from the system OpenSSL version:
```
prisma/engine/utils.py :: query_engine_name() -> f'prisma-query-engine-{platform.binary_platform()}'
```
On EL9.8 with OpenSSL 3.5.5 this resolves to `rhel-openssl-3.5.x`, but `@prisma/engines` 5.17.0 only ships the `rhel-openssl-3.0.x` variant (which `prisma generate` / `prisma py fetch` actually downloads). The runtime then can't find `prisma-query-engine-rhel-openssl-3.5.x`:

```
Expected .../prisma-query-engine-rhel-openssl-3.5.x ... to exist but neither were found or could be executed.
Try running prisma py fetch
```

Key facts:
- The binary **is** downloaded (the `rhel-openssl-3.0.x` variant is in `~/.cache/prisma-python/binaries/5.17.0/.../@prisma/engines/`).
- The 3.0.x-compiled engine dynamically links `libssl.so.3`/`libcrypto.so.3` and is **ABI-compatible and fully runnable** on OpenSSL 3.5 (`--version` and `query_raw SELECT 1` both pass). The platform name is a misjudgment, not a real incompatibility.
- `prisma migrate deploy` succeeds (it uses the node Prisma CLI, which resolves the platform differently); only the prisma-python **runtime client** fails — which is misleading during triage.

### Reproduction
```bash
openssl version      # OpenSSL 3.5.5
# install litellm 1.94.0, prisma generate, then start proxy:
# startup log: NotConnectedError; cache only has query-engine-rhel-openssl-3.0.x
ls ~/.cache/prisma-python/binaries/5.17.0/*/node_modules/@prisma/engines/
```

### Workaround
prisma's `ensure()` reads `PRISMA_QUERY_ENGINE_BINARY` first and, if set, uses that path and skips platform/version validation. Point it at the downloaded `query-engine-rhel-openssl-3.0.x` (ABI-compatible) before any prisma client connects:

```bash
export PRISMA_QUERY_ENGINE_BINARY="$HOME/.cache/prisma-python/binaries/5.17.0/<hash>/node_modules/@prisma/engines/query-engine-rhel-openssl-3.0.x"
```
We automate this at startup (glob the cache for the newest `query-engine-rhel-openssl-*.x`).

### Suggested fix
Either ship/extract the `rhel-openssl-3.5.x` variant, or have prisma-python fall back to the `3.0.x` variant when `3.5.x` is absent (they are ABI-compatible on `libssl.so.3`). This is arguably a prisma-python / `@prisma/engines` packaging issue, but it blocks LiteLLM startup on a common enterprise Linux + OpenSSL 3.5 combination, so noting it here.

---

## Issue E — Admin UI crashes on `crypto.randomUUID` when served over HTTP (non-secure context)

### Title
Admin UI throws `TypeError: crypto.randomUUID is not a function` when accessed over plain HTTP (non-secure context); no polyfill shipped

### What happened
When the admin UI is accessed over `http://<ip>:4000` (HTTP, non-localhost), any feature that calls `crypto.randomUUID()` throws and the feature breaks:

```
Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: crypto.randomUUID is not a function
```
Typical trigger: the "New conversation" button (generates a conversation id via `crypto.randomUUID()`).

### Root cause
`crypto.randomUUID()` (and `crypto.subtle`) are only available in a secure context (HTTPS or localhost). Over plain HTTP + IP, `window.crypto.randomUUID` is `undefined`. This is a browser security policy, but the UI ships no polyfill, so self-hosted deployments that serve the UI over plain HTTP are broken out of the box.

### Expected behavior
The admin UI should work over plain HTTP (the default self-hosted deployment) without requiring a reverse proxy / TLS just to click "New conversation". A `crypto.randomUUID` polyfill (via `crypto.getRandomValues()`, which *is* available in non-secure contexts) would fix it.

### Files
```
litellm/proxy/_experimental/out/**/*.html   (UI static bundle; ~12 call sites use randomUUID)
```

### Workaround
Inject a `crypto.randomUUID` polyfill (RFC4122 v4 via `crypto.getRandomValues`) into the UI HTML `<head>` at startup. Alternatively, put the UI behind HTTPS or access via `http://127.0.0.1:4000/ui` (localhost is a secure context).

### Suggested fix
Ship a `crypto.randomUUID` polyfill in the UI bundle (gated on `!crypto.randomUUID`), so HTTP deployments work without a reverse proxy.

title: [Bug]: Usage tab merges public model groups that share the same underlying model
body:
### Check for existing issues

### What happened?

## Problem

When multiple public model groups route to the same underlying LiteLLM model, raw spend logs preserve the correct `model_group`, but Usage tab daily aggregates can merge or miss those model groups.

Example:

- `a -> openai/gpt-4o-mini`
- `b -> openai/gpt-4o-mini`
- `c -> openai/gpt-4o-mini`

Raw logs show separate `model_group` values for `a`, `b`, and `c`, but the daily spend aggregate uniqueness does not include `model_group`, so rows can collapse in the Usage tab.

## Expected behavior

Usage tab should show separate usage for each public model group.

## Actual behavior

Usage can show missing model groups or mismatched counts/spend when public model groups share the same backend model.

## Reproduction

1. Configure public models `a`, `b`, and `c` to all route to `openai/gpt-4o-mini`.
2. Send requests to each model.
3. Check `LiteLLM_SpendLogs`: rows include correct `model_group`.
4. Check Usage tab / daily activity: public model group usage can be merged or missing.

## Root cause

Daily spend aggregate unique keys and upsert selectors include the underlying `model`, but not `model_group`.

## Fix

Include `model_group` in daily spend unique constraints, upsert selectors, transaction keys, and migration indexes.

### Steps to Reproduce

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure multiple public model names that point to the same underlying LiteLLM model:

