author: juarbela

title: [Bug]: explicit `additionalProperties: true` is forwarded to Anthropic `output_format.schema` and 400s (filter only fills in when absent)
body:
### What happened?

When a `response_format: {"type": "json_schema", ...}` schema contains an **explicit** `"additionalProperties": true` on an object, LiteLLM forwards it unchanged into Anthropic's native structured-outputs field `output_format.schema`. Anthropic rejects it with a 400:

```
output_format.schema: For 'object' type, 'additionalProperties: true' is not supported.
Please set 'additionalProperties' to false
```

`AnthropicConfig.filter_anthropic_output_schema` only **adds** `additionalProperties` when the key is **absent** — it never coerces an explicit non-`false` value:

https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/litellm_internal_staging/litellm/llms/anthropic/chat/transformation.py#L598-L601

```python
# Anthropic requires additionalProperties=false for object schemas
# See: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/structured-outputs
if result.get("type") == "object" and "additionalProperties" not in result:
    result["additionalProperties"] = False
```

Because `additionalProperties` is not in the unsupported/strip set, an explicit value is copied verbatim by the catch-all `else: result[key] = value` branch, and the `not in result` guard then never fires.

**Expected:** the value is coerced to `false` for object schemas (at every nesting depth), matching what Anthropic's own SDKs do, so the request succeeds instead of 400ing.

**Why coercing is correct here.** Anthropic's [structured outputs docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/structured-outputs) list under *Supported features*: "`required` and `additionalProperties` (must be set to `false` for objects)", and under *Not supported*: "`additionalProperties` set to anything other than `false`". The official SDKs unconditionally overwrite rather than fill-in-if-absent:
- [anthropic-sdk-python `_parse/_transform.py`](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python/blob/main/src/anthropic/lib/_parse/_transform.py) — `json_schema.pop("additionalProperties", None)` then `strict_schema["additionalProperties"] = False`
- [anthropic-sdk-typescript `transform-json-schema.ts`](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-typescript/blob/main/src/lib/transform-json-schema.ts) — same coercion

**Affected paths:** the native `output_format` path — `azure_ai` Claude, direct `anthropic`, and bedrock native structured outputs. `vertex_ai` is unaffected because LiteLLM deliberately forces Vertex Claude onto the permissive tool-use path (#18625 / #19201), which ignores these keywords.

**Real-world impact.** On our proxy this silently sends ~10–20% of daily Claude structured-output traffic to a cross-provider fallback (Azure rejects → falls back to Vertex). With no fallback configured it is a hard client-facing 400.

**Note on scope:** this is *not* covered by the recent keyword-stripping work in the same function (#33981 / #34313 / #34319, shipped in v1.95.0) — those diffs contain zero `additionalProperties` changes. Prior art that did contain the correct coercion, both closed unmerged: #22447 (included a test literally named *"additionalProperties: true should be overridden to false for objects"*) and #22500. The current add-only guard was introduced by the still-open #21045.

### Steps to Reproduce

**A. Minimal unit-level reproduction (no API key required)** — this is the clearest signal:

1. Install/check out LiteLLM at `v1.96.0` (also reproduces on `v1.95.0` and current `main` / `litellm_internal_staging`).
2. Run:

```python
from litellm.llms.anthropic.chat.transformation import AnthropicConfig

cases = {
    "top-level explicit true": {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": True,
                                "properties": {"a": {"type": "string"}}},
    "nested under properties": {"type": "object", "properties": {
                                "o": {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": True,
                                      "properties": {"a": {"type": "string"}}}}},
    "inside array items":      {"type": "object", "properties": {
                                "r": {"type": "array", "items": {
                                      "type": "object", "additionalProperties": True,
                                      "properties": {"a": {"type": "string"}}}}}},
    "dict sub-schema form":    {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": {"type": "string"},
                                "properties": {"a": {"type": "string"}}},
    "control: key absent":     {"type": "object", "properties": {"a": {"type": "string"}}},
}

def leaked(o):
    out = []
    if isinstance(o, dict):
        for k, v in o.items():
            if k == "additionalProperties" and v is not False:
                out.append(v)
            out += leaked(v)
    elif isinstance(o, list):
        for v in o:
            out += leaked(v)
    return out

for name, schema in cases.items():
    result = AnthropicConfig.filter_anthropic_output_schema(schema)
    print(f"{name:26s} -> leaked non-false additionalProperties: {leaked(result) or 'NONE (ok)'}")
```

3. Observe that every explicit form survives the filter and would be sent to Anthropic:

```
top-level explicit true    -> leaked non-false additionalProperties: [True]
nested under properties    -> leaked non-false additionalProperties: [True]
inside array items         -> leaked non-false additionalProperties: [True]
dict sub-schema form       -> leaked non-false additionalProperties: [{'type': 'string'}]
control: key absent        -> leaked non-false additionalProperties: NONE (ok)
```

Only the `control` case (key absent) is handled correctly. Expected: all five print `NONE (ok)`.

**B. End-to-end reproduction against a real Claude deployment on the native `output_format` path** (we used `azure_ai/claude-sonnet-4-6`; direct `anthropic/` works too):

1. Configure a Claude model on a native-`output_format` provider, e.g.:

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: claude-sonnet-4-6
    litellm_params:
      model: azure_ai/claude-sonnet-4-6
      api_base: os.environ/AZURE_AI_API_BASE
      api_key: os.environ/AZURE_AI_API_KEY
```

2. Send a structured-output request whose schema has an explicit `additionalProperties: true`:

```bash
curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
    "model": "claude-sonnet-4-6",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Emit a minimal valid result."}],
    "max_tokens": 250,
    "response_format": {"type":"json_schema","json_schema":{"name":"r","schema":{
      "type":"object",
      "required":["rules"],
      "properties":{"rules":{"type":"array","items":{
        "type":"object",
        "required":["rule_id"],
        "properties":{"rule_id":{"type":"string"}},
        "additionalProperties":true}}}}}}
  }'
```

3. Observe HTTP 400 (see log output below).

4. Change `"additionalProperties": true` to `false` and re-send — it succeeds. That isolates the trigger to the explicit `true`.

> ⚠️ **Reproduction gotcha:** if the model group has a fallback to another deployment on a *different* provider (e.g. `vertex_ai`), LiteLLM transparently retries there and returns **HTTP 200**, hiding the Azure rejection. We chased this for several rounds. To see the 400, either remove the fallback or address the Azure deployment **directly by its `model_id`**, and/or confirm the serving provider via `custom_llm_provider` in `LiteLLM_SpendLogs`.

### Relevant log output

```
litellm.BadRequestError: Azure_aiException - b'{"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"output_format.schema: For \'object\' type, \'additionalProperties: true\' is not supported. Please set \'additionalProperties\' to false"},"request_id":"req_011CdiGH686teY8qpkxwe2mP"}'
```

### Are you a ML Ops Team?

No

### What LiteLLM version are you on?

v1.96.0 (also reproduces on v1.95.0 and current `litellm_internal_staging`)

title: [Bug]: Standalone virtual-key soft_budget alert is not sent to Slack
body:
## Summary

A standalone virtual key with a configured `soft_budget` exceeds the budget but does not emit a `soft_budget_crossed` Slack alert, even after subsequent valid requests.

## Environment

- LiteLLM: `v1.93.0` (`ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database`)
- Deployment: Kubernetes, multiple LiteLLM proxy replicas
- PostgreSQL and Redis configured
- The key is a virtual key with no team association

Relevant proxy configuration:

```yaml
general_settings:
  alerting:
    - slack
  alert_types:
    - budget_alerts
  alert_to_webhook_url:
    budget_alerts: os.environ/SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL
  alerting_args:
    budget_alert_ttl: 86400
```

## Reproduction

1. Create or update a standalone virtual key with `soft_budget: 0.001`.
2. Make a valid request with the key that incurs about `$0.0103` usage.
3. Confirm through `GET /key/info?key=...` that the key has a soft budget and that its spend exceeds it.
4. Wait for asynchronous spend persistence.
5. Make two further valid requests using the same virtual key.
6. Wait longer than the Slack batching flush interval.

The key has no `team_id`; however, the soft-budget alert code constructs a `CallInfo` with `event_group=KEY`, so team membership does not appear to be required.

## Expected behavior

Once the key's spend is at or above its `soft_budget`, a later request should cause LiteLLM to send a Slack `soft_budget_crossed` alert.

## Actual behavior

No Slack alert is received after the budget is exceeded and subsequent valid requests are made.

## Checks already completed

- All LiteLLM pods have a non-empty `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` environment variable.
- The live `litellm-config` ConfigMap contains `alerting: [slack]`, `budget_alerts` in `alert_types`, and `alert_to_webhook_url.budget_alerts: os.environ/SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL`.
- The virtual key's `/key/info` response confirms a soft budget and spend above it.
- The key is not associated with a team.
- `llm_requests_hanging` is independently producing a Pydantic validation error when a request has `model=None`; this appears unrelated to the missing budget alert.

## Suspected cause

The key soft-budget check uses `valid_token.spend`:

```python
if valid_token.soft_budget and valid_token.spend >= valid_token.soft_budget:
    asyncio.create_task(proxy_logging_obj.budget_alerts(...))
```

Please confirm whether linked budget-table `soft_budget` values are reliably propagated into `valid_token.soft_budget` for standalone virtual keys, and whether cache/batched spend tracking can leave this field stale despite `/key/info` showing the updated spend.

A second concern: budget-alert deduplication is set before the asynchronously queued Slack POST is confirmed. If a Slack send fails, this may suppress retries for `budget_alert_ttl` (24h), while the delivery failure is only debug-logged.

title: [Bug]: Grace periode during key rotation not working `TypeError: Litellm_VerificationTokenView` object
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [ ] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

## Summary 

LiteLLM's `key/regenerate` endpoint accepts `grace_periode` parameter that should keep the old key valid for transitional period after regeneration.
Both old and new keys are expectedto work until grace periode elapses.

On the LiteLLM version v1.89.0 , the grace periode is **recorded in database** but the **old key fails to authenticate** with `TypeError` .

## Affected version  
- Litellm docker version 1.89.0
- File : `litellm/proxy/utils.py`

## What works 

1. the `key/regenerate` API **accepts** `grace_periode` parameter without error 
2. The old key 's hash is correctly stored in the `LiteLLM_DeprecatedVerificationToken` table with
  - `token` - SHA-256 hash of old key 
  - `active_token_id` - links to new key's `token_id`
  - `revoked_at` - timestamp = creation time + grace period
3. The new key created and work properly 

## What doesn't work 

When a request authenticates with the **old key** after regeneration , LiteLLM finds the deprecated token in database but crashes while reading the result : 

```
TypeError: 'LiteLLM_VerificationTokenView' object is not subscriptable
``` 

### Error response

```json
{
    "error": {
        "message": "Authentification Error, 'LiteLLM_VerificationTokenView' object is not subscriptable",
        "type": "auth_error",
        "params": "None",
        "code": "401"
    }
}
```

##Root cause 
The bug is in `litellm/proxy/utils.py`, line **3645**:

```python
if response["team_model"] is None:                                # BUG : dict-style subscript
      response["team_models"] = []                                   # BUG : same 
```
the `response` variable is a `LiteLLM_VerificationTokenView`  **object** ( a prisma model ) not a dict 

## Call chain  

```
chat/completions (with old key)
-> auth_check.py:2483  _fetch_key_object_from_db_with_reconnect()
  -> utils.py: 3645   get_data()
    -> response["team_models"]  <- TypeError here 
 ```
 

## Fix 

Three changes in the `get_data` methode around line 3500 in  `utils.py`

### 1. Convert prisma model to dict

```python
# before broken 
if response["team_models"] is None:


# Fixed version 
if hasattr(response,"model_dump"):                      # check if Pydantic v2 model
    response = response.model_dump() 
elif hasattr(response,"dict"):                                  # check if Pydantic v1 model
    response = response.dict()

if response.get("team_models") is None:

```

### 2. Use `get()` instead of `[]` for field access

```python
# before 
if response["team_members_with_roles"] is not None

# after 
if response.get("team_members_with_roles") is not None
```

### 3 Remove `last_refreshed_at` before reconstructing 

 `model_dump()` includes `last_refreshed_at` but the code passes it again as keyword argument when constructing `LiteLLM_VerificationTokenView` causing a "multiple values for keyword argument" error:


```python
# before ( broken)
response = LiteLLM_VerificationTokenView(**response, last_refreshed_at=time.time())

# after ( fixed)

response.pop("last_refreshed_at", None)
response = LiteLLM_VerificationTokenView(**response, last_refreshed_at=time.time())

```


### Steps to Reproduce

1. Re Generate an existing key with `grace_periode`
2. Try to use the old key ( still in grace periode )
3. Error in authentification

```shell

```

Proxy

v1.89.0

title: [Bug]: /key/update lets a non-admin caller set max_budget, budget_limits, and temp_budget_increase above their own delegation ceiling
body:
## Description

`/key/generate` enforces a delegation ceiling: a non-admin caller cannot mint a key whose budget exceeds their own `max_budget`. This is implemented twice in `litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/key_management_endpoints.py`, once for the scalar `max_budget` and once for `budget_limits` (multi-window budgets):

- `_common_key_generation_helper` computes `delegation_ceiling = user_api_key_dict.max_budget` (or the caller's team budget for session tokens) and rejects `_requested_max_budget > delegation_ceiling` for non-admin, non-UI-session-team-key callers (key_management_endpoints.py:900-920).
- The same function then calls `_check_budget_limits_delegation_ceiling(budget_limits=data.budget_limits, delegation_ceiling=delegation_ceiling, ...)` (key_management_endpoints.py:922-928), which rejects any `budget_limits[*].max_budget` above that same ceiling (key_management_endpoints.py:668-716).

Neither check is wired into `update_key_fn` (key_management_endpoints.py:2607), and there is no equivalent check anywhere else on that path.

`update_key_fn` does gate *who* may touch budget fields at all: `_validate_update_key_data` computes `_is_budget_change` for `max_budget`/`spend`/`budget_limits` (key_management_endpoints.py:2447-2451) and routes non-proxy-admin callers through `_check_key_admin_access` (key_management_endpoints.py:2479-2487, defined at key_management_endpoints.py:5980). That function only checks *identity* (proxy admin, team admin for the key's team, or org admin for the team's org, key_management_endpoints.py:5980-5996) — it never compares the new budget value to the caller's own `max_budget`. So a team admin who is not a proxy admin, and who is fully authorized to call `/key/update` on their own team's keys, can set:

- `max_budget` to any finite non-negative value (the only validation on update is the finiteness/non-negative check at key_management_endpoints.py:2698-2702, no ceiling comparison)
- `budget_limits` to any list of finite windows, unbounded (no call to `_check_budget_limits_delegation_ceiling` anywhere in the update path)
- `temp_budget_increase` to any value (this field is not part of `_is_budget_change` at all, so it does not even trigger the identity check, let alone a ceiling check)

## Impact

A team admin whose own key is capped at, say, `max_budget: 10` can raise a teammate's key (or their own key, if self-service update is reachable via `caller_is_creator`) to an effectively unlimited budget through `/key/update`, entirely bypassing the delegation model that `/key/generate` enforces for the identical fields. This defeats the purpose of the ceiling added for `max_budget` and `budget_limits` (GHSA-q775-qw9r-2r4g), and gives `temp_budget_increase` no ceiling at all on either endpoint.

## Suggested fix

Compute the same `delegation_ceiling` in `update_key_fn` / `_validate_update_key_data` (caller's own `max_budget`, or team budget for session tokens, mirroring key_management_endpoints.py:900-904) and, for non-proxy-admin callers, reuse `_check_budget_limits_delegation_ceiling` for `data.budget_limits` and the existing scalar comparison for `data.max_budget`, gated the same way `_is_budget_change` already is. `temp_budget_increase` should be checked against the ceiling too: the boosted effective budget (existing `max_budget` or `budget_limits` window plus the increase) should not exceed the caller's own `max_budget`.

## Related

Distinct from #35247 (`temp_budget_increase` was a no-op on `budget_limits` keys) and its fix in #35265, which corrected *whether* the boost applies but did not touch *who* is allowed to grant it or *how large* a boost a non-admin caller may grant. This issue is about the missing authorization ceiling on the update path, not the enforcement-side bug those fixed.

title: stream_chunk_builder concatenates every choice into one message when n > 1
body:
### What happened?

`stream_chunk_builder` merges every choice of every chunk into a single message, so an `n > 1` streamed response is reassembled into one choice whose content is the interleaved concatenation of all completions. The result is text no model produced.

```python
import litellm
from litellm.types.utils import Delta, ModelResponseStream, StreamingChoices

def c(i, txt, fin=None, role=None):
    d = {"content": txt}
    if role:
        d["role"] = role
    return ModelResponseStream(id="chatcmpl-1", created=1, model="gpt-4o",
                               object="chat.completion.chunk",
                               choices=[StreamingChoices(index=i, delta=Delta(**d), finish_reason=fin)])

# what an n=2 OpenAI stream looks like after CustomStreamWrapper: one choice per
# chunk, index alternating 0/1
chunks = [c(0, "AAA", role="assistant"), c(1, "BBB", role="assistant"),
          c(0, " aaa"), c(1, " bbb"), c(0, None, "stop"), c(1, None, "stop")]

r = litellm.stream_chunk_builder(chunks, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}])
print("choices:", len(r.choices))
print("content:", repr(r.choices[0].message.content))
```

```
choices: 1
content: 'AAABBB aaa bbb'
```

Expected two choices, `'AAA aaa'` and `'BBB bbb'`. A single-choice stream through the same call is correct, so this is specific to `n > 1`:

```
control n=1 -> choices: 1 content: 'AAA aaa'
```

### Root cause

`ChunkProcessor.get_combined_content` (`litellm/litellm_core_utils/streaming_chunk_builder_utils.py`) iterates every choice of every chunk and joins the deltas into one string:

```python
for chunk in chunks:
    choices = chunk["choices"]
    for choice in choices:
        ...
        content_list.append(content)
combined_content = "".join(content_list)
```

and `build_base_response` in the same file emits a single hardcoded `{"index": 0, ...}` choice. `stream_chunk_builder`'s fast path in `litellm/main.py` likewise appends `chunk["choices"][0]` content regardless of its index. Nothing partitions the chunks by `choices[0].index`.

### Why it matters beyond the return value

The reassembled response is not only handed back to the caller. It is used for cost and token accounting and for success callbacks, it is returned directly when `complete_response=True`, and it is what gets written to the response cache. So a cached streamed `n=2` call later replays text that no model generated, and the token accounting is computed against that concatenation.

### Not a duplicate

The closest prior reports are #3276 ("chat.completion.chunk's index is invalid when using n>=2 and stream=True") and #3526 ("Chat completion quits early when n>2 and stream=True"), both closed and both about the SSE chunks emitted to the client rather than the reassembled `complete_streaming_response`; neither mentions `stream_chunk_builder`. The `stream_chunk_builder` PRs I found (#23663, #8009, #5025, #32954) are unrelated. No issue or PR mentions grouping choices by index.

Worth noting that the wrapper layer is fine: running the same content through the real `CustomStreamWrapper` with `custom_llm_provider="openai"` yields correct per-index deltas. Only the reassembly is wrong.

### Suggested direction

Partition by index at the top of `stream_chunk_builder`, before the fast path: collect the distinct `chunk["choices"][0]["index"]` values, and when there is more than one, split into one chunk list per index (routing choice-less chunks, such as the trailing `include_usage` chunk, to the first group only), recurse once per group so all the existing single-choice assembly is reused untouched, then concatenate the resulting choices with the index reset per position and sum `completion_tokens` across groups. The `n = 1` path stays byte-identical, which keeps the blast radius bounded on a hot path.

I am filing this rather than opening a PR because I already have #35118 open against this same function and did not want to stack a second change on it or create a conflict for the reviewer. Happy to send the fix once that one lands, or sooner if you would rather have it now.

### Relevant log output

_No response_

No

Reproduced against `main`; the two functions involved are unchanged between the latest release and `main` apart from typing syntax.

title: fix: json_tool_call response not unwrapped for Vertex AI Claude (parameter envelope)
body:
## Bug

When using `response_format: {"type": "json_schema", ...}` with `vertex_ai/claude-*` models, the response `message.content` contains `{"parameter": {"facts": [...]}}` instead of the expected `{"facts": [...]}`.

## Root Cause

litellm converts `json_schema` response_format to a `json_tool_call` tool for Anthropic models. Claude responds with a tool_use content block. `_convert_tool_response_to_message()` unwraps `{"values": ...}` (line 2494 in `anthropic/chat/transformation.py`) but does not handle the `{"parameter": ...}` wrapper that Vertex AI Anthropic returns.

Bedrock has a similar unwrapper (`_unwrap_bedrock_properties`) for the `{"properties": ...}` key, but neither handles `"parameter"`.

## Reproduction

```python
import litellm
import json

# Any complex Pydantic schema with $defs triggers this
schema = {
    "$defs": {"Fact": {"type": "object", "properties": {"what": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["what"]}},
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {"facts": {"type": "array", "items": {"$ref": "#/$defs/Fact"}}},
    "required": ["facts"],
    "title": "FactExtractionResponse"
}

response = litellm.completion(
    model="vertex_ai/claude-opus-4-6",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Python is fast."}],
    response_format={"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {"name": "FactExtractionResponse", "schema": schema, "strict": False}},
    max_tokens=200,
)

content = json.loads(response.choices[0].message.content)
print(content.keys())  # dict_keys(['parameter']) -- should be dict_keys(['facts'])
```

## Impact

Any downstream tool that parses `message.content` and expects the schema-defined structure gets an unexpected wrapper. For example, [Hindsight](https://github.com/vectorize-io/hindsight) silently drops all extracted facts (vectorize-io/hindsight#3028).

## Environment

- litellm: 1.88.1 (also reproduced on latest main)
- Model: `vertex_ai/claude-opus-4-6`
- Auth: GCP Application Default Credentials
- Behavior: 100% consistent, not intermittent

Will submit PR with fix + tests.

title: [Bug]: Expired UI session tokens pollute SpendLogs — dashboard info-route 401s are recorded as failed LLM requests
body:
### What happened?

Every `/ui` login mints a virtual key under `team_id="litellm-dashboard"` with a 24h expiry (`LITELLM_UI_SESSION_DURATION`). When that key expires, any dashboard tab left open keeps replaying it against the info routes the UI polls (`/key/list`, `/user/info`, `/models`, `/model/info`, ...). Each 401 is then **written to `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` as a failed LLM request** — the Usage/Logs pages show rows with `Type: LLM`, a session id, `Unknown item` for the model, and null values for most fields.

The practical impact is that a stale browser tab is indistinguishable from key abuse in the spend logs. In our deployment (gateway fronting Bedrock spend), an open weekend tab produced a multi-hour burst of "failed LLM requests" that triggered a key-compromise investigation before we traced it to this:

```
Key Expiry time 2026-08-01 10:37:52  /  current time 2026-08-03 19:05:27
```

(~2 days stale, still politely retrying every poll interval.)

A secondary confusion: `LAST ACTIVE` on the key is stamped on the *attempt*, not on success, so the Keys page shows keys "active" half an hour after their own expiry — which reinforces the key-abuse misread.

### Root cause

The failure-logging gate admits **LLM API routes OR info routes**, in two places:

1. `ProxyLogging._is_proxy_only_llm_api_error` (`litellm/proxy/utils.py`) — gates `_handle_logging_proxy_only_error`, which builds the failure through `litellm_logging_obj` / `StandardLoggingPayload` (the LLM logging path — hence the `Type: LLM` rendering) and fans it out to failure callbacks (DB, s3, langfuse, ...).
2. `_ProxyDBLogger.async_post_call_failure_hook` (`litellm/proxy/hooks/proxy_track_cost_callback.py`) — the same `is_llm_api_route(route) or is_info_route(route)` condition in front of the SpendLogs DB write.

The comment above the gate says it exists so management-endpoint auth failures *don't* get logged ("This fixes a security issue where we would log temporary keys/auth info from management endpoints"). But `LiteLLMRoutes.info_routes` (`litellm/proxy/_types.py`) is precisely the set of endpoints the dashboard polls with its session token — so the carve-out re-admits exactly the traffic the fix was written to exclude.

Since a GET to `/key/list` has no `messages`/`prompt`/`input`, the `call_type` normalization in `_handle_logging_proxy_only_error` never fires, and the row keeps its route-derived call type — rendered as an LLM request in the UI.

### Prior reports

This has been reported at least three times; all were closed by the stale bot, none fixed:

- #19894 — "UI session token authentication failures polluting LiteLLM Spend Logs"
- #12806 — "Unknown team (litellm-dashboard) generate thousands of Auth error requests" (6 orgs affected in the thread; attempted fix #12845 closed unmerged)
- #16118 — "LiteLLM generates excessive failure logs during runtime"

Related: #35665 proposes tagging UI-issued session credentials so revocation can be scoped — the same discrimination this fix needs (this fix uses the existing `team_id == UI_SESSION_TOKEN_TEAM_ID` marker).

Note: the new `ExpiredUISessionKeyCleanupManager` deletes the expired *key rows*, but does not stop the failure spend-log writes — the two are complementary.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start the proxy with a database and log into `/ui`.
2. Let the session key expire (default 24h; set `LITELLM_UI_SESSION_DURATION=10m` to speed it up), keeping the tab open.
3. Interact with the tab (or just let its polling run).
4. Observe rows in the Logs/Usage pages: `Type: LLM`, session id set, `Unknown item` model, `team_id=litellm-dashboard`, hashed key of the expired session token.

### Proposed fix

For UI session tokens only (`team_id == UI_SESSION_TOKEN_TEAM_ID`), stop admitting **info-route** failures into the failure-logging paths. Everything else is unchanged:

- info-route failures from real virtual keys → still logged (whatever the original reason info routes were admitted for, it stays intact),
- LLM-route failures from the UI session token (playground test calls) → still logged,
- management routes → still never logged.

PR with the change + tests: (attached)

### Relevant log output

```shell
Authentication Error - Expired Key. Key Expiry time 2026-08-04 07:16:29.794000+00:00 and current time 2026-08-04 07:16:55.272249+00:00
INFO: "GET /key/list?... HTTP/1.1" 401 Unauthorized
# -> row appears in LiteLLM_SpendLogs with status=failure, Type: LLM, session id set
```

v1.93.1 (mechanism verified unchanged on litellm_internal_staging HEAD)

title: [Feature]: Dynamic TPM allocation per team / key / model
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### The Feature

## Summary

LiteLLM's current TPM enforcement uses a static output token estimate of 1024 when `max_tokens` is absent from the request.
This is insufficient for real-world usage where different  teams, and keys have vastly different output token patterns per model.

## Current behaviour 

### Static 1024 floor 
**File:** `litellm/proxy/hooks/parallel_request_limiter_v3.py`

```python
DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS_ESTIMATE = 4096
_TPM_FLOOR_FRACTION = 4

#when max_tokens is absent:
output_floor = DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS_ESTIMATE  // _TPM_FLOOR_FRACTION
# (4096 // 4 ) = 1024 ( static for all models/key/teams)
```

##  Proposed Feature 

When `max_tokens` is absent from the request the TPM reservation uses `default_estimated_output_tokens ` from team / key  config instead of static 1024 floor


### Core: Per key per model `default_estimated_output_tokens `

Add `default_estimated_output_tokens_per_model ` field to the key's `metadata` ( JSON column , no DB migration needed ). This is a JSON object mapping model names to their estimated output token count 

```bash
POST /key/generate
{
  "team_id": "team-1",
  "tpm_limit": 1000000
  "metadata": {
    "default_estimated_output_tokens": 2048
    "default_estimated_output_tokens_per_model": {
      "gpt-4":4096,
      "gpt-3.5-turbo": 1026
    }
  }
}


Allow teams to have `default_estimated_output_tokens `override:

```bash
POST /team/update
{
  "team_id": "team-1",
  "tpm_limit": 1000000
  "metadata": {
    "default_estimated_output_tokens": 4096
    "default_estimated_output_tokens_per_model": {
      "gpt-4":8192,
      "gpt-3.5-turbo": 2048
    }
  }
}
```

## Backward compatability 

- if no `default_estimated_output_tokens` or `default_estimated_output_tokens_per_model` is configured behaviour is unchanged 
- Uses existing `metadata` JSON Column on keys and teams **no DB Migration required**

# Resolution priority 

Priority order for output token estimation:
1. `max_tokens` / `max_completion_tokens` from request ( if present )
2. key.metadata.default_estimated_output_tokens_per_model[model] 
3. key.metadata.default_estimated_output_tokens
4. team.metadata.default_estimated_output_tokens_per_model[model] 
5. team.metadata.default_estimated_output_tokens


### Motivation, pitch

This is a security and faireness issue. The current static floor allows TPM limit bypass, which can cause cost overruns and unfair resource allocation between teams and keys 

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

No

title: [Bug]: Lowest-cost routing does not resolve provider-prefixed model pricing
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

  `cost-based-routing` treats provider-prefixed model names such as `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` as missing from the model cost map, even though
  the corresponding bare entry `gpt-5.6-luna` exists

  `LowestCostLoggingHandler.async_get_available_deployments()` performs a direct lookup with
  `litellm.model_cost.get(item_litellm_model_name, {})`. It does not use the provider-prefix resolution performed by `get_model_info()`
  and the regular cost calculator

  When the deployment model is `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`, the lookup misses and both input and output costs default to `5.0`, producing a
  routing cost of `10.0`. Other provider-prefixed OpenAI models receive the same fallback cost, so the strategy can select a more
  expensive deployment based on its original list order

  For example, `openai/gpt-5.6-sol` can be selected ahead of `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`, even though Luna has substantially lower input and
  output prices

  Expected behavior: lowest-cost routing should resolve `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` to the existing `gpt-5.6-luna` cost-map entry, consistent
  with `litellm.get_model_info()` and regular completion cost calculation

### Steps to Reproduce

```python
import asyncio

import litellm
from litellm.caching.caching import DualCache
from litellm.router_strategy.lowest_cost import LowestCostLoggingHandler


async def main() -> None:
    deployments = [
        {
            "model_name": "test-group",
            "litellm_params": {"model": "openai/gpt-5.6-sol"},
            "model_info": {"id": "sol"},
        },
        {
            "model_name": "test-group",
            "litellm_params": {"model": "openai/gpt-5.6-luna"},
            "model_info": {"id": "luna"},
        },
    ]

    handler = LowestCostLoggingHandler(router_cache=DualCache())
    selected = await handler.async_get_available_deployments(
        model_group="test-group",
        healthy_deployments=deployments,
    )

    print(f"selected={selected['model_info']['id']}")
    print(f"prefixed_entry={litellm.model_cost.get('openai/gpt-5.6-luna')}")
    print(f"bare_luna_input_cost={litellm.model_cost['gpt-5.6-luna']['input_cost_per_token']}")
    print(f"bare_sol_input_cost={litellm.model_cost['gpt-5.6-sol']['input_cost_per_token']}")


asyncio.run(main())

```

title: [Bug]: datadog_llm_observability callback: tool_calls and cache tokens sent in meta.metadata instead of their designated API fields (meta.output.messages[].tool_calls and span metrics)
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

The datadog_llm_observability callback stringifies all messages before sending them to the DD LLM Obs intake API, losing the structured fields that Datadog's UI depends on to render tools, prompts, and token-level cache metrics.

**Root Cause**

Two separate mapping gaps in DataDogLLMObsLogger.create_llm_obs_payload:

1. Tool calls → nested metadata dict instead of Message.tool_calls

_extract_tool_call_metadata places tool calls in meta.metadata as:

```
{
  "output_tool_calls": {
    "0": {
      "function": { "name": "task", "arguments": "..." },
      "id": "toolu_bdrk_01F8reQpVqbKBRYRkdthjYZT",
      "type": "function"
    }
  }
}
```

DD's API expects them on the output message:

```
{
  "meta": {
    "output": {
      "messages": [{
        "role": "assistant",
        "content": "",
        "tool_calls": [
          { "name": "task", "arguments": {...}, "tool_id": "toolu_bdrk_...", "type": "function" }
        ]
      }]
    }
  }
}
```

2. Cache tokens → usage_object blob in metadata instead of span metrics

The full usage object is dumped into meta.metadata.usage_object:

```
{
  "usage_object": {
    "cache_creation_input_tokens": 35007,
    "cache_read_input_tokens": 16695,
    "prompt_tokens": 16872,
    "prompt_tokens_details": { ... }
  }
}
```

DD's API expects these as top-level span metrics:

```
{
  "metrics": {
    "input_tokens": 16872,
    "output_tokens": 704,
    "cache_read_input_tokens": 16695,
    "cache_write_input_tokens": 35007,
    "non_cached_input_tokens": 177
  }
}
```

**Impact**

Feature Data present?	DD can parse it?	Why not

**Tools panel (agent obs)**	
Data present?: Yes — meta.metadata.output_tool_calls	
DD can parse it?: No	
Why not: DD reads meta.output.messages[].tool_calls, not metadata

**Cache hit ratio**	
Data present?: Yes — meta.metadata.usage_object.cache_read_input_tokens	
DD can parse it?: No	
Why not: DD reads span metrics.cache_read_input_tokens, not nested metadata

**Cache write tokens**	
Data present?: Yes — meta.metadata.usage_object.cache_creation_input_tokens	
DD can parse it?: No	
Why not: DD reads metrics.cache_write_input_tokens

**Tool definitions**	
Data present?: Available in request tools	
DD can parse it?: Not sent at all	DD reads meta.tool_definitions
Why not: DD reads meta.tool_definitions

**Tool results**	
Data present?: In input messages	
DD can parse it?: Stringified by handle_any_messages_to_chat_completion_str_messages_conversion	
Why not: DD reads Message.tool_results

**Observed Metadata Payload (actual)**

First span (cache write, tool call):

```
{
  "cache_hit": false,
  "model_name": "bedrock/global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-6-v1",
  "model_provider": "bedrock",
  "output_tool_calls": {
    "0": {
      "function": {
        "name": "task",
        "arguments": "{\"description\": \"Find DD LLM obs callback code\", ...}"
      },
      "id": "toolu_bdrk_01F8reQpVqbKBRYRkdthjYZT",
      "type": "function"
    }
  },
  "usage_object": {
    "cache_creation_input_tokens": 35007,
    "cache_read_input_tokens": 0,
    "prompt_tokens": 35010,
    "completion_tokens": 363
  }
}
```

Second span (cache hit, no tool call):

```
{
  "cache_hit": false,
  "usage_object": {
    "cache_creation_input_tokens": 176,
    "cache_read_input_tokens": 16695,
    "prompt_tokens": 16872,
    "completion_tokens": 704
  }
}
```

Note: cache_hit: false despite cache_read_input_tokens: 16695 — this is the LiteLLM response-cache flag, not prompt cache. The field name is confusing and doesn't map to DD's concept of cache hits.


**Suggested Fix**

1. Map tool_calls onto output messages

In _get_response_messages, preserve tool_calls on the assistant message mapped to DD's ToolCall schema:
```
def _get_response_messages(self, standard_logging_payload, call_type):
    # ... existing extraction of choices[0]["message"] ...
    message = choices[0]["message"]
    dd_message = {"role": message.get("role", "assistant"), "content": message.get("content", "")}
    
    if "tool_calls" in message:
        dd_message["tool_calls"] = [
            {
                "name": tc["function"]["name"],
                "arguments": json.loads(tc["function"]["arguments"]) if isinstance(tc["function"]["arguments"], str) else tc["function"]["arguments"],
                "tool_id": tc.get("id", ""),
                "type": tc.get("type", "function"),
            }
            for tc in message["tool_calls"]
        ]
    return [dd_message]

```
2. Map tool role messages to ToolResult on input

When processing input messages:
```
if msg.get("role") == "tool":
    dd_msg = {
        "role": "tool",
        "tool_results": [{
            "tool_id": msg.get("tool_call_id", ""),
            "result": msg.get("content", ""),
            "name": "",  # resolve from matching assistant tool_call if available
        }]
    }
```

3. Forward cache metrics to span metrics dict

```
usage_obj = standard_logging_payload.get("usage_object") or {}
cache_creation = usage_obj.get("cache_creation_input_tokens", 0)
cache_read = usage_obj.get("cache_read_input_tokens", 0)
prompt_tokens = usage_obj.get("prompt_tokens", 0)

if cache_creation:
    metrics["cache_write_input_tokens"] = float(cache_creation)
if cache_read:
    metrics["cache_read_input_tokens"] = float(cache_read)
if prompt_tokens and (cache_creation or cache_read):
    metrics["non_cached_input_tokens"] = float(prompt_tokens - cache_read)
4. Send tool_definitions on meta
# In create_llm_obs_payload, if tools are in the request:
tools = kwargs.get("tools") or standard_logging_payload.get("tools", [])
if tools:
    meta["tool_definitions"] = [
        {"name": t["function"]["name"], "description": t["function"].get("description", ""), "schema": t["function"].get("parameters", {})}
        for t in tools if t.get("type") == "function"
    ]
```

**Environment**

- LiteLLM version: v1.96.0-rc.1
- Provider: AWS Bedrock (Anthropic Claude Sonnet 4.6)
- DD callback mode: Agentless (direct API to api.datadoghq.com)
- enable_anthropic_prompt_caching: true

**Related**
- _process_input_messages_preserving_tool_calls exists but is dead code
- _tool_calls_kv_pair extracts to flat KV — this approach doesn't match DD's API schema
- DD API reference: https://docs.datadoghq.com/llm_observability/setup/api/?tab=example

That covers the full scope. The stringification is the root problem — tools, cache, multi-modal, and prompt structure are all downstream casualties of the same handle_any_messages_to_chat_completion_str_messages_conversion call.

title: Feature request: add an OpenAI-compatible Fusion model on top of Auto Router
body:
## Problem

LiteLLM's Router and Auto Router are well suited to selecting one deployment/model for a request. There is a related use case where the caller wants to fan out one prompt to several candidate models in parallel and then ask an aggregator model to synthesize the final answer (Mixture-of-Agents / Fusion, similar to Together MoA and Hermes MoA).

Today this requires an external orchestration service, even though LiteLLM already provides the provider translation, retries/fallbacks, callbacks, spend tracking, rate limiting, and OpenAI-compatible API surface needed by each sub-call.

## Proposed feature

Add an optional composite/Fusion model which is exposed through the normal OpenAI-compatible endpoint:

```json
{
  "model": "fusion/coding",
  "messages": [
    {"role": "user", "content": "Review this implementation"}
  ]
}
```

The Fusion layer would:

1. Select a configured candidate set, optionally through Auto Router.
2. Call reference model groups in parallel using the existing LiteLLM Router.
3. Drop failed/timed-out candidates according to a configurable policy.
4. Send successful candidate responses to an aggregator model, also through the existing Router.
5. Return the aggregator response in the normal Chat Completions format.

## Suggested configuration

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: coding-fast
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-5-mini

  - model_name: coding-deep
    litellm_params:
      model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5

  - model_name: coding-alt
    litellm_params:
      model: gemini/gemini-2.5-pro

  - model_name: fusion-aggregator
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-5

fusion_models:
  - model_name: fusion/coding
    selector:
      type: static
      models:
        - coding-fast
        - coding-deep
        - coding-alt
    aggregator:
      model: fusion-aggregator
    fusion_params:
      min_successful_responses: 2
      max_parallel_requests: 3
      reference_timeout: 45
      aggregator_timeout: 90
      failure_mode: best_effort
      tool_calling: aggregator_only
```

An Auto Router selector could later be configured as:

```yaml
selector:
  type: auto_router
  candidate_models:
    - coding-fast
    - coding-deep
    - coding-alt
  top_k: 3
```

## Important implementation boundary

The existing Router currently has a useful single-deployment selection contract. It would be safer to keep that contract unchanged and add a separate Fusion Orchestrator above it:

```
Fusion Orchestrator
  -> existing LiteLLM Router (reference calls)
  -> existing LiteLLM Router (aggregator call)
```

This would avoid making every routing strategy handle a multi-deployment return value. A future selector interface could expose an optional `RoutingPlan` / Top-K API while preserving the current single-model API for backward compatibility.

## MVP scope

- Chat Completions API.
- Static candidate model groups.
- Async parallel reference calls.
- One aggregator model.
- Best-effort and fail-closed policies.
- Aggregator-only tool calling; reference calls do not execute tools.
- Final aggregator streaming after reference calls complete.
- Correlation metadata for reference/aggregator calls.
- Reuse existing Router behavior for retries, fallbacks, callbacks, budgets, and spend tracking.
- Reject recursive/nested Fusion configurations.

## Open questions

- Should configuration live under a new `fusion_models` section or be represented as a special model type in `model_list`?
- Should Top-K Auto Router selection be introduced as a new optional selector API rather than changing `async_get_available_deployment()`?
- What is the preferred usage/cost representation for the N+1 underlying calls?
- Should Responses API and tool-call judging be part of the initial implementation or follow-up work?

## Success criteria

- Existing LiteLLM clients work by changing only the model name to a configured Fusion model.
- Reference calls run concurrently and respect per-call timeout/cancellation.
- A partial provider failure does not unnecessarily fail the whole request.
- All underlying calls remain visible to existing callbacks and spend tracking.
- Existing non-Fusion Router strategies and configurations remain backward compatible.

Would this direction fit the Router/Proxy architecture? I would be happy to contribute an MVP implementation once the configuration and extension boundary are agreed.

title: [Bug]: Responses API sends metadata to a strict OpenAI-compatible upstream although the client does not pass metadata
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

We use LiteLLM Proxy with a custom OpenAI-compatible `/v1/responses` backend.

Our Python application calls `litellm.aresponses()` without passing a `metadata` argument. However, the upstream backend rejects the request with:

```text
Unsupported parameter: metadata
```

Changing the client-side model prefix from `openai/test-responses-model` to `litellm_proxy/test-responses-model` does not change the result.

The observed flow is:

```text
LiteLLM Python client 1.90.4
  -> LiteLLM Proxy 1.93.0
  -> custom OpenAI-compatible /v1/responses backend
  -> HTTP 400: Unsupported parameter: metadata
```

The application call site is equivalent to:

```python
raw_response = await litellm.aresponses(
    model="litellm_proxy/test-responses-model",
    input=input_value,
    instructions=instructions,
    store=False,
    text=text,
    max_output_tokens=max_output_tokens,
    api_key=api_key,
    api_base=proxy_url,
    timeout=request_timeout_seconds,
)
```

No `metadata` argument is passed by the application.

We cannot yet prove which Proxy component introduces or retains the field. The confirmed observation is that it is absent from the client call site, while the upstream rejection identifies a top-level `metadata` parameter.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a Proxy deployment using the OpenAI provider with a custom OpenAI-compatible Responses endpoint:

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: test-responses-model
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/test-upstream-model
      api_base: https://strict-upstream.example/v1
      api_key: os.environ/UPSTREAM_API_KEY

litellm_settings:
  drop_params: true
```

2. Call the Proxy using `litellm.aresponses()` as shown above, without a `metadata` argument.
3. Use an upstream Responses implementation that rejects unsupported top-level parameters.
4. Observe the upstream error:

```text
Unsupported parameter: metadata
```

### Expected behavior

LiteLLM's internal routing, authentication, tracing, or logging metadata should not be serialized into the public OpenAI `metadata` request field.

Only metadata explicitly supplied by the API caller should be sent as Responses API metadata. Internal values should remain in LiteLLM-specific structures such as `litellm_metadata`.

If the field is retained from another Proxy code path rather than introduced by the Proxy, there should be a documented way to prevent it from reaching a deployment whose upstream does not support it.

### Actual behavior

A top-level `metadata` parameter reaches the upstream request and causes the complete Responses call to fail with HTTP 400.

Global `drop_params: true` does not prevent the failure.

### Workaround

Adding a deployment-level drop rule prevents the error:

```yaml
litellm_params:
  additional_drop_params:
    - metadata
```

We validated this workaround on LiteLLM Proxy 1.95.0. After applying it, the following succeeded against the same strict upstream:

- `/v1/responses` non-streaming JSON
- `/v1/responses` SSE streaming
- `/v1/chat/completions` with tool calls
- Proxy SpendLogs attribution

### Relevant log output

```text
HTTP 400
Unsupported parameter: metadata
```

Sensitive hostnames, model names, credentials, account identifiers, and request IDs have been replaced with placeholders.

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy — native `/v1/responses` routing to a custom OpenAI-compatible upstream.

### What LiteLLM version are you on?

- Proxy where the failure was observed: 1.93.0
- Python client: 1.90.4
- Proxy where the workaround was validated: 1.95.0

### Additional context

Possibly related, but not duplicates:

- #19700 — `additional_drop_params` / metadata handling on another request path
- #6022 — separation of public `metadata` and internal `litellm_metadata`
- #25402 — hardcoded metadata leakage during `/v1/responses/compact` fallback

Could you confirm where the top-level `metadata` field may be introduced or retained on the normal Proxy `/v1/responses` path?

We can provide additional sanitized tracing if needed.

title: [Bug]: LiteLLM_SpendLogs has no (api_key, startTime) index — budget-window spend reseed seq-scans the table and can saturate the DB (P2028)
body:
### What happened?

Under normal traffic, our proxy fleet started failing spend-update transactions with Prisma `P2028` ("Unable to start a transaction in the given time", surfaced via `db_exceptions` Slack alerts from `_commit_spend_updates_to_db`). The Postgres instance (AWS RDS, 2 vCPU) was pinned at ~94% CPU for the duration.

RDS Performance Insights showed essentially **all** DB load came from a single tokenized statement:

```sql
SELECT "api_key", SUM("spend")
FROM "LiteLLM_SpendLogs"
WHERE "api_key" = $1 AND "startTime" >= $2
GROUP BY "api_key"
```

PI stats during the incident window: **avg 1.18 s per execution**, ~3.2 calls/sec sustained (~3,800 executions in 20 min) → ~3.75 average active sessions on a 2-vCPU instance = CPU saturation → concurrent spend-log commit transactions could not start within their 60 s timeout → `P2028`.

### Root cause

The query is issued by `SpendCounterReseed.window_from_spend_logs()` (`litellm/proxy/db/spend_counter_reseed.py`), called from `_authoritative_floor_spend()` in `proxy_server.py`. This runs on the **request path** whenever a Redis budget-window counter is cold (fresh pods, TTL expiry, quiet-traffic periods), for keys/teams with `budget_duration`-style windows.

But `schema.prisma` defines only these indexes on `LiteLLM_SpendLogs`:

```prisma
@@index([startTime])
@@index([startTime, request_id])
@@index([end_user])
@@index([session_id])
```

There is **no index on `api_key`** (and none on `team_id`, which the `entity_type == "Team"` branch of the same function filters on). When `$2` (the window start) covers a large fraction of the table — e.g. a daily/weekly window — the `startTime` index is not selective, so Postgres walks the rows and filters `api_key` one by one. Cost grows linearly with table size, and the reseed can storm when counters go cold across multiple pods simultaneously.

### Verification of the fix

Adding the composite index:

```sql
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY "LiteLLM_SpendLogs_api_key_startTime_idx"
ON "LiteLLM_SpendLogs" ("api_key", "startTime");
```

changes the plan to an Index Scan with both conditions in the Index Cond, and execution time drops from **~1,180 ms to 0.106 ms**:

```
GroupAggregate  (cost=0.55..8.58 rows=1 width=72) (actual time=0.062..0.063 rows=0 loops=1)
  ->  Index Scan using "LiteLLM_SpendLogs_api_key_startTime_idx" on "LiteLLM_SpendLogs"
        Index Cond: ((api_key = '...'::text) AND ("startTime" >= ...))
Execution Time: 0.106 ms
```

### Suggested fix

Add to `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` in `schema.prisma` (+ migration in `litellm-proxy-extras`):

```prisma
@@index([api_key, startTime])
@@index([team_id, startTime])
```

so the per-request budget-window reseed is an index range scan regardless of spend-log table size.

### Relevant log output

```
DB read/write call failed: 504: {"is_panic":false,"message":"Transaction API error: Unable to start a transaction in the given time.","meta":{"error":"Unable to start a transaction in the given time."},"error_code":"P2028"}
[Non-Blocking]LiteLLM Prisma Client Exception - update spend logs: 504 ...
  File "litellm/proxy/db/db_spend_update_writer.py", line 1136, in _commit_spend_updates_to_db
    async with prisma_client.db.tx(timeout=timedelta(seconds=60)) as transaction:
```

### Version

LiteLLM v1.93.0 (`litellm-database` image), Postgres 16 (AWS RDS), 3 proxy instances, Redis enabled.

title: [Feature]: honor x-litellm-tags header on MCP gateway routes (tools/list, tools/call)
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### The Feature

Parse the `x-litellm-tags` request header on MCP gateway requests (`/mcp` and `/{server_alias}/mcp`) and attach the tags to the spend logs of MCP operations (tools/call, tools/list), the same way LLM routes already do.

Current behavior (verified in the v1.93.0 and v1.95.0 sources):

- LLM routes parse the header in `LiteLLMProxyRequestSetup.add_litellm_data_to_request` (`litellm/proxy/litellm_pre_call_utils.py`, `if "x-litellm-tags" in headers:`), so tags land in `LiteLLM_SpendLogs.request_tags`.
- On the MCP path nothing reads the header: `_experimental/mcp_server/mcp_server_manager.py` (tool-call spend logging) has no tags handling, and in `_experimental/mcp_server/server.py` the `request_tags` parameter of `_get_tools_from_mcp_servers` is never populated by any caller.
- The only MCP component that merges `x-litellm-tags` is the sampling handler (MCP server calling back into `/chat/completions`), which is a different flow.
- PR #29122 / LIT-3304 covers tag propagation for auto-executed MCP sub-calls spawned from `/chat/completions`, not header-supplied tags on direct MCP gateway calls.

Proposal: extract tags from the headers in `MCPRequestHandler.process_mcp_request` (or in the logging setup for MCP tool calls) and include them as `metadata.tags` in the request data used for spend logging, mirroring the LLM route behavior.

### Motivation, pitch

We expose MCP servers to API consumers through an API gateway (Gravitee) with LiteLLM as the MCP proxy. The gateway injects `x-litellm-tags: application: <app>,service: <api>` on every proxied request. For LLM routes this gives us per-application usage attribution in LiteLLM; for MCP routes the same header is silently ignored, so MCP usage cannot be attributed to gateway applications and all calls appear only under the shared virtual key identity. Honoring the header on MCP routes would make tag-based attribution consistent across LLM and MCP traffic.

However, if I change the LiteLLM Model Name to `vertex_ai/claude-sonnet-5@default`, the custom costs are calculated and logged perfectly. ### Expected Behavior Both `vertex_ai/claude-sonnet-5` and `vertex_ai/claude-sonnet-5@default` appear in the UI dropdown. `vertex_ai/claude-sonnet-5` should correctly trigger Vertex AI Anthropic token parsing (including cache tokens) and apply custom pricing overrides, just like the `@default` alias does. ### Actual Behavior `vertex_ai/claude-sonnet-5` fails to map to the correct Vertex-Anthropic cost calculator logic. Because it cannot parse the caching tokens properly, it drops the custom pricing overrides and defaults the cost to `$0.00`. ### Environment - **LiteLLM version:** 1.93.0 - **Provider:** Vertex AI - **Client:** OpenCode ### Suggested Fix Update `model_prices_and_context_window.json` to ensure `vertex_ai/claude-sonnet-5` is properly aliased to `vertex_ai/claude-sonnet-5@default` so it inherits the correct Vertex Anthropic pricing and token-counting architecture. Below I posted a screenshot where you see logs with costs and some without. The only difference is that i only changed the Litellm-Modelname. The ones with the cost has the name: `vertex_ai/claude-sonnet-5@default` ### Steps to Reproduce 1. In the LiteLLM Proxy UI, click "Add Model". 2. Select provider: Vertex AI. 3. In the "LiteLLM Model Name" dropdown, select `vertex_ai/claude-sonnet-5`. 4. Set a custom model name (e.g., `claude-sonnet-5-some-foo`). 5. Send a request with custom per-token pricing (e.g., via OpenCode passing Input: $3, Output: $15). 6. Check the proxy logs/usage: Cost shows `$0.000000`. 7. Edit the model in LiteLLM UI and change the LiteLLM Model Name to `vertex_ai/claude-sonnet-5@default`. 8. Send the exact same request. 9. Check the proxy logs/usage: Cost is calculated correctly based on the custom pricing. ### Relevant log output ```shell ``` ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? _No response_ ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? 1.93.0 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_
author: cuberinooo

title: [Bug]: read-replica routing serves virtual-key auth reads, so revoked keys keep working and new keys are rejected while the replica lags
body:
## Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate

Nothing covers replica routing and key authentication together. #33021 is about pool params and IAM URL params on the same feature, and #35742 is about the reader URL never being assembled on the CLI path; both are orthogonal to which reads get routed. #28265 (open PR, warm `user_api_key_cache` on `/key/generate`) touches the same auth-cache-miss path and would mask half of the second symptom below, but not the revocation one

## What happened?

With `DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA` set, `RoutingPrismaWrapper` routes every `find_unique` / `find_first` to the reader (`litellm/proxy/db/routing_prisma_wrapper.py:16` and `:55`). That set includes the virtual-key lookup that authentication depends on: `get_key_object` misses the cache, calls `_fetch_key_object_from_db_with_reconnect` (`litellm/proxy/auth/auth_checks.py:2595`), which reaches `PrismaClient.get_data` and its `find_unique` on `LiteLLM_VerificationToken` (`litellm/proxy/utils.py:3455`) through `VerificationTokenRepository.table`, and that property resolves to `self.prisma_client.db` (`litellm/repositories/verification_token_repository.py:49`), which is the routing wrapper

The result is two failures whenever the replica is behind, both reproduced below:

Revoked keys keep working. `/key/delete` writes to the writer and then invalidates the cache entry, with the intent stated in the code itself: "UPDATE KEY CACHE - invalidate so next read re-fetches from DB" (`litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/key_management_endpoints.py:6141`). With routing on, that next read is served by the replica, which still has the pre-revocation row, so the proxy re-caches the revoked key and keeps authorizing it. The existing auth cache does not contain this; the revocation path is built on the assumption that the next DB read is authoritative

New keys are rejected. A key created through `/key/generate` exists only on the writer until replication catches up. The first request using it misses the cache, reads the replica, finds nothing, and returns 401 `token_not_found_in_db` for a key the API just issued

In both cases the exposure window is replication lag plus the cache TTL (`DEFAULT_IN_MEMORY_TTL` defaults to 5s, `litellm/constants.py:342`), so a replica that is seconds behind gives seconds of a revoked key still working, and an endpoint under load or catching up on WAL gives correspondingly more. The same routing applies to the team, user, end-user, budget and object-permission lookups in `auth_checks.py`, so permission and budget changes have the same lag, though the two symptoms above are the ones I reproduced

## Expected behavior

Authentication and authorization reads should be authoritative: the virtual-key lookup, and ideally the team / user / permission reads that decide whether a request is allowed, should go to the writer even when read routing is enabled, leaving the replica for reads that tolerate eventual consistency (spend views, logs, list endpoints, UI queries)

At minimum, a revoked key must not become usable again because the invalidating write and the following read are served by different endpoints

## Steps to Reproduce

Replication lag is made deterministic here by using two independent Postgres instances and freezing the second one at a snapshot, so the "replica" is simply behind by exactly the operations that follow the snapshot. No lag simulation or timing games are needed

`compose.yml`:

```yaml
name: rr-lag
services:
  pgw:
    image: postgres:17-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: litellm
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: litellm
      POSTGRES_DB: ai_gateway
    ports: ['5432:5432']
  pgr:
    image: postgres:17-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: litellm
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: litellm
      POSTGRES_DB: ai_gateway
    ports: ['5433:5432']
```

`config.yaml`:

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: fake-model
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-4o-mini
      api_key: sk-fake
      api_base: http://127.0.0.1:9/v1
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  store_model_in_db: true
```

The unreachable `api_base` is what makes the result unambiguous: 401 means authentication rejected the key, 500 means authentication accepted it and only the upstream call failed

```bash
docker compose up -d --wait

# 1. writer only, so migrations run and a key is created
LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=sk-lag-1234 LITELLM_SALT_KEY=sk-salt LITELLM_LOG=INFO \
DATABASE_URL='postgresql://litellm:litellm@127.0.0.1:5432/ai_gateway' \
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port 4000 --num_workers 1 &

KEY=$(curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4000/key/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-lag-1234' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"key_alias":"lag-demo","models":["fake-model"]}' | jq -r .key)

# 2. snapshot the writer into the second instance: this is the replica, frozen at this point
docker exec rr-lag-pgw-1 pg_dump -U litellm -d ai_gateway --clean --if-exists > snapshot.sql
docker exec -i rr-lag-pgr-1 psql -q -U litellm -d ai_gateway < snapshot.sql

# 3. revoke the key on the writer; the replica still has the row
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4000/key/delete -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-lag-1234' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"keys\":[\"$KEY\"]}"

# 4. restart with read routing on
kill %1
DATABASE_URL='postgresql://litellm:litellm@127.0.0.1:5432/ai_gateway' \
DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA='postgresql://litellm:litellm@127.0.0.1:5433/ai_gateway' \
LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=sk-lag-1234 LITELLM_SALT_KEY=sk-salt LITELLM_LOG=INFO \
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port 4000 --num_workers 1 &

# 5. the revoked key still authenticates
curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'revoked_key=%{http_code}\n' -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"fake-model","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'

# 6. and a key created right now does not
NEW=$(curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4000/key/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-lag-1234' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"key_alias":"lag-demo-2","models":["fake-model"]}' | jq -r .key)
curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'new_key=%{http_code}\n' -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $NEW" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"fake-model","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
```

Running the same revocation with `DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA` unset is the control, and it returns 401 immediately

## Relevant log output

```shell
# control: no read routing, revocation takes effect at once
delete=200
use_after_revoke=401

# read routing on against the frozen replica, same revocation
$ docker exec rr-lag-pgw-1 psql -U litellm -d ai_gateway -tAc \
    "select count(*) from \"LiteLLM_VerificationToken\" where key_alias='lag-demo-2';"
0
$ docker exec rr-lag-pgr-1 psql -U litellm -d ai_gateway -tAc \
    "select count(*) from \"LiteLLM_VerificationToken\" where key_alias='lag-demo-2';"
1
$ for i in 1 2 3; do sleep 3; curl ... /v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"; done
attempt1=500
attempt2=500
attempt3=500

# a key issued two seconds earlier, same proxy
new_key=401
{"error":{"message":"Authentication Error, Invalid proxy server token passed. Received API Key = sk-...Yv3A,
Key Hash (Token) =f348c488...  Unable to find token in cache or `LiteLLM_VerificationTokenTable`",
"type":"token_not_found_in_db","param":"key","code":"401"}}
```

Both were reproduced from source at `a625d1e1ca` (current `litellm_internal_staging` head), with startup logging `read-replica routing enabled via DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA`

## What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

## What LiteLLM version are you on ?

v1.94.0-dev.3 (source at a625d1e1ca)

title: [Bug]: LiteLLM UI strips SERVER_ROOT_PATH subpath on conversation select and message send
body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

When LiteLLM is configured with a _SERVER_ROOT_PATH_ (e.g., litellm), navigating to an existing conversation or sending a new message strips the subpath prefix from the browser URL, routing the UI back to the root domain.

**Expected Behavior**
The SERVER_ROOT_PATH subpath should be preserved in the URL during navigation and chat state updates:
[https://domain.com/litellm/ui/chat/](https://domain.com/litellm/ui/chat/)

**Actual Behavior**
The subpath is dropped, redirecting/updating the route to:
[https://domain.com/ui/chat/](https://domain.com/ui/chat/)

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure LiteLLM with SERVER_ROOT_PATH="litellm"
2. Access the LiteLLM UI via the subpath URL: [https://domain.com/litellm/ui/chat/](https://domain.com/litellm/ui/chat/).
3. Perform either of the following actions:

- Select an existing conversation from the chat history sidebar.
- Type a message and click Send in a new conversation.
4. Observe the URL in the browser address bar.

author: ddwong1984

title: [Feature]: Add optional Microsoft Graph user search to Invite User modal
body:
## The Feature

Add an optional Microsoft Entra ID / Microsoft Graph directory search to the LiteLLM Admin UI “Invite User” modal.

When enabled by environment/config, proxy admins could search users from their Microsoft tenant by name or email, select a result, and have LiteLLM prefill the existing invite/create-user form with the selected user’s email and optionally metadata such as Azure object id.

This would not auto-provision users, sync groups, map RBAC, or replace SCIM. It would only make the existing manual invite flow easier and less error-prone for Microsoft Entra customers.

## Motivation, pitch

Today, admins creating internal users in LiteLLM need to manually type user emails. In organizations using Microsoft Entra ID, this is easy to mistype and does not help admins discover the right user.

SCIM and automatic Entra group/member sync are documented as Enterprise/Premium flows, and this proposal is intentionally narrower: an OSS-safe optional directory lookup that still uses the existing `/user/new` invite flow.

## Proposed behavior

- Add optional Microsoft Graph config, e.g. tenant/client credentials or reuse compatible Microsoft SSO config where appropriate.
- Add a backend endpoint for proxy admins to search Microsoft Graph users.
- Add a searchable selector in the Invite User modal.
- Selecting a result fills `user_email`.
- Existing `/user/new` behavior remains unchanged.
- Feature is disabled when Microsoft Graph config is absent.

## Component

UI Dashboard + Proxy

## Duplicate check

I searched existing issues for Azure AD invite user directory search, Microsoft Graph invite user, and SCIM Azure users invite and did not find an obvious duplicate.
